news.abstract: Clinton Administration's stand that it has right to attack Iraq to force Saddam Hussein to open sites to weapons inspectors is based on succession of Security Council resolutions and statements and on United Nations Charter; American and other diplomats are pressing Security Council for new resolution declaring Iraq in 'material breach' of its commitments, move opposed by Russia (M)
news.title: U.N. Resolutions Allow Attack on the Likes of Iraq

news.abstract: Sonia Gandi, campaigning for Congress Party, is only figure who has shown any signs of rousing Indian electorate from widespread apathy; noncandidate draws large crowds across nation reminiscent of enthusiasm stirred by her mother-in-law, late Indira Gandhi, and her slain husband, Rajiv Gandhi; few believe she alone can restore party to dominant position it long held; polls indicate swing toward Bharatiya Janata Party, Hindu nationalist group; photo (M)
news.title: Vast India Seeks a Focus in Its Election Campaign

news.abstract: Israel's planning for its 50th anniversary celebration is in disarray, as Tourism Min Moshe Katsav resigns role in effort, citing negative stories leaked to press by Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu's office; agrees not to quit Government after Netanyahu condemns press attacks; resignation follows successive resignations of three directors of planning committee, which is mired in political, budgetary and personal squabbles; date of formal start of celebration has been changed several times and many events canceled or changed (M)
news.title: Israel's 50th Anniversary Preparations Are Mired in Squabbling

news.abstract: Indonesian security forces are preparing for social unrest as millions of people lose their jobs during nation's deepening recession; situation at steel plant in Surabaya noted; map (M)
news.title: Bad News, Silver Lining For Indonesian Laborers

news.abstract: Cristobal Martinez-Bordiu, surgeon who cared for Gen Francisco Franco and married Franco's only child, dies at age of 75 (M)
news.title: Cristobal Martinez-Bordiu, 75, Surgeon Who Cared for Franco

news.abstract: South Korea's Pres-elect Kim Dae Jung reaches landmark agreement with business and unions that lays groundwork for layoffs throughout nation and brings country big step closer to resolving its economic crisis (M)
news.title: Seoul Agrees on Layoffs and New Cuts in Effort to End Crisis

news.abstract: Diplomatic emissaries have descended on Baghdad in current crisis with Iraq, all of them opposed to heavy bombing that US has threatened and all of them willing to consider compromise with Saddam Hussein to prevent it; negotiations underscore vast division over UN inspections of Iraq's military sites; map (M)
news.title: Push for Peace Shows Split Over Inspections

news.abstract: United Nations chief weapons investigator Richard Butler tells Security Council that recent proposals floated by Iraq to defuse crisis over weapons inspections are not good enough (M)
news.title: Top U.N. Arms Monitor Is Said to Call Iraqi Plans to End Crisis Inadequate

news.abstract: Two Marine Corps F-18 fighters on training mission collide over Persian Gulf, killing one of pilots; photo (S)
news.title: One Pilot Is Killed as 2 U.S. Marine Jets Collide Over the Gulf

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  A senior U.S. commander has expressed concern that Indonesia could be on the verge of social and political instability.
news.title: U.S. Commander Sounds Alert on Indonesia Unrest

news.abstract: Brig Gen Guy M Vander Linden, who is in charge of naval operations in southern Europe, acknowledges that jet that sheared ski lift cables in Cavalese, Italy, on Feb 3 was flying well below approved minimum altitude and that pilot, Capt Richard J Ashby, reportedly told his lawyer that he came up to cable too suddenly for evasive actions; says aircraft appears to have stayed within its assigned 10-nautical-mile-wide flight corridor although it did stray from its point-to-point flight track; marine aviators familiar with plane involved, EA-6B Prowler, dispute suggestion, attributed to Ashby, altimeter failure may have caused plane to fly too low; map (M)
news.title: Jet in Italy Flew Too Low, A Top U.S. Official Admits

news.abstract: Canadian salmon fishermen and state of Alaska reach tentative agreement to drop countersuits involving blockade of an Alaskan ferry in Prince Rupert, British Columbia, during summer of 1997 (S)
news.title: Canadians and Alaska to Halt Lawsuits

news.abstract: Existing United Nations Security Council resolutions appear to offer ample legal basis for renewed American and British military action against Iraq, but politically the two countries are on shakier ground; there is no agreement with France, Russia, China and other countries over what the Iraqis have to do to comply with Council's inspection requirement and avoid military attack; scale of contemplated bombing is far more ambitious than previous strikes; goal and outcome are uncertain (M)
news.title: The Issues Are Political More Than Legal at U.N.

news.abstract: Profile of and interview with Brazilian Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso, leftist intellectual turned champion of free market, who has made low inflation the new religion of Brazilians; Cardoso is most responsible for turning Brazil into a global player, and forcing its people and industries to compete--to varying degrees--in a modern econoy; photo (M)
news.title: Brazil's Reformist Chief Rides a Bucking Bronco

news.abstract: Survey of neo-Nazi scene in eastern Germany; sociologists, politicians and residents assert that across the former East Germany, neo-Nazi wave is building on spoiled hopes of Germany's unification, drawing as much on nostalgia for clear-cut conformism of Communist dictatorship as on equally unambiguous nationalism and racial exclusivism of Nazism; styling themselves, moreover, as freedom fighters--paradoxically in tradition of leftist guerrilla warfare--young neo-Nazis are seeking to establish what they call 'national liberated zones'; Interior Ministry statistics show that of 6,400 violence-prone neo-Nazis estimated to be in Germany, 3,700--more than half--live in eastern Germany; in first six months of 1997, police recorded 4,829 crimes committed by neo-Nazis--353 of them involving violent attacks; map (M)
news.title: Neo-Nazis Carving Out Fiefs in Eastern Germany

news.abstract: Defense Sec William S Cohen seeks to contain political fallout in Italy over deaths caused when American jet clipped ski lift's cable, pledging full cooperation in joint investigation and review of all NATO training flights in Italy; despite his pledges and apologies, it is clear that divisions remain over investigation and its consequences (M)
news.title: Cohen Tries To Calm Italy Over Deaths At Ski Lift

news.abstract: Asian students in United States colleges--from South Korea, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand--are feeling economic squeeze as currencies of those countries have fallen hard over several months; students see bank accounts halved, parents thrown out of work, family businesses dissolved; a number of students have merely toned down spending habits that had been fed by boom times at home; but others are struggling to stay in United States, where they have found broader range of programs in technology, business, science and the arts in a less stringent atmosphere than back home; photo (L)
news.title: Economic Troubles Back Home Squeeze Asian Students in U.S.

news.abstract: United Nations' long-muddled 'oil-for-food' program, plan allowing Iraq to sell some oil to meet urgent needs of its people, is finally beginning to make a difference, although problems and shortfalls remain, particularly in medicine and medical equipment; lack of medicine is caused not only by sanctions but also by Govt decisions to build palaces and monuments (M)
news.title: U.N.'s Long-Muddled 'Oil-for-Food' Program Makes Progress in Iraq

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  Ivy League and other prestigious universities in the United States compete vigorously to recruit the best and the brightest of each year's crop of African-American high school graduates. Last June Malaika Jones was one of them.
news.title: 'Black' Colleges Are Luring Back Their Own From the Ivy Leagues

news.abstract: SEOUL—  From 7 A.M. to well into the evening, in hundreds of small classrooms across the country, young Koreans are struggling to learn English conversation.
news.title: A Little English Goes Far in Seoul

news.abstract: British tabloids are recycling news about late Princess Diana and are casting about for stand-in figures to halt flagging circulation; photo (M)
news.title: London Journal; Diana's Hereafter, an Eternity of Newsstand Life

news.abstract: LONDON—  The word "Montessori" can produce an astonishing array of responses, from "too lax" to "too strict" to "cultish." The images range from pre-schoolers running wild to others forced to sit still with folded hands.
news.title: The Many Faces of Montessori

news.abstract: Crew of US Air Force jet that shared ski lift cables in northern Italy killing all 20 passengers aboard cable car, issue message of sympathy to families of victims; US officials deny charges that delay in handing over jet's mission recorder is part of attempted cover-up (M)
news.title: Jet Crew Voices Sympathy for Ski Lift Victims' Kin

news.abstract: Israel's Chief Rabbinate categorically rules out any cooperation with non-Orthodox branches of Judaism on conversions and religious rites, but stops short of overtly discarding proposed compromise; Reform and Conservative leaders in Israel and US say decision represents outright rejection and call it declaration of war; say they will immediately resume legal and political battles for recognition of their conversions, which they suspended during search for compromise; Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu, who has been dogged by issue since he took office and has sought to avoid confrontations between various streams of Judaism, hails decision; says it promotes national consensus among Jewish people and state of Israel (M)
news.title: Israel's Chief Rabbis Reject Call By Non-Orthodox on Conversion

news.abstract: American Jewish Committee, in move reflecting resurgence of Jewish life in Germany, opens permanent office in Berlin at site once owned by Jewish family that fled Nazis; ceremonies attended by high-level German, US and Israeli officials (M)
news.title: U.S. Jewish Group Sets Up Office In Berlin as Sentinel Against Bias

news.abstract: Rev Jesse Jackson visits Kenya for second time in three months as Pres Clinton's special envoy in effort to defuse ethnic tensions and keep democratic reforms on track (S)
news.title: World News Briefs; Jesse Jackson in Kenya In Effort to End Violence

news.abstract: Arrest of three anti-kidnapping agents from police force in Morelos state, Mex, including chief of its anti-kidnapping squad, lends credence to allegations by businessmen and human rights activists that have been long scoffed at by authorities, that police have been protecting kidnapping gangs terrorizing area south of Mexico City; map (M)
news.title: Police-Kidnapper Links Seen in Mexico

news.abstract: UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan cancels long-planned trip to Middle East to help work toward peaceful solution of Iraqi crisis as diplomatic efforts intensify; efforts of Russia, France and Arab League to find formula acceptable to Iraq as well as Security Council discussed (M)
news.title: U.N. Chief Cancels Trip to Mideast as a Hunt for Compromise Continues

news.abstract: Palestinian police ban pro-Iraqi demonstrations on West Bank and Gaza Strip, which have turned into anti-American displays and clashes with Israeli soldiers; Palestinian Authority fears demonstrations could raise tensions with Israel and harm ties with United States (S)
news.title: Ban on Protests In West Bank

news.abstract: United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan, urging flexibility in finding peaceful solution to Iraqi crisis, holds UN should not insist on humiliating Pres Saddam Hussein; sounds his strongest reservations yet about military option; Britain circulates document about Iraqi chemical weapon not previously mentioned publicly by UN inspectors (M)
news.title: No Need to Humiliate Iraq, The Secretary General Says

news.abstract: Marine Corp relieves Lt Col Stephen L Watters of command of squadron of jets like one that severed cables of Cavalese, Italy, ski lift because he told crew members to destroy potential evidence in probe; probe has broadened to include his squadron, which was not involved in incident, because it rotates with squadron involved; at issue is whether crews break altitude rules for training flights (M)
news.title: Inquiry on Ski-Lift Deaths Leads Marines to Relieve a Colonel

news.abstract: Fear of political instability spurred by economic crisis has brought more Indonesian troops into streets, with Surabaya, nation's second-largest city, on full alert; residents, despite outward nonchalance, are nervous about reports of latest riots in smaller towns; only major eruption in Jakarta is seen likely to have big impact on nation's stability; map; photo (M)
news.title: Edginess Becomes a Way of Life for Indonesians

news.abstract: Some members of White House panel of experts on illnesses of Persian Gulf war veterans, noting United States preparations to bomb Iraqi poison gas sites, cite possible link between veterans' illnesses and exposure to Iraqi poison gas, letter to Pres Clinton; Prof Marguerite Knox, letter's main author, disputes recent news reports suggestings illnesses result soley from wartime stress; Prof Arthur L Caplan, letter signer, warns American troops are still not adequately defended against chemical or biological arms (M)
news.title: Bombing Gas Sites May Pose Risk of Gulf War Syndrome

news.abstract: Irish Republic and Britain say they will soon decide whether to expel Sinn Fein, Irish Republican Army's political wing, from Northern Ireland peace talks because of new violence attributed to IRA; Irish Prime Min Bertie Ahern and British Min Mo Mowlam comment (S)
news.title: World News Briefs; Britain and Ireland Weigh Sinn Fein Ouster

news.abstract: Mexican Pres Ernesto Zedillo expresses confidence that war on drugs is succeeding, interview; cites unprecedented drive against narcotics corruption in army; holds United States process of annually certifying anti-drug efforts of scores of nations is probably detrimental to war on drugs; discusses political reform; outlines what seems to be hardening approach to Zapatista guerrillas in Chiapas state; discusses nation's economic recovery; cites concern over mounting crime; photo (M)
news.title: A Growing Optimism on Ending Graft in Mexico

news.abstract: BANGKOK—  Despite the opposition of the World Bank and the doubts of many economists, Indonesia confirmed Wednesday that it intended to stabilize its battered currency by pegging it at a fixed rate.
news.title: Jakarta's Plan To Peg Rupiah Powers a Rally Across Region

news.abstract: Defense Sec William S Cohen visits aircraft carrier USS George Washington, which polices 'no flight' zone over southern Iraq; says he hopes American military buildup in area will result in peaceful end to confrontation with Iraq; photo (M)
news.title: On U.S. Carrier, Not Just a Routine Day

news.abstract: United Nations weapons inspectors reportedly have found 1995 document indicating Russia discussed selling Iraq equipment that could be used to develop biological weapons; Iraq offers to open for limited time small number of sites it has closed to arms inspectors; United States and Britain continue to insist on full access to all sites (M)
news.title: A Possible Russian Link to Iraq Arms Buildup

news.abstract: Brazilian lawmakers approve bills to strip down social security benefits and job protections; measures are cornerstone of Govt's four-year plan to stabilize economy (M)
news.title: Brazil Congress Votes to Scale Down Social Security Benefits

news.abstract: Military analysis of possible United States confrontation with Iraq; America's vast weaponry is seen insufficent to accomplish what Pres Clinton has stated as goal of military action: to 'substantially reduce or delay' Iraq's ability to develop and deliver weapons of mass destruction; senior American military officials say there is wide gap between political aims administration has set forth and military ability to achieve them (M)
news.title: American Arms vs. Iraq

news.abstract: Russian officials announce they have arrested retired military intelligence official, Pavel Popovskikh, in connection with killing of investigative journalist three years ago; journalist, Dmitri Kholodov, had been investigating corruption in Russian military when he was killed by opening booby-trapped suitcase (M)
news.title: Russia Arrests Ex-Colonel In '94 Killing Of Journalist

news.abstract: Palestinians, one day after Israel began celebrating its 50th year of independence, gather in Ramallah, West Bank, to plan different sort of commemoration: 50th anniversary of what they call 'the catastrophe'; nakbah, which also means calamity or disaster, is Arabic word that Palestinians use to describe their defeat and exodus in 1948 Arab-Israeli war that followed Israel's declaration of independence; at conference, organized by Palestinian Authority's ministry of culture, politicians, intellectuals, educators and community leaders gather to plan year of activities memorializing their loss; photo of Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat (M)
news.title: 1948-98: 50-Year Palestinian 'Catastrophe'

news.abstract: Japanese Prime Min Ryutaro Hashimoto's uncertain stewardship of his country's economy discussed; officials in Washington and Asian capitals are increasingly alarmed and angered by Hashimoto's reluctance to stimulate fragile Japanese economy; they fear that his inaction could worsen Asian financial crisis and provoke global slowdown; they foresee economic confrontation about international repercussions of Japan's domestic economic policy, rather than about trade barriers; photo (M)
news.title: For a Shaky Japanese Economy, The Premier Is a Hesitant Steward

news.abstract: Sec Gen Kofi Annan sends technical team to Iraq to clear up confusion over so-called presidential sites that Saddam Hussein has declared off-limits to United Nations inspectors (M)
news.title: Technical Team Is Sent to Iraq To Try to Define Off-Limits Sites

news.abstract: Pres Clinton and top aides begin preparing nation for war in Iraq and for grim prospect of civilian casualties on the ground and of American pilots shot down from the skies; Clinton says he would not be deterred by Russia's opposition to an attack on Iraq if Pres Saddam Hussein does not allow United Nations weapons inspectors unfettered access; photo of memorial in Baghdad to people killed by American bombs in an attack on suburb of Amiriya on Feb 13, 1991 (M)
news.title: Another Rebuff to Iraq

news.abstract: Pres Boris Yeltsin's opposition to American military action against Iraq is shared by Russia's political and business elite and the average Russian and reflects potent combination of foreign policy and commercial interests; economic ties include $3.8 billion agreement signed by Lukoil, Russia's premier oil company, to develop Iraq's Qurna oilfield once economic sanctions are removed; many Russians still find it hard to accept that US has the power, will and resources to launch a military campaign in the face of determined Russian opposition; however, there is no serious talk of providing military assistance to Baghdad or desire for renewing cold war hostilities with US; Russia also has a generally satisfactory record of observing economic sanctions against Iraq; graph of Russian opinion poll on conflict (M)
news.title: Russia's Stake In Iraq Bolsters Anti-War Cry

news.abstract: American scientists will seek to determine whether new form of anthrax created by Russians through genetic engineering is merely theoretical or a practical weapon and whether it is able to defeat the vaccine American troops will soon get to protect them from anthrax (M)
news.title: Gene-Engineered Anthrax: Is It a Weapon?

news.abstract: French police rule out any connection between car crash that killed Diana, Princess of Wales, and a white Fiat once owned by a celebrity photographer (M)
news.title: French Police Rule Out Lead in Diana's Death

news.abstract: Peru, in what some call ambitious family planning program run amok, reportedly pressures poor women to undergo sterilization operations; program has led to deaths of at least two women and injured hundreds; critics say health workers, hurrying to meet quotas, are not telling women about alternative methods of contraception or that sterilization is usually irreversible; say many state doctors perform sloppy operations, at times in unsanitary conditions; photo (M)
news.title: Using Gifts as Bait, Peru Sterilizes Poor Women

news.abstract: Mohamed al-Fayed, whose son, Dodi, died in Paris car crash with Diana, Princess of Wales, backs theory that couple was murdered, newspaper interview; her family and Buckingham Palace score stand (M)
news.title: Now Murder Is Suggested In the Death Of Diana

news.abstract: India's election campaign is rocked by series of bomb explosions that kill at least 30 peoplein southern city of Coimbatore as thousands gather for rally by Hindu nationalist leader Lal Kishinchand Advandi (S)a
news.title: Bomb Blasts at Campaign Rally in India Kill 30

news.abstract: Three former Croatian soldiers who testified before war crimes tribunal say they have been repeatedly subjected to beatings and death threats; Zdenko Bando, Milan Levar and Zdenko Ropac say that hundreds of ethnic Serbs, as well as Croats who opposed the nationalist movement, were executed and buried in mass graves around town of Gospic by the Croation Army, paramilitary groups and police; say documents they turned over to The Hague implicate senior Croatian officals, including Defense Min Gojko Susak; photo (M)
news.title: Threats Worry 3 Who Tied Croatian Army to Atrocities

news.abstract: Local officials in southern China, after years of neglect, are getting serious about protecting elephants and other wildlife, punishing poachers severely; say elephant population has stabilized at over 200 (M)
news.title: Elephants Are Friends, China Tells Its Farmers

news.abstract: Enos Mafokate, 52, barred by apartheid from becoming show jumper, runs only riding academy for young blacks in South Africa, Soweto; photos (M)
news.title: Soweto Journal; Horseplay It's Not: Blacks Dream of Finishing First

news.abstract: India's Hindu nationalist party, led by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, is expected to make major gains in voting set to begin across India ; expectation that party may do well enough to form government, or at least head governing coalition, is disturbing to many Muslims and to other Indians who reject Hindu nationalism; anxieties have been growing, with troops moved into some areas and curfews set to bar election violence; Sonia Gandhi, Italian-born Roman Catholic who pits her soaring personal popularity against tarnished image of her Congress Party, poses strongest challenge to nationalists; map; photo (L)
news.title: HINDU-FIRST PARTY EXPECTED TO GAIN IN INDIA'S ELECTION

news.abstract: MAINZ, Germany—  Just when some upscale winegrowers in Germany hoped she had gone away, the Blue Nun has returned.
news.title: The Blue Nun Gets a Makeover/ Call Her 'Fruity,' Not Sweet : The World's 'Oldest Wine Brand' Goes Upscale

news.abstract: Turkish prosecutors again signal determination to restrict speech that threatens national unity; indict Istanbul Mayor Reccep Tayip Erdogan on charges leader of Islamic-oriented party called on his supporters to form holy war; also order arrest of entire 57-member directorate of only legal Kurdish-based political party; cite party calendar that includes picture of jailed Kurdish leader Leyla Zana and list of Kurds and other victims of 'mystery killings' (M)
news.title: Turkey Charges Leading Politicians as Threat to Nation's Unity

news.abstract: United States, in scheduling possible bombing attack on Iraq, considers wide range of factors, including intricacies of Muslim religious calendar, dates for moonless nights and Pres Clinton's travel plans; awaits political judgment on diplomatic efforts to end impasse; photo (M)
news.title: Time to Bomb: Olympics Bad, No Moon Good

news.abstract: Republican-dominated chorus in Congress and in foreign-policy circles is demanding long-term strategy to oust Iraqi Pres Saddam Hussein; options include enlarging existing no-fly and no-drive zones, in Iraq, tightening economic embargo, disbursing billions in frozen Iraqi assets to provisional Government and setting up 'Radio Free Iraq' to stir public opposition and arming; photo (M)
news.title: The G.O.P. Is Urging Hussein's Ouster

news.abstract: Canadian Government mounts legal challenge to right of Quebec Province to secede without agreement of rest of country; lawyers argue before Supreme Court, asserting that unilateral secession would go both against Constitution and international law; tough stance seeks to end most divisive issue and end uncertainty that has dangled over country for more than 30 years (M)
news.title: Canada Seeks Legal Advice On the Status Of Quebec

news.abstract: China Airlines Airbus jumbo jet, on flight from Bali to Tapiei, crashes during landing in fog and rain at Taipei's international airport killing 197 passengers and crew members, including Taiwan's central bank governor Sheu Yuandong and five Americans; photo; map (M)
news.title: Over 200 Die as Taiwan Jet Crashes in Bad Weather

news.abstract: British Government moves closer to temporarily expelling Sinn Fein, political wing of Irish Republican Army, from Northern Ireland peace talks because of involvement in killing of civilian week ago in Belfast (M)
news.title: Britain Takes Step Toward Ousting I.R.A. Ally at Ulster Talks

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  A confrontation between Indonesia and its main creditors moved closer Monday as Indonesian officials said the government would press ahead with a plan aimed at stabilizing its currency despite opposition to its strategy from the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, the United States and the European Union.
news.title: Indonesia Edges Toward a Showdown With IMF

news.abstract: Anti-American protests break out at Cairo university as top Egyptian officials warn United States policy toward Iraq undermines America's standing in Mideast (M)
news.title: Egypt's Leader Warns of Anti-U.S. Ire

news.abstract: Jordanians react angrily to Israeli commission report absolving Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu of blame in botched Sept effort by Israeli secret service to assassinate Islamic militant leader Khaled Meshal in Amman; senior official says suspension of security cooperation ordered by King Hussein after incident may be extended as long as Danny Yatom remains head of Israel's secret service (M)
news.title: Jordan Is Angered by Israeli Findings on Assassination Fiasco

news.abstract: Sinn Fein, Irish Republican Army's political wing, says it will ask Irish Republic court to block any move to expel it from Northern Ireland peace talks; Irish Prime Min Bertie Ahern rejects Sinn Fein appeal to break with British on expulsion issue, holding there is reason to believe IRA was involved in two recent killings (M)
news.title: I.R.A. Ally Asks Irish Court to Block Ouster From Peace Talks

news.abstract: Ruling Islamic party that has molded Sudan into religious state is enacting new constitution officals say will allow return to party politics, banned since 1989, and greater political freedom; 6,500-member National Congress meeting, Khartoum, debates and adopts constitutional changes that seek to wed principles of Islamic state with free speech and party politics (M)
news.title: Sudan to Loosen Islamic Rule a Bit

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, charging Iraqi Pres Saddam Hussein lies and cheats to cling to chemical and biological arms, says he is prepared to order air strikes to 'seriously diminish' Iraqi threat to region and world, televised speech at Pentagon; seeks to rally public support for possible action; repeatedly says he hopes diplomats can persuade Hussein to comply with weapons inspections; says force cannot eliminate Iraq's ability to make such arms; appears with Defense Sec William S Cohen, Vice Pres Al Gore and Gen Henry Hugh Shelton after military briefing by Joint Chiefs of Staff; photo (M)
news.title: CLINTON DESCRIBES GOALS FOR A STRIKE ON IRAQI ARSENALS

news.abstract: When Gregory Washington met Craig Washington, he saw something he had never observed in someone with his last name: white skin. "I thought he was going to be black," said Gregory, an African-American, of his first meeting with a new co-worker at a company in Torrance, California. "I told him he was the first white Washington I'd ever seen. I joked that we must be brothers."
news.title: Among Blacks, Washington Ranks as the Top Surname

news.abstract: B J Habibie, Indonesian Pres Suharto's evident choice for Vice President and potential successor, is technological whiz, political naif and economic eccentric viewed by many as loose cannon; military, despite longstanding antagonism toward him, endorses him after he is nominated by all three political parties; he lacks strong power base beyond Suharto and may be unable to retain power on own; photo (M)
news.title: Suharto's Choice as No. 2: Whiz or Loose Cannon?

news.abstract: Love lives of South Africa's president and former presidents are making headlines; Pres Nelson Mandela, 79, is involved with Graca Machel, widow of late Mozambique president; P W Botha, 82 and recently widowed, is engaged; F W de Klerk, 61, is divorcing wife to wed Elita Georgiadis, wife of Greek shipping tycoon, spurring speculation that his recent resignation from politics was prompted by affair; his National Party has little tolerance for such behavior; photos (M)
news.title: Johannesburg Journal; Of Leaders and Lovers: A South African Epidemic

news.abstract: State Sec Madeleine K Albright, Defense Sec William S Cohen and national security adviser Samuel R Berger take part in unruly public forum, Ohio State University, Columbus, in bid for public support for attack on Iraq; face tough questions, catcalls and concern about American goals; chanting by some 200 anti-war protesters sometimes drowns out officials; forum is televised live around world (M)
news.title: TOP CLINTON AIDES FIND DOUBT ON IRAQ AT CAMPUS IN OHIO

news.abstract: Gov Manuel Bartlett Diaz's outlines plan to seek ruling party's presidential nomination, interview; scores party leaders as timid bureacrats unwilling to stand up to opponents; bid to wrest control of troubled party from foreign-trained economists and technocrats and return it to old guard stirs enthusiasm in party and undermines Pres Ernesto Zedillo's authority; map; photo (M)
news.title: 'Dinosaur' Stirs Mexico's Old Guard

news.abstract: India's muslims feel anxious about rising tide of Hinduism in their country; since 1947, when partioning of British-ruled Inida set off vast migration of Muslims and Hindus across frontiers of newly independent nations of India and Pakistan, there have been few moments when India's 120 million Muslims have felt so vulnerable; Muslims' current anxiety is that when election results are known, about two weeks hence, a new govt will be formed by Hindu nationalist group, Bharatiya Janata Party, which has maintained wide lead over other parties; for India's Muslims, a Hindu nationalist govt would come to power with legacy many find frightening; there is no escaping what Hindu hard-liners intend--that India should abandon sense of itself as mosaic of different faiths, and establish primacy of Hindu majority, now 700 million in population of 980 million; photo (L)
news.title: A Rising Hindu Tide Frightens India's Muslims

news.abstract: Sec Gen Kofi Annan, who is traveling to Iraq, stops off in Paris and gets firm backing from French Pres Jacques Chirac for his last-ditch effort to bring peaceful resolution to crisis over weapons inspections (S)
news.title: France Gives Strong Support To U.N. Chief

news.abstract: Switzerland's Cabinet rejects Jewish man's claim for financial damages for wrongful deportation of his parents, who were killed at Auschwitz; in first case of its kind in Switzerland, Charles Sonabend, 67, asked Swiss Govt for maximum $68,000, or $34,000 per victim, allowed under law; Govt turns away his claim, maintaining it was filed too late and not justified (S)
news.title: Swiss Reject Claim Over 2 Jews Deported in '42

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, day after American policy toward Iraq was picked apart at town hall meeting at Ohio State University, tries to reassemble pieces, declaring that country would ultimately support an American military assault; declares 'If it's necessary for us to act, I believe that America will do what it always does. I Believe it will unite'; asserts that UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan's mission to Baghdad is 'a critical opportunity to achieve the outcome that all of would prefer: a peaceful and principled end to this crisis'; says he has asked Vice Pres Gore to postpone trip to South Africa next week to remain in Washington; Clinton photo (M)
news.title: CLINTON SETS OUT TO REVIVE SUPPORT FOR STAND ON IRAQ

news.abstract: Palestinian Authority shuts down nine radio and television stations in West Bank in attempt to stifle public expressions of pro-Iraqi sentiment among Palestinians; move is intended to avoid raising tensions with United States and Israel (S)
news.title: Arafat Shuts Stations Over Iraq Support

news.abstract: UN team commissioned by Sec Gen Kofi Annan to map Iraq's 'sensitive sites' concludes after three days that total area is 12.2 square miles, including 3.9 square miles covered by lakes; says many of buildings are guest houses and only one is palace; UN special commission to disarm Iraq has estimated that over 27 miles and 1,500 buildings are in off-limits sites; UN official charges Iraqi shell game to divide commission and UN; commission chairman Richard Butler, who has not been included in Annan's Baghdad talks, says issue is access, not size of area (S)
news.title: U.N. Team Calls Iraq Sites Smaller Than Thought

news.abstract: UN Security Council more than doubles amount of oil that Iraq will be allowed to sell to buy food, medicine and other essential goods; approves Sec Gen Kofi Annan's proposal to allow $5.2 billion in sales every six months (S)
news.title: U.N. Expands Quota for Iraq's Oil Sales

news.abstract: Great Brington Journal about great concern in small English village about huge crowds expected to visit Althorp, family home of late Princess Diana; photos; map; Earl Spencer, Diana's brother, proposes to convert stable complex into museum, set uip cafe, gift shop and 500-car parking lot in village that has 200 inhabitants and no traffic lights; Earl, who lives mostly in South Africa, also plans open-air rock concert in Diana's memory and alienates neighbors on other side of his 5,800-acre estate by proposing to sell 400 acres of woodland to developers (M)
news.title: Great Brington Journal; There'll Always Be a Shrine to Diana, but Must It Be Here?

news.abstract: Clinton Administration officials say new Pentagon report has found that direct costs of absorbing Poland, Hungary and Czech Republic into NATO will be $1.5 billion over ten years, much less than earlier estimates; reason is said to be that countries' defense infrastructures are in better condition than believed; critics of NATO enlargement charge manipulation of figures to placate Senators before crucial vote (S)
news.title: Pentagon Report Plays Down Cost of Expanding NATO

news.abstract: Fernando Abril Martorell, former Deputy Prime Minister and a key figure in Spain's transition to democracy after Franco dictatorship, dies at 61 (S)
news.title: Fernando Abril Martorell, 61, Key Spanish Aide

news.abstract: US advises American citizens to leave Iraq as soon as possible; Pres Clinton meets with his top foreign policy aides to discuss their options once United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan completes his trip to Baghdad; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Is Advising Its Citizens to Leave Iraq as Soon as Possible

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II elevates 20 prelates to rank of cardinal; Pope receives 19 of them during outdoor ceremony in Rome; one cardinal is hospitalized; Pope also names two other men cardinals 'in pectore,' procedure to keep their identities secret; Francis Cardinal George of Chicago and James Cardinal Stafford, former archbishop of Denver, are among new cardinals (M)
news.title: Pope Elevates 20 Cardinals, Who Include 2 Americans

news.abstract: Central Intelligence Agency's report on 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion, one of most secret documents of cold war, is released to National Security Archive under Freedom of Information Act; report lays blame for disastrous invasion of Cuba on agency's own institutional arrogance, ignorance and incompetence; document also cautions those who would use CIA to overthrow enemies, saying that job belongs to Pentagon and its broad arsenal of military forces; report was written by then-CIA Inspector Gen Lyman Kirkpatrick; photo (M)
news.title: C.I.A. Bares Its Bungling in Report on Bay of Pigs Invasion

news.abstract: Excerpts from then-CIA Inspector Gen Lyman Kirkpatrick's report on 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion (M)
news.title: The C.I.A. on the C.I.A.: Scathing View of Invasion

news.abstract: One of the most secret documents of the cold war is out, 36 years after it was written. It is the Central Intelligence Agency's own inquiry into the Bay of Pigs fiasco, the invasion to overthrow Fidel Castro that caused the deaths of nearly 1,500 raiders. With brutal honesty, the report put the blame squarely on what it described as arrogance, ignorance and incompetence within the C.I.A. itself.    The report painted a picture of an agency shot through with deadly self-deception, and concluded that its secret operations were ''ludicrous or tragic, or both.'' The document also warned those who would use the C.I.A. to overthrow enemies that such efforts belong to the Pentagon.
news.title: C.I.A.'s Self-Critique In Bay of Pigs Fiasco

news.abstract: Residents of Iraq's capital of Baghdad seem placid, cool and almost nonchalant despite possibility of military action by US because of Government's refusal to allow UN inspectors unfettered access to suspected weapons sites; photo (M)
news.title: Despite Threat of Missiles, the Iraqi Capital's People Take a Crisis in Stride

news.abstract: India's general election progresses through second of three crucial days, with 200 million voters going to polls, but with results still clouded because of political turmoil in Uttar Pradesh, country's largest and most populous state with biggest electoral prize; public opinion polls suggest victory by either coalition Government led by Hindu nationalist group, or rival coalition of so-called secular parties opposed to Hindu nationalism; many political observers say election is most confused since Indira Gandhi called election in 1977 after 20-month period of emergency rule; map; photo (M)
news.title: Turmoil in India's Largest State Clouds Vote

news.abstract: Accord reached between UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan and Iraqi Pres Saddam Hussein reportedly will allow inspections of eight presidential sites previously off limits, including variety of buildings and grounds enclosed in three compounds in Baghdad, as well as around Tikrit, Mosul and Basra; apparently does not address issue of other presidential properties, excluded from eight listed by Baghdad, identified by inspectors as suspect weapons areas or places where crucial documents may be hidden; Iraq has reportedly been persuaded to drop time limit of 60 days it wanted to impose on inspections of presidential sites (M)
news.title: Accord Is Reported to Open Eight Iraqi Sites

news.abstract: British and Irish Governments say terrorist attacks by splinter groups oppposed to Northern Ireland peace talks will not be allowed to derail negotiations; Gerry Adams, leader of Sinn Fein, Irish Republican Army's political wing which has been temporarily suspended because of links to recent killings of civilians, says party will not be deterred by Republican militants opposed to group's participation in talks (M)
news.title: New Attacks Will Not Halt Irish Talks

news.abstract: Pres Saddam Hussein of Iraq reportedly agrees to lift ban on arms inspections at presidential properties by UN personnel, possibly defusing crisis that brought Iraq to brink of military showdown with US; agreement is reached after three-hour meeting between Hussein and UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan; Iraq reportedly agrees to give up most of demands, including time limit on inspections of presidental sites; accord reportedly changes some of methods used in inspecting presidential sites, but apparently does not address issue of other presidential properties excluded from eight listed by Baghdad--including those identified by UN as suspected weapons areas or places where crucial documents may be hidden; UN officials are hopeful it will meet Washington's requirements; photo (M)
news.title: IRAQI AGREES TO INSPECTIONS IN A DEAL WITH U.N. LEADER; WASHINGTON AWAITS DETAILS

news.abstract: The 7 million ethnic Chinese in Indonesia make up just 3 percent of the population, but they control a large share of economic wealth. On a visit to Singapore, Juwono Sudarsono, deputy governor of the National Resilience Institute, an arm of the Indonesian Defense Ministry that trains senior civilian and military officials, discussed the situation of the Chinese minority with Michael Richardson of the International Herald Tribune.
news.title: Q&A / Juwono Sudarsono, Defense Official : Racism in Indonesia Undercuts Unity

news.abstract: Deputy Prime Min Tariq Aziz of Iraq and United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan face the press in Baghdad and questions about what is left unanswered by agreement granting weapons inspectors unfettered access across Iraq; Aziz is testy, and Annan is very much the statesman; photo (M)
news.title: A Testy Hussein Deputy and a Candid U.N. Chief Fence With the Press

news.abstract: European allies warmly hail accord granting United Nations weapons inspection full access to Iraqi sites; Pres Jacques Chirac of France speaks with Pres Clinton; Prime Min Tony Blair says Britain will push for Security Council resolution authorizing military response if Pres Saddam Hussein fails to keep word; foreign ministers of European Union offer praise; photos (M)
news.title: Europeans Offer Praise For Accord With Iraq

news.abstract: Transcript of Pres Clinton's news conference on agreement between United Nations and Iraq over access by weapons inspectors; photo (M)
news.title: In the Words of Clinton: 'What Really Matters Is Iraq's Compliance'

news.abstract: Many Kuwaitis express mixed feelings about agreement between United Nations and Iraq granting weapons inspectors unfettered access to Iraqi sites; say agreement probably averts deaths of many fellow Arabs, but also leaves in power Iraqi leader whose forces invaded and occupied their country eight years ago (M)
news.title: A Buildup For Kuwait Followed By Letdown

news.abstract: Kim Dae Jung, one of Asia's most vigorous voices for democracy and political tolerance, is inaugurated as South Korea's President and immediately calls for reconciliation and cooperation with North Korea; he also calls for far-reaching changes in South Korea's economy and political structure to pull nation out of its financial crisis; photo (M)
news.title: South Korea's New President Appeals to North to End Decades of Division

news.abstract: Brazil's obsession with beauty has made plastic surgery popular in Rio de Janeiro, where many plastic surgeons perform expensive cosmetic surgery on wealthy patients and orthopedic surgery on poor free of charge; photo (M)
news.title: Rio Journal; The Beauty of It! Face Lifts Pay for Poor's Surgery

news.abstract: Dr Kanatjan Alibekov, defector from former Soviet biological weapons program who is now known as Ken Alibek, says that Moscow's cold war plans for World War III included preparing 'hundreds of tons' of anthrax bacteria and scores of tons of smallpox and plague viruses; Alibek was second-in-command of branch of Soviet program and defected to US in 1992; he says Russian military was still running biological weapons program in 1991, year after Mikhail S Gorbachev ordered it halted; has written highly classified study of Soviet biological weapons program for US Government; says he believes a vestige of Moscow's cold war biological-weapons program is continuing in Russia under guise of defensive research; photo (M)
news.title: Soviet Defector Warns of Biological Weapons

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair says Millennium Dome, Britain's ambitious monument to next century which is scheduled to open on Dec 31, 1999, will be built on time and on budget; dome has been derided as extravagant irrelevancy, a political vanity project and colossal waste of $1.24 billion; it was designed by architect Richard Rogers and will be built in Greenwich to mark place where Greenwich Mean Time was introduced in 1884 and where new century will officially dawn (M)
news.title: Blair Puts His Weight Behind Dome Of Millennium

news.abstract: Republican and Democratic lawmakers make demands for quick test of Pres Saddam Hussein's promise to allow United Nations weapons inspectors unfettered and unconditional access throughout Iraq; some senators remain deeply skeptical of accord reached by United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan and Hussein; growing number of legislators express guarded optimism as they are briefed by senior officials of Clinton Administration; House Speaker Newt Gingrich says he 'strongly supports' initiative Clinton has taken (M)
news.title: Lawmakers Demand Prompt Test of Hussein's Promise to U.N.

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  With forest fires in Indonesia threatening to cast another pall of smoke-borne pollution over Southeast Asia, officials in the region appealed Wednesday for international aid to help prevent a recurrence of the 1997 crisis that is estimated to have cost more than $1.3 billion in damage to health, disrupted industry and transport and lost tourism.
news.title: ASEAN Seeks Funds to Avert Another Costly Season of Haze

news.abstract: NEW DELHI—  Never mind that gold is losing its glitter as an investment worldwide, Subhash Bhola's jewelry shop is doing brisk business. So are hundreds of other gold stores that cram the same middle-class neighborhood in New Delhi.
news.title: Demand Is Constant/An 'Excessive Fondness' : For Indians, Ignoring World, All That Glitters Is Gold

news.abstract: Dharam Pal Yadav, gangster from Sambhal, India, who is accused of murder, is running for re-election to Parliament; dominant issue in campaign is criminalization of politics as symbolized by Yadav; map; photo (M)
news.title: Not a Crook? Voters in India Don't Always Care

news.abstract: William J Broad and Judith Miller special report, The Hunt for the Germs of War, discusses seven-year hunt by United Nations weapons inspectors for secret biological weapons in Iraq; notes that in 1995 Iraq grudgingly admitted that it had made enough deadly microbes to kill all people on earth; says despite progress in penetrating Iraqi secrecy, UN inspectors remain uncertain about most of Pres Saddam Hussein's facilities to wage biological warfare; map; photos (M)
news.title: THE DEAL ON IRAQ: SECRET ARSENAL: The Hunt for the Germs of War -- A special report.; Iraq's Deadliest Arms: Puzzles Breed Fears

news.abstract: Leaders of Turkey's banned pro-Islamic party are trying to reorganize themselves in another party, but federal prosecutors and their own former leader, Necmettin Erbakan, are watching them suspiciously (M)
news.title: Under Close Scrutiny, Turkey's Pro-Islam Party Has a Makeover

news.abstract: French Pres Jacques Chirac, his popularity soaring in public opinion polls because of credit given to French diplomacy in avoiding an attack on Iraq, says in interview that France would not support calls for automatic military response if Iraq fails to live up to its latest agreement on weapons inspections (M)
news.title: Chirac Wary of Quick Attack If Iraq Breaks Inspection Deal

news.abstract: Luis Roldan, man who was chief of Spanish Civil Guard in Socialist Govt of Felipe Gonzalez, is sentenced to 28 years for embezzling millions of dollars in public funds, taking kickbacks and evading taxes; Roldan is among best known of a dozen senior political and financial figures who faced corruption charges after late 1980's economic boom (S)
news.title: World News Briefs; Ex-Official in Spain Gets Corruption Sentence

news.abstract: United States and Mexican authorities monitor drug trafficking scene in Mexico for signs of successor to Amado Carrillo Fuentes, who was Mexico's most influential drug trafficker, and who died during surgery last year; US official says that Rafael Munoz Talavera, long-time smuggler with links to same cartel, had emerged as likely heir (M)
news.title: The Man Likely to Be Mexico's No. 1 Trafficker (the Job's Open)

news.abstract: Russia Pres Boris N Yeltsin, in special Govt meeting that is half encounter group and half staged show trial, lashes out at his Govt for failing to correct country's ailing economy and threatens Cabinet shakeup (M)
news.title: Yeltsin Gives His Cabinet Public Rebuke On Economy

news.abstract: Assessment of question of whether United States' standing in Middle East has suffered, with Iraq crisis now in remission; some diplomats and experts argue that crisis demonstrated that there is still no viable alternative to American power in region, or to American mediation between Israel and Palestinians; many Arabs and some Israeli commentators attribute outpouring of support for Iraq on Arab streets to popular perception that United States maintains double standard in Middle East (M)
news.title: As Iraqi Tension Eases, Arabs Criticize U.S. Role

news.abstract: Indonesia's dubious scheme to peg its battered currency to US dollar was suggested by Steve H Hanke, little-known American economist who promoted idea; plan has worked recently in smaller countries like Bulgaria, Lithuania and Argentina, but is dubious remedy for big country whose banking system needs major overhaul; IMF has threatened to cut off aid and Pres Clinton is sending Walter Mondale to talk with Pres Suharto; Hanke offers tart conservative prescriptions in Forbes magazine and is officer of Canadian company that has profited by betting against Asia's falling currencies; he dismisses skeptics, interview; photo (M)
news.title: American With Cure-All Enlivens Jakarta Crisis

news.abstract: World Court in The Hague rules it has authority to decide whether Libya should surrender two suspects for trial on charges of blowing up Pan American Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988; rejects US and British claims to jurisdiction (S)
news.title: World Court Claims Jurisdiction In Pan Am Flight 103 Case

news.abstract: Mexican Government deports Father Michel Henri Jean Chanteau, French priest who served for 32 years in Indian parish in state of Chiapas, turning campaign against foreigners in Chiapas into new confrontation with Catholic Church; he is fifth foreign priest, including two Americans, to be deported from Chiapas since Zapatista rebellion erupted in 1994; photo (M)
news.title: Mexico Expels French Priest in Latest Move Against Outsiders in Rebel Area

news.abstract: Maj Gen Romeo Dallaire of Canada, former commander of UN peacekeeping troops in Rwanda, tells UN tribunal that 1994 massacre of at least 500,000 people could have been halted if small, well-armed force had been sent in early with that objective; says his force was too small, ill-equipped and poorly trained, and lacked legal mandate to intervene; unanswered is why UN officials apparently ignored his warning that Rwandan Government was planning massacre and why he was not given new mandate to step in; questions are politically delicate for Sec Gen Kofi Annan, who in 1994 was head of UN peacekeeping operations; documents leaked to reporters last year suggested Dallaire had warned Annan; map (M)
news.title: General Tells Rwanda Court Massacre Was Preventable

news.abstract: Cambodia's two main rival factions declare cease-fire, raising tentative hopes for peace plan and competitive elections later in year; forces loyal to Second Prime Min Hun Sen and Prince Norodom Ranariddh make separate announcements (S)
news.title: Cambodian Truce Declared, Raising Hopes for New Vote

news.abstract: Much of Beijing is being cleared by real-estate developers to make way for high-rise apartments, office buildings and shopping centers; familiar syndrome of urban renewal, long delayed by China's isolation and poverty, is unfolding fast, changing face of ancient city; single-story compounds and narrow alleys that made up much of Beijing are nearly all scheduled for demolition--their condition deemed beyond repair and their use of space too extravagant for modernizing metropolis; photos of artist Deng Haifan's paintings of life in old Beijing (M)
news.title: A Burst of Renewal Sweeps Old Beijing Into the Dumpsters

news.abstract: Election in Lower Saxony, Germany, on March 1 will decide whether Premier Gerhard Schroder keeps his majority in state legislature for opposition Social Democrats; commentators say if Schroder fares well, result will strengthen his bid to challenge Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Sept national elections (M)
news.title: Kohl's Rival Faces a Vote That's Make Or Break

news.abstract: Number of Americans studying abroad has jumped 84 percent over last decade; with average bill for private schools in US now more than $20,000 a year--and costs elsewhere in world much lower--growing number of American families are finding that experience that once was largely restricted to well-to-do is turning into something that middle class can no longer afford to ignore; number of students seeking bargain educations abroad has grown so quickly that backlash has been seen, both at American schools and those in foreign countries; University of Pennsylvania charges students going abroad same amount they would pay on Philadelphia campus; some countries that heavily subsidize higher education have taken to charging foreigners full price; graph (M)
news.title: Americans Abroad Learning Studies Now Offer a Bargain

news.abstract: Some South Korean politicians say that US recognition of North Korea would help stabilize Korean Peninsula; US appears committed to its policy of applying economic sanctions against North Korea and limiting official contacts (M)
news.title: New Shape To Triangle Tying U.S. And Koreas

news.abstract: British Government is expected to charge Army Maj Milos Stankovic with providing classified NATO information and documents to Bosnian Serb leadership during last two years of Balkan war; senior Western diplomats say he seriously undermined effectiveness of United Nations peacekeeping effort in Bosnia (M)
news.title: British Officer Said to Give NATO Plans to Bosnian Serbs

news.abstract: Interview with Gopal Godse, Hindu nationalist who recounts his role in plotting assassination of Mohandas K Gandhi in 1948 because of his evenhandad attitude toward Muslims; says he is proud of his role and feels vidicated by current elections returns, which point to best showing by Hindus ever in Indian national elections; map; photo (M)
news.title: Hindu Still Proud of Role In Killing the Father of India

news.abstract: Andre Bronner, French navigator, fulfills childhood dream by building lighthouse on Isla de los Estados, bleak island in Cape Horn off Argentine coast, that is replica of 1884 structure that inspired Jules Verne's last novel, The Lighthouse at the End of the World; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Isla de los Estados Journal; Dream Fulfilled at End of the World

news.abstract: Richard Butler, chief of UN weapons inspection team, clashes with Nizar Hamdoon, Iraq's envoy to UN, over critical part of recent arms inspection pact reached with Sec Gen Kofi Annan that helped avert American military action; Hamdoon, in CNN interview, says Iraq expects inspection teams at eight presidential sites to be subordinate to diplomats appointed by Annan to accompany them, but Butler says agreement clearly gives him overall responsibility for new monitoring arrangements; photo (M)
news.title: Iraqi Diplomat and U.N. Expert Differ Sharply on Terms of Pact

news.abstract: Israeli Government sends out diplomatic feelers to end increasingly costly military involvement in southern Lebanon; Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu says Government is ready to comply with UN resolution calling on it to withdraw, if Lebanon cooperates in insuring security along border (M)
news.title: Israel Seeks Deal to Quit Buffer Zone In Lebanon

news.abstract: BRUSSELS—  Passengers leaving the Anderlecht Metro station in Brussels on a recent evening were subjected to an unusually stringent ticket control.
news.title: Charges of Incompetence and Laxity Are Leveled at Fragmented Forces : Belgian Police Face Growing Distrust

news.abstract: UN Security Council unanimously endorses Sec Gen Kofi Annan's agreement with Iraq on weapons inspections, but without authorizing automatic military response of Baghdad fails to comply; majority of members--led by China, France and Russia--rebuff US and Britain by holding out against any explicit threat, particularly wording that would appear to give green light to American attack in event Iraq violates agreement; Pres Clinton reiterates threat of American military action, warning Iraq against blocking inspectors from carrying out their work; says unanimous vote sends clearest possible signal that Iraq must make good on commitment to give unfettered access to weapons inspectors; US Amb Bill Richardson says resolution reinforces US policy, and does not bar military strikes, which US believes it already has power to carry out (M)
news.title: U.N. REBUFFS U.S. ON THREAT TO IRAQ IF IT BREAKS PACT

news.abstract: Incomplete returns from India's general election indicates alliance led by Bharatiya Janata Party, Hindu nationalist group, has easily outpolled alliance led by Congress Party, but apparently not by enough seats to assure nationalists outright Parliamentary majority; photo (M)
news.title: Early Results in India Show Gains for Hindu Nationalists

news.abstract: Serbian police uses truncheons, water cannon and tear gas to disperse estimated 30,000 ethnic Albanians during march in Pristina, Kosovo Province, to protest recent killing of more than 20 civilians by paramilitaries; serious unrest in province, where 90 percent of people are ethnic Albanians, erupted on February 27 when four policemen were killed in ambush by rebels from Kosovo Liberation Army; map (M)
news.title: Serbia's Police Crush Protest By Kosovo's Ethnic Albanians

news.abstract: Former Vice Pres Walter F Mondale, following meeting with Indonesian Pres Suharto, says he urged him to press ahead with painful economic reforms demanded by the International Monetary Fund to solve country's economic crisis; says they discussed current efforts to restore stability and economic growth to Indonesia and steps needed to restore confidence; is visiting Jakarta as emissary of Clinton Administration; photo (M)
news.title: Mondale, Clinton's 2d Envoy, Urges Suharto to Press Reforms

news.abstract: Viktor N Mikhailov, Russia's powerful and pugnacious Atomic Energy Minister, is abruptly relieved of duties in move that has startled Russian and Western experts; Kremlin says Mikhailov was ssked to leave to concentrate more on scientific research; explanation is discounted by Western officials, who speculate action may be related to disputes over nuclear cooperation with Iran or suspicions of corruption in connection with sale of uranium to US (M)
news.title: Atom Chief Of Russia Is Removed From Post

news.abstract: Tens of thousands of German municipal workers stage brief strikes to bolster union demands in wage talks; at issue is future of costly social guarantees that Germans take for granted (M)
news.title: Strikes by German City Workers Frame Political Battle to Come

news.abstract: Mayor Michael Haupl says Vienna will go ahead with plan to build Holocaust memorial designed by Rachel Whiteread; plan stirred controversy in small Jewish community because memorial will be placed above excavations of medieval synagogue (M)
news.title: Vienna to Go Ahead With Holocaust Shrine

news.abstract: The day after the United Nations Security Council stopped short of endorsing an explicit military threat against Iraq, the Clinton Administration contended that the United States has the authority to use force if Iraq does not comply with United Nations weapons inspections.    President Clinton said the Council's resolution warning of ''severest consequences'' if Iraq defied the agreement sent ''a clear message.''
news.title: U.S. Warns of Force If Iraq Breaks Word

news.abstract: Walter F Mondale, Pres Clinton's special envoy, fails to win commitment from Indonesian Pres Suharto that he will end resistance to economic reforms that are part of $43 billion International Monetary Fund bailout; Deputy Treasury Sec Lawrence H Summers tells Senate subcommittee that Clinton will not support added IMF emergency aid unless Suharto makes 'adequate progress' toward reforms he agreed to in Jan; senior officials say Clinton signals Suharto will not be allowed to ignore accord, despite concerns about impact of aid cutoff (M)
news.title: U.S. Is Linking Aid to Jakarta To Its Reforms

news.abstract: National People's Congress, annual rite that brings together some 3,000 delegates from all parts of China, is set to open, Beijing; is expected to formally elect Zhu Rongji as Prime Minister; he has begun forcing through wary Communist Party plan to cut bureaucracy, including 4 million Government jobs; Congress, which ratifies decisions made in secret by party leaders, has evolved into more active body, with year-round professional staff helping to iron out details of new laws; photo (M)
news.title: Congress In China: No Teeth, Strong Jaws

news.abstract: German prosecutors arrest suspected Nazi war criminal accused of killing 500 people at Maidanek death camp in Poland in 1943; refuse to identify suspect and decline to confirm news reports that his name is Alfons Goetzfried (S)
news.title: Ex-Nazi Is Seized; Accused of Gunning Down 500 at Maidanek

news.abstract: Liu Dalin opens Shanghai Sex Museum, where he displays his private collection of several thousand sex-related historical objects; contends that China should be more open about sexual matters; photo (M)
news.title: Shanghai Journal; Behind a Great Wall of Reticence, Some Sex Toys

news.abstract: Gregoris Staktopoulos, Greek journalist who spent decade in prison in connection with murder of George Polk, distinguished CBS news correspondent, in northern Greece in 1948, dies at age 88 (M)
news.title: Gregoris Staktopoulos, 88; Imprisoned in Death of George Polk, a Reporter in Greece

news.abstract: Vatican found Sri Lankan Priest Tissa Balasuriya guilty of heresy and excommunicated him in 1997, but he has been reunited with his church and excommunication order has been lifted (M)
news.title: Excommunicated Priest Is Reunited With Vatican

news.abstract: Israeli Parliament re-elects Ezer Weizman to second five-year term as President after unexpectedly charged campaign for largely ceremonial office; Weizman beats back challenge by Likud party candidate Shaul Amor; photo (M)
news.title: After a Battle, Israel President Is Re-elected

news.abstract: LONDON—  They are sleek and fast. They travel the globe from Melbourne to Monte Carlo, surrounded by models and princes, actors and corporate moguls, and watched by some 460 million avid television spectators. And there are only 22 in each race.
news.title: Advertisers Find a Formula They Like in Auto Racing

news.abstract: Indonesian crisis deepens as rupiah plummets 10 percent on concern that International Monetary Fund would suspend $3 billion loan due on Mar 15 unless Pres Suharto stops backtracking on promised economic reforms (S)
news.title: Indonesia's Crisis Deepens Over Reform Rift

news.abstract: Serbian police and paramilitary units unleash helicopter gunships and armored personnel carriers against armed Albanian separatists in Kosovo Province, forcing dozens of Serbian families and Albanian women and children to leave and cordoning off scores of villages to keep outsiders away; Serbian interior ministry says 20 Albanians and 2 Serbian policemen are killed; spokesman for Kosovo's Albanian political leader, Ibrahim Rugova, says houses were burned and massacres were carried out, proving brutality of Belgrade regime; photo; map (M)
news.title: Gun Battles in Serbia Raise Fear of 'Another Bosnia'

news.abstract: Communist and Green members of French Parliament pass resolution demanding full parliamentary investigation of French role in Rwanda; want probe of how French military aid to Hutu-dominated Government there in early 1990's may have contributed to killing of hundreds of thousands of Tutsi and moderate Hutu in 1994; decision to hold only limited parliamentary inquiry into matter is called 'diversionary maneuver' by medical charity Doctors Without Borders; group says France's reputation would be at stake if questions about its role in situation are not cleared up (M)
news.title: France Limits Legislative Inquiry on Rwanda Role

news.abstract: India's main Hindu nationalist party grows increasingly confident that it will be able to form country's new government; election results show neck-and-neck finish between two rival politial blocs, one an alliance led by Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party and other a loose combination of Congress party and alliance known as United Front; but Congress Party leadership meeting breaks up in disagreement over whether bid for power is viable, or even desirable (M)
news.title: Hindu Bloc Moves Closer To Power

news.abstract: International Montary Fund delays release of $3 billion in aid for Indonesia until at least Apr, citing Pres Suharto's failure to meet basic conditions for aid; Min Marie Muhammad earlier warned that any delay would hurt investor confidence and slow recovery of currency (M)
news.title: I.M.F. Delays Indonesian Aid; Reforms Seem to Be Stalled

news.abstract: Serbian policemen cracked down on a separatist movement in the province of Kosovo yesterday, firing mortar rounds at villages, setting fire to homes and appearing to shoot at men indiscriminately, according to those who fled the zone.     The attacks apparently left many dead in the province, where ethnic Albanians constitute 90 percent of the population. Many of the Albanians view the Serbian police and military as an army of occupation.
news.title: Serbs Pound Kosovo To Repel Separatists

news.abstract: Ability of Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger separatist guerrillas to carry out suicide bombings like recent attack in Colombo that killed 36 people reflects their remarkable success in acquiring explosives and weapons from around third world; Tigers' military procurement practices show how easy it is to find weapons, pay for them with money moved through major banks and move arms across borders; highlight how ill prepared governments are to deal with light weapons traffic; map (L)
news.title: Tamil Guerrillas in Sri Lanka: Deadly and Armed to the Teeth

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  The "elk test" is turning the German auto industry upside down.
news.title: Spin Control:Opel and VW In a Flip Flap

news.abstract: HarperCollins, in highly unusual move, apologizes for suggesting its decision to cancel publication of book East and West, by Chris Patten, former Hong Kong Governor, was spurred by book's shortcomings; agrees to pay Patten unspecified sum; apology is public embarrasment for Rupert Murdoch, whose News Corp owns publisher; he ordered cancellation out of concern book would jeopardize his relationship with Chinese leaders; backs Eddie Bell, HarperCollins executive chairman (M)
news.title: Publisher Apologizes to Hong Kong Chief for Canceled Book

news.abstract: United States Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright is on official two-day visit to Italy; blames Pres Slobodan Milosevic of Yugoslavia for most of bloodshed in Kosovo and says that US is 'not going to stand by and watch' Serbian authorities crush political freedoms in province; on Iran, Albright says that Washington is looking for 'a pattern of action' that would demonstrate, over time, that Iran is moderating its behavior; Albright meets with Pope John Paul II at Vatican, meeting that focuses on his visit to Cuba in January; photo of Albright with Pope (L)
news.title: Albright Warns Serbs on Kosovo Violence

news.abstract: Africans nations are seen resentful of what they perceive as international loan agencies' swift response to Asian nation's distressed economies, contrasting Asian rescue effort with what appears to many Africans as stingy, demanding and never-ending program of life support for Africa; example of Ivory Coast cited; Ivory Coast has just been granted $2 billion in new loans, but to get there, Govt negotiated for nine months, finally agreeing to stinging measures that give uncomfortable impression that economic policy would henceforth be made at fund's headquarters in Washington; Ivory Coast Finance Min Niamien Ngoran says 'One can easily get the impression of a double standard'; World Bank and IMF officials say size and speed of their response to crisis in Asian countries is justified by importance of their economies to global financial system; map (L)
news.title: Africans Resentful as Asia Rakes In Aid

news.abstract: Representatives from women's organizations from around world are meeting at United Nations for two weeks to take stock of progress two and half years after United Nations international conference on women in Beijing put forward proposals for govt action on women's rights; even skeptics say they are impressed at extent to which many govts have followed through on their pledges; they attribute this largely to pressure from increasingly strong local and international women's orgns (M)
news.title: Women See Key Gains Since Talks In Beijing

news.abstract: Pres Clinton's nomination last year of James C Hormel, who is gay, to be ambassador to Luxembourg appears hopelessly stalled on Capitol Hill; Hormel is 65-year-old philanthropist and heir to Hormel meat-processing fortune; group of conservative Senate Republicans has placed hold on his nomination, and Sen Trent Lott, Senate majority leader, says he has no plans to bring nomination to vote (M)
news.title: Senators Keep Gay Nominee for Luxembourg Post in Limbo

news.abstract: Senior Serbian officials and Western diplomats say that sweep in central Kosovo province by hundreds of Serbian police and paramilitary units appears to have failed to capture or kill most of ethnic Albanian rebels operating in area; action, which threatens to ignite another major conflict in Balkans, has left scores of people dead and dozens of houses burned (M)
news.title: Serbs Claim Victory Over a Separatist Militia

news.abstract: Three-day Serbian assault on Prekaz, stronghold of ethnic Albanian separatists in Kosovo province, ends with Belgrade claiming victory; at least 26 ethnic Albanians and 2 police officers die, but death toll may be much higher; devastation described; map; photo (M)
news.title: Ravaged Kosovo Village Tells of a Nightmare of Death

news.abstract: Women's rights groups throughout Islamic world are increasingly speaking out against what they call Muslim system of apartheid, where texts of Koran and appendages attached in Middle Ages are invoked to deny equal rights to women; issue of how women are viewed is at heart of much conflict in Muslim nations, from fundamenalist policies in Afghanistan and Iran, to demands to abolish discrimination in family laws in Morocco and Tunisia; activists in Morocco, Tunisia and Algeria--where women rank among more emancipated in Arab world--say UN international women's conference in Beijing in 1995 was important catalyst for defining issues and planning action; say support has grown because women are caught in growing contradictions and shifts within Islamic societies; situation in Morocco--where women still need permission from male relative to marry, name children or work and suffer other forms of discrimination--discussed; photos (M)
news.title: Cry of Muslim Women for Equal Rights Is Rising

news.abstract: National debate to legalize assisted suicide in Spain is stirred by broadcast of videotape of suicide of 55-year-old quadriplegic Ramon Sampedro by television station; Sampedro, who was cause celebre in struggle to legalize procedure became quadriplegic in accident 29 years ago; had fought unsucessfully in courts for years for right to be helped to die (M)
news.title: A Suicide Tape on TV Inflames the Issue in Spain

news.abstract: JAKARTA—  Amid the puddles and crumbling walls of Jakarta's morning market is the city's Chinatown, a labyrinth of shops, warehouses and narrow alleys navigated by stooped old women.
news.title: Ethnic Chinese Try to Keep Out of Harm's Way

news.abstract: Foreign ministers of US, France and Germany agree on need for firm and clear measures to stop violence in Serbian province of Kosovo before it spreads to other nations; Sec of State Madeleine K Albright wants mix of diplomacy and punitive sanctions in dealing with Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic from six members of contact group that monitor former Yugoslavia, but Russia remains opposed and France noncommital; British and Germans are expected to support Americans, with Italians edging closer to French; Albright says Belgrade must understand seriousness of situation in Kosovo province, where Serbs have cracked down extremely harshly on independence movements by ethnic Albanians, who make up 90 percent of population; says regime in Belgrade should pay price for damage it has already done (M)
news.title: Albright Tours Europe to Whip Up Resolve to Punish Serbia

news.abstract: Serbian police release bodies of 51 ethnic Albanians killed in crackdown on outlawed Kosovo Liberation Army, bringing known death toll in fighting to 77; victims include 25 women and small children; most are from Prekaz, rebel stronghold, and include rebel commander, Adem Jashari and over 20 family members; Serbs claim rebels killed women and children to keep them from surrendering; mounting evidence indicates unarmed civilians, and apparently all males detained by police, were executed, often in front of their wives and children; photo; map (M)
news.title: On a Garage Floor in Kosovo, A Gruesome Serbian Harvest

news.abstract: Dragoljub Kurnarac, former Bosnian Serb paramilitary commander, pleads guilty before internation Yugoslav war crimes tribunal, Hague, to raping Muslim women during Bosnian war in 1992; is first person to plead guilty to rape as war crime; pleads not guilty to several other charges; plea surprises prosecutors (M)
news.title: An Ex-Bosnian Serb Commander Admits Rape of Muslims in War

news.abstract: Analysis of Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic's drive to crush budding uprising by ethnic Albanian majority in Serbia's Kosovo province; discusses threat that violence could knindle wider Balkan war; Milosevic has used Kosovo issue before, beginning with his 1987 transformation into Serbian nationalist leader (M)
news.title: New Tinderbox, Same Fuse: A Serb Comes Full Circle

news.abstract: Pres Suharto, wrangling with International Monetary Fund over terms of economic rescue plan, reflects Indonesians' resentment of being humiliated by IMF; part of conflict seems to stem from IMF pressure for overhaul of economic system, while Suharto apparently wants quick fix to bail out his wealthy and influential family and friends; IMF deal attacks many of their vested interests (M)
news.title: Crisis Aside, What Pains Indonesia Is the Humiliation

news.abstract: South Korean continues to detain hundreds of political prisoners, including accused spies, labor activists and leftists; Pres Kim Dae Jung, former prisoner, remains deeply suspicious of Communists and is reluctant to expend his political capital by rapidly freeing political prisoners; pledges to release them gradually; photo (M)
news.title: Seoul Leader, Ex-Inmate Himself, Is Slow to Free Political Prisoners

news.abstract: The President of India asked the main Hindu nationalist party yesterday to form a coalition Government, stirring fears among many Indians, particularly the Muslim minority, that the party would dismantle the country's historical commitment to equality for people of all faiths.     The nationalists, the Bharatiya Janata Party, now seem likely to cobble together enough votes to form a parliamentary majority after a tumultuous national election that ended on Saturday with no clear victor.
news.title: Hindu Party in India Chosen for Coalition

news.abstract: Six Iraqis who worked in concert with Central Intelligence Agency in failed plots against Saddam Hussein have been declared threats to American national security in court ruling so secret their lawyers cannot read it; ruling by Federal Judge D D Sitgraves means that they may be deported to their homeland, where they would probably face execution; Iraqis are Ali Yasin Mohammed Karim, Safa al-Betat, Adil Hadi Awadh, Mohammed Jawer al-Ammary, Mohammed Tuma and Ali Saleh (M)
news.title: 6 Iraqis Who Aided C.I.A. Are Ordered Deported From U.S.

news.abstract: Pres K R Narayanan asks Hindu nationalist party to form coalition Government in India, stirring fears among many Indians, particularly Muslim minority, that party will dismantle country's historic commitment to equality for people of all faiths (M)
news.title: Hindu Party Asked to Form A Government For India

news.abstract: Danish voters go to polls in general election on March 11; issue that has put Prime Min Poul Nyrup Rasmussen on defensive is same one that Pia Kjaersgaard, head of small right-wing Danish Peoples Party, has made her centerpiece: immigration (M)
news.title: Immigrants Cast Shadow Over the Danish Election

news.abstract: Pres Suharto takes his oath of office for seventh time, calling on Indonesians to pull together in this time of economic hardship; he is locked in confrontation with International Monetary Fund, which is demanding that he dismantle Indonesia's system of monopolies and favoritism in return for $40 billion rescue package; photo (M)
news.title: At Pivotal Time, Suharto Gets a 7th Term

news.abstract: Clinton Administration decides to move up Pres Clinton's trip to China to late June, from Nov, in effort to avoid any deterioration of relations between US and China over human rights and other issues; senior Administration officials say that Chinese officials are enthusiastic over proposal for earlier meeting; rescheduled trip is likely to follow on heels of Paula Jones sexual misconduct trial against Clinton, which is to start on May 27 in Little Rock; Administration officials say trial has nothing to do with rescheduling China trip (M)
news.title: CLINTON MOVES UP HIS TRIP TO CHINA TO LATE IN JUNE
