news.abstract: Pres Suharto calls on Indonesians to tighten their belts, saying rapid growth in prosperity they have enjoyed over last 25 years is gone for good; it is his strongest public statement about economic crisis that has made almost all of Indonesia's 200 million people suddenly poorer; Suharto begins his seventh five-year term as President; assembly endorse B J Habibie as new Vice President; photo (M)
news.title: Tighten Belts, Suharto Tells His People, It's All Over

news.abstract: Prime Min Viktor S Chernomyrdin says Russia will push to ratify second strategic arms reduction treaty in order to prepare way for Pres Clinton to visit Moscow for summit meeting by middle of year (M)
news.title: Russia Vows To Push Pact Cutting Arms

news.abstract: There is sense of outrage across France after authorities dig up body of actor Yves Montand from Paris cemetery and take it to laboratory for DNA tests to settle claim of Aurore Drossard, 22, that she is his unacknowledged child; while Montand was alive, he declined to submit to blood tests ordered in paternity suit brought by Anne-Gilberte Drossard on behalf of her daughter; appeal by his family, including two heirs to fortune said to be about $3.7 million, produced court order last fall to open his tomb for DNA test; photos (M)
news.title: Paris Journal; Beyond the Grave, DNA Haunts Yves Montand

news.abstract: Gen Augusto Pinochet, Chile's former dictator, assumes much-disputed Senate seat that protects him from prosecution for crimes committed during his 17 years in power; thousands of people demonstrate against him (M)
news.title: As Thousands Protest, Pinochet Assumes Chilean Senate Seat

news.abstract: PARIS—  "Paris, here we are!" gushed gigantic billboards as the Swedish cut-price clothing firm, H&M, brought its wear for the first time to a global fashion capital.
news.title: Swedish Outlet Chain Gambles It Can Change Consumer Tastes : Will Cheap Chic Win Over Stylish French?

news.abstract: India's quest for new government falters when main Hindu nationalist party falls into dispute with major ally, leaving door open for possible rival bid for power by Congress Party; in a sequence that exasperates many Indians, Jayalalitha Jayaram, former movie actress facing investigation in $1 billion fraud scandal, emerges as spoiler of what had seemed only 48 hours ago to be almost certain ascent to power by Hindu nationalists; her case reviewed; photo of Atal Bihari Vajpayee, man nominated by nationalists to be Prime Min (M)
news.title: With the Way to Power Open, Hindu Nationalists Falter

news.abstract: Ibrahim Rugova, President of self-declared Republic of Kosovo, who comes close to being revered among ethnic Albanian majority in Pristina, Serbia, comments on situation; says he is passionately committed to nonviolence; map (M)
news.title: Kosovo Leader Urges Resistance, but to Violence

news.abstract: Manuel Pineiro, ruthless but urbane spymaster who for more than 30 years led Cuba's intelligence apparatus and directed its efforts to export revolution to third world, dies in car crash in Havana; photo (M)
news.title: Manuel Pineiro, Spymaster For Castro, Is Dead at 63

news.abstract: United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan asks United States House Republican leaders to justify their decision to hold up payment of back dues to United Nations until Administration agrees to provision cutting off aid to groups that support abortion (M)
news.title: Annan Tries to Untangle U.N. Dues From Abortion

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  If you find yourself in New York in need of an Armani suit, chances are you'll hit one of the many department stores uptown.
news.title: New York's Specialty Shops Bounce Back With Trendy Lines

news.abstract: Lerik, Azerbaijan, produces astonishing number of centenarians despite poverty, poor medical care and ignorance; residents work very hard and eat little, mostly vegetables, fruit and sour cheeses, not yogurt; most researchers credit clean, stress-free living and genetics; photos; map (m)
news.title: Lerik Journal; Yogurt? Caucasus Centenarians 'Never Eat It'

news.abstract: Senate votes 93-0 to urge creation of United Nations tribunal to try Iraqi Pres Saddam Hussein as war criminal; Sen Arlen Specter, resolution's main sponsor, comments; House approved similar resolution in Nov (M)
news.title: Senate Urges U.N. to Try Iraqi as a War Criminal

news.abstract: SEOUL—  President Kim Dae Jung granted amnesty to more than 5.5 million of his countrymen on Friday — for everything from traffic tickets to spying — and freed 2,304 people from jail, including some of the nation's best-known political prisoners.
news.title: Kim's Decree Benefits Millions; Some Dissidents Are Left Out : South Korea Grants Sweeping Amnesty

news.abstract: Woo Yong Gak, North Korean who may be world's longest-serving political prisoner, is not included in South Korea's amnesty of traffic offenders and prisoners; amnesty touched 5.5 million people, mostly by erasing records of speeding tickets, and led to release of 74 people regarded by human rights groups as political prisoners; Woo, held since 1958, has refused to renounce belief in Communism and North Korean Government; photos (S)
news.title: Longtime Dissident Still Held by Seoul

news.abstract: Pres Clinton scores Republican efforts to slip unrelated controversial provisions into emergency spending bills, radio speech; hints he may veto bill if Congress attaches ban on financial aid to groups that offer abortion services abroad; scores Republican efforts to bar Federal Communications Commission from ordering free broadcast time for political candidates (M)/
news.title: Clinton May Veto Funds Bill on Abortion Issue

news.abstract: India's Congress Party elects Sonia Gandhi president, re-affirming family dynasty that has long governed party; she scores Hindu nationalists as 'threat' to secular ideals of independence leaders, speech; Hindu nationalists, after days of uncertainty, win support of Jayalalitha Jayaram, whose control of 27 parliamentary seats makes her key to their efforts to win parliamentary majority; she accompanies letter of support with fierce denunciation of nationalist leaders (M)
news.title: Indian Congress Party Picks Sonia Gandhi

news.abstract: Interview with Min Stephane Dion, bilingual professor who is Canada's official crusader for national unity, chosen in 1996 by Prime Min Jean Chretien to stand up to Quebec separatists; he notes how his views differ from those of late father, Leon, considered intellectual leader of Quebec's search for identity (M)
news.title: A Quebecer Trumpets The Case For Canada

news.abstract: World Bank forces Russia's most ardent reformers to scale back their plan to convert state-run pension system into a program of private individual retirement accounts; thought plan is too risky and pressed for an incremental approach that would leave state-financed pension system with a major role; critics say World Bank dogmatically imposed its vision of a paternalistic state role in social welfare; dispute illustrates enormous influence of World Bank and International Monetary Fund over Russia's social and economic policy and also shows that World Bank's role in encouraging social change is more complex--and more contentious--than generally realized; graph (M)
news.title: World Bank Vs. Reformers on How to Still Feed Russia When It's 64

news.abstract: China continues to keep its media market closed to Rupert Murdoch even though he has curried favor when Chinese leadership for 10 years; Murdoch has invested over $1 billion in Star TV, Asian satellite television network that is intended to be New Corp's route to China, but winning approval to broadcast, collecting subscriptions fees and selling advertising are proving difficult; New Corp points to Star TV's partial ownership of Phoenix Satellite Television Co of Hong Kong as an important is modest sign of progress (M)
news.title: China Keeps Murdoch And His TV On Hiatus

news.abstract: A bar owner in Auburn, California, has been convicted of two infractions for allowing patrons to light up in violation of the new state anti-smoking law. It was apparently the first such trial under the law that bans smoking in more than 35,000 bars and casinos. The owner, Bill Ostrander, was fined a total of $300
news.title: AMERICAN TOPICS : California Bar Owner Becomes Butt Of the State's No-Smoking Statute

news.abstract: Robert McBride, former guerrilla for African National Congress, is arrested in Mozambique during effort to purchase weapons; visit to Mozambique remains mystery; African National Congress says his visit was not authorized and that McBride was acting on his own; says it is not involved in arms deal (M)
news.title: Official's Arrest Puzzles South Africa

news.abstract: Exit polls suggest leftist parties of French Prime Min Lionel Jospin's nine-month-old Government coalition will defeat conservative opposition in about half of country's 22 regional assemblies in light voting (M)
news.title: French Leftists Surge in Regional Elections

news.abstract: US House of Representatives approves broad trade bill promoting private US investment in 48 countries of sub-Saharan Africa, some among poorest countries in world, that will give them preferential treatment if they move toward democracy and free-market economies; bill allows duty-free and quota-free exports to US for 10 years, encourages creation of free-trade zones and creates position in office of US trade representative to focus on African issues; other provisions noted; proponents say it underscores fundamental shift in American relations with Africa that favors trade over aid; measure still needs Senate approval (M)
news.title: Bill to Push Africa Trade Is Approved

news.abstract: Israeli Government criticizes as unacceptable intention of British Foreign Sec Robin Cook to visit site of disputed new Jewish settlement in eastern Jerusalem; Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu may refuse to meet him; planned visit is part of Cook's three-day visit to Middle East as representative of European Union (M)
news.title: Israel Calls British Aide's Visit To Disputed Site Unacceptable

news.abstract: Israel resolves dispute with Britain over planned visit of Foreign Sec Robin Cook to site of controversial new Jewish neighborhood in eastern Jerusalem by agreeing that Cook will travel there with Israeli, rather than Palestinian officials (M)
news.title: Briton Settles Dispute Over Visit to Israeli Site

news.abstract: RANGOON—  Burma's economy, squeezed for years by Western sanctions and weakened by the economic crisis affecting much of Asia, is in tatters.
news.title: Do Sanctions Really Work? Debate Is On In Burma

news.abstract: Armenians turn out in large numbers to vote in presidential election that Western political analysts say could profoundly affect stability in oil-producing Caucasus region; 12 candidates are competing in contest (S)
news.title: Armenians Turn Out To Elect New Leader

news.abstract: New nationalist-oriented Cabinet takes office in Indonesia; faces tough negotiations with international lenders over how best to solve deepening economic crisis (S)
news.title: Indonesia's New Cabinet Takes Office

news.abstract: Names of 9,000 people, many of Spaniards and their decendants who disappeared during military rule in Argentine from 1976 to 1983, are presented to Spanish judge in Madrid, Spain, sharply widening his inquiry into Argentine-sponsored terrorism (S)
news.title: Spain Expands Inquiry Into Argentine State Terror

news.abstract: United Nations aid officials say people of Adet, Sudan, are victims of campaign by Islamic Government to starve people in rebel-held territories because they support guerrillas fighting for autonomous south; Government has banned relief flights to all but four airstrips in region; UN officials say ban has crippled relief operation at time when people have little food left in storage after two years of drought; say food is being stockpiled in places like Adet, while children in neighboring towns are beginning to starve; map; photo (M)
news.title: Sudan Hinders U.N. Aid as South Faces Famine

news.abstract: HONG KONG—  A recent telephone call to a major stock brokerage, asking when the manager would be available, produced a confusing reply: "He will call you after the phone."
news.title: Proficiency of English Declines as Schools Switch to Teaching It as a Second Language : Tongue-Tied in Hong Kong

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu cancels dinner with British Foreign Sec Robin Cook, charging that visiting official had violated agreement by meeting with Palestinians at planned site of disputed Jewish settlement in Jerusalem; photo (M)
news.title: Netanyahu Angrily Cancels Dinner With Visiting Briton

news.abstract: Senate Appropriations Committee approves $18 billion in financing for International Monetary Fund, but only if fund formally votes to make major changes in way it lends money to nations in distress; Treasury Sec Robert E Rubin and some Republicans immediately express strong opposition (M)
news.title: Senate Panel Tries to Get I.M.F. to Tighten Its Lending Process

news.abstract: PRAGUE—  Helena Bihariova, 26, did not deserve to die on the night of Feb. 17. Her only crime was to be a dark-skinned Czech citizen of Gypsy origin in the northern Czech town of Vrchlabi.
news.title: As Czech Skinheads Escalate Attacks, Gypsies Start to Put Up a Fight

news.abstract: BEIJING—  Swinging their truncheons, a dozen "intellectual property police" strode into action along Beijing's Zhongguancun street. At the sight of them, the hawkers of pirated compact discs and CD-Roms hurriedly gathered their wares and decamped.
news.title: Illegal Trade in Homemade Computers Thrives : Beijing's 'Backyard' Industry

news.abstract: Senate takes up issue of NATO expansion as afterthought, debating it for second day in row only after chaotic scheduling short-circuits debate on education; Sen John Warner, who is leading opposition to expansion, criticizes Senate for its lack of interest in foreign policy (M)
news.title: Senate Struggles to Pay Attention to the Remapping of NATO

news.abstract: Some $450 million in international aid and two years of United Nations administration fail to turn Vukovar, Croatia, into an example of how minority ethnic population can be successfully integrated into one of nationalist states in former Yugoslavia; of 120,000 ethnic Serbs who lived in eastern Slavonian enclave two years ago, nearly half have fled; there have been dozens of assaults and three ethnic Serbs have been killed by local Croatians, who assumed control on enclave in Jan from United Nations; map (M)
news.title: Despite U.N. Role, Serbs Find No Peace in Croatia

news.abstract: First of two articles, Help Unwanted, on unemployment in France and the pressure on Government to reverse the escalation in jobless benefits; pattern of worker entitlement, protest and Government capitulation is deep-rooted in France and has swollen welfare state into one of most comprehensive and costly in Europe, with much of the burden borne by employers; employers say payroll taxes and benefits are main reasons why the are not creating jobs; French economy is expected to post healthy 3 percent gain in 1998, but it will not produce many new jobs; graph; photo (M)
news.title: French Jobless Find the World Is Harsher

news.abstract: PARIS—  Information warfare was born with hackers, anarchistic whiz-kids who got so bored waiting for their turn running a big IBM mainframe at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology that they turned to pranks such as taking a piano apart, then reassembling it atop the chapel spire.
news.title: U.S. Military Draws Up Battle Plans on How to Win an 'Info War'

news.abstract: Debate in United States Senate over NATO expansion provokes Sen Joseph Biden to erupt in protest when Sens John Warner and Daniel Patrick Moynihan object to redrawing NATO's boundaries to admit Hungary, Poland and Czech Republic, and others in later rounds, including Baltic states, that would form 'iron ring' around Russia; Biden's protesting remarks about 'iron ring' noted (S)
news.title: 'Iron Ring' Around Russia? Comment Provokes Outburst

news.abstract: Indonesian officials begin meetings with International Monetary Fund officials, with both sides offering signals of flexibility on deadlock that has caused halt in disbursements of international aid; officials seek to deal with Indonesia's huge burden of corporate debt, problem that IMF had not previously addressed; photo (M)
news.title: Indonesia-I.M.F. Talks Show Flexibility on Ending Impasse

news.abstract: Chinese Prime Min Zhu Rongji lays down ambitious benchmarks for sweeping social change, pledging to make ailing state-owned industries solvent, overhaul country's banking system and redesign Govt, cutting its staff by half--all within three years; but zeal for economic revolution that Zhu displays at his first news conf as leader of Govt is not matched by any hint of rapid political change; he flatly rules out an official reappraisal of 1989 military crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrators in Tiananmen Square, which killed hundreds and has left lingering wound in society; Zhu says that subsidized housing--a hallowed benefit for country's workers--will be phased out entirely; photo (M)
news.title: NEW CHINA LEADER PROMISES REFORMS FOR EVERY SECTOR

news.abstract: Russia faces new threat of falling oil prices, just as it appears that Russia appears to have weathered economic turmoil that battered Asia; decline in world pprice for oil is expected to result in billions of dollars in lost tax revenue; its is hurting Russia's major oil companies and making it harder for them to make needed investments (M)
news.title: Oil-Price Drop Threatens to Squelch Russia's Economic Rebound

news.abstract: PARIS—  This year should see the handheld computer graduating from a costly gadget to a relatively inexpensive and productive tool.
news.title: Handheld Computer Starts to Come of Age

news.abstract: Dowager Countess of Enniskillen, formerly Nancy MacLennon, American journalist and consular officer, dies on Feb 24 at Kinloch House, her home in Amulree, Perthshire, north of Edinburgh, at 80 (S)
news.title: Lady Enniskillen, 80, Journalist and Diplomat

news.abstract: An hour after President Clinton urged Senate approval of NATO's expansion, the majority leader, Trent Lott, put off action. Mr. Lott said he was frustrated by a filibuster on a bill to set up education savings accounts. Approval had been expected as early as next week for adding three nations to NATO.    Article, page A5.
news.title: Lott Puts Off Vote On Adding to NATO

news.abstract: Turkish Prime Min Mesut Yilmaz, after surviving attempt by religious conservatives to bring down his Govt this week, is confronting an even more powerful group: the military commanders who effectively put him into office last year, and military is pushing back; Islamic-oriented members of Parliament try to topple Yilmaz after his Education Minister ordered ban on wearing of head scarves by female university students; motion fails; Yilmaz has expressed ambivalence about ban on head scarves, which military commanders view as symbols of religious fundamentalism; in recent days, military commanders have complained that Yilmaz is not fighting hard enouh against fundamentalism (M)
news.title: Turkish Premier Confronts Military Over Islam

news.abstract: Journey of four Cuban baseball players and a coach who fled their country on small boat and then seemed to vanish takes puzzling turn with swirl of vague, unconfirmed reports that they washed ashore in Dominican Republic, weakened but alive after nine days at sea; map (M)
news.title: Fugitive Cuban Athletes Are Said to Reach Safety

news.abstract: LONDON—  Whether it's New York or London, Frankfurt or Madrid, stock markets seem to go in only one direction these days.
news.title: Europe Joins America in Golden Rush To the Market

news.abstract: Pres Clinton's coming trip to Africa reflects growing influence on foreign policy of African-Americans like Mayor Wellington E Webb of Denver, who wants US to put Africa at top of its foreign policy agenda (M)
news.title: Blacks Seek Focus on Africa Policy

news.abstract: Richard Butler, who heads United Nations commission disarming Iraq, plans rapid-fire inspections of previously off-limits Presidential properties to determine which will get spot inspections later--with much less notice; insists that this is only beginning of this phase of inspection process; there is speculation among diplomats that once the UN team has visited the eight Presidential sites, Iraq will argue that this phase of arms investigation is over and that country can move closer to a lifting of sanctions (M)
news.title: Rapid-Fire Inspections Planned for Iraq Sites

news.abstract: With another crucial test looming between Iraq and the United Nations, the head of the commission disarming Iraq said he plans rapid-fire inspections of previously off-limits Presidential properties. That will determine which buildings will get spot inspections later, with less notice. And the new procedures could set off a new conflict.    Article, page 8.
news.title: For Iraq, U.N. Plans Rapid-Fire Searches

news.abstract: Pres Clinton's 12-day trip to Africa will emphasize positive changes that have taken place in recent years; military rule is giving way to democracy, South African apartheid is gone and reforms have bolstered a continent-wide economic expansion; Clinton will seek to persuade American audience that Africa not only exists but matters and to impress on Africa that it and US must pursue a relationship marked by mutual respect, shared economic interests and deep veins of common history; map (M)
news.title: Africa Enduring Rebirth Awaits Clinton's Arrival

news.abstract: Nicholas D Kristof analysis on the confounding of the expectation that was widely held in Japan and elsewhere in Asia just a few years ago that their economies were ascendant while America was in decline; says the kind of hubris and triumphalism that blinded Asians to their problems may well do the same to US; says that when things are going well, one is always liable to credit the billiance of one's economic and social structure (M)
news.title: Changing Fortunes: Hubris and Humility as U.S. Waxes and Asia Wanes

news.abstract: SURABAJA, Indonesia—  Welcome to the executive suite at the five-star Hotel Majapahit, a celebration of marble, Oriental rugs and gold plate.
news.title: Silent Hotels / Building Boom Goes Bust : 5-Star Luxury at Bargain Prices

news.abstract: Interview with Alban Maginness, who became first Catholic mayor of Belfast, Northern Ireland, after Protestants lost their long control of city council last year; he cites efforts to reach out to Protestants; Sammy Wilson, Protestant councilman, says split between Protestant Unionists and Catholic Nationalists on council continues; photo (M)
news.title: Belfast Journal; The Chain This Catholic Wears Speaks Volumes

news.abstract: American and European officials say Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic may have made just enough concessions over conflict in Kosovo Province to confound State Sec Madeleine K Albright's efforts to intensify Western sanctions against him; Albright is set to leave for Europe to increase pressure on Milosevic to open serious talks on political autonomy with ethnic Albanians, who make up 90% of population in Serbian province; will meet, Bonn, with ministers of Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Russia, members of contact group that monitors events in former Yugoslavia (M)
news.title: Yugoslavs Try to Outwit Albright Over Sanctions

news.abstract: Rep Louise M Slaughter, leader in drive against female genital mutilation, makes public Health and Human Services Department analysis that found over 160,000 girls and women in immigrant communities in United States may have been victims of traditional practice or are at risk of being subjected to it; practice has been illegal in US since 1997; report is based on statistical analysis by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (M)
news.title: Mutilation Seen as Risk For the Girls Of Immigrants

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II, mixing spiritual and political in nation bracing for critical elections, beatifies Nigeria's first candidate for sainthood, Rev Cyprien Michael Iwene Tansi, and presides over Mass for some million people, Onitsha, Nigeria; repeatedly alludes to human rights situation and need for greater democracy in Nigeria; photo (M)
news.title: Nigerians Pin High Hopes on Pope's Visit

news.abstract: Brief biographical sketches of Grigory A Yavlinsky, Sergei Kiriyenko, Boris Y Nemtsov and Yuri M Luzhkov, who are often mentioned as Pres Boris N Yeltsin's next Prime Minister (M)
news.title: 4 Who Would Succeed Chernomyrdin

news.abstract: French Pres Jacques Chirac, in televised speech, expresses concern about offers of far-right National Front party of Jean-Marie Le Pen to help keep mainstream conservatives in power in wake of closely fought regional elections; warns against cooperating with extremists and damaging France's reputation for upholding democratic values; photos (M)
news.title: Chirac Acts to Thwart Far-Right's Push for Power

news.abstract: R W Apple analysis contends that Pres Clinton by going to Africa has demonstrated that US no longer considers it peripheral; maintains that there is widespread skepticism about Clinton's goal of establishing important economic links with Africa; says Clinton is raising expectations, perhaps beyond his capacity to fulfill them (M)
news.title: Into Africa

news.abstract: Russian Pres Boris N Yeltsin dismisses his entire Cabinet, including his loyal and dedicated aide, Prime Min Viktor S Chernomyrdin; says dismissals are effort to make economic reforms more energetic and effective; although much is made of Yeltsin's move, there are only three major victims so far: Chernomyrdin, First Deputy Prime Min Anatoly B Chubais, controversial economic reform leader, and Interior Min Anatoly S Kulikov; most of other Cabinet members will almost certainly keep their jobs; Yeltsin names Energy Min Sergei Kiriyenko as First Deputy Prime Minister until he names permanent Prime Minister (M)
news.title: YELTSIN DISMISSES HIS ENTIRE CABINET IN SHOW OF POWER

news.abstract: Alessandra Stanley analysis contends that when Russian Pres Boris Yeltsin dismissed his entire Cabinet, question was not just why, but who was really behind decision; maintains that bombshell mostly appears to be messy blend of Yeltsin's will and wishes of some of his closest advisers; says that while some observers paint decision as backstage maneuver by powerful bankers seeking to consolidate their influence, economic reformers chose to view shake-up as small victory for their team; photo (M)
news.title: The Reformers Did It. No, Blame the Bankers.

news.abstract: US officials say that Russia has agreed to sell Yugoslavia tanks, attack helicopters and other weapons in move that could threaten delicate peace in Balkans; deal, which was arranged in Moscow in Dec, has not been made public, and US officials say they are in dark about details (M)
news.title: Russia Reported to Agree to Sell Heavy Weapons to Yugoslavia

news.abstract: KUALA LUMPU—  The Malaysian Navy has launched a small fleet. The police have descended almost nightly on squatter villages, arresting those without working papers. And trawler captains convicted of ferrying illegal immigrants have been sentenced to three years in prison and six lashes with a rattan cane.
news.title: That's the Official Name of Its Crackdown on Illegal Immigrants : Malaysia to Indonesians:Go Away

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, speaking to thousand children in meadow near school in Mukono, Uganda, expresses regret for role of US in African slavery, as he reels off list of errors in American policy toward continent that includes turning to ruthless dictators as allies during cold war; Clinton has been under some pressure at home to issue formal apology for slavery, but he stops well short of such explicit statement; Clinton meets with Pres Yoweri K Museveni and praises his efforts to expand Uganda's economy and educate its people; map; photos (M)
news.title: IN UGANDA, CLINTON EXPRESSES REGRET ON SLAVERY IN U.S.

news.abstract: PRAGUE—  Two of Prague's top hotels have been blacklisted by the U.S. government because they have been purchased by a company with purported links to the government of Libya, and American travelers have been warned that they could face criminal penalties if they stay at them.
news.title: Americans Are Warned Not to Stay at 2 Hotels Linked to Tripoli : U.S. Plays Anti-Libya Card in Prague

news.abstract: Foreign Min Yevgeny M Primakov tells Sec of State Madeline K Albright in Moscow that Russia's foreign policy will remain unchanged despite political turmoil; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Ties Unaffected, Russian Tells Albright

news.abstract: Pres Clinton is spending 11 days in Africa, but he is really making two different trips: one to Africa and one to South Africa; South Africa is of Africa, but different too; its economy dwarfs that of any other African countries; some 300 American companies do business there; in Nelson Mandela, South Africa has President whose international stature rivals Clinton's (M)
news.title: A Touchy South Africa Takes Pains Not to Kowtow

news.abstract: United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan, in speech to Israel Council on Foreign Relations, accuses Israel of chain of 'provocative acts' that he says contributed to crisis in Israeli-Arab relations; says fundamental formula of Oslo agreements, land for peace, is key principle to Middle East peace
news.title: Annan Is Stern But Friendly On Israel Visit

news.abstract: Midway through Pres Clinton's tour of six African countries, it may be too early to know how trip has affected African-Americans--Clinton's most faithful constituency; conversations with several people in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, reveal that Clinton's every move and word are being carefully dissected by African-Americans from all walks of life; photos (M)
news.title: Blacks on a Brooklyn Street: Both Cynics and Optimists Speak Out

news.abstract: Former Clinton Administration officials and human rights experts say Clinton Administration ignored warnings of impending genocide in Rwanda, including Central Intelligence Agency study saying 500,000 people could die if country exploded; say even when it was clear that hundreds of thousands of Rwandans were in mortal danger, US stopped United Nations from taking action that might have saved those lives (M)
news.title: Critics Say U.S. Ignored C.I.A. Warnings of Genocide in Rwanda

news.abstract: US analysts say arrest of Mexico's drug-enforcement chief, Gen Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, in 1997 shows much wider military involvement with drug traffickers than Mexican authorities have acknowledged; classified Drug Enforcement Administration report says arrest of Gutierrez Rebollo followed secret meetings between Mexican Army officers and country's biggest drug mafia; US officials say there is growing evidence that military officers discussed deal to let drug gang operate in exchange for huge bribes, and that some arrangement may have been in place before gang's leader, Amado Carrillo Fuentes, died after extensive plastic surgery last year; photos (M)
news.title: U.S. OFFICIALS SAY MEXICAN MILITARY AIDS DRUG TRAFFIC

news.abstract: Sen Jesse Helms says he opposes permanent international criminal court proposed by Pres Clinton to deal with crimes such as frenzy of killing in Rwanda; Helms says he opposes giving United Nations 'trapping of sovereignty' that court would represent; Helms's threats come as team of American legal experts meets with representatives from 100 other nations over how court will operate (M)
news.title: Helms Vows To Make War On U.N. Court

news.abstract: SEMENYIH, Malaysia—  Nine people were killed Thursday as hundreds of illegal Indonesian immigrants rebelled at a detention camp here hours before they were to be deported across the Strait of Malacca.
news.title: Fiery Uprising Kills 8 Detainees in Camp And a Police Officer : Crackdown In Malaysia Sets Off Riot By Illegals

news.abstract: Canada's long struggle to stay united takes unusual turn as one of country's most prominent politicians, Jean Charest, switches parties so he could spearhead effort to defeat Quebec separatists in coming provincial elections; polls suggest Charest could win election against current separatist government; Liberal Party victory, bringing Charest into office as Premier, could forestall third referendum on independence for French-speaking province (M)
news.title: Top Conservative Jumps Parties to Take On Quebec Separatists

news.abstract: One of Russia's most prestigious military institutions, Frunze Naval Academy, is first and only naval academy in country to accept female cadet; Cadet Lyudmila Yolshina says she was not greeted with anything like hostility that drove Shannon Faulkner from The Citadel after only one week; she says she was told to report any problems to superiors, and her fellow cadets fear consequences if they harass her; mostly, she seems surrounded by amused condescension; but cadets and faculty of Frunze draw line at her dream of serving on combat ship; Russian women have extraordinary record of combat bravery in wartime, yet they are relegated to lowly support position in rear during peacetime; Yolchina was accepted at Funze only after writing letter to Pres Boris N Yeltsin and Defense Min Igor D Sergeyev, imploring them to let her continue family tradition of naval service; photos (M)
news.title: St. Petersburg Journal; Russian Woman Sails Solo in a Sea of Cadets

news.abstract: BANGKOK—  International narcotics specialists and U.S. drug-enforcement officials are increasingly concerned that North Korea may be involved in illegal drug transactions to gain hard currency for its depleted Treasury.
news.title: Law Enforcers Link North Korea to Drug Trade : A Pyongyang Connection?

news.abstract: Shaolin Monastery at foot of China's Song Mountain in Henan is fabled home of Zen Buddhism and of Asian martial arts; students study thousands of special martial moves there; De Yang, 32, is acclaimed master of monastery's stylized and sometimes bizarre routines of strength and self-defense; De Yang says practice of martial routines is simply physical expression of meditation exercises used in pursuit of spiritual enlightenment; monastery has become major tourist attraction in China; photo; map (M)
news.title: Shaolin Temple Journal; Where Zen and Kung Fu Got Off to a Flying Start

news.abstract: Pres Boris N Yeltsin names Sergei Kiriyenko, little-known 35-year-old technocrat, as Russia's new Prime Minister and warns that he would disband Parliament if it rejects nomination; Yeltsin stunned nation by dismissing several Cabinet members, including his longtime Prime Minister, Viktor S Chernomyrdin; Kiriyenko was plucked from obscurity to fill Chernomyrdin's post after aides told Yeltsin that he could not himself take on role of Acting Prime Minister, as he planned, because it would be unconstitutional; Yeltsin appears to be keeping field open by selecting Kiriyenko, but there is streak of recklessness to strategy; Yeltsin is not well and if he should die or become incapacitated, Kiriyenko would take over as President for three months until new elections are called (M)
news.title: Threatening Parliament, Yeltsin Names Neophyte Premier

news.abstract: South African Pres Nelson Mandela, meeting with Pres Clinton in Cape Town, says United States, as leader of world, should reach out to its enemies and seek talk of peace; Mandela praises some Clinton policies but stoutly defends South Africa's right to remain friendly with nations US considers rogues, like Libya, Iran and Cuba; Mandela gives Clinton emotion-drenched tour of Robben Island, where he spent 18 years as political prisoner, confined to tiny cell and forced to do backbreaking labor; Clinton notes that Mandela emerged from that confinement not in anger, but in hope and determination to put things right; Mandela expresses reservations about African trade bill passed by House of Representatives that would require African nations to privatize their economies and liberalize their political systems in order to attain free access to American markets; photos; map (M)
news.title: From Mandela, a Gentle Admonishment

news.abstract: President Boris N. Yeltsin picked a little-known technocrat, only 35 years old, as Russia's Prime Minister and said he would disband Parliament if it rejected the nomination.
news.title: For Russian Premier, A Youthful Neophyte

news.abstract: Prime Min Atal Bihari Vajpayee of India strengthens his week-old Hindu nationalist coalition by assuring Indians that policies will not depart from those of previous governments; nationalists are expected to have trouble holding coalition together over longer term; photo (M)
news.title: India's Confident Leader Faces a Key Vote Today

news.abstract: Scandal surrounding efforts of late drug baron Amado Carrillo Fuentes to take over Grupo Financiero Anahuac reveals how far drug money-laundering has reached into upper echelons of Mexico's financial system; Carrillo, beginning in Mar 1995, sunk about $12.6 million into ownership position in bank, which he was already using to launder money; his drive to control bank was thwarted when regulators seized bank in Nov 1996 because big shareholder was implicated in fraud unrelated to drugs; money-laundering probe began in Apr 1997, when police found Anahuac company car at safe house used by drug cartel (M)
news.title: How Cartel Tried to Buy Bank Group In Mexico

news.abstract: Analysis of demand by Turkey's powerful military for vigorous drive against Islamic extremism; generals hold they fulfill duty to guard state and that today's greatest danger is fundamentalism (M)
news.title: Secularism And Islam

news.abstract: Indonesia's normally quiet universities have begun to respond to economic crisis; students are usually careful to confine nearly daily demonstrations against deprivations to campuses, which are ringed by armed police officers; movement has remained tenative and well behaved, dominated by conservative wing that seeks to avoid confrontation and violence; map; photo (M)
news.title: Indonesian Students Keep Protests Well Within the Pale

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, visiting South Africa as part of 12-day African tour, marks moral courage of long struggle against apartheid, Soweto; comments on gritty, complex task of state-building; says United States aid programs should be extended; Pres Nelson Mandela elaborates on his remarks during news conference with Clinton that US helped white regime during his struggle against apartheid, television interview; photo (M)
news.title: Clinton Commemorates the Struggle to End Apartheid

news.abstract: Thousands of Israeli Arabs march, Sheik Dannun, Israel, protesting Israeli expropriation of their villages; mark anniversary of similar 1976 protest during which Israeli forces killed six Israeli Arabs; map; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli Arabs March Home, To a Place They Can't Live In

news.abstract: News analysis of Pres Clinton's visit to South Africa as part of African visit; even though one of Clinton's central themes is partnership, which is widely welcomed as break with paternalism of past, he left behind major question over terms of potential partnership; US could crush comparatively small nations and economies of continent in its embrace because of its overwhelming economic and political power (M)
news.title: After Clinton's Trek: Fear of a Crushing Embrace?

news.abstract: Six largest US military contractors who stand to gain billions of dollars in sales if Senate approves NATO expansion, have made enormous investments in lobbyists and campaign contributions to promote cause in Washington; have spent $51 billion on lobbying in past two years; their zeal, as well as extensive spadework by Clinton Administration and support by Senate Foreign Relations Committee chairman Jesse Helms, have made it virtually certain that Senate will approve treaty to admit Poles, Hungarians and Czechs; industry is also concentrating efforts abroad, setting up partnerships in Eastern Europe to give companies foothold (M)
news.title: ARMS CONTRACTORS SPEND TO PROMOTE AN EXPANDED NATO

news.abstract: Regional political structure in oil-rich Caspian Sea basin is threatening Armenia's hold on Nagorno Karabakh, part of neighboring Azerbaijan over which it gained control in 1994; rush for unatapped reserves and billions of dollars in planned investments have loosened Russia's grip on region and turned oil-rich Azerbaijan into new hub of regional influence (M)
news.title: Oil-Rich Neighbor Eclipsing Armenia

news.abstract: Interview with Kuan Hsui-chin, one of Tapiei's licensed prostitutes who expresses bitterness over shutdown of city's 18 legal brothels by crusading Mayor Chen Shui-bian in 1997; photo (M)
news.title: Taipei Journal; The Mayor Won't Abide Licensed Licentiousness

news.abstract: US Middle East negotiator Dennis Ross will return to Washington to brief Pres Clinton on reactions by Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat and Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu to new peace proposals; leaders of American Jewish groups say they have been assured by Sec of State Madeleine K Albright that US will not present Israel with ultimatum for withdrawing from West Bank (M)
news.title: No Ultimatum for Israel, Albright Assures U.S. Jewish Groups

news.abstract: Norodom Ranarridh returns to Cambodia to run for re-election as Prime Minister against Hun Sen, with whom he shared power and who ousted him in coup nine months ago; political analysts say July election will amount to verdict on $2 billion international effort to plant seeds of democracy in country ravaged by wars and killings for more than 30 years, but warn that unless political violence and manipulation are brought under control, election will not be free and fair; photo (M)
news.title: Exiled Leader's Return to Test Cambodian Democracy

news.abstract: Senegal, once regarded as model of political progressiveness and stability under former Pres Leopold Sedar Senghor who resigned in 1980 after more than 20 years in office, has become cautionary example of cynicism; while other countries were rejecting one-party past in 1990's and organizing increasingly competitive elections, many Senegalese have complained that elections are routinely won by ruling party that buys votes or manipulates results to maintain 38-year lock on power (M)
news.title: Once Seen As a Political Beacon, Senegal Backslides

news.abstract: Russian Pres Boris Yeltsin says he will not run for re-election in 2000; refrains from endorsing any of potential candidates (M)
news.title: Yeltsin Says He Won't Run For Another Term in 2000

news.abstract: Russia is in search of national idea that can define its essence and inspire its citizens, but struggle has thus far been exercise in conflict and confusion; new national anthem has no words because nobody can agree on what it should say, politicians are still squabbling over tricolor flag and Government commission established in summer 1997 to develop national idea has come up empty-handed; even though disputes over nature of Russian soul has dominated Russian life for centuries, question of national purpose has acquired fresh urgency as nation struggles to redefine itself following collapse of Soviet empire, which provided so much of its identity and mission for 20th century; Yeltsin Government would like to have concept, slogan or sound bite to mobilize public and counter Communists, who while minority at least have an ideology, but has failed to convince public that it has compelling vision of what lies at end of country's long hard road from socialism; photo (M)
news.title: Post-Communist Russia Plumbs Its Soul, in Vain, for New Vision

news.abstract: US envoy Dennis B Ross concludes four-day round of shuttle diplomacy in Middle East after apparently failing to break year-old deadlock in Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations; Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly rejected outright key American proposal for withdrawal from 13 percent of West Bank--part of package said to also include specific actions by Palestinians to fight terrorism as well as timetable for future steps; Ross's failure appears to confront US with options of either exerting greater pressure on Netanyahu by making proposals public, or of abandoning role of mediator (M)
news.title: U.S. Effort Fails To End Impasse In the Mideast

news.abstract: Looting of Greek Orthodox churches in northern Cyprus, where Turkish troops landed in 1974, has brought hundreds of magnificant artworks onto international art market and, in recent months, led to series of spectacular raids by police in Germany; Bavarian police recovered collection of stolen Greek Orthodox icons in Oct and arrested Aydin Dikman, Turkish citizen who has lived in Germany since 1961; German authorities say he is one of Europe's most prolific art thieves; map; photos (M)
news.title: Greek Orthodox Church Icons Ravaged in the Turkish Part of Cyprus

news.abstract: Steven Erlanger analysis notes that US negotiator Dennis B Ross made some headway during his recent meetings with Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat, but Sec of State Madeleine K Albright said that it was 'not nearly enough' for breakthrough in impasse; contends that stalemate is not only damaging Israel's position in Middle East but Washington's too; photo (M)
news.title: On the Road to Talks: Israeli Pace Annoys U.S.

news.abstract: Pres Clinton visits Mokolodi Nature Preserve in Botswana and goes on safari with Hillary Rodham Clinton in Chobe River Valley; Clinton, in speech at nature preserve, calls for Senate approval of environmental treaty to limit growth of deserts; map; photo (M)
news.title: Botswana Is Pleased To Be Host To Clinton

news.abstract: Florian Raunig, Albanian-speaking Austrian, is head of four-member civilian monitoring group that has been posted by Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe to assess conditions in lawless territory that runs along Albanian-Serbian border (M)
news.title: Albania Calls In European Monitors to Watch Kosovo Border

news.abstract: British residents in Hong Kong were granted one-year extension of their visas in April 1997, four months before Britain handed former Crown Colony back to China; those visas expire en masse on March 31, and thousands of Britons must prepare to leave; British leaving this time are generally young; they work as bartenders, waitresses and short-order cooks in pubs and restaurants; photo (M)
news.title: Hong Kong Journal; A Bit of the Old Empire Shows Britons the Door

news.abstract: Clinton Administration and Sen Alfonse M D'Amato, who has led investigations into wealth looted by Nazi Germany, say they will set up commission to determine if any Holocaust-era assets are still in American banks (M)
news.title: Inquiry to Ask if Nazi Loot May Also Be in U.S.

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  The World Bank is warning that $3 billion in emergency food and medical aid will be needed over the next year to help Indonesia provide essential supplies to millions of people affected by drought and the economic crisis.
news.title: In a Process That's 'Going to Be Years': World Bank's Estimate For Jakarta:$3 Billion

news.abstract: Greece, which did not make list of 11 countries ready to adopt euro in 1999, now ponders its chances for becoming eligible in 2001 despite its belated efforts to trim its debt and shrink its overindulged state sector; joining the euro club is goal firmly held by Prime Min Costas Simitis and cherished by many Greeks (M)
news.title: Joining Euro A Dim Hope For Greece

news.abstract: China agrees to release a noted dissident, Wang Dan, for medical reasons and send him into exile; release is part of agreement by US to drop sponsorship of resolution condemning China's human rights policies; Wang has been at top of list of Chinese dissidents that Clinton Administration has been trying to get released (M)
news.title: U.S. Reports China Has Agreed to Free Tiananmen Leader

news.abstract: United Nations special investigator Abdelfattah Amor rejects charges by Scientology movement that German Government is using Nazi tactics of persecution and ill treatment against it (M)
news.title: U.N. Derides Scientologists' Charges About German 'Persecution'

news.abstract: Four former Salvadoran national guardsmen convicted of killing three American nuns and a lay worker in 1980 say for first time that they acted only after receiving 'orders from above'; El Salvador and US have always officially argued that killers acted on their own; human rights groups and relatives of victims--Maura Clark, Jean Donovan, Ita Ford and Dorothy Kazel--have always maintained that executions were ordered by military authorities; United Nations Truth Commission report in 1993 concluded that Col Carlos Eugenio Vides Casanova and Gen Jose Guillermo Garcia had ordered official coverup; both men have been granted residence in US and now live in Florida; four guardsmen are Daniel Canales Ramirez, Carlos Joaquin Contreras Palacios, Francisco Orlando Contreras Recinos and Jose Roberto Moreno Canjura; photos (M)
news.title: 4 Salvadorans Say They Killed U.S. Nuns on Orders of Military

news.abstract: Indonesia is within days of signing new accord with International Monetary Fund to try to rescue its collapsing economy, and fund's leadership is fending off criticism that it is giving in too much to demands of Pres Suharto; new accord delays imposition of earlier requirements that Indonesia end its subsidies on electricity, gasoline and number of basic food items; Indonesian officials say fund's attempt to terminate subsidies are stoking anti-Government protests across country (M)
news.title: Indonesia to Sign 3d I.M.F. Rescue Pact

news.abstract: Hamas and Palestinian officials accuse Israel of assassinating a suspected Hamas bomb maker, Muhyiaddin al-Sharif, on West Bank (S)
news.title: Israelis Accused in Killing

news.abstract: French court finds Maurice Papon guilty of complicity in Nazi crimes against humanity because as a Vichy official he turned Jews over to the Germans in World War II; imposes 10-year prison sentence, with deprivation of civil rights; finding both comforts and disconcerts country Papon served as high-ranking civil servant for 50 years; Papon remains free while he appeals, and both sentence and his continuing freedom draw criticism from those who expected more severe sentence; photo (M)
news.title: Ex-Vichy Aide Is Convicted And Reaction Ranges Wide

news.abstract: Hillary Rodham Clinton proves a political asset to Pres Clinton during their trip to Africa, which she visited a year ago and pressed her husband to visit; White House aides acknowledge that Clinton partnership has been more visible in Africa than it has been since 1994; map; photo (M)
news.title: The Clintons as Teammates, Dovetailing in Africa

news.abstract: Maurice Papon, who was convicted in France of having been accomplice to Nazi crimes against humanity during World War II, is ordered by French criminal court to pay nearly $750,000 in damages and legal fees to victims and their lawyers (M)
news.title: Ex-Vichy Aide Is Ordered to Pay $750,000 in Damages and Fees

news.abstract: Interview with 16-year-old Parinya Kiatbusaba, Thailand's kick-boxing sensation, who is also transvestite; photos (M)
news.title: Bangkok Journal; Was That a Lady I Saw You Boxing?

news.abstract: Federal grand jury is investigating whether Loral Space and Communications and Hughes Electronics illegally gave China space expertise that significantly advanced Beijing's ballistic missile program; officials say criminal inquiry was dealt serious blow when Pres Clinton recently approved export to China of similar technology from Loral; decision was opposed by Justice Department, which argued that it would be difficult to prosecute companies if Government gave blessings to deal; companies have denied wrongdoing (M)
news.title: Companies Are Investigated For Aid to China on Rockets

news.abstract: Pres Clinton warns Japan in unusually explicit terms that it must change course if it hopes to pull economy out of long-running decline that has worsened in recent weeks; says country's current strategy is clearly not appropriate to times; praises Prime Min Ryutaro Hashimoto as able man, but says there is clearly ongoing struggle with entrenched bureaucracy; comments add to pressure from Treas Sec Robert E Rubin and leaders of several of world's biggest economic powers, who have repeatedly warned that Japan's economic decline and its inability to absorb imports from neighboring countries threaten to hurt Asia's fragile recovery; yen falls to six-and-a-half-year low against dollar in mounting evidence that Japan is heading into one of worst downturns since end of World War II (M)
news.title: Clinton Warns Japan: Fire Up Economy to Stem a Decline

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  The Dow Jones industrial average topped 9,000 points for the first time Friday, reflecting seemingly insatiable demand for stocks from investors around the world.
news.title: Unemployment Goes Up but Optimism on Economy Prevails : U.S. Stocks Breach the 9,000 Barrier

news.abstract: Germany's opposition Greens party, which seemed to be staking out role as political kingmaker not too long ago, is being depicted more as court jester; swing might be easily dismissed were it not for fact that come Sept, German voters will decide who will lead nation into new millennium; because of Germany's political system, small parties like ecologically minded Greens are coalition-builders that help carry big parties to power (M)
news.title: For Greens Of Germany, The Outlook Is Murky

news.abstract: United Nations Commission on Human Rights investigator Fatma-Zohra Ksentini report names US, Germany, Australia, Britain and Netherlands as biggest toxic-waste exporters, and says masses of toxic waste are still being sent to Africa; Ksentini says dumping is human rights violation (M)
news.title: West Hinders Inquiry on Dumping as Rights Issue

news.abstract: US authorities, in sweeping new effort to control travel across Mexican border, have begun calling in border-crossing documents held for decades by millions of Mexicans to replace them with high-tech visas carrying digital fingerprint; documents being replaced allow over 100 million legal border crossings each year by business people, tourists and shoppers from Mexico; hope is that new cards, which State Dept calls laser visas, will help screen out criminals and illegal immigrants; replacement of old border-crossing cards has many Mexicans upset by $45 processing fee and nervous that their applications may be denied; map; photo (M)
news.title: In Mexico and the U.S., New Visas Produce Stress

news.abstract: Officers of SAB bank in Sarajevo, Bosnia, say large cash accounts of embassies, World Bank, European Commission and other international organizations are frozen and perhaps lost; dispute over bank's ownership caused a run, and depositors can no longer withdraw their money; some foreign banking experts say they expect trouble to be cleared up soon, but many Bosnians say they believe foreigners do not know Bosnia (M)
news.title: Case Study Shows Why Bosnians Shun Banks

news.abstract: Sudan is ruled by conservative Islamic party that has sought to spread Islam among people and discourage other religions; Government has fought to subdue southern Christian rebels who want return to secular government; despite this, Khartoum's churches are filled to overflowing with Christians, worshipping freely, and those congregations are growing; Government has refused to permit any new churches to be built in city or outlying slums, and it has bulldozed dozens of Christian schools; map; photo (M)
news.title: Sudan Christians Take War's Culture Clash North

news.abstract: Albanian rebel groups in Kosovo, Serbia, have swelled in numbers in recent weeks--in part by infusion of new troops and weapons smuggled over border from Albania; there are indications guerrillas have been joined by mercenaries; rapid and startling growth of insurgency has prompted fears that unrest in province could explode into next Balkan war; map (M)
news.title: Ranks of Albanian Rebels Increase in Kosovo

news.abstract: Series, Israel at 50, on ethnic and cultural diversity that has evolved in half-century since founding as Jewish state; interview with Ilan and Aviva Pivko, affluent secular Jews, who defend their hedonism as necessary embellishment that creates environment that looks and feels better, and who regard Israeli-Arab conflict and violence it has spawned as backgound noise; photo (M)
news.title: ISRAEL AT 50: Many Voices, Not All in Unison, in the Spirited Israel of the 1990's; THE SECULAR JEWS: Beauty Is Truth. That Is All the Stylish Need to Know.

news.abstract: Series, Israel at 50, on ethnic and cultural diversity that has evolved in half-century since founding as Jewish state; Sephardic Jews, immigrants or descendants of immigrants from North Africa and Middle East who make up 48 percent of Israel's population, carry keen sense of grievance for what they consider discrimination because of Sephardic background; level of their schooling and unemployment rate has been below that of European, or Ashkenazic Jews; residents of Netivot Sephardic community comment; photo (M)
news.title: ISRAEL AT 50: Many Voices, Not All in Unison, in the Spirited Israel of the 1990's; THE SEPHARDIM: A Sense of Grievance Over a Life Spent 'on Standby'

news.abstract: Series, Israel at 50, on ethnic and cultural diversity that has evolved in half-century since founding as Jewish state; fate has left many Israeli Arabs between two worlds--in which they are second-class citizens among Israelis and Israelis among Arabs; actress Salwa Nakkara, Arab born and raised in Israel, comments (M)
news.title: ISRAEL AT 50: Many Voices, Not All in Unison, in the Spirited Israel of the 1990's; THE ISRAELI ARABS: Too Israeli an Arab, and Vice Versa

news.abstract: Series, Israel at 50, on ethnic and cultural diversity that has evolved in half-century since founding as Jewish state; roughly 800,000 immigrants who swept into country with weakening and collapse of Soviet state have carved out special niche while happily resisting melting pot; some residents of Russian community in Ashdod say they are in harmony in Israel, even though they regard non-Russian Israelis as 'others;' Bella Portnova, violinist with Ashdod chamber orchestra, comments; photo (M)
news.title: Edgy Strangers Happily Resist The Melting Pot

news.abstract: Former US Senator George J Mitchell, mediator at Northern Ireland peace talks, presents Protestant and Roman Catholic negotiators with set of urgent compromise proposals as deadline nears for peace settlement; says proposals will give negotiators comprehensive look at many problems that persist, but that both sides are close to bringing talks to successful conclusion; photos (M)
news.title: Ulster Talks Get Urgent Compromise Plan

news.abstract: Gen Georg Meiring, chief of South Africa's Army criticized for role in presenting President Nelson Mandela with bogus report on left-wing plot to overthrow Government, resigns; says he has lost trust he needs to function properly; has been widely criticized for handling of report, which never went through proper military intelligence channels and was reportedly based on single source; photo (M)
news.title: South African Military Chief Quits Over False Coup Report

news.abstract: Palestinian Authority says Muhyiaddin al-Sharif, suspected bomb-maker found slain in West Bank and who was wanted by Israel for series of suicide bombings that killed scores of Israelis, was murdered in fued within militant Islamic group Hamas, and not by Israel; arrests five members of group for murder; Hamas dismisses findings and renews threat to carry out revenge attacks against Israel, which has emphatically denied any role in killing (M)
news.title: Hamas Killed Its Own, Say Palestinians

news.abstract: Brazilian conservationists are locked in dispute with residents of area near Iguacu Falls National Park over permanent closing of 13-mile road that runs through park, which is one of Brazil's most popular tourist attractions and has been designated by UNESCO as part of world's patrimony; residents say closing brought them severe economic hardships (M)
news.title: 2 Brazil Towns Fight for Road Closed for a Wildlife Park

news.abstract: Iran and Iraq, in important step toward resolving their bitter enmity, begin major exchange of prisoners of war held since end of long and bloody war decade ago; approximately 4,000 prisoners, majority Iraqis, have been repatriated; vast majority of those still in captivity are held by Iran (M)
news.title: Iran and Iraq Begin Big Trade of P.O.W.'s

news.abstract: Fresh from accompanying President Bill Clinton on his trip to Africa, J. Brian Atwood, head of the U.S. Agency for International Development, held talks with international and French government officials in Paris. He also spoke with IHT editors and reporters, and following are excerpts of his remarks about U.S. assistance to African countries.
news.title: Q & A / J. Brian Atwood, U.S. Development Agency : Clinton Seeks Better Start in Africa, and France Understands Why

news.abstract: Paris Journal on new regulations for musicians who want to perform in Metro: they may do so in station corridors, but not on platforms or in cars, and must audition before Metro official to obtain badges; Antoine Naso, who runs badge program, says he tries to imagine what public would like to hear; photo of American singer-guitarist Morty Baumann auditioning; map; rules have led to decline in number of performers, and marked improvement in quality of music heard (M)
news.title: Paris Journal; If You Hear Mozart Arias, This Is a Metro Station

news.abstract: Russian Pres Boris Yeltsin summons opponents to Kremlin for moment of political theater, to demonstrate his grip on power and show support for his new Prime Minister, Sergei N Kiriyenko; television cameras capture Yeltsin projecting image of strength, although meeting itself is somewhat less than definitive (S)
news.title: Yeltsin Tries to Garner Legislators' Votes for His Premier Nominee

news.abstract: Thomas S Foley, former US House Speaker who is now Ambassador to Japan, is employing soft, diplomatic approach, and trying to learn Japanese, at time when US is using blunt language to get Japan to stimulate its economy; Foley argues same case, but with less heat; he also enjoys luxurious mansion, large staff and status as minor deity in Tokyo; photo (M)
news.title: New U.S. Diplomat Tries to Speak Japan's Language

news.abstract: Chinese tourists are now flocking overseas, spending handfuls of cash and emerging as major source of tourism income for battered economies of Southeast Asia; planeloads of Chinese arrive daily in Thailand, most popular and affordable destination; photos; Chinese tourists now roam and shop freely, without Chinese officials who used to keep close watch; Shanghai travel agent says he hopes to take groups to Hawaii, but US is not yet issuing routine tourist visas (M)
news.title: The Chinese Burst Onto the Tourist Scene

news.abstract: Daniel Kurtzer, new US Ambassador to Egypt, is Orthodox Jew and first Jew to be US Ambassador to major Arab country; that has stirred some mistrust and resentment in Cairo; Osama al-Baz, top adviser to Pres Hosni Mubarak, has criticized Egyptian journalists for their hostile reception of Kurtzer, whom he portrays as true friend of Arabs; photos (M)
news.title: Cairo Journal; Blazing a Fresh Trail, Getting a Rancid Welcome

news.abstract: British Prime Min Tony Blair and Irish Prime Min Bertie Ahern are trying to work out compromises on disputed issues between Protestant and Roman Catholic political leaders in effort to meet April 9 deadline for peace agreement in Northern Ireland (M)
news.title: With a Deadline Tonight, Ulster Negotiators Study Compromises

news.abstract: PARIS—  Almost no one disputes the potential of "smart" cards. The ubiquitous plastic cards embedded with foil-covered computer chips are being used for everything from pay phones to parking meters, from vending machines to mobile phones.
news.title: Are 'Smart' Cards Getting Too Wise to Get Off the Drawing Board?

news.abstract: Edmund Jensen, president and chief executive of Visa International Inc., is retiring in December after a four-year tenure that saw Visa expand into chip-card technology. He recently discussed the future of smart cards with Gina Rarick of the International Herald Tribune.
news.title: Q & A / Edmund Jensen, President of Visa : Large Retailers May Spur Revolution in Chip Cards

news.abstract: Militant Islamic groups have been mobilizing and expanding in Morocco; they have gained followers in shantytowns in Casablanca and other cities by assisting sick and unemployed, and are recruiting high school teachers and university students; photo (M)
news.title: Morocco Finds Fundamentalism Benign but Scary

news.abstract: Independent experts who reviewed Iraq's progress in eliminating biological weapons at Baghdad's request have rejected President Saddam Hussein's contention that he no longer has a germ warfare program.    Their report called Iraqi disclosures ''incomplete and inadequate,'' and said Baghdad had failed to convince them that biological weapons have been eliminated.
news.title: Experts Dispute Iraq On Germ Weapons

news.abstract: Swiss Guards, colorfully dressed soldiers who have defended Pope and Vatican gates since 16th century, are in want of leader; search for suitable commander, which has dragged on for five months, has become baffling mystery inside Vatican and beyond; honor, once coveted by Swiss aristocrats, has lost some of its luster; to noblemen and commoners alike, salary is uninviting, reportedly about $30,000 a year; Lt Col Alois Estermann is favorite to be appointed commander, but he is not aristocrat; his photo (M)
news.title: Rome Journal; Pope's Little Army Scrambles to Recruit a Chief

news.abstract: Negotiators in Northern Ireland peace talks miss their April 10 deadline for settlement but work feverishly into morning hours; negotiations are being guided by Prime Ministers Tony Blair of Britain and Bertie Ahern of Ireland as representatives of eight participating Northern Ireland political parties work to reach consensus on final draft; draft was presented to them on April 7 by George J Mitchell, former US Senate majority leader who is chairman of talks; photo (M)
news.title: Britain and the Irish, North and South, Work Toward Ulster Accord

news.abstract: NEWARK, New Jersey—  A Romanian citizen living in the United States admitted in court this week that he was part of a ring that had stolen religious artifacts from France and that he was trying to sell them in the United States, federal officials said.
news.title: Romanian Confesses to Role In a Religious Artifact Ring

news.abstract: United Nations suspends its investigation into allegations of massacres of Rwandan refugees in Congo, after weeks of harassment and detention of Canadian member of team, Christopher Harland; United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Mary Robinson says there is no longer any excuse for behavior of Pres Laurent Kabila's Government in Congo (M)
news.title: U.N., Stymied by Congo Leader, Halts Inquiry on Rwanda Killings

news.abstract: Palestinian Authority and Hamas meet to defuse growing feud over who killed Muhyiaddin al-Sharif, Hamas bomb-maker wanted by Israel for several terrorist attacks who was found murdered in Ramallah; Palestinian Authority accuses expatriate leaders of Hamas of trying to provoke confrontation by pushing internal leaders to break longstanding agreement not to criticize Palestinian leadership in public; accuses Hamas of killing Sharif in internal feud out of suspicion he was collaborating with Israel (M)
news.title: Palestinians and Hamas Feud Over Killing of a Bomb Maker

news.abstract: US officials and private analysts say Pakistan's test of new liquid-fueled missile able to strike deep inside India is based on technology smuggled from North Korea; say weapon is enhanced version of North Korean Rodong missile, which is advanced version of Scud missile developed in Moscow in 1960's (M)
news.title: U.S. Says North Korea Helped Develop New Pakistani Missile

news.abstract: Article examines Colombia's emerald trade, which has been enmeshed in murky undercurrent of drug trafficking and violence involving Medellin drug lords wishing to expand money laundering; trade is controlled by Victor Carranza, who is under arrest for raising paramilitary force of 2,000 men that reportedly operated as death squad; US intelligence officials say he is major drug trafficker and smuggler; Colombia produces 60 percent of world's emeralds; map; photos (M)
news.title: Bogota Journal; Emeralds' Luster Hides a Darker Side

news.abstract: Catholics and Protestants in Belfast react positively to tentative peace accord; many gather together to pray; photo (M)
news.title: On Brink of Peace, Catholics and Protestants Pray

news.abstract: Interview with former US Sen George J Mitchell, Northern Ireland peace negotiator, who says he accelerated pace of negotiations that led to agreement after threat by unidentified paramilitary group to murder high-profile person associated with talks (M)
news.title: Mitchell Feared the Killing of a Leader

news.abstract: 35-year-old Sergei Kiriyenko, Pres Boris Yeltsin's besieged nominee for Prime Minister, has shown himself to be adept politician in brief period on national stage; his liabilities, mainly his youth and limited Government experience, are also his potential strengths since he has not been in Government long enough to make many enemies; he may be leader who can pursue market-economy measures without debilitating ideological battles that hobbled some predecessors; photo (M)
news.title: Yeltsin's Nominee, Besieged, Is Not Without Allies

news.abstract: Interview with Harriet Mayor Fulbright, wife of former US Sen J William Fulbright, who is visiting Paris to discuss progress on exchange of French and American exhibits of popular art on behalf of President's Committee on the Arts and Humanities (M)
news.title: Famous Name in Fellowships Turns to Art Exhibits

news.abstract: Three years after Dayton peace accords committed NATO countries and international organizations to rebuild shattered economy of Bosnia, $7 billion spent annually is paying off as reconstruction of country is picking up speed; largely responsible for efforts are nearly 200 nongovernmental organizations from 24 countries that will spend approximately $1 billion in 1998 rebuilding infrastructure and social services (M)
news.title: Aid Groups Are Hands That Help In Bosnia

news.abstract: Palestinian police arrest dozens of Hamas members in West Bank and Gaza Strip, including alleged leader of plot to kill another member of militant Islamic movement; Hamas dismisses allegations as 'mockery' and issues statement that its own investigation confirmed that Palestinian Authority chief, in collusion with Israel, killed Muhyiaddin al-Sharif, member of organization's military wing held responsible by Israel for several terror attacks (M)
news.title: Palestinian Police Arrest Suspected Hamas Killer

news.abstract: Mexican police raid farming cooperative in Chiapas state after Indian supporters of Zapatista rebels declared independence from state government; arrest 20 people, including 11 foreigners, some of whom were human rights observers (S)
news.title: 11 Foreigners Are Detained In Mexico Raid

news.abstract: Many of loudest voices among Irish New Yorkers react with suspicion or derision to agreement intended to end strife between Catholics and Protestants in Northern Ireland; but in Irish neighborhoods of city, many Irish-Americans gradually begin to accept agreement as stunning but welcome gift (M)
news.title: In New York, as in Belfast, A Blend of Irish Voices

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II delivers grave and at times dark Easter message at St Peter's Square; warns of fratricidal strife and slaughter that still exists around world; photo (M)
news.title: Pope's Words On Easter Call For Dialogue Toward Peace

news.abstract: Clinton Administration handling of satellite technology exports to China by key Clinton supporters illustrates competing forces that buffet President on China policy; classified Pentagon report in May 1997 concluded that scientists from Hughes Electronics and Loral Space and Communications had turned over expertise that significantly improved reliability of China's nuclear missiles, even though companies were ordered to keep tight rein on such sophisticated technology sought by Chinese military; criminal probe of companies was reportedly undermined when Clinton approved Loral's exports to China; White House denied any political interference in issue, but Chinese reportedly concluded that Administration policy on issues like spread of weapons and human rights abuses could be reversed by corporations; Loral is headed by largest personal donor to Democratic Party last year; Administration's China policy has come under intense Congressional scrutiny in last year; at issue is influence American contributors have on China policy (M)
news.title: U.S. BUSINESS ROLE IN POLICY ON CHINA IS UNDER QUESTION

news.abstract: People of Northern Ireland go to their churches to celebrate Easter and to pray for permanent peace promised by historic agreement signed by leaders of Protestant majority and Roman Catholic minority; many of them barely remember when there was no sectarian violence; forgiveness and hope for peace are themes at most Catholic and Protestant churches, but not at breakaway church founded by Rev Ian Paisley, who kept his Democratic Unionist Party out of peace negotiations; Paisley, publicly described by opponents as xenophobe and fascist, attacks peace agreement and urges his congregation of 300 mostly older people to vote against it in May 22 referendum; one of his congregants voices fear about terrorists being released, theme Paisley has been stressing; under peace accord, many Catholic and Protestant paramilitary prisoners would be eligible for early release within two years; photo (M)
news.title: For Most in Belfast, an Easter of Joy and Hope

news.abstract: Catherine Bertini, executive director of United Nations World Food Program, says young children in North Korea appear better nourished than they did year ago, but serious food shortage continues there; says North Korean officials are still not cooperating fully with her agency, which solicits and distributes most of aid to nation of 23 million people; several reports suggest that food aid earmarked for general public is being eaten or stockpiled by officials and army; reports of groups such as Doctors Without Borders are far more dire than Bertini's assessment (M)
news.title: Despite Gains, North Korea Is Pressed On Food Aid

news.abstract: Human rights activists, Russian press and some of Moscow's leading politicians accuse Government of Pres Boris Yeltsin of engaging in clumsy power play by annulling victory of populist Andrei Klimentyev, who won race for Mayor of Nizhny Novogorod in election that was embarrassment for advocates of market reform; Klimentyev has since been dragged to jail to face corruption charges; town is highly touted bastion of reform and hometown of Sergei Kiriyenko, designated Prime Minister, and of Boris Nemtsov, top Kremlin aide; map; photo (M)
news.title: Heavy Hand Squelches Yeltsin Foe

news.abstract: Interview with Bruno Megret, soft voice of France's far right who is regarded as brain behind political strategy that has convulsed French politics by undermining country's political center (M)
news.title: On Far Right, A Soft Voice Undermines French Center

news.abstract: Interview with Italian business tycoon Giovanni Agnelli, who says he welcomes change to single European currency and to more open markets; map; photo (M)
news.title: Rome Journal; A Delphic Oracle Has Seen the Future, and Likes It

news.abstract: Former South African Pres P W Botha reportedly agrees to appear before country's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, day before he was to stand trial for refusing to obey repeated commission subpoenas (S)
news.title: Apartheid-Era Chief Said to Yield to Panel

news.abstract: NEW YORK—  Having decided that there is safety in big numbers, two pairs of American banks announced $90 billion worth of mergers Monday, bulking up to compete more efficiently in an international industry that increasingly emphasizes size.
news.title: Nations Bank Drives $62 Billion Merger : A New BankAmerica:Biggest of U.S. Banks

news.abstract: Turkish commandos stage raid into northern Iraq and capture Kurdish rebel commander, Semdin Sakik, who recently defected from guerrilla leadership (S)
news.title: Turkish Commandos Capture a Kurdish Leader in Raid Into Iraq

news.abstract: Nine IRA members are released from Irish prison early to strengthen support for Northern Ireland peace agreement; move is considered show of support for Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams, who faces internal opposition to accord (S)
news.title: As First Step in Peace Accord, Ireland Frees 9 I.R.A. Prisoners

news.abstract: Trial of former South African Pres P W Botha is postponed for day while his lawyers and Truth and Reconciliation Commission negotiate to avoid embarrassing and politically divisive proceedings; 82-year-old Botha faces contempt charges for ignoring subpoenas to testify about anti-apartheid policies (S)
news.title: Looking for Compromise, South Africa Postpones Botha Trial

news.abstract: Treasury Sec Robert Rubin outlines US initiative to avoid future economic convulsions in Asia; calls for drastic updating of international financial markets, and requirement that nations disclose embarrassing financial data; he and Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan propose that US consider barring foreign banks from operating in US unless home countries impose strong regulation on their financial institutions; Indonesia, Thailand and South Korea all lacked such controls before their banks began crumbling under weight of bad debt and plunging currencies (M)
news.title: U.S. Treasury Chief Offers Plan to Avoid Crises Like Asia's

news.abstract: Arrest of Teheran's mayor, Gholamhossein Karabaschi, becomes focus for struggle between hard-liners and moderates since election of Pres Mohammad Khatami; Khatami supporters hope for greater political and cultural tolerance and protest mayor's arrest; photo; conservatives denounce Karabaschi as corrupt and hail arrest as part of anti-corruption campaign (S)
news.title: Teheran Mayor's Arrest Focuses Iranian Power Struggle

news.abstract: United States works quietly with other nations to defuse growing confrontation between Russia and Latvia that theatens to damage Washington's already fraying relationship with Moscow; Latvian Cabinet has agreed on changes in its citizenship laws to answer Russian contention that Latvia mistreats Russians who live there; American official says Clinton Administration is concerned over Moscow's 'bullying rhetoric and tactics' against Latvia, including threats of economic sanctions (M)
