news.title: U.S. Is Trying to Defuse a Growing Russia-Latvia Confrontation

news.abstract: Throngs of Hindus bath in Ganges during kumbh mela, major festival at Hardwar, in northern India; millions of pilgrims gather at holy site, one of four where it is celebrated; photo; map (M)
news.title: Ancient Hindu Festival Thrives in Computer-Age India

news.abstract: Trial of former South African Pres P W Botha begins after negotiations to avoid proceedings against him break down; Botha, defiant apartheid-era leader, is known for his stubborn and combative way when he led country; he faces charges of contempt for refusing to go before country's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which wants to question him about his role in authorizing widespread artrocities that took place during his decade in power; Truth Commission, hoping to avoid politically divisive spectacle of taking Botha to court, had agreed to many concessions Botha had sought, but in the end it was not enough (M)
news.title: Botha Trial Begins After Talks to Avoid It Fail

news.abstract: Israel frees longest-serving Palestinian prisoner held without trial, signaling softening of policy criticized as one of country's most serious violations of human rights; Ahmad Qatamesh had been jailed for 5 years and 7 months without trial on suspicion of being leader of Popular Front for Liberation of Palestine, militant group opposed to Israeli-Palestinian accords; his release follows growing campaign by Israeli human rights groups, lawyers, leftist politicians and writers against detention without trial; Qatamesh denies Israeli television report that he agreed to renounce anti-Israeli violence in exchange for his release; photo (M)
news.title: Easing Its Stand on Detentions, Israel Frees a Palestinian

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  The European commissioner overseeing the historic shift to a single currency brought a message of reassurance here Wednesday, saying that while the advent of the euro will represent "an unprecedented challenge," the transition from 11 currencies to one should bolster the global economy without unduly roiling foreign exchange markets.
news.title: Amid Uncertainty, Policymakers Talk Up Currency : Trans-Atlantic Cheer for Euro

news.abstract: German Emilio Ornes, influential publisher of newspaper El Caribe in Dominican Republic and longtime champion of freedom of the press in Latin America, dies at age 78; photo (M)
news.title: German Ornes, 78, Publisher And Advocate of Free Press

news.abstract: Report by United Nations chief arms inspector, Richard Butler, concludes that Iraq is no closer to meeting requirements for lifting of sanctions than it was last fall, when Baghdad began to disrupt efforts to locate and destroy its remaining weapons of mass destruction; evidence in report of Iraq's failure to provide any new information on its weapons, coupled with new outburst of defiance from Baghdad, raises once again prospect of confrontation between Iraq and United States, which has twice threatened military action against Iraq for impeding weapons inspections; Butler's report is turned over to Sec Gen Kofi Annan and is likely to go to Security Council by weekend; Iraqis step up pressure to have sanctions lifted, a move diplomats did not expect in earnest until next sanctions review in October (M)
news.title: U.N. REPORT SEES NO IRAQI PROGRESS ON WEAPONS ISSUE

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  China has used its strong economy and apparent immunity to Asia's financial turmoil to gain significant diplomatic favor with its previously suspicious neighbors at the expense of Japan, which has failed to meet regional expectations of leadership, officials and analysts say.
news.title: Japan's Lack of Leadership Pushes ASEAN Toward Cooperation With China

news.abstract: Dith Pran, Cambodian journalist whose ordeal of forced labor, starvation and beatings by Khmer Rouge was portrayed in 1984 film The Killing Fields, says that Pol Pot's death may have dashed hopes to try him for crimes against humanity, but adds that it will not end quest for justice by survivors of his four-year reign of terror (M)
news.title: Survivor of Killing Fields Is Resolute in Quest for Justice

news.abstract: Apple Computer, self-styled rebel of American computer industry, removes images of Dalai Lama from an advertising campaign in Asia for fear of offending China; Apple has used Tibet's exiled spiritual leader in United States, where he appears as one of series of revolutionary figures from politics, academia, culture and business; but he will be conspicuously absent from Apple's ads in Hong Kong; photo (M)
news.title: Apple Removes the Dalai Lama From Its Ads in Hong Kong

news.abstract: Thai officers poke and prod body of former Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot, Sahook, Cambodia, taking fingerprints and other evidence to prove that man responsible for over million deaths is dead; examination falls short of full autopsy; foreign journalists view body; his widow, Mea Son, says he died in his sleep; Cambodian troops and Khmer Rouge defectors pursue last group of guerrilla holdouts, led by Ta Mok; map; photo (M)
news.title: In Death, Indignity for Despised Killer

news.abstract: POMPEII—  Buried in a matter of hours under several meters of ash and pumice stone during a cataclysmic eruption of Vesuvius in 79 A.D., Pompeii is the most perfectly preserved city to come down to us from the ancient world. Last year almost 2 million people visited the site, well over half a million more than the Uffizi Gallery in Florence, making the antique ghost town the most popular single attraction in Italy.
news.title: In the Battle for Pompeii, A Plan to Reverse Decay

news.abstract: High-tech revolution has transformed Israel, founded 50 years ago as socialist experiment by defiant European Jews, into Mideast Silicon Valley; nation abounds with signs of prosperity as high-tech exports grow; current indicators point to incipient recession and tensions with Palestinians have battered tourism and could start scaring off investors; graphs; map; photo (L)
news.title: Israel Redefines Its Dream, Finding Wealth in High Tech

news.abstract: Israel's new-found economic success leads many Israelis and Americans to question size of United States aid package; Israel, largest beneficiary of US aid, has been getting $3 billion in American economic and military aid for last several years, even as overall foreign aid budget has fallen; has proposed phasing out economic aid and increasing military aid, for eventual overall cut of 20 percent; Congressional members who favor larger cuts fear offending American Jews or Israel's powerful lobby (M)
news.title: Awash in U.S. Aid. Could Float Fine Without It.

news.abstract: Since Pol Pot's death, the Clinton Administration has intensified its effort to bring the leaders of the Khmer Rouge to trial, asking experts to prepare indictments of several figures for gross rights abuses, American officials said.
news.title: Net for Rebel Leaders

news.abstract: Myanmar, formerly Burma, produced estimated 2,600 tons of opium in 1997, enough to make over 200 tons of heroin--at least 60 percent of world total; military junta, which has tolerated opium trafficking since it seized power in 1988, says that it wants to eradicate all opium within five years; some diplomats view eradication claim skeptically because land devoted to opium cultivation has doubled under junta's rule and country's mismanaged economy has grown to rely on laundered drug profits; map; photo (M)
news.title: Where Opium Reigned, Burmese Claim Inroads

news.abstract: International Atomic Energy Agency is moving close to declaring Iraq free of nuclear weapons, and some US experts are raising alarms and charging agency with complacency; they say Iraq's record of deception and its wealth of talented scientists point to both intention and ability to recreate atomic program quickly (M)
news.title: A Clean Bill For the Iraqis On A-Arms? Experts Upset

news.abstract: Myanmar, formerly Burma, provides at least 60 percent of the world's supply of heroin, but the military Government insists it is ready to crack down and eradicate all opium production within five years.
news.title: A Burmese Tangle Over Opium Trade

news.abstract: Body of Pol Pot, one of century's great mass killers, is cremated near Cambodian-Thai border; only dozen people witness cremation, including small group of photographers who are invited to record event (M)
news.title: At Cremation Of Pol Pot, No Tears Shed

news.abstract: First direct talks in four years between North and South Korea collapse, with each side blaming other; talks began in Beijing, China, on April 12 (M)
news.title: Talks Between 2 Koreas Collapse in Mutual Blame

news.abstract: Christoph Cardinal Schonborn, head of embattled Austrian Roman Catholic Church, apologizes for behavior of predecessor, Hans Hermann Cardinal Groer, who is accused of having molested young seminarians (M)
news.title: New Austrian Cardinal Apologizes for Predecessor's Sex Crimes

news.abstract: Reporter's Notebook on some activities of Pres Clinton and Hillary Rodham Clinton during visit to Chile (M)
news.title: Reporter's Notebook; First Lady Visits Real People in Chile

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  Wang Dan, a leader of the 1989 democracy movement in Beijing, arrived Sunday in Detroit, a day after being freed from a Chinese prison in the latest in a series of moves aimed at easing strains in U.S.-China relations.
news.title: Wang Dan, a Leader of '89 Protests, Arrives in Detroit : China Dissident Frail but Free

news.abstract: Small group of unarmed Palestinian shepherds clashes with three Jewish settlers in Hebron, and a settler is killed (M)
news.title: Settler Killed, Palestinian Wounded in Clash Over Land

news.abstract: Profile of Noel Godin, Belgian pie-thrower who feels he must 'entarte' people who are particularly full of self-importance and particularly lacking sense of humor; Microsoft chairman, Bill Gates, was target in February; photo (M)
news.title: Brussels Journal; The Philosopher With a Pie, and a Glint in the Eye

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat will travel to London on May 4 for separate meetings with Sec of State Madeleine K Albright aimed at reviving stalled peace talks; announcement is made by British Prime Min Tony Blair after meeting with Arafat in Gaza while on Middle East tour; US State Department says meetings will be held to determine whether American proposals on further Israeli withdrawals from West Bank and other issues can provide basis for breakthrough and lead to talks on permanent peace settlement; photo (M)
news.title: Albright to See Netanyahu And Arafat In London

news.abstract: Archbishop Trevor Huddleston, a British Anglican who spent years fighting apartheid in South Africa and helped make its abuses widely known, dies at age 84; photo (L)
news.title: Archbishop Trevor Huddleston, 84, Dies; Fought Apartheid From Its Earliest Days

news.abstract: US and Britain begin classified operation to remove highly enriched uranium and spent nuclear fuel from volatile Caucasus nation of Georgia, fearing it could fall into hands of Chechen gangs, Iran or other aspiring nuclear power; American military and civilian personnel are at research reactor in Tblisi, using large protective containers to pack 8.8 pounds of highly enriched uranium and 1.76 pounds of highly radioactive spent fuel, which will be flown by US Air Force to Britain to be reprocessed at Dounreay nuclear complex in Scotland; operation was undertaken two years after efforts to enlist help from Russians failed and after France rebuffed US request to accept material; British played role after Clinton Administration refused to move it to US because of potential challenges from American environmentalists; Georgia will be paid approximately $125,000 for material; map (M)
news.title: U.S. AND BRITAIN RELOCATE A CACHE OF NUCLEAR FUEL

news.abstract: HANNOVER—  The Great Exhibition of 1851 in London, of which the Hanoverian Queen Victoria and her husband and cousin Prince Albert were prime movers, started the craze for giant international expositions. Curiously, although numerous similar events have been held around the globe since, no German city has ever hosted one. But today's Hanoverians will finally get the chance when the capital of Lower Saxony stages Expo 2000, which opens June 1 of the millennial year.
news.title: Hannover Races to Get Its Futuristic Expo Ready for Opening in 2000

news.abstract: European Union drops legal challenge to Helms-Burton Act, under which US can impose penalties on companies that use American properties in Cuba that were seized by Castro Government three decades ago; decision is major step toward defusing dispute over sanctions that has riled trans-Atlantic relations for more than three years; both sides caution they are still far from final settlement of dispute, and that if talks break down, European Union could file new action with World Trade Organization (M)
news.title: Europeans Drop Lawsuit Contesting Cuba Trade Act

news.abstract: Sinn Fein, Irish Republican Army's political wing, is rapidly changing its public image; has become less aggressive in public, more tolerant of oposition, funnier and even better dressed now that it has attained make-or-break role in Northern Ireland peace effort (M)
news.title: Sinn Fein Is Relaxing Demeanor And Image

news.abstract: Ex-Prime Min Edouard Balladur and parade of high-ranking former French officials tell unusual televised French parliamentary hearing on France's military role in Rwanda that they did all they could to stop French-trained ethnic Hutu forces in 1994 from slaughering ethnic Tutsi minority; killings took more than 500,000 lives; French troops were stationed in Rwanda during period as part of United Nations peacekeeping force (M)
news.title: At Inquiry, French Officials Say They Tried in Rwanda

news.abstract: South Korea says it will end effort to win Japanese compensation for South Korean women forced into Japanese military brothels in World War II; will pay each of 152 registered 'comfort women' $22,700, supplemented by $4,700 each from victims' rights groups; Pres Kim Dae Jung pledges to continue to seek apology from Japan; says Government will not interfere with continued demands by women and nongovernment organizations for Japanese compensation (M)
news.title: Seoul Won't Seek Japan Funds for War's Brothel Women

news.abstract: Internal battle over future of Russian Government bursts into open as fight for control of economic policy between small group of big business owners who have amassed huge fortunes and Government economic reformers; newspaper owned by Boris Berezovsky, Russia's richest and most ruthless tycoon, announces that pitched battle over Pres Boris Yeltsin's nomination of Sergei N Kiriyenko as Prime Minister can only be avoided if Yeltsin abandons market reformers trying to better regulate sale of state property; Berezovsky is believed to be acting with other leading tycoons and has forged key alliances; ex-Prime Min Viktor S Chernomyrdin echoes his call that reformer Anatoly B Chubais be denied post as head of electrical power monopoly; photos (M)
news.title: BEHIND THE BATTLE FOR RUSSIAN POST, ECONOMIC CONTROL

news.abstract: Asst Treas Sec Timothy F Geithner, urging House subcommittee to approve added $18 billion for International Monetary Fund, faces harsh questioning on United States support for IMF bailout of Indonesia in light of nation's human rights violations; he and Karin Lissakers, US representative to IMF, hold Clinton Administration uses its influence to spur human rights; human rights dispute is part of broader Congressional examination of IMF (M)
news.title: I.M.F. Loans to Rights Violators Are Attacked in Congress

news.abstract: British Prime Min Tony Blair, faced with outcry from political opponents, environmentalists and Scottish interests, defends decision to store and reprocess nuclear material in Scotland from old Soviet reactor; confirms New York Times report that Britain has agreed to US request to accept uranium and spent nuclear fuel (M)
news.title: Blair Defends His Decision To Accept Atom Material

news.abstract: Thomas Arturo Gonzalez Velazquez, lawyer who accused top generals and relatives of Pres Ernesto Zedillo of narcotics graft as defense tactic in corruption trial of Mexican Government's drug czar, Gen Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, is slain Guadalajara; photo (M)
news.title: Accuser of Top Generals Slain in Mexico

news.abstract: Americans are beginning to react against policy of continued sanctions against Iraq by organizing their own relief projects for Iraqi people; Americares, private relief organization based in New Canaan, Conn, says it will carry out first American airlift of over 75,000 pounds of medicines and hospital supplies to Baghdad, where nearly eight years of sanctions have crippled civilian medical system (M)
news.title: Americans, Flouting U.N. Embargo, Organize Relief for Iraqis

news.abstract: Senior US and Western officials say planning for possible capture of Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic was set back late last summer after US officials discovered that French military officer, Maj Herve Gourmillon, had held secret meetings with Karadzic and French were covering it up (M)
news.title: French Said to Hurt Plan to Capture Karadzic

news.abstract: BALIKPAPAN, Indonesia—  One by one, Gabriella Fredriksson tracked down the five little bears she had released into the forest.
news.title: In Borneo's Fading Jungles, a Grim Tale of Wildlife

news.abstract: Senior US officials say plans for capturing people indicted on war-crimes charges in Bosnia, including fugitive Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic, went awry last year after US military officers learned that French Army Maj Herve Gourmelon had been meeting secretly with Karadzic (M)
news.title: Leak Caused NATO to Drop Bosnia Effort On Fugitives

news.abstract: Pres Saddam Hussein makes his most direct threat to provoke another crisis over arms inspections unless economic embargo on Iraq is lifted by United Nations Security Council; Iraqi Cabinet issues statement saying US will 'pay dearly' for not heeding warning; Deputy Prime Min Tariq Aziz demands in letter to Security Council that sanctions be lifted 'immediately without any new restrictions or conditions' (M)
news.title: Iraq Again Threatens to Halt Arms Inspections

news.abstract: Congressional Republican leaders drop Clinton Administration's request for $18 billion for International Monetary Fund from popular spending bill, delivering potentially fatal blow to one of Pres Clinton's top foreign policy goals (M)
news.title: G.O.P. Snubs White House On Billions For the I.M.F.

news.abstract: British Prime Min Tony Blair blocks publication of Government restrictions on Northern Ireland's flashpoint summer parades, saying that he wants to avoid destabilizing province at 'volatile time' (M)
news.title: Blair Blocks Release of Rules for Parades in Northern Ireland

news.abstract: NEW DELHI—  When Abha Bhatnagar was growing up, her mother forbade her to go outdoors. She was not trying to keep her daughter out of trouble. "She was trying to keep my skin from getting dark," said Mrs. Bhatnagar, who disobeyed the order. Now she regrets that her olive skin is not lighter. But she believes there is a solution: fairness cream, which she recently started using on her face.
news.title: Especially in India/Fair Color as a Cultural Virtue : Creams for a Lighter Skin Capture the Asian Market

news.abstract: Belgians already outraged by despicable crimes of pedophile-rapist Marc Dutroux are infuriated even more after he carries out brief escape from prison; photos; citizens who feel humiliated and ridiculed by bungling poice and, by extention, inept Government ask how Dutroux, who was recaptured after four hours, could have been left without handcuffs in custody of only one policeman; demands grow for Government to resign (S)
news.title: Bungling in Sex Criminal's Escape Riles Belgians

news.abstract: Truck laden with 22 tons of stainless steel suitable for making missiles is intercepted by customs officials in Azerbaijan en route from Russia to Iran; map; Russian officials had failed to halt shipment despite warning from US intelligence, raising questions about promise to clamp down on such sales to Iran; special alloy can be used to make fuel tanks for Scud missiles (S)
news.title: Iran Nearly Got A Missile Alloy From Russians

news.abstract: US will seek freeze on Yugoslav assets held overseas, in response to warnings that heavy fighting in Kosovo Province is on verge of spilling into Albania; map; State Departments has reports of 'myriad deaths' in Kosovo, where 90 percent of population is ethnic Albanian (S)
news.title: U.S. Eyes Curbs on Belgrade As Albanian Deaths Mount

news.abstract: Clinton Administration, in major move against international crime, is co-sponsoring UN resolution aimed at curbing illicit trafficking in firearms; resolution drafted by Britain and Canada is rewritten to appease US gun lobbyists, by clarifying that it does not call for action on possession of handguns or domestic sales; NRA still opposes any UN role in firearms issues (S)
news.title: U.S., in a Shift, Backs U.N. Move to Curb Illicit Trade in Guns

news.abstract: Standoff between US and Russia apparently derails plans for UN Security Council debate on changing level of nuclear inspections in Iraq from high surveillane to long-term monitoring, whch would be small gesture to Iraq; US Amb Bill Richardson cites concerns reported by inspection chief Richard Butler (S)
news.title: U.S.-Russia Impasse Is Said to Delay a U.N. Debate on Iraqi Arms Inspections

news.abstract: Agreement between Panama and US on drug interdiction center that would have permitted American troops to stay in Panama after US gives up control of Panama Canal on Dec 31, 1999 has unraveled four months after it was announced by Pres Ernesto Perez Balladares; Panama has demanded extensive changes in accord, and negotiators say they do not know if they will be able to produce replacement; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Accord With Panama on Troops Hits a Snag

news.abstract: Foreign Min Mohammed Said al-Sahaf says economic embargo imposed against Iraq in 1990 is eroding and with it Baghdad's isolation; views increased trade and donations, including from Americans, as evidence of general distaste for indefinite sanctions because of their effect on Iraqi people (M)
news.title: Through Trade and Aid, Iraqi Official Says, Embargo Is Eroding

news.abstract: Leaders of 11 European countries will meet in Brussels on May 2 to approve final plans for introduction of single currency on Jan 1; despite some remaining feuding, they are expected to spell out exchange rates at which their individual currencies will be locked together; France and Germany, two most important nations, are still fighting over who will run new European central bank as well as about basic economic principles; most economists say euro's long-term prospects are better than they dared imagine few years ago; graphs (M)
news.title: 11 NATIONS TAKING NEXT PIVOTAL STEP TOWARD THE EURO

news.abstract: Lieut Gen Seri Temiyavej is head of Thailand's Central Investigation Bureau, equivalent of FBI; Seri claims that he has never taken bribe; he has become national folk hero and symbol of reform effort that could reshape Thailand's notoriously corrupt political system; photo (M)
news.title: Folk Hero Strips Teflon From Thailand's Corrupt

news.abstract: Its image has been tarnished, its need for billions in aid questioned in Congress. But to most Americans, Israel remains a worthy recipient of support, and to almost half it is a ''special place,'' rather than just another country, the latest nationwide New York Times poll shows.    American attitudes toward Israel have dipped and risen over its 50 years with the roll of events, but never by much. This month, 57 percent of 1,395 people polled across the country said they had a generally favorable opinion of Israel.
news.title: For Better or Worse, Israel Is 'Special' in U.S. Eyes

news.abstract: Germany Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats are trounced in election in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany's slowest-growing state; German People's Union wins almost 12 percent of vote, putting far-right group into eastern state assembly for first time; photos (M)
news.title: Kohl's Party Routed in East; Far Right Enters Assembly

news.abstract: Ordinary Chinese are increasingly suing powers that be, including their employers, state enterprises and police, acts of defiance against their broad and previously unchecked powers over people's lives; respond to far-reaching overhaul of legal system and rapid changes in economic and social order; number of cases resolved in favor of plaintiff is rising fast, despite laws that are sometimes unclear and unpredictable courts; photo (L)
news.title: A Day in Court, and Justice, Sometimes, for the Chinese

news.abstract: Clinton Administration and champions of Poland battle over proceeds of sale of $240 million in investments made by Polish American Enterprise Fund with foreign aid money; Zbigniew Brzezinski, Polish-born former national security adviser, opposes plan by Treasury and Agency for International Development to return half of money to United States, interview; national security adviser Samuel R Berger favors return of money (M)
news.title: Polish Aid Fund Turns Profit, Posing a Problem

news.abstract: Aleksandr I Lebed enhances his presidential hopes by winning place in runoff election for governor of Krasnoyarsk, vast Russian region; partial tally shows he leads pack, with 43 percent of vote; Valery M Zubov, Kremlin-backed incumbent, is second, with 36 percent (M)
news.title: Ex-General Leads in a Crucial Vote in Siberia, but Faces a Runoff

news.abstract: De Beers Corp maintains tight security in Sperrgebeiet, rich diamond bed along Namibia's southern coast; expects diamonds will be depleted in another 25 years and weighs moves to open ecologically fragile desert area to public; map; photo (M)
news.title: Oranjemund Journal; Find a Diamond in the Sand? Just Don't Pick It Up

news.abstract: Article in series Israel at 50 discusses how peace-loving artists Adi Yekutieli, Israeli Jew, Ahmed Bweerat, Israeli Arab, and Suliman Mansour, Palestinian, produced traveling exhibit of canvas murals that is symbolic guide to living together peacefully; notes that process proved far more tortured than any of them imagined, and was microcosm of mistrust and betrayal that mirrored hostilities they had set out to overcome; photos (M)
news.title: Jews and Arabs, Painting a Mural Together, Find a Mosaic of Mistrust

news.abstract: Canadian Prime Min Jean Chretien meets with Cuban Pres Fidel Castro in Havana; Castro agrees to negotiate foreign investment protection agreement with Canada and agrees to pay $10 million to Canadian insurance company that lost its business in Cuba after 1959 revolution; Chretien fails to win any concessions from Castro on human rights; photo (M)
news.title: Chretien Finds Castro Willing to Deal, but Not on Rights

news.abstract: An effort to have an Israeli Jew, an Israeli Arab and a Palestinian work together to produce a mural depicting a future without fear proved far more tortured than any of them imagined -- a microcosm of mistrust and betrayal that mirrored the hostilities they had set out to overcome.    On a personal level, in private, the men forged a bond and shared a deep mutual respect. But burdened by history and communal expectations, their mural became a battleground of symbols.
news.title: Israel Mural Reveals The Fault Lines at 50

news.abstract: Security Council decides to extend sanctions against Iraq, ignoring threats from Baghdad that it will disrupt future arms inspections if sanctions are not lifted; Bill Richardson, US representative, says United Nations weapons inspectors have found that Iraq still has long way to go in accounting for all of its weapons of mass destruction; Council, in gesture to Iraqis, who have recently allowed greater access to arms inspectors, does not limit future sanctions reviews to six-month intervals but reverts to system of permitting reviews every 60 days; US has vowed to veto any lifting of sanctions until Iraq has met number of requirements, including verifiable disarmament and return of prisoners and property seized in invasion of Kuwait (M)
news.title: Restrictions on Iraq Will Stay in Force, U.N. Council Rules

news.abstract: Wine has been part of life in Georgian Republic for over 5,000 years, and for much of that time Manavi and other villages in Kakheti district have been wine heartland; nearly every family has known nothing but wine business for many generations; each village produces distinct variety, and it is all but impossible to find anyone who does not swear that his or her village makes very finest; map; photo (M)
news.title: Manavi Journal; Georgia's Celestial Wine: Is the World Ready?

news.abstract: Richard Butler, United Nations' chief arms inspector for Iraq, says experts found active mustard gas in artillery shells, raising new questions about over 500 similar shells still unaccounted for in Iraq; shells were found in 1996, but not tested until March, in face of Iraqi opposition; Min Mohammed Said al-Sahaf again holds Iraq destroyed all barred weapons in 1991 (M)
news.title: U.N. Experts Report Finding Mustard Gas in Iraqi Shells

news.abstract: Democracy drive is growing on university campuses across Indonesia; students seem unsure whether movement will end with bloody crackdown or people's revolution, but are increasingly willing to confront police; are gaining support among middle class, which blames Pres Suharto for economic crisis, by denouncing corruption and rising prices; protests are eroding Suharto's aura of authority and omnipotence and creating new confusion about where nation is heading; map; photos (M)
news.title: 'People Power' Unrest on Indonesian Campuses

news.abstract: PARIS—  No army's forces have been so frequently battle-tested as those of Israel. And no other people has lived so long so massively outnumbered by surrounding foes and so convinced of being annihilated if their enemies got the chance as have Israelis.
news.title: And Interwoven With Civil Life : An Army Forged by Wars

news.abstract: Japanese Government offers bill to broaden military ties with United States and let it offer logistical support to American forces in Japan in event of crisis; measure brings Japan step closer to playing larger security role in region; Sec State Madeleine K Albright and Min Keizo Obuchi sign related accord that underscores expanded support from Japan (M)
news.title: Japanese Move to Broaden Military Links to the U.S.

news.abstract: First round of appointments to Russia's new Cabinet are announced after Pres Boris N Yeltsin meets with Prime Min Sergei N Kiriyenko, and it reveals no surprises, no political concessions and hardly any change; seems to confirm view that Yeltsin's sudden dismissal of his Cabinet was targeted at Prime Min Viktor S Chernomyrdin and Anatoly B Chubais; another victim, Interior Min Anatoly S Kulikov, is replaced by Sergei V Sepashin; Boris Y Nemtsov, economic reformer, will remain Deputy Prime Minister, Yevgeny M Primakov Foreign Minister and Mikhail M Zadornov Defense Minister (M)
news.title: After Sound and Fury in Russia, Cabinet Change Is Slight

news.abstract: Italy will be among 11 countries that will formally join European Monetary Union on May 2; only year ago it was considered one of least likely countries to qualify for single currency plan's strict financial controls; Prime Min Romano Prodi's coalition Government, supported by rare consensus among labor unions, business and taxpayers, made heroic strides in cutting spending and raising revenue to bring down Italy's deficit to European standards; concern is that once in, Italy will relax and fail to sustain necessary and more painful fiscal discipline and structural reform; graph (M)
news.title: Italy Savors Victory in Euro Race, But Doubt About Future Lingers

news.abstract: National debate is under way in Irish Republic over provision of new Northern Ireland peace agreement that would grant early release to Irish Republican Army prisoners convicted of terrorist acts, possibly including murder; agreement will be put to separate referendums in Ireland and Northern Ireland on May 22 (M)
news.title: Debate in Ireland Centers on Provision to Free I.R.A. Prisoners

news.abstract: Mexican Labor Ministry, responding to US Labor Dept report that found favoritism toward unions aligned with Mexico's ruling party in labor elections, criticizes US for going beyond terms of North American Free Trade Agreement (M)
news.title: Bias Said to Hurt Independent Mexican Unions

news.abstract: Senate rejects attempt to create tribunal within NATO to help resolve conflicts that might affect alliance before they erupt into full-blown hostilities; votes 62 to 37 to reject proposed amendment to plan to add Poland, Hungary and Czech Republic to military alliance (M)
news.title: Senate Rejects Bid to Create a NATO Unit to Resolve Conflicts

news.abstract: Sec of State Madeleine K Albright meets with Chinese Foreign Min Tang Jiaxuan in Beijing; says US and China are building 'constructive, strategic partnership'; Albright has begun two days of high-level meetings; Pres Clinton will go to China for summit meeting in June (S)
news.title: U.S. and China Gain Rapport, Albright Says

news.abstract: Israel's Indpendence Day, year's most joyous day, follows directly on Memorial Day, its most painful; since a day in Jewish calendar starts previous evening and ends at sundown, Israel's 50th birthday party--fireworks, street music, dancing--takes off at sundown after 24 hours of wrenching commemoration for the more than 20,000 soldiers who have fallen in battle (Reporter's Notebook column) (M)
news.title: Before Celebrating a Nation, Remember the 20,000 Soldiers Who Died Defending It

news.abstract: Pres Clinton says that he is encouraged by Iraqi cooperation with United Nations weapons inspectors and that he expects to reduce number of American troops who are now deployed in Persian Gulf region to keep watch on Iraq (M)
news.title: Clinton Is 'Encouraged' by Iraqi Progress on Arms Inspections

news.abstract: United States is preparing to back $1 billion payment in international emergency aid to Indonesia, despite evidence that Pres Suharto's family and friends are continuing to undermine efforts to break up multibillion-dollar monopolies they control; Treasury officials acknowledge that Indonesia has failed to meet some of most important conditions that were imposed by International Monetary Fund in return for $40 billion bailout package; say, nevertheless, that United States expects to vote in favor of gradual resumption of aid when monetary fund's board meets next week; Clinton Adm says it is satisfied that Indonesia is making 'adequate progress' toward meeting IMF demands (M)
news.title: U.S. SET TO BACK $1 BILLION OUTLAY TO AID INDONESIA

news.abstract: United States State Dept, in its annual report on international terrorism, contends that Iran remains 'most active state sponsor of terrorism' despite last year's election of a more moderate President, Mohammad Khatami, and 'more conciliatory' rhetoric adopted by Khatami and his deputies; report, required by Congress, finds that Teheran Govt was responsible for at least 13 assassinations last year, most of them in northern Iraq against members of Iran's main opposition groups; number of casualties from international terrorism dropped last year: 221 people died in terrorist acts in 1997, compared with 314 in 1996; more than third of 304 acts of international terrorism took place in Colombia; deadliest terrorist attack took place in Egypt, when 58 foreign tourists and 4 Egyptians were killed in attack by Muslim extremists at temple near Luxor; State Dept singles out seven state sponsors of terorism: Cuba, Iran, Iraq, Libya, North Korea, Sudan and Syria (M)
news.title: U.S. Report Calls Iran No. 1 Terror Sponsor, Despite New Leader

news.abstract: Russian Pres Boris N Yeltsin assembles new team that is strikingly young, pro-reform and from outside Moscow; Russian political establishment was stunned when Yeltsin selected 35-year-old Sergei V Kiriyenko as his new Prime Minnister; Yeltsin went further by filling out top ranks of his Govt with squad of young politicians cut from same cloth; key appointment is Yeltsin tapping Oleg Sysuyev as third of three deputies to Kiriyenko; appointment is a major setback to Russia's business tycoons, as well as Communists, who had hoped to install one of ther own at pinnacle orf new Govt (M)
news.title: Yeltsin's New Outsider Team: Young, Reformist and Green

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  Starting from the Declaration of Independence, it took the United States nearly 90 years to establish a fully fledged common currency, and a further 50 years to set up the Federal Reserve system in 1913.
news.title: By Any Measure, Europe's New Monetary Union Is a Historic Exploit

news.abstract: Break in reservoir of zinc mine in southern Spain releases about 150 million cubic feet of acidic sludge into Guadimar River near Aznalcollar, contaminating croplands and Donana wildlife reserve and causing serious environmental disasters; photo; map; makeshift dikes stop toxic waste from swamping reserve, but poisonous flow has cut through northern part of vital buffer zone around park; heavy-metal pollution will immediately enter food chain during crucial breeding season for many species; Donana Park is on main route for Europe's migratory birds and home to many mammals but farms and tourism have been encroaching on fertile region; environmentalists have warned of danger from Los Frailes Mine thirty miles away; large open-pit mine is owned by Toronto-based Boliden Ltd (M)
news.title: Big Sludge Spill Poisons Land in Southern Spain

news.abstract: Horrors of war crimes by Nazi-backed Ustashe regime in Croatia are revived with arrest in Argentina of Dinko Sakic, one of most important accused war criminals still alive; Sime Klaic, who was imprisoned in Jasenovac concentration camp run by Sakic, recalls torture and murder of three captured American aviators; Sakic, living in Argentina, discussed his past in broadcast interview last month; Croatia bows to heavy international pressure and requests extradition; trial would compel Croatia to examine its wartime history, but could also serve revisionists like Pres Franjo Tudjman who prefer to minimize Ustashe atrocities; Jewish survivor describes Sakic overseeing execution of several hundred Jewish women and children; other accounts also quoted; brutality of Ustashe regime, which killed 31,000 of Croatia's 39,000 Jews and about 200,000 Serbs, is rarely mentioned in schoolbooks; Sakic's wife's brother headed Ustache secret police, and she is also accused by survivors of committing murders; photos; map (M)
news.title: War Crimes Horrors Revive As Croat Faces Possible Trial

news.abstract: Dan Polland, American Baptist missionary expelled from Russia in March, is granted visa to return to his church in Vanino, remote port town in Russian Far East (S)
news.title: Baptist Gets Visa to Return to Russia

news.abstract: Pres Clinton hails Senate approval of NATO membership for Poland, Hungary and Czech Republic, saying it will make Europe safer for its citizens and a more prosperous trading partner for US; comments to workers at Therma Inc in Palo Alto, supplier to high-tech industry; Clinton is in California to visit daughter at Stamford, and to raise money for Democratic candidates in Silicon Valley and Los Angeles (S)
news.title: Clinton Predicts a Safer and Richer Europe

news.abstract: European Union plan to begin common currency among 11 countries in 1999 gets underway after leaders of 15 member nations, meeting, Brussels, resolve dispute between France and Germany over who should run new European central bank; leaders name Wim F Duisenberg of Netherlands, German-backed candidate, to eight-year term after he says he plans to retire by mid-2002; France had sought written agreement that he would leave after four years to make way for French candidate, Jean-Claude Trichet; photo (L)
news.title: EUROPEANS ACCEPT A SINGLE CURRENCY DESPITE LATE SNAG

news.abstract: State Sec Madeleine K Albright visits Mongolia, basking in attention of nation's plucky young democratic reformers; meets with Prime Min Tsahiagiyn Elbegdorj, who says Monglia implements both political and economic changes, while cherishing human rights; photo (M)
news.title: Albright Finds Unalloyed Love in a Newly Minted Democracy

news.abstract: Heroin addiction is spreading in Myanmar, world's top opium exporter, where sharing of syringes has led to world's highest rate of infection with AIDS virus; foreign medical researchers put total number of addicts at some 500,000 and estimate several hundred thousand have become HIV-positive (M)
news.title: Opium Puts Myanmar In Crisis Over AIDS

news.abstract: Economic change sweeping Latin America has largely bypassed Uruguay, where welfare state faces biggest test in years, union-sponsored plebiscite opposing new law to let private companies compete with Government's electric monopoly; unions seek to make Pres Julio Maria Sanguinetti, centrist who pushed law through Congress, into lame duck and propel socialist to presidency next year; map; photo (M)
news.title: The Welfare State Is Alive, if Besieged, in Uruguay

news.abstract: Pres Clinton scrambles to repeal law he signed in Feb 1996 to impose one-year moratorium on use of antipersonnel land mines starting in Feb 1999; Defense Department opposes law, warning of serious threats to American troops around world, although it has no current plans to use mines; Clinton stand angers highly organized and vocal critics of land mines; national security adviser Samuel R Berger has appealed to law's sponsor, Sen Patrick J Leahy, to push for its reversal (M)
news.title: Clinton Seeks To Overturn Land Mine Moratorium

news.abstract: Vice Pres Al Gore meets with Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu in Tel Aviv and Yasir Arafat in West Bank city of Ramallah to press for breakthrough at impeding Israeli-Palestinian peace talks; meets with Pres Hosni Mubarak and other Egyptian officials in Cairo (M)
news.title: Gore, in Mideast, Prods Sides Before Talks

news.abstract: United States aides are pessimistic that meetings in London between State Sec Madeleine K Albright and Israeli and Palestinian leaders will lead to breakthrough; suggest Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu will not accept US call for roughly 13 percent withdrawal from West Bank (M)
news.title: U.S. Pessimistic Before Middle East Talks

news.abstract: ROME—  — This weekend's unseemly battle over the presidency of the European Central Bank could rattle currency and bond markets temporarily and might even cause interest rates to rise sooner than expected in Germany and France this spring, several leading European economists said Sunday.
news.title: Central Bank Debacle May Shake Market Confidence, for Now

news.abstract: Analysis of Pres Jacques Chirac's successful drive to deny full eight-year term to Wim F Duisenberg as head of new European central bank; he has forced Duisenberg, backed by all other European Union leaders and all 15 EU central bankers, to agree to retire early; economists hold move will weaken common currency; photo (M)
news.title: Chirac, the 'Bulldozer,' at the Birth of the Euro

news.abstract: LONDON—  Another struggle, another eleventh-hour compromise, and finally, after years of arduous effort, Europe has agreed to launch the euro. So what's it worth?
news.title: How Much Is a Euro? About$1.1

news.abstract: Gojko Susak, Croatia's Defense Minister, dies at age 53 from lung cancer; photo (M)
news.title: Gojko Susak, Defense Minister of Croatia, Is Dead at 53

news.abstract: Interview with Italian Prime Min Romano Prodi, who will arrive in US for state visit on May 5, and who praises US for supporting euro, new European currency; photo (M)
news.title: Italy's Leader, Due on Visit, Praises U.S. for Backing Euro

news.abstract: Excitement over anticancer drugs angiostatin and endostatin shifts from laboratory to public after reports that tests eradicated tumors in mice with no side effects; many cancer institutes, doctors and cancer support groups report surge of phone calls from those desperate or merely curious; drug manufacturer, Entremed Inc, says it will be 12 to 18 months before first stages of trials on humans begin, and maybe several years before drugs are available on market, if at all; cancer experts say trials could be especially complicated, given that angiostatin and endostatin work unlike other treatments by attacking blood vessels that feed tumors, starving them of blood they need to grow; some warn against putting too much faith in treatment that has not been proved on anything but mice, noting that medicines that often work on mice do not help humans; comments by prominent New York City oncologist Dr Larry Norton noted; Entremed stock soars in trading on May 4, rising by $39.75 per share (M)
news.title: China's Leading University Celebrates and Ponders

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  It can come as a surprise to hear labor union spokesmen across the Continent expressing only guarded enthusiasm for the single European currency and the streamlined new Europe it is expected to bring.
news.title: They Fear Fewer Jobs, Lower Wages and Pressure for More Productivity : European Unions Warily Greet the Euro

news.abstract: Indian Defense Min George Fernandes breaches longstanding taboo by declaring publicly that China, not Pakistan, is India's main military threat; says India should move to declare itself nuclear weapons state if review of military policy by India's new Government supports his view; says India should awaken to fact that Chinese military activities and alliances have begun to encircle it (M)
news.title: India's New Defense Chief Sees Chinese Military Threat

news.abstract: French Pres Jacques Chirac, whose conservative Gaullist party has crumbled around him under weight of financing scandals, election losses and personal rivalries, privately warns supporters to stop bickering or face loss of one of last bastions, namely, Paris City Hall (M)
news.title: As Gaullist Party Crumbles, Chirac Tries to Quell Factionalism

news.abstract: UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan visits International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda during trial of Col Anatole Nsengiumva, who is charged with inciting Hutu mobs to kill Tutsi during 1994 civil war; says there has been extensive improvements in tribunal over past six months; his suspension of its top administrative officers little over year ago for mismanagement and questionable financial transactions recalled (M)
news.title: U.N. Chief Pays a Visit To Tribunal For Rwanda

news.abstract: Family members and acquaintances of Cpl Cedric Tornay, member of Vatican's Swiss Guards, say nothing in his record or behavior in Vatican suggested he would fatally shoot commanding officer, Lieut Col Alois Estermann, and wife Galdys Meza Romano, before committing suicide; as Vatican officials paint portrait of troubled young man with deep professional grudge, others who knew him are struggling to match image with their own more banal impressions of 23-year-old vice corporal (M)
news.title: They Say Life Is Hard Guarding The Pope

news.abstract: Interpol reports new miniature pistol that resembles key ring, that costs $20 and can fire two 32-caliber cartridges, is slipping undetected through some airport metal detectors and X-ray machines and is readily available in southern Europe; two have been seized at airport in Athens and others at airports in England and Australia; weapon is made of metal but is likely to pass through airport security checks because passengers typically put key rings, coins and other metal objects in tray that is passed around detector; Interpol says even if weapon is passed through detector, it is not likely to set of alarm unless machine is set to high level of sensitivity; diagram (M)
news.title: Gun That Looks Like Key Chain Fools Security X-Rays at Airports

news.abstract: Interview with former US Sen George J Mitchell, who brokered peace agreement between Catholics and Protestants in Northern Ireland and has won respect and adulation of Irish; photo (M)
news.title: Gray Eminence in U.S., Now Bright Star for Irish

news.abstract: Peace talks between Sudanese Government and southern rebels end in Nairobi, Kenya, on note of progress, as both sides agree to accept internationally supervised vote on self-determination for southern half of nation (M)
news.title: Sudanese And Rebels Call for Vote In the South

news.abstract: Chatichai Choonhavan, former Prime Minister of Thailand, dies at age 76; photo (M)
news.title: Chatichai Choonhavan, 76, Ex-Prime Minister of Thailand

news.abstract: Howard W French special report on failure of United Nations investigation to establish facts in one of most troubling mysteries of Congo's seven-month civil war: disappearance and presumed killings of tens of thousands of Hutu refugees; refugees disappeared as they were being driven clear across Africa's third-largest country by rebel army of Laurent Kabila in his successful effort to overthrow dictator Mobutu Sese Seko; UN puts toll at 180,000 people; failure of inquiry was fault of many--not just Congolese; though Kabila pledged to cooperate, Congolese used every tactic to frustrate inquiry; UN made crucial concessions to Kabila's Government that weakened inquiry; Congo's neighbors, particularly Rwanda and Uganda, that sponsored Kabila's rebellion were hostile to any investigation that might disclose details of their involvement; Western nations, led by US, were eager to cement their ties to new authorities in Kinshasa and pressed UN to give in to Congolese demands; map; photo (M)
news.title: COLD TRAIL: A special report.; Congo Not Alone in Ending Massacre Inquiry

news.abstract: Indonesian Government finds itself on increasingly perilous course after three days of riots and protests by students and workers; it has little choice but to reform economy, but with each step it risks alienating another segment of society; Indonesia must restructure its shattered banking system to fulfull commitments to International Monetary Fund; many of these institutions are owned by Pres Suharto's friends and business partners of his family (M)
news.title: Risky Task In Indonesia: Cleaning Up Banks' Mess

news.abstract: Lack of tangible progress at latest round of US-Israeli-Palestinian talks in London raised few eyebrows after so many false starts over past 16 months; what may have been more significant was that Clinton Administration was no longer self-effacing 'facilitator,' but full-fledged negotiator--sitting opposite Israel; shift was evident in defiant tone with which Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu treated US demand that Israel withdraw from 13 percent of West Bank as minimum price for reviving peace talks in Washington (M)
news.title: Mideast Turnabout

news.abstract: European govts, increasingly frustrated by rising volume of American cigarettes smuggled into Europe, decide to turn to Washington for help in investigating suspected involvement of American tobacco companies, starting with R J Reynolds Tobacco Co; it will be first time for Eureopean Union to formally request help from United States Govt in combatting illicit cigarette trade, and arises out of a conviction that American tobacco companies are in complicity (M)
news.title: Europe Turning To U.S. to Fight Illicit Cigarettes

news.abstract: Rwandan leaders give hostile reception to United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan, who visits Rwanda on what he calls 'healing mission,' and admits to Parliament that UN had done too little to stop 1994 massacres of Tutsi civilians; just before Annan's speech, Foreign Min Anastase Gasana embarrasses Annan with 10-point indictment of UN's role in country's history, culminating in killing of hundreds of thousands of people four years ago (M)
news.title: Annan Given Cold Shoulder By Officials In Rwanda

news.abstract: Domestic violence is becoming a public issue in Poland, nation where sanctity of the family is of almost mythical importance and where most homes are organized along strict patriarchal; often quoted Polish proverb says 'If a man does not beat his wife, her liver rots'; women's groups are now discussing issue of domestic violence, holding 'tribunals' where women tell their stories and seminars to sensitize police and prosecutors, who have often dismissed their complaints; a national billboard campaign alerts Poles to idea that brutality is more than just a family spat; one poster shows badly beaten woman, and says, simply, 'Because the soup was too salty'; statistics are notoriously hard to pin down in Poland, but in 1995 the courts recorded 33 percent rise in number of domestic vilence cases, suggesting that more women are reporting such incidents; photos; map (L)
news.title: Dark Underside of Polish Family Life: Violence

news.abstract: White House aides disown comments by Hillary Rodham Clinton about need for Palestinian state and insist that she was speaking only for herself; Mrs Clinton's comments come when she tells group of Arab and Israeli teen-agers that creating a state of Israel is 'very important for the broader goal of peace in the Middle East;' Clinton speaks via satellite to teenagers meeting in Villars, Switzerland, as part of program called Seeds for Peace; photo of Mrs Clinton and Pres Clinton (M)
news.title: Aides Disavow Mrs. Clinton on Mideast

news.abstract: Thousands of Canadians received tainted blood from Canadian Red Cross in 1980's, and now red cross has become symbol of disillusionment, painful reminder of how badly their faith in the compassion of Canada has become; late last year an independent commission reported that Canada's blood system has failed to protect sick Canadians who received blood in 1980's; commission concluded that Govt had not adequately supervised Red Cross; agency has been stripped of its responsibility for blood system, and compensation was offered to about 1,000 people with AIDS; but some 42,000 Canadians contracted hepatitis C, which attacks liver and can be fatal; worried about setting too wide a precedent for compensation, federal and provincial authorities jointly set up compensation fund worth about $750 million; but fund was for benefit only of those who contracted diseasee between 1986 and 1990, when screening test was used in United States, but ignored in Canada; compensation package has become huge moral and political issue; photo (L)
news.title: Tottenham Journal; The Cross They Carry Is the Red Cross's Blunder

news.abstract: Pres Clinton to send mediator Richard C Holbrooke and special representative Robert S Gelbard to Belgrade to press Pres Slobodan Milosevic to end fighting in Kosovo, where ethnic Albanian majority seeks greater autonomy from Serbia (S)
news.title: U.S. Dispatches Its Balkans Mediator With a Warning to the Serbs

news.abstract: United States, continuing to send seemingly conflicting signals to Pres Suharto, gives Indonesia $1 billion in loan guarantees but cancels joint training exercise with Indonesian military; has declined to link aid to ease economic crisis with warnings against repression of dissidents; Export-Import Bank president James Harmon says loan package is aimed at contributing to stability and easing social unrest; students burn effigy of Suharto, Jakarta; photos (M)
news.title: U.S. Backs Indonesian Loans But Cancels Military Exercise

news.abstract: South Africa's National Sports Council seeks international boycott of nation's rugby league after league president Louis Luyt refuses to resign or apologize for humiliating Pres Nelson Mandela; Luyt has angered many in nation and sport by making Mandela defend self for two days in court during Luyt's successful legal battle to halt probe by Sports Min Steve Tshwete of charges that league practices are corrupt and racist (M)
news.title: Rugby in South Africa Scrums to a New Boycott

news.abstract: Recent beating death of Bishop Juan Jose Gerardi has shaken Guatemalans' confidence that long civil war is really over and plunged Pres Alvaro Arzu's Government into crisis; human rights and civic groups hold murder, three days after Gerardi made public exhaustive Roman Catholic Church probe of human rights abuses during civil war, was intended to thwart action against abusers by frightening survivors, witnesses and Government; reject Government stand that he was likely crime victim; map; photo (M)
news.title: Bishop's Death Shakes Hopes for Guatemala Peace

news.abstract: Johannesburgh High Court overturns South Africa's sodomy laws, effectively declaring gay sex legal (S)
news.title: South African Court Ends Sodomy Laws

news.abstract: Philippines Vice Pres Joseph P Estrada, former B-movie actor, is favorite to become next President in upcoming elections; polls show Estrada beating his chief rival, House Speaker Jose de Venecia, who is backed by Pres Fidel V Ramos; map; photo (M)5
news.title: As Filipinos Vote, Movie Idol Has a Starring Role

news.abstract: Analysis of attacks by Rwandan leaders angry at United Nations for failing to intervene in 1994 genocide in Kigali, Rwanda; says UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan took political beating to protect Western nations, particuarly US, which heard early warnings of slaughter but resisted getting involved until it was too late; holds if outside world deserves blame, discord during Annan's visit highlights another ugly reality: It is convenient for Government to blame rest of the world for failing to save Rwanda from itself (M)
news.title: Ugly Reality In Rwanda

news.abstract: Israeli and American officials acknowledge that Israeli-Palestinian summit meeting offered by Pres Clinton cannot be held on May 11, but they indicate that it will still be held, perhaps in late May; Dennis Ross, American mediator in Middle East, holds separate meetings with Yasir Arafat, Chairman of Palestinian Authority, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu; Ross, after meeting with Arafat, says differences that remain are not large (M)
news.title: U.S. Envoy, Again in Israel, Sees Netanyahu and Arafat

news.abstract: Foreign and Finance Ministers of Group of Eight countries, meeting in London as part of summit meeting in Birmingham next week, impose investment ban on Serbia and freeze its assets abroad as their concern grows about violence in Kosovo; they also freeze overseas assets of Yugolsavia, which is made up of Serbia and Montenegro; because Yugoslavia's leader Slobodan Milosevic has not met conditions set by West to withdraw special police forces from Kosovo and begin negotiations, sanctions are approved by all countries except Russia and Japan (M)
news.title: West Puts Pressure on Serbs With a Ban on Investment

news.abstract: In some of world's poorest nations, villagers who are themselves often illiterate yet who understand their children need education to succeed in life are beginning to make schooling a community effort and priority for spending what small amounts of money they are able to pool; these efforts are not popular with large organizations actively involved in third-world development; Carol Bellamy, executive director of Unicef, told mothers and teachers in Afghanistan who had been hoping for more help with their home schools that providing education was responsibility of government; her view is widely shared at World Bank and in many government aid agencies (M)
news.title: Third World Fills a Void As Villagers Run Schools

news.abstract: Luis Luyt, president of South African Rugby Football Assn, reverses decision and will resign, amid call by National Sport Council's call for international boycott of South African rugby; governing body for sports had demanded that entire executive board of rugby quit, that it apologize to Pres Nelson Mandela for taking him to court earlier in year, and that it cooperate with investigation into charges of racism and corruption in rugby (S)
news.title: Rugby Chief Quits, Averting South Africa Boycott

news.abstract: Interview with Vicente Fox Quesada Fox, Governor of Guanajuato, Mex, who is campaigning for Presidency, even though election is in 2000; photo; map (M)
news.title: Valladolid Journal; Early Bird Begins Mexico's 2000 Presidential Race

news.abstract: Paraguay's governing party claims victory in Presidential elections, with only heavily contested exit polls available and electoral officials complaining of considerable fraud, creating momentum for celebrating among party faithful in advance of official tallies (M)
news.title: Ruling Party In Paraguay Says It Won; Fraud Alleged

news.abstract: Interview with Lo Hsing-han, former opium warlord of Golden Triangle of 1960's who currently has reputation as one of Myanmar's most influential businessmen; US views has prosperity as evidence that Myanmar's economy is awash in laundered drug money and that it military leaders have encouraged those who trade in drugs to invest in its development projects; photo (M)
news.title: Road to Riches Starts In the Golden Triangle

news.abstract: Outdoor funeral is held in Sarno, Italy, for 90 victims of mudslides caused by torrential rains; photo; map (M)
news.title: Italian Town Buries 90 After Mudslide

news.abstract: Mexican Govt deports 40 members of Italian delegation of human rights observers who clashed repeatedly with authorities during weeklong tour through conflict-torn Chiapas state; enacted tough Constitutional clause that allows President Ernesto Zedillo to expel foreigners deemed undesirable; photo (S)
news.title: Vexed, Mexico Deports 40 in Italian Rights Group

news.abstract: India conducts three underground nuclear tests at its Pokharan desert testing range in Rajasthan state, nearly 24 years after detonating only nuclear device; move seemingly signals determination to abandon decades of ambiguity regarding possession of nuclear weapons; Prime Min Atal Bihari Vajpayee, leader of Hindu nationalist party that has advocated embrace of nuclear weapons as step toward great-power status, makes announcement congratulating scientists and engineers; spokesman says tests will help scientists design variety of nuclear weapons for fast-developing missile program; tests are widely welcomed in India, with hardly any immediate dissent from opposition political parties and little sign of Ghandian pacifism that was strong element in policy in early years after independence; are condemned by international community; Clinton Administration expresses deep disappointment; is reviewing trade and financial sanctions under US nuclear nonproliferation laws; Britain voices dismay; Germany calls tests 'slap in the face' for 149 countries that signed nuclear nonproliferation treaty; UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan expresses 'deep regret;' Pakistan weighs nuclear test of its own, which would be its first; blames Western nations, particularly US, for failing to heed its recent warnings about nuclear ambitions of Vajpayee Govt; map; photos (M)
news.title: TESTS BRING A SHARP OUTCRY

news.abstract: Paraguay's governing Colorado Party sweeps presidential elections, defeating coalition of opposition parties to maintain its half-century-long hold on power (M)
news.title: Ruling Party in Paraguay Maintains Its Long Grip on Presidency

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, risking more signs of friction in his Mideast policy, orders Sec of State Madeleine Albright to meet with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel in Washington on May 13 to resolve latest impasse in peace talks; move, also aimed at easing US-Israeli tensions, follows failure of talks in London to seal agreement with Netanyahu on scope of further pullbacks from West Bank in return for stronger Palestinian moves against Muslim militants; photo (M)
news.title: Albright Gets New Mission: Patch Rift With Israel

news.abstract: Difficulty of creating advertising theme for Northern Ireland peace accord demonstrates delicate political and emotional undercurrents that have come to fore as Catholics and Protestants intensify campaigns for or against it before May 22 referendum; several leaders who favor pact acknowledge that persuading people to back it has been more complicated than previously imagined; Irish are being asked to approve something that arouses apprehension among all voters; very notion of political campaign to resolve decades of seething hatreds seems alien to place where differences have long been settled with violence; residents of Belfast are so suspicious of promises of peace that political parties are finding little enthusiasm for referendum; photo (M)
news.title: Irish Accord Proves To Be Trickier Sale Than First Imagined

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  President Bill Clinton vowed Tuesday to apply U.S. laws imposing strong sanctions against India after its underground nuclear tests, and he implored other countries in the region not to follow India "down the path of a dangerous arms race."
news.title: Spy Agencies Under Attack for Providing No Warning : Clinton Vows to Punish India

news.abstract: Text of letter from Prime Min Atal Bihari Vajpayee to Pres Clinton explaining rationale for India's nuclear tests (S)
news.title: Indian's Letter to Clinton On the Nuclear Testing

news.abstract: China condemns India's underground nuclear tests with notable brevity and restraint (S)
news.title: China Is 'Seriously Concerned' But Restrained in Its Criticism

news.abstract: Britain proposes $520 million aid package for Northern Ireland as part of effort to win voter approval of peace accord (S)
news.title: Britain to Spend $520 Million to Pep Up Ulster

news.abstract: Min Ariel Sharon, who is considered key to Israeli Government approval of any peace deal, says he will not join Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu in his meeting with State Sec Madeleine K Albright; protests Netanyahu's unauthorized 'promises'; stand will stiffen Netanyahu's resistance to United States pressure for further withdrawal from West Bank (M)
news.title: Sharon Won't Join Netanyahu in Meeting Albright

news.abstract: Pakistani leaders demand United States and other world powers act decisively to isolate India after its five nuclear tests; strongly hint that strength of international response will shape their decision on whether to detonate own nuclear bombs; Min Gohar Ayub Khan holds invoking of mandatory sanctions under US law is not effective response (M)
news.title: Next-Door Neighbor Demands That World Powers Shun India

news.abstract: India, ignoring appeal from Pres Clinton, carries out two more underground nuclear tests; Government of Prime Min Atal Bihari Vajpayee approved tests in face of threatened economic sanctions; Clinton announces wide-ranging sanctions, including end to most United States aid and threat to use US vote to deny India International Monetary Fund and World Bank loans, news conference, Berlin; Japan and number of other nations halt, cut or defer aid; map; photo (L)
news.title: INDIA CARRIES OUT 2 MORE ATOM TESTS DESPITE SANCTIONS

news.abstract: Flooding in Argentina caused by El Nino has forced 100,000 people from their homes and caused more than $1.5 billion in damage since it began in Apr; Pres Carlos Saul Menem has seized opportunity to spur flagging popularity, traveling to many stricken areas to buoy his image as take-charge leader; his backers seek Constitutional change to allow him to run for third term; photo (M)
news.title: Floods Giving Argentine President a Political Lift

news.abstract: Min Yevgeny M Primakov reaffirms Russia's refusal to join other countries in economic sanctions to punish India for resuming nuclear tests; Russia'a complaints against testing have been muted, reflecting its close commercial ties with India and view of India as counterweight to China (M)
news.title: Kremlin Soft-Pedals Its Rebuke to India, and Opposes Sanctions

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, visiting Germany, sharpens his criticism of Indian Government, calling five underground nuclear tests 'terrible mistake;' imposes raft of economic sanctions; House Speaker Newt Gingrich scores Clinton for punishing India while overlooking China's sale of missile technology to Pakistan and Iran; Sen Jesse Helms holds India constitutes emerging nuclear threat to United States; other members of Congress generally score India, back Clinton's move and deplore US failure to anticipate tests; Chancellor Helmut Kohl does not immediately set sanctions, but says Germany will clearly oppose tests; photo (M)
news.title: Clinton Calls Tests a 'Terrible Mistake' And Announces Sanctions Against India

news.abstract: Key to Indonesia's future lies increasingly in hands of its powerful military, as nation suffers its worst crisis in 30 years, its capital seething with rage and Pres Suharto struggling to keep control; the one institution with an efficient nationwide orgn, and one institution that enjoys broad support among most Indonesians, may ultimately decide whether it is time for Suharto to heed widespread calls to step aside afer 32 years in power; Suharto has worked hard to insure loyalty of military, appointing his supporters to all top positions (News analysis) (M)
news.title: Role of Military: A Potential Unifier Split by Conflicting Goals

news.abstract: House overwhelmingly approves bill to punish foreign countries that persecute people for their religious beliefs; lopsided vote, 375 to 41, masks many lawmakers' ambivalence toward a popular bill that aims to champion religious liberties worldwide, but which critics say will imperil religious minorities, create hierarchy of human rights violations, and hurt United States foreign policy; under bill, countries that permit or endorse pattern of violent attacks or other persecution of religious believers would automatically face cutoff of United States aid, other than food and medical supplies, restrictions on exports and American opposition to loans by international financial institutions, including International Monetary Fund; among countries criticized in debate are China, Pakistan, Indonesia and Sudan; bill is unlikely to be adopted by Senate, which is expected to pass a measure giving President more flexibility in dealing with nations accused of religious persecution (M)
news.title: House Votes to Bar Religious Abuses Abroad

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu gets warm, bipartisan reception on his visit to Washington, in hallways and lunchrooms of Congress; through day of courtesy calls, fresh fruit and speechmaking, Netanyahu is welcomed with kind of full-throated, bipartisan heartiness that he rarely receives at home (M)
news.title: Tension? What Tension? Not on a Smiley Day for Netanyahu.

news.abstract: Sen Jesse Helms, chairman of Senate Foreign Relations Committee, proposes $100 million aid package for Cuba that he contends will improve lives of Cubans while weakening hold of Fidel Castro; proposal, which is endorsed by more than 20 others Senators from both parties, would channel food and medical assistance to Cuban people through Roman Catholic Church and politically independent relief organizations (S)
news.title: Helms Plans $100 Million Aid Package for Cuba

news.abstract: State Sec Madeleine K Albright and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel end second round of talks in Washington without achieving breakthrough on reviving stalled Middle East peace negotiations; but senior American and Israeli officials say that lower-level aides from each side will continue working on issues on Friday and over weekend (M)
news.title: U.S. Talks With Israel On Mideast Move Slowly

news.abstract: Burning season in Mexico is lasting far longer than usual amid drought, with nearly 10,000 forest and brush fires having claimed scores of lives, forced airport closings and left at least 50 million Mexicans choking in smoke that covers thousands of square miles; Mexico City declares environmental alert because of smoke, urging residents to stay inside; fires are also burning out of control in Guatemala and Honduras; Mexico says it will accept fire-fighting aid offered by United States; map; photos (M)
news.title: Huitzilac Journal; A Long Fire Season Torments Mexico

news.abstract: Indonesian Pres Suharto, responding to rioting, returns hurriedly from Cairo and rolls back new fuel-price rises imposed at International Monetary Fund insistence; confers with advisers and top generals as calls for his ouster grow on streets and from public figures; tanks guard suddenly quiet streets of Jakarta and Presidential Palace; young looters still roam streets; more rioting is reported in Jogjakarta, Solo and Ugung Pandang; Lt Gen Prabowo, Suharto's son-in-law, says there are no splits in military; ethnic Chinese citizens, whose homes and stores have come under attack, take refuge in hotels or gather at airports seeking to flee nation; foreigners also throng to airports after American Embassy advises United States citizens to leave; embassy plans charter flights to evacuate Americans; other nations also prepare to evacuate citizens; Pres Clinton says Indonesians must decide own political future; calls for reform; map; photo (M)
news.title: SUHARTO REVERSES HIKE IN FUEL PRICE DEMANDED BY I.M.F.

news.abstract: Indonesia's central bank again stops acting as middleman in foreign-currency transactions, further weakening confidence in battered economy; outlook for Indonesian currency, rupiah, becomes murkier (M)
news.title: Central Bank In Indonesia On Sidelines; Worry Grows

news.abstract: Prime Min Atal Bihari Vajpayee indicates that India will not hesitate to deploy nuclear arms, magazine interview; Pres Clinton, at Birmingham, Eng, economic summit meeting, wins accord on firm statement criticizing India, but fails to mobilize other nations to take punitive action; photos (M)
news.title: New Delhi Premier Indicates Resolve to Produce Nuclear Weapons

news.abstract: Violence against Indonesia's ethnic Chinese residents, who make up about 5 percent of population but own 75 percent of nation's wealth, has been ugly sideshow in every Indonesian political upheaval since colonial days; Jakarta's Chinese are fleeing or cowering in shops in wake of looting and arson by angry mobs; fear trip to airport after attacks by mobs searching cars for Chinese passengers (M)
news.title: The Target Of Violence In a Time Of Wrath

news.abstract: Brazilian Congress rejects constitutional amendment to raise minimum age for retirement, dealing significant defeat to Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso's plans for social security reforms; amendment would have required men to work until they turned 60 and to be employed for 35 years to qualify for benefits, and women to be 55 and to work for at least 30 years; labor unions and opposition parties complained that changes would have penalized unskilled laborers, who tend to enter work force at earlier ages and would be required to work more years until age 60 (M)
news.title: Brazil Congress Rejects President's Plan for Pension Changes

news.abstract: Whether Pakistan should test nuclear weapons in response to recent underground tests by India has caused intense debate among Pakistanis; many residents of Rawalpindi are ambivalent and, like their leaders, seem deeply torn by issue that could decide country's future; national pride and deep-seated fear of Indian aggression have led many to demand quick response in form of tests, but concern over devastating economic sanctions that would follow--together with recognition of country's desperate domestic needs--have led others to argue for caution; map; photo (M)
news.title: On the Street, Pride and Worry Over Tests

news.abstract: Leaders of eight major industrial countries attending economic summit in Birmingham, England, agree to cooperate more in battling international crime; pledge to do more to help world's poorest countries; focus on issues of common interest, including how to create more jobs and stop global warming; thousands of protestors surround site of meeting in central Birmingham, demanding more action by rich nations to relieve poorest countries of their debts; photo (M)
news.title: Rich Leaders Turn Eye to Crime and Debt

news.abstract: Loss of Parliamentary seats by National Party in three recent local elections is seen as first sign of possible big swing away from party that ruled South Africa from 1947 to 1994; loss is first tangible evidence that support for builder of apartheid is being lost to Democratic Party--heir to white liberal anti-apartheid parties of 1970's and 1980's (M)
news.title: Apartheid's Architects Losing White Votes in South Africa

news.abstract: Underground nuclear tests by India shifts focus of economic summit of eight leading industrial nations in Birmingham, England; Pres Clinton steps up criticisms of India in hopes of dissuading Pakistan from following suit; has so far had little success in persuading allies to follow US lead by imposing economic sanctions on India (M)
news.title: Summit Talks Shift Focus To Atom Tests By New Delhi

news.abstract: Foreign Min Gohar Ayub Khan says Pakistan has decided to begin testing nuclear weapons in response to recent tests by India, but other Government officials are less clear on whether decision has been made (M)
news.title: Pakistan Seems Mixed On Holding Nuclear Test

news.abstract: Fresh details surrounding Kristallnacht, outburst of anti-Semitic violence in Germany that presaged Holocaust, have been extracted from Government archives in Moscow that have been storing Nazi documents seized by Soviet troops in 1945; newly unearthed documents suggest German insurance companies not only connived with Nazis to avoid paying Jewish policyholders for damages to synagogues and thousands of Jewish shops and homes, but sometimes also exceeded Government guidelines and canceled all policies on which Jews had been paying premiums for years (M)
news.title: Insurers Swindled Jews, Nazi Files Show

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, on final day of Birmingham, Eng, meeting of leaders of world's eight leading industrial nations, urges Russian Pres Boris Yeltsin to press for ratification of pending nuclear weapons treaty even as US and allies search for way to head off nuclear arms race between India and Pakistan; fails to win broad support for economic sanctions against India; says India is swimming against currents of history (M)
news.title: Clinton Seeks to Limit Effects of India's Test by Pressing Yeltsin on Arms Pact

news.abstract: Annual summit of world's seven major industrial democracies and Russia become formally known as Group of Eight as full recognition is finally given to Russia (S)
news.title: The Group of Seven Now Eight, Officially

news.abstract: Rioting and looting in Indonesia, often described as spasm of anti-Government violence, has more complex motivations that will not be easily remedied, even if Indonesia becomes completely democratic; underscore emergence of volatile underclass in cities like Jakarta, including people who came to city during country's economic boom but now find themselves unemployed; many are embittered that they must struggle to survive while wealthy continue living good life; see their thievery as kind of Robin Hood-style self-help program, and say they are ready to loot again in absence of change; rioting has caused more then 500 deaths and damage to more than 4,900 buildings (M)
