news.abstract: Article in series Dead Zones describes plight of Zambian children orphaned by AIDS and often cast out by relatives to fend for themselves; in 1997 alone, AIDS orphaned 1.7 million children, more than 90 percent of them in sub-Saharan Africa; photos; demographic map; UN says that Zambia, which has never embraced birth control, has highest proportion of orphans in world, estimated 23 percet of all children under 15; Lukasa has more than 90,000 children on streets, and even those with relatives are often the last to get food, shoes and schooling, and suffer beatings and sexual abuse; harsh lives of several abandoned children described (L)
news.title: In Zambia, the Abandoned Generation

news.abstract: Swiss and French tests for poison gas on Iraqi missile warheads appear to have reached results contrary to those from American tests that showed presence of VX, deadly nerve agent; Iraq has admitted loading Sarin on weapons, but not VX, and may argue that US tests were rigged (S)
news.title: New Tests Dispute U.S. Finding of Iraq Nerve Gas

global_music.title: I Don't Want to Miss a Thing

news.abstract: Russia's central bank, seeking to restart stalled financial activity, will let insolvent banks use about $1.65 billion in ruble reserves; is gambling that errant banks will use reserves to settle delinquent bills, not buy dollars, move that would further drive down value of ruble; plans to print more rubles to replenish reserve; photo (M)
news.title: Russia to Pump Huge Ruble Reserve Into Banks

news.abstract: Israelis preparing for Jewish New Year crowd Jerusalem market that was target of many past terrorist bombings, ignoring threat of reprisals for Israeli Army slaying of two Islamic militants; skepticism about outlook for peace softens somewhat on reports that State Sec Madeleine K Albright has promised to meet in United States with Israeli and Palestinian leaders (M)
news.title: No Holiday From Fear, Or Hope, In Israel

news.abstract: Murder by gang from untouchable subcaste that has gained from 'reservations' of jobs, schooling and political offices for untouchables of member of lower subcaste, Meerut, India, calls attention to ways in which efforts to erase lines of prejudice have made caste more important than ever in India; tensions between subcastes over division of benefits exploded over unsanctioned romance between boy from lower subcaste and girl from more powerful group; map; photos (M)
news.title: Caste Hate, and Murder, Outlast Indian Reforms

news.abstract: Clinton Administration officials are dismayed by projections that Nikola Poplasen, extreme nationalist, has defeated American-backed incumbent, Biljana Plavsic, in presidential election in Serbian-populated half of Bosnia; his victory could undo American efforts to reintegrate Bosnian Serbs, Croats and Muslims into single nation (M)
news.title: U.S. Dismayed at Apparent Victory of Hard-Line Bosnian Serb

news.abstract: Officials say Pres Clinton is likely to delay trip to India and Pakistan, planned for mid-Nov, because both nations tested nuclear devices in May and have shown little interest in defusing their arms race (M)
news.title: Clinton Likely To Delay Trip To Pakistan And India

global_music.title: I Don't Want to Miss a Thing

news.abstract: Pakistani Prime Min Nawaz Sharif leaves for visit to United States after facing Parliamentary opposition to his proposal to make Islamic justice supreme law of the land (M)
news.title: After Dispute In Pakistan, Leader Leaves For U.S. Visit

news.abstract: Russian Pres Boris N Yeltsin's clout seems to be ebbing and new Prime Min Yevgeny M Primakov is clearly calling the shots; Yeltsin has become less visible presence, but makes rare appearance in public to attend gala concert at Moscow's Conservatory; he leaves before intermission; photo (M)
news.title: A Humbled Yeltsin Is Fading Away

news.abstract: Until recently, it seemed that Augusta Aparecida Pettinari's fortunes and the country's economic reform plan ran on parallel tracks, like twin locomotives taking the young receptionist and the modern currency toward a steadily more promising future.    As once-rampant inflation was brought down to negligible levels, Ms. Pettinari joined an emerging class of consumers, whose salaries for the first time maintained their purchasing power from one paycheck to the next. She smiles now as she remembers buying appliances, of going to the movies and of writing a check for a new dress.
news.title: Brazilians Fret as Economic Threat Moves Closer

news.abstract: Special report on Mobil oil spill off Nigerian coast in January, which has become subject of vehement dispute and catalyst for pent-up claims fed by poverty and state neglect; as Nigeria approaches delicate transition from military rule to democracy, delta region's long-festering problems pose threat of widespread violence; sabotage against pipelines is becoming routine, and poverty-stricken villagers are making huge financial demands on Mobil; since oil was discovered in delta region 42 years ago, enormous wealth has been taken by Western companies and by country's military rulers; now Mobil is facing billions of dollars in claims from population that feels it has been long ignored and Government of Gen Abdulsalam Abubakar is making conciliatory gestures but initiating little real reform; maps; photos (M)
news.title: OIL RICH, OIL POOR: A special report.; High Claims in Spill Betray Depth of Nigerian Poverty

news.abstract: Switzerland, which because of its location is subject to much of Europe's north-south traffic, is trying to create plan that would balance transport needs of European Union with protecting its scenic valleys from noise and air pollution created by truck traffic (M)
news.title: Swiss Hills Are Alive With Sound of Diesels

global_music.title: I Don't Want to Miss a Thing

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, during September 21 visit to UN, will face organization likely to strip US of General Assembly vote by end of 1998 for nonpayment of dues totaling more than $1.5 billion; organization's largest contributor is currently Japan, which kept dues payments up to date despite recession; organization has been kept afloat by delaying payment for peacekeeping forces to Japanese, Europeans and some developing countries and applying funds to operating budget; Pres Clinton is viewed by many UN diplomats and officials as too weak or unwilling to battle hostile Congress to preserve pivotal American role; US remains without chief representative to organization since departure of Bill Richardson and blocking of appointment of Richard C Holbrooke as successor by Republicans (M)
news.title: Darkest Hour at U.N. For Richest Deadbeat

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  As official Indonesian investigators prepare to question former President Suharto for the first time this week about his wealth, experts are cautioning that any criminal wrongdoing will be hard to prove and that the tracing and recovery of money and assets will be equally difficult, especially if they are outside Indonesia.
news.title: As Investigation Begins, Indonesian Laws Favor Ex-President : Suharto's Wealth May All Be Legal

news.abstract: Sweden's governing Social Democrats ride pledge to expand country's huge welfare programs to thin victory in national election, signaling shift to left; received 36.5 percent of vote, and conservative Moderates 22.7 percent; though result represents significant drop in support for Social Democrats, who received slightly more than 45 percent of vote in 1994, it appears sufficient to allow them to form alliance with parties farther left; would keep Prime Min Goran Persson in power and frustrate bid by Carl Bildt, Moderate leader, to regain office he occupied from 1991 to 1994 (M)
news.title: Swedish Party Pledging Expanded Welfare Gains Slim Victory

news.abstract: KUALA LUMPUR—  Malaysian policemen wearing black ski masks and carrying submachine guns smashed their way into the house of Anwar Ibrahim, the country's former deputy prime minister, late Sunday night and arrested him, just hours after he had led the largest political demonstration in this city's history.
news.title: Demonstration Was Largest in the Capital's History : Malaysia Police Seize Anwar After Anti-Mahathir Protest

news.abstract: Japanese officials express irritation at what they perceive as American arrogance and scapegoating of Japan, accusing US of rejecting Japan's overtures to grapple with Asian economic crisis in early stages; bridle at suggestion that they are part of problem rather than solution, and that Japan is culprit in Asian crisis; article notes Japan proposed setting up $100 billion fund to help Southeast Asian countries pull through when crisis was in infancy year ago, but was swiftly rebuffed by US; notes Japan was first major country to pay attention to crisis unfolding in Thailand in summer 1997, and tried without success to get world leaders attending Denver summit to discuss economic instability in Asia; simmering resentments in Tokyo may grow with September 22 summit between Prime Min Keizo Obuchi and Pres Clinton in New York, since one of its purposes is to give Clinton chance to impress on Obuchi importance of rapid action to revive Japan's economy (M)
news.title: Japan Sees Itself as a Scapegoat Of Washington in the Asia Crisis

global_music.title: I Don't Want to Miss a Thing

news.abstract: Pres Mohammad Khatami of Iran addresses opening session of United Nations General Assembly for first time, portraying Iran as freedom-loving and law-abiding country; asks for help in resolving crisis in neighboring Afghanistan; refrains from criticizing US; his criticisms of Israel are milder than usual; photo (M)
news.title: Iranian President Paints a Picture of Peace and Moderation

news.abstract: Russia's leaders offer more assurances that country's fiscal crisis can be tamed without provoking high inflation or social unrest, but with key positions in new Government unfilled, few people accord promise much weight; neither Pres Boris Yeltsin nor Prime Min Yevgeny Primakov has settled on choice for Finance Minister, perhaps most important post next to Primakov's (M)
news.title: Russians Vow To End Crisis, But Key Posts Go Unfilled

news.abstract: Tanzania charges two men with 11 counts of murder in connection with bombing of US Embassy in Dar es Salaam on August 7; they are Mustafa Mahmoud Said Ahmed, Egyptian national, and Rashid Saleh Hemed, Tanzanian; action contrasts with decision by Kenya to extradite two suspects to US; sets up potential diplomatic conflict with US and might hamper investigation (M)
news.title: Tanzania Charges Two in Bombing of American Embassy

news.abstract: Malaysian riot police officers, acting to quell biggest show of dissent faced by Prime Min Mahathir Mohamad in his 17 years in office, fire tear gas and water cannons to disperse thousands of people protesting arrest of former Deputy Prime Minister, Anwar Ibrahim; former deputy is being held under Internal Security Act, which allows indefinite imprisonment without charges or trial of people deemed threat to national security; photo (M)
news.title: Malaysian Police Break Up Protests on Arrest

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair of Britain addresses opening session of UN General Assembly, where he urges revamping of way world's financial institutions deal with global economic turmoil and says procedures of World Bank and International Monetary Fund must be updated (M)
news.title: Remodel World Bank And I.M.F., Blair Urges

global_music.title: I Don't Want to Miss a Thing

news.abstract: Irish Prime Min Bertie Ahern and David Trimble, First Minister of new Northern Ireland Assembly, call on Irish Republican Army to agree to begin phased disarmament; Trimble earlier discussed problem with Sinn Fein president Gerry Adams (S)
news.title: Two Political Leaders Ask I.R.A. to Disarm

news.abstract: Germany's baby boomers have come of age, new elite drawn largely from former West Germany; have grappled with nation's history, understand its shame and see future with self-confidence their parents lack; will define agenda in business, style, arts and, increasingly, in politics as dominant Germany faces new era; photos (M)
news.title: 'New' Germans Find Escape From Tainted Past

news.abstract: Amb Christopher R Hill, Pres Clinton's special envoy for Kosovo, tours valley filled with about 20,000 ethnic Albanian refugees to refute Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic's stand that there is no human crisis in province; says refugees, fearing hostile Serbian forces posted in their villages, have been sleeping in fields, many without shelter; map; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Aide Drives to Valley of Kosovo Refugees

news.abstract: Many foreign diplomats are now saying results of election in Bosnia are not disaster for Western strategy they first thought; others say problem is bad, but may be handled; less hard-line politicians across nation are doing well, despite victory of nationalist Nikola Poplasen in race for Bosnian Serb presidency (M)
news.title: Moderate Serbs in Bosnia Remain a Political Force

news.abstract: Pres Boris N Yeltsin gives shape to Russia's new Cabinet with decree that creates inner cabinet, or presidium, made up of Prime Min Yevgeny M Primakov and his six top deputies; decree also offers greater voice to regional leaders; elevates to Cabinet status Central Bank's new head, Viktor Gerashchenko, and Academy of Sciences head Yuri Osipov; Primakov, having trouble assembling Government, names Valentina Matviyenko Deputy Prime Minister for social issues, post rejected by at least three leading politicians; she will be first woman in top Government post; photo (M)
news.title: Yeltsin Creates Inner Cabinet Of Primakov and 6 Deputies

global_music.title: I Don't Want to Miss a Thing

news.abstract: Philippine Airlines, the oldest carrier in Asia, went out of business at midnight Wednesday after 11th-hour talks mediated by the government failed to resolve differences between the Philippines' richest man and its toughest labor union.
news.title: Owner and Union Can't Agree on Saving Carrier : 'Everything Is Over,' as Philippine Airlines Shuts Down

news.abstract: German election remains too close to call, with polls suggesting weariness with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's long rule is partly offset with doubts about challenger Gerhard Schroder; Schroder, centrist, shifts oratory to left; photo (M)
news.title: A Centrist Shifts to Left To Attract German Votes

news.abstract: Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic, scoffing at warnings that West might use force to end fighting in Kosovo, presses ahead with tank and artillery offensive; chases some 10,000 ethnic Albanian civilians into hills and sets fire to many of their homes; new refugees spend night in cold and damp with no shelter and little food; map; photo (M)
news.title: Defying Warnings, Serbs Press Attacks on Kosovo Albanians

news.abstract: Former East German Communists could win enough votes in German national elections to play important swing role and have good chance of becoming minority partner in governing coalition in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania; could make it hard for Gerhard Schroder to form majority governing coalition by stealing votes from his left-of-center Social Democrats; Schroder has ruled out coalition with ex-Communists, move that would be political suicide in western Germany; map (M)
news.title: Swing Vote in East Worries Germans

news.abstract: Padre Pio, Capuchin monk and mystic who died in 1968, attracts over six million pilgrims a year to remote mountaintop monastery in southern Italy and his hometown, San Giovanni Rotondo; Pio, not yet recognized as saint by Vatican, has vast, worldwide following that blends medieval piety with kind of modern cult celebrity and commercialism; some 70,000 people gather in San Giovanni for vigil on anniversary of his death; map; photos (M)
news.title: San Giovanni Rotondo Journal; Saint or No, an Old-Time Monk Mesmerizes Italy

global_music.title: I Don't Want to Miss a Thing

news.abstract: Iran drops death threat imposed on British author Salman Rushdie in 1989 by Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, and Britain responds by restoring full diplomatic relations; Foreign Min Kamal Kharrazi asserts that Govt 'has no intention, nor is it going to take any action whatsoever, to threaten the life of the author of The Satanic Verses or anybody associated with his work, not will it encourage or assist anybody to do so'; although an Iranian foundation continues to offer $2.5 million bounty for death of 51-year-old Indian-born British author, whose novel Kharrazi says still offends Iranians, Kharrazi says his Govt dissociates itself from any reward that has been offered; Rushdie, interviewed in London, says 'It's over' and 'The fatwa will be left to wither on the vine' (M)
news.title: Iran Drops Rushdie Death Threat, And Britain Renews Teheran Ties

news.abstract: Russian Govt, as it lays out ways to spend its way out of roiling economic crisis, takes harsh line with international creditors, warning them of potential default on its long-term debt if more Western aid is not delivered (M)
news.title: Russia Warns It Might Default if Western Aid Is Withheld

news.abstract: Scene in Peggy's Cove, Nova Scotia, described; residents of Peggy's Cove and other villages along coast will always remember those anxious, terrifying and deeply saddening first days after crash of Swissair Flight 111 on Sept 2; but hordes of reporters and satellite trucks are gone, tourist buses have come back, fishermen have gone back to their boats; everyone wants to know whether Peggy's Cove will ever be the same again; photo of tourists looking out at crash site; map (M)
news.title: Peggy's Cove Journal; On Nova Scotia's Shore, Will Sadness Be Forever?

news.abstract: Senior official of IMF warns that he will neither submit to 'blackmail' of Russian leaders who threaten national default if they are denied billions of dollars in aid, nor let Congress 'impose conditions' on fund in return for $18 billion in new contributions from United States (M)
news.title: I.M.F. Resists 'Blackmail' by Russia and U.S.

news.abstract: BRATISLAVA, Slovakia—  As Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar of Slovakia cut the ribbon on a short stretch of highway near here last week, the German supermodel Claudia Schiffer flashed her million-dollar smile and said Slovakia was a beautiful country.
news.title: Meciar Turns Out the Stars to Get Votes

global_music.title: I Don't Want to Miss a Thing

news.abstract: Article on drug violence in Santa Catarina and neighboring towns in Baja California, Mexico, notes that 18 members of two Mexican Indian families were recently killed in drug-related massacre in El Sauzal; map; photo (M)
news.title: Santa Catarina Journal; Drug Gangs' Deadly Toll: Indian Villagers in Baja

news.abstract: British Airways says it will not permit writer Salman Rushdie to fly on its planes, despite Iran's assurances that it will not carry out its death sentence against him (S)
news.title: Author Banned By British Air

news.abstract: DRESDEN—  Throughout their campaigns, Helmut Kohl and Gerhard Schroeder kept clear of the issue of emerging right-wing extremism with an agility they usually reserved for avoiding specifics on how they would create new jobs, save money and sustain Germany's enormous social welfare system all at the same time.
news.title: A Campaign Secret:The Emergence of Right-Wing Extremism

news.abstract: Gerhard Schroder, with promise to restore 'social justice to Germany,' winds up his campaign to replace German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in elections on Sept 27; despite erosion of his lead, Schroder appears to have better chance of success than any of his four predecessors as Social Democratic candidates who tried to defeat Kohl over last 16 years (M)
news.title: Vague, Yes, But Schroder Could Unseat Chancellor

news.abstract: Pres Boris N Yeltsin names Mikhail Zadornov as Finance Minister; he held same job under last Prime Minister, Sergi Kiriyenko; Deputy Prime Min Aleksandr Shokhin resigns in response to appointment after mere nine days on job; Dmitri Yasilyev, head of Russian securities regulation commission, also resigns; Shokhin photo (M)
news.title: Yeltsin Plugs a Hole in His Kremlin Team, but Then Two New Ones Appear

news.abstract: Analysis of the missteps by South Africa that caused its military intervention in Lesotho to go terribly wrong; intervention was intended to quell Lesotho's internal political struggles but has instead created large-scale economic and diplomatic problems that are going to cost South Africa millions and take years to repair; photo; map (M)
news.title: How Did Pretoria Err? Lesotho Counts the Ways

news.abstract: Wahid el Hage, the man accused of being a leader of Osama bin Landen's terrorist organization in Kenya, and Haroun Fazil, who is accused of being one of his top aides, have been leading lives of middle-class family men, not young, unemployed firebrands usually associated with terrorism; el Hage is linked indirectly to mysterious 1991 murder of Mustapha Shalabi in Brooklyn; Shalabi had been Sheik Abdel-Rahman's sponsor when he entered US, but they fell out when Sheik demanded that part of the money they were raising for Islamic rebels fighting Russians in Afghanistan be diverted to effort to overthrow Pres Hosni Mubarak of Egypt (M)
news.title: Public Face of Terror Suspect: Low-Key Family Man

news.abstract: Colonial leaders of Macao contend that China's announcement that it will deploy troops in Macao after it takes possession of colony on Dec 20, 1999, represents a new interpretation of 1987 joint declaration that set terms for handover; fear troops will be used more for law enforcement than defense; most residents of Macao, however, are exhausted by colony's gang wars and might actually welcome troops (M)
news.title: Macao Astir Over Troops In Handover To Beijing

news.abstract: Human rights officials chronicle what they say is arbitrary arrests and torture of ethnic Albanian civilians by Serb authorities seeking to discourage popular support of a separatist guerrilla force fighting for independence in Kosovo province; say extrajudicial methods used by officials under control of Yugoslav President, Slobodan Milosevic, run parallel to military intimidation by special police force and Yugoslav Army; photos; map (M)
news.title: In Kosovo Death Chronicles, Serb Tactic Revealed

news.abstract: Pino Alarcchi, executive director of United Nations Drug Control Program, reports that bad weather and tensions with Iran have slashed opium production in Afghanistan and hampered its opium exports for European heroin makets; adds, however, that poppy cultivation is up and has spread to two eastern provinces where it had not been report earlier; says Taliban's religious leaders want to cooperate with UN but movement is too fragmented to act (M)
news.title: Afghanistan's Opium Output Drops Sharply, U.N. Survey Shows

news.abstract: European leaders congratulate both Gerhard Schroeder and Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who Schroeder defeated in German national elections; there is widespread sense that move by German voters to left after generation is historic turning point that is not so much about ideology as about German self-confidence and assertiveness (M)
news.title: Europeans Congratulate Both Winner And Loser

news.abstract: Clinton Administration and International Monetary Fund are arranging package of more than $30 billion in loans for Brazil to limit damage to Latin America's biggest economy from Asian financial crisis, even though bailout plan is calculated risk that could sink country into deep recession; package is aimed at preserving value of Brazilian currency and reversing withdrawals by increasingly nervous foreign lenders; Brazil has become front line in struggle to halt spreading financial crisis, because of its power to pull down markets and plunge countries into recession; stakes for US are considerable since its economy dominates Latin America, which accounts for 20 percent of America's exports, and is home to thousands of American-owned factories; looming opposition to financing plan, both in Republican-controlled Congress and among private lenders, discussed (M)
news.title: Calculated Risk: U.S. and I.M.F. Lead Push for Brazil Bailout Plan

news.abstract: Gerhard Schroeder defeats incumbent Helmut Kohl to become Chancellor, ending era in Germany and opening new one in Europe, where center-left governments currently dominate continent's politics; decisive victory after hard-fought campaign is seen as clear expression of weariness of Germans with Kohl's 16-year rule; reflects new priorities that confront continent grappling with competitive pressures of global economy, overburdened welfare systems and high unemployment; Schroeder's Social Democrats gained estimated 40.9 percent of vote, up from 34.6 percent in 1994, and Christian Democrats 35.1 percent, or six-percent decline; Schroeder, whose campaign stressed joblessness and state of economy, faces central issue of how to adjust Germany's expensive welfare system to global competition without dismantling it and at same time create jobs; photo; chart (M)
news.title: GERMAN VOTERS END AN ERA, REJECT KOHL AFTER 16 YEARS AND PICK A SOCIAL DEMOCRAT

news.abstract: US Sec of State Madeleine K Albright meets jointly with Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat in New York to push for agreement on key details of long-stalled peace agreement between Israel and Palestinians; photo (M)
news.title: Albright Meets With Netanyahu And Arafat for Joint Talks

news.abstract: Japan Leasing Corp, Japan's second-largest leasing company and affiliate of troubled Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd, files for bankruptcy, becoming country's biggest postwar bankruptcy (M)
news.title: A Top Lender in Japan Files for Bankruptcy

news.abstract: Germany's Chancellor-elect Gerhard Schroeder will seek to form coalition Government with environmentalist Green Party, opening way for first 'Red-Green' Government in 49-year history of postwar republic; final election results show Schroeder's Social Democrats and Greens sweeping to comfortable 21-seat majority in 656-member Parliament as weariness with Helmut Kohl's 16-year rule and anger over high unemployment prompted decisive vore for change; photo (M)
news.title: New German Leader to Seek Coalition With the Greens

news.abstract: Iran's Foreign Min, Kamal Kharrazi, in speech before Asia Society in New York City, rebuffs overture by US to re-establish relations between both countries; accuses Clinton Administration of clinging to outdated policy of hostility toward Iran; notes new tone toward Iran by Pres Clinton and Sec of State Madeleine K Albright, but says language alone cannot provide basis for invitation to political dialogue (M)
news.title: A Top Iranian Aide Rejects U.S. Overture on New Ties

news.abstract: Man in the News biographical profile of Germany's Chancellor-elect Gerhard Schroeder, whose biggest challenge will be to define who he really is; begun political career as Marxist in late 1960's, but evolved into immaculately tailored politician who uses television to project success as much as social justice; prides himself on having modernized left-of-center Social Democratic Party; was born in Lower Saxony in 1944; grew up poor; never knew father who died fighting for Germany in Romania; worked as hardware salesman before finishing secondary school at 22; put himself through law school at Gottingen University with support from Government; earned law degree in 1976, when he was 32; photo (M)
news.title: The Right-Leftist on Top: Gerhard Schroder

news.abstract: News analysis says victory by Social Democrat Gerhard Schroeder in German national elections to become Chancellor-elect ushers in new phase in German political life; victory represents eastward shift away from conservative Rhineland culture of Chancellor Helmut Kohl and first postwar Chancellor, Konrad Adenauer, toward as yet untried forms of government (M)
news.title: Germany's Shift East

news.abstract: Rabbi Yitzhak Kadouri is playing bizarrely important role in Israel's political life; Iraqi-born mystic who is over 100 years old, has been used at festive political rallies to win votes for Shas, religious party that represents Sephardic Jews and has grown to be third largest political entity in Israel; wears fixed smile and dreamy gaze, which some take to be faith and others to be senility, and has recently been caught in unholy war of words among Israel's leaders over boundaries between religion and politics, rationalism and mysticism; many leaders have questioned Kadouri's lucidity and have complained about his exploitation; photo (M)
news.title: Jerusalem Journal; Aged Rabbi at Center of an Unholy War of Words

news.abstract: Taliban diplomat Abdul Hakeem Mujahid says United Nations is using seat of Afghanistan as tool of pressure on Islamic emirate to change its policies and to impose on it kind of coalition government what will be consequently secular government; says defeat of remaining forces of US-backed Mujahedeen armies is movement's first priority (M)
news.title: Taliban's Man in Queens Wants the U.N. to Listen

news.abstract: Celia W Dugger analysis of willingness expressed by Prime Min Atal Behari Vajpayee of India and Prime Min Nawaz Sharif of Pakistan to sign nuclear test-ban treaty; says the two leaders will need to convince their restive publics that they got something substantial in return; notes that response to their speeches at United Nations, in which they said their countries were ready to sign treaty within year if sanctions against them were lifted, was optimistic in US; maintains that Sharif and Vajpayee face politically insecure futures and would pay high price with voters if they signed treaty without bringing home goods (M)
news.title: For Pakistan And India, Atom Pact Is Hard Sell

news.abstract: There are neither cheers nor boos in Israel following Pres Clinton's intervention in stalemated peace talks--indication that few believe there has been diplomatic breakthrough worth celebrating or condemning; many Israelis debate Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu's intentions and political repercussions for him if peace agreement is reached during next round of three-way talks (M)
news.title: New Peace Diplomacy Gets Mostly Shrugs in Israel

news.abstract: Pres Clinton meets with Yasir Arafat and emphasizes work that Palestinians need to do to combat terrorism as Israelis withdraw from additional 13 percent of West Bank; Clinton's aides say he is determined to complete interim agreement between Israel and Palestinians in few weeks; car apparently being equipped as bomb explodes in Ramallah, killing Hamas participant; photo (M)
news.title: Clinton Presses Terrorism Issue in 2d Meeting With Arafat

news.abstract: Ethnic Albanians in Gornji Obrinje and neighboring villages bury 34 people who were killed on Sept 26, two days after villages came under siege by Yugoslav Army and Serbian forces; killings appear to show that forces of Yugoslav President, Slobodan Milosevic, have been conducting campaign of terror and destruction against ethnic Albanian civilians in Kosovo that is intended to intimidate them, but which appears instead to be inspiring even stronger defiance; map; photos (M)
news.title: Massacres by Serbian Forces in 3 Kosovo Villages

news.abstract: White House says Pres Clinton has postponed visit to India and Pakistan, whose tests of nuclear devices in May set off alarm around world; says Clinton will not make separate visit to Bangladesh, but will go ahead with plans to attend meeting of Asia Pacific Economic Conference in Malaysia in mid-Nov (M)
news.title: Clinton Putting Off Visits to India and Pakistan

news.abstract: Federal prosecutors in Manhattan charge Mamdouh Mahmud Salim with taking part in conspiracy to attack US military sites abroad; Salim is associate of Osama bin Laden, Saudi exile suspected in embassy bombings in Africa; Salim was arrested in Munich, Germany, in Sept; prosecutors say they will seek his extradition (M)
news.title: U.S. Charges Bin Laden Suspect in Larger Plot

news.abstract: Over 400 important paintings have not been displayed in Iran since 1979 Islamic revolution; paintings, deemed too provocative to be seen, are kept in Museum of Contemporary Art vault; Ali Reza Semiazar, museum's new director, has won permission from Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance to put some of Western collection on regular display, reflecting Pres Mohammad Khatami's call for greater cultural openness; photo (M)
news.title: Teheran Journal; Lifting the Veil, Just a Bit, on West's Decadent Art

news.abstract: International Monetary Fund, in unusually pessimistic report, says that it expects Russian economy to contract by 6 percent this year and next, and Japan to sink into its deepest recession since end of World War II; report, issued day before finance ministers from around world arrive in Washington, DC, for annual meetings of World Bank and IMF, also scales back estimates of how fast other economies will grow; it urges 90 percent of world's central banks to cut interest rates in effort to spur growth and calls for greater cuts in US (M)
news.title: On Eve of Key Meeting, I.M.F. Paints a Gloomy Global Picture

news.abstract: New law banning buying and selling of blood takes effect in China on Oct 1, reflecting growing awareness that nation's heavy reliance on paid blood donors is contributing to rapid spread of AIDS (M)
news.title: Hoping to Control Spread of AIDS, China Bans the Sale of Blood

news.abstract: Richard Butler, head of United Nations' Iraqi disarmament commission, says that he has ordered Scott Ritter, American inspector who quit in anger in August, to stop revealing information he gathered on the job (M)
news.title: Top U.N. Arms Inspector Tries to Quiet Ex-Iraq Team Member

news.abstract: Brazilians prepare to vote on Oct 4; polls predict that Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso, highly acclaimed for putting inflation under control, will handily win re-election; but behind voters' preferences is a kaleidoscope of doubts and difficulties that Brazilians face as their economy grinds to virtual halt, and they prepare for humiliation of ceding some degree of sovereignty for expected $30 billion in aid from International Monetary Fund; Cardoso's closest rival, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, union leader from leftist Workers' Party, opposes bailout and contends administration lacks an effective industrial and employment policy; photo (M)
news.title: On Election Eve, Doubts Cloud Brazilians' Outlook

news.abstract: 42-year-old man who says he is lone survivor of a massacre in which 13 ethnic Albanians were summarily shot and killed in Golubovac village in Kosovo recalls how he was herded into a garden with other men and told to lie flat on ground; recounts how police demanded to know who were members of Kosovo Liberation Army, and then started shooting; survivor, father of eight children, is advised by Western diplomats and by researcher for Human Rights Watch not to give his name for fear of jeopardizing his safety; photo; map (M)
news.title: Survivor of Kosovo Massacre Describes the Killing Garden

news.abstract: Treasury Secretary Robert E Rubin asserts that United States will press for 'new openess in international finance' that will require private financial institutions to disclose far more information about their loans around world and force investors to pay their share of cost of bailing out troubled nations, speech in NYC to annual conference on the Americas, held by Dow Jones & Co (M)
news.title: Rubin Urges More Disclosure in Global Finance and Making Investors Pay Bailout Share

news.abstract: Special Report, A Fund of Trouble, on recriminations and criticisms besetting International Monetary Fund, as world's finance ministers gather in Washington for annual meeting of IMF and World Bank; just about everything that could have gone wrong in world economy has: worst downturn in Japan since World War II, economic meltdown in Russia, depression in Indonesia that is plunging 100 million people below poverty line, and deep fears over what happens next in Latin Amreica; what makes this year's meeting of IMF most remarkable is that harshest criticisms are directed at monetary fund itself, and, by extension, at United States Treasury, which is viewed as power behind the fund; 53 years after IMF was created, it is under attack from all sides, charged not only with worsening a bad situation by misjudging the economics, but with being politically tone-deaf in some of most volatile capitals in world, from Jakarta to Moscow; photos (L)
news.title: A FUND OF TROUBLE: A special report.; As Economies Fail, the I.M.F. Is Rife With Recriminations

news.abstract: TOKYO—  Asia's financial crisis may have started in Thailand, but its solution, say many, must begin in Japan.
news.title: Tradition or Change?Japan Dithers

news.abstract: Egypt celebrates 25th anniversary of October 1973 war against Israel, starting festivities with mass wedding of 250 couples in shadow of Great Pyramids; both Egypt and Israel claim victory in the war, which was a turning point in Arab-Israel relations, prompting the first real consideration of concept of land for peace; photo (M)
news.title: Cairo Journal; Praising Love and War, Beneath the Pyramids

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  The chairman of UBS AG, Europe's biggest bank, and three of his top executives abruptly quit Friday to take responsibility for damaging losses in the near-collapse of a U.S. investment fund.
news.title: UBS Chairman Joins Casualty List From Hedge Fund's Setback : 4 Executives At Big Bank Lose Jobs Over Losses

news.abstract: Several influential Republicans, including Sens Richard G Lugar, Don Nickles and Pete V Domenici, criticize Clinton Administration's approach toward ending crisis in Kosovo, which calls for air strikes in Kosovo and elsewhere in Serbia if Pres Slobodan Milosevic of Yugoslavia does not agree to remove his special police forces from province, permit aid to refugees and begin serious negotiations toward a political settlement (M)
news.title: Republicans Criticize Clinton On Kosovo

news.abstract: Secretary of State Madeleine K Albright expresses disappointment at economic confusions within new Russian Government of Prime Minister Yevgeny M Primakov; cites talk about printing new money, indexing wages, imposing price and capital controls and restoring state management of parts of the economy; warns Russia against the 'many voices' there who want to shift emphasis in Russia's interaction with the West from one of partnership to one of assertiveness, opposition and defiance for its own sake (M)
news.title: Economy Shift In Russia Worries U.S., Albright Says

news.abstract: Patrols in Bosnia by American and other NATO forces have become mostly routine, although troops still run into roadblocks, angry crowds and illegal weapons caches, but mission has not figured out how to leave; nobody in Clinton Administration will admit there is no end in sight, for fear of further irritating Congress, but evidence is clear; NATO has broken ground on new headquarters near Sarajevo, UN is spending $34 million to buff up its camps and extend runways at Tuzla; photos; map; many central promises of Dayton accords remain unfulfilled; Sarajevo's streets bustle, but most of country remains economically listless; unified government barely exists, and then only under foreign pressure; NATO commander Gen Wesley K Clark sys 99 percent of military task is completed, but warns of very high risk of fighting if forces dare to go home (M)
news.title: Force in Bosnia Fails at One Task: A Pullout

news.abstract: Number of city dwellers living in poverty in China, group virtually nonexistent decade ago, is now growing rapidly as unskilled workers lose out in rapid transformation to market economy; millions of urban poor, distinct from poor migrants from countryside, cannoot afford basic food, clothing or shelter; photo of 50-year-old itinerant garbage collector in Xian whose dilapidated, but free, home was demolished to make way for new apartments he cannot afford; photo; old planned economy assigned nearly all urban Chinese to work units, which guaranteed them housing and subsidized food, medical care, pensions and schooling; system has crumbled in last few years as state companies close or downsize or lack funds to pay benefits (M)
news.title: Poverty Spreads, and Deepens, in China's Cities

news.abstract: Trinidad and Tobago draws international condemnation, but broad support at home, as it withdraws from UN and Inter-American rights conventions over curbs on death penalty; decision to speed up hangings of convicted criminals is widely supported by public alarmed over rising crime rates; map; Trinidad Atty Gen Ramesh L Maharaj says numerous, lengthy appeals drag out process; conventions require commuting to life in prison any death sentence when prisoner has been held more than five years (M)
news.title: In the Caribbean, Support Growing for the Death Penalty

news.abstract: Malaysian Prime Min Mahathir Mohamad's record of achievement over last 17 years is threatened by political cat fight stemming from his arrest of heir apparent, Anwar Ibrahim, on charges of corruption and illegal sex acts; Mahathir, 72, fostered economic liberalization, drove Malaysians to be more productive and to embrace high technology, created opportunities for ethnic minorities and sense of national pride; dizzying turnaround has left country teetering economically and politically (M)
news.title: Feud Eclipses Time of Glory For Leader Of Malaysia

news.abstract: American intelligence officials report new evidence linking owner of Sudanese factory destroyed by US missile strike to terrorist group backed by Osama bin Laden, suspected mastermind of US embassy bombings in Africa; Salih Idris reportedly has had dealings with Islamic Jihad, which gets money from bin Laden; Idris denies charge (M)
news.title: New Evidence Ties Sudanese To Bin Laden, U.S. Asserts

news.abstract: Communist Party, which currently controls Russian Government and has undergone resurgence by playing on economic discontent, is working hard to cast itself as outsider in Government it helps to run in demonstration planned for Moscow on October 7, and to keep focus of protests on Pres Boris Yeltsin and his policies; photos (M)
news.title: Protests Set for Moscow, but Over What?

news.abstract: Japan's top financial officials tell American counterparts country's banking system is acutely short of capital, with top 19 banks in deeper trouble than Tokyo has ever before admitted; Bank of Japan Governor Masaru Hayami tells Treas Sec Robert E Rubin and Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan in Washington meeting that capital supporting banks has dwindled to dangerously low levels, such that they may be banned from operating internationally; other senior Japanese officials, in reflection of confusion surrounding Japan's financial crisis, dispute dispute Hayami's presentation; insist reserve levels have not declined to dangerous levels; conflicting explanations come as financial leaders of world's major economies hold annual meetings of International Monetary Fund and World Bank to grapple with economic crisis many fear has spun out of control; Rubin presses for changes at fund and bank that would improve their ability to head off crises; other officials, including World Bank president James D Wolfensohn, argue that countries should focus their energies on immediate crisis and postpone broader discussion of remaking global financial system (M)
news.title: JAPANESE TELL U.S. THAT THEIR BANKS ARE IN BIG TROUBLE

news.abstract: Joseph C McCarthy dies at age of 79; he was lone American in secret unit of Allied pilots that carried out brazen British bombing raid on strategic German dams in 1943; photo (M)
news.title: Joseph C. McCarthy, Pilot in '43 Dam Buster Raid, Dies at 79

news.abstract: Brazilian voters give Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso comfortable lead in first round of balloting, apparently maintaining leadership of country struggling against economic crisis; with 27 percent of vote counted, he appears to have won 51.3 percent of vote, compared with 33.9 percent for main rival, Luiz Inacio lula da Silva; photo (M)
news.title: Cardoso Seems to Be Re-elected in Brazil, Averting Runoff

news.abstract: World Bank, amid spread of global economic crisis, fears being transformed from slow-moving development agency into financial fire truck, programmed to squirt streams of cash at countries under speculative attack; finance ministers from world's seven largest economies, attending bank's and IMF's annual meeting in Washington, warn that without radical strengthening of international financial system crisis will spread far beyond Asia and Russia to affect entire developing world; IMF has lowered economic growth forecasts for developing world as whole, predicting that economies will expand by 2.3 percent in 1998 and 3.6 percent in 1999--compared with 5.8 percent in 1997 (M)
news.title: World Bank Worried by Pressure for Quick-Fix Fiscal Action

news.abstract: Moscow Journal describes mix of fatalism and gallows humor with which Russians are facing economic crisis; drawing; photo (M)
news.title: Moscow Journal; Ruble Is on 'Tilt,' but Russians Keep Their Balance

news.abstract: Article on new Meteor line of Paris Metro--first to be built since 1935 and first to be fully automated (M)
news.title: Driverless Trains Have Paris Debut

news.abstract: Report by UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan accuses Serbian security forces of continuing punitive operations against ethnic Albanians in Kosovo Province as part of campaign of terror and violence; is unequivocal in conclusions--based on accounts from UN High Commissioner for Refugees, diplomats in region and Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe--bolstering assessments by NATO and American officials; catalogues hallmarks of Serb drive against ethnic Albanians; calls it collective punishment to teach that price of supporting separatists is high and will be even higher in future; says Serbian security forces have used terrror and violence against civilians to force people to flee homes or where they sought refuge, under guise of separating them from fighters of Kosovo Albanian paramilitary units; expresses concern about appearance of Serbian-laid land mines in new areas, away from Serbia's borders with Albania and Macedonia; puts number of displaced people at about 280,000; US envoy Richard C Holbrooke meets with Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic in Belgrade and reportedly warns that he must take further steps to withdraw military units from Kosovo or face NATO attack; US and NATO officials say Yugoslav Army still has substantial forces in Kosovo, despite some withdrawals; NATO Sec Gen Javier Solana says Milosevic has failed to respond adequately to UN Security Council demand for withdrawal of forces and that alliance is ready to act (M)
news.title: Serbs Continue Kosovo Terror, Annan Asserts

news.abstract: Latin American officials, increasingly angry at what they consider lenient treatment Russia has received in its $4.5 billion bailout by International Monetary Fund, warn programs being offered to protect their own countries are too paltry; criticisms by Mexico's central bank governor, Guillermo Ortiz, noted (M)
news.title: Latin Americans Say Russian Bailout Leaves Too Little for Them

news.abstract: US envoy Richard C Holbrooke meets with Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic in Belgrade; reportedly warns he faces NATO attack unless he withdraws military from Kosovo Province; reportedly told Milosevic he had to insure that 250,000 ethnic Albanian refugees who have fled their homes in fighting in past six months be allowed to return safely; photo (M)
news.title: Holbrooke Meets Milosevic on Pullback

news.abstract: Weapons experts say French tests appear to have found traces of chemicals linked to nerve gas VX on Iraqi warheads, finding that would confirm earlier American test results; diplomats charge that France is delaying release of findings to avoid undermining Iraq's push at United Nations to lift economic sanctions; France denies withholding results; says they are expected to be 'consistent' with earlier tests that found no traces of VX (M)
news.title: France Detects Iraqi Nerve Gas, Experts Assert

news.abstract: World Bank president, James D Wolfensohn, breaks with United States-International Monetary Fund approach to managing global financial crisis, speech to World Bank-IMF meeting, Washington; holds too little attention is being paid to growing ranks of unemployed and threats to political stability in rush to stabilize currencies and reform economies; speech brings into open months of tensions between sister institutions over strategy for dealing with crisis; Treasury Sec Robert Rubin urges institutions to settle differences; Pres Clinton urges search for way to temper volatile swings of international marketplace; again proposes that major nations set up 'precautionary lines of credit' to help countries caught up in financial turmoil despite adopting tough reforms; Adminstration holds preliminary talks on British Prime Min Tony Blair's call for emergency economic summit meeting; IMF managing direct Michel Camdessus says crisis can be overcome; insists burden of economic reform falls on individual nations; says IMF cannot resume funding Russia until its new Government embraces reform; photo of Pres Clinton (M)
news.title: Dissension Erupts at Talks On World Financial Crisis

news.abstract: United States envoy Richard C Holbrooke fails to extract any concessions on troop pullback from Kosovo Province or return of refugees in talks with Yugoslav President, Slobodan Milosevic; diplomats see plans for more talks as bid by Milosevic to stall NATO air strikes; he has begun using threatened attacks to consolidate support among Serbs; photo (M)
news.title: Holbrooke Is Unable to Wrest Concessions From Milosevic

news.abstract: Russia vows to veto any UN Security Council authorization of air strikes against Yugoslavia and warns of 'serious international consequences' if NATO uses force to halt ethnic conflict in Kosovo Province; stepped-up involvement in Kosovo crisis comes as Russia is pressing West to rescue its foundering economy; comes amid increasingly open hostility to West, which many Russians blame for promoting policies that have led to economy's near-collapse (M)
news.title: Russia Vows to Block the U.N. From Backing Attack on Serbs

news.abstract: European governments are challenging United States leadership in addressing world financial crisis as turmoil persists and Congress continues to block new funding for International Monetary Fund; are flexing their muscles as economic power at IMF-World Bank meeting of finance ministers and central bankers, Washington, after year spent largely on sidelines while US worked closely with IMF to curb turmoil; favor shifting more power into existing IMF policy-setting committee, move that would limit direct US influence over fund; score opposition in Republican-controlled Congress to providing full $18 billion sought by Pres Clinton for IMF; are more sympathetic than US to World Bank stress on poverty-fighting over austerity programs and to its questioning of blanket opposition to controls on international flow of capital; photo (M)
news.title: Europe Sharpening Its Challenge To the U.S. Over Economic Crisis

news.abstract: Clinton Administration and Congressional Republicans are working frantically on bill to give International Monetary Fund added $18 billion as fund seeks to avert global financial meltdown; agree money is urgently needed; debate curbs sought by conservatives on future lending by IMF, which has been criticized by both Republicans and Democrats for mismanaging global financial crisis (M)
news.title: Wrangling Over I.M.F. Bill at Fever Pitch

news.abstract: World's finance ministers and central bankers end gloomy International Monetary Fund-World Bank joint meeting, Washington, with no strategy to lift global markets out of downward spiral, but plethora of new ideas; participants repeatedly blamed Japan for problems, as well as hedge funds and currency speculators (M)
news.title: Meeting of World Finance Leaders Ends, With No Grand Strategy but Many Ideas

news.abstract: South Korean Pres Kim Dae Jung arrives in Japan for state visit; calls for closer partnership and end to longstanding tensions between neighbors; Japanese officials seem ready to reciprocate by making unusually humble apology for colonial past (M)
news.title: Korean Leader, Visiting Japan, Urges Healing of Old Wounds

news.abstract: Roger Vivier, leading shoe designer whose innovations in heel and toe shapes changed silhouette of women's shoes, dies at age 90; photo (M)
news.title: Roger Vivier Is Dead at 90; Raised Heels to New Heights

news.abstract: United Nations war crimes tribunal, Hague, says Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic's Government bars United Nations from probing reported war crimes in Kosovo, Serbia, and denies visas sought by tribunal; says Government has threatened to close tribunal's office in Belgrade if court continues to collect evidence on alleged Kosovo massacres (S)
news.title: Belgrade Bars U.N. War-Crimes Investigators

news.abstract: Republican Congressional leaders present Clinton Adm with list of lending conditions that they want imposed on IMF in order for Congress to approve $18 billion in new money for IMF; list is not made public, but Congressional officials say it includes demand that IMF open its books for public scrutiny, that it end its practices of lending to foreign govts at below-market interest rates, and that it shorten lending perod on most loans (M)
news.title: Republicans List Terms for I.M.F. Payout

news.abstract: Federal prosecutors in Manhattan say that Govt is considering asking for death penalty for two of suspects arrested after bombings of United States Embassies in Kenya and Tanzania in August; suspects for whom death penalty may be sought are Mohamed Rashed Daoud al'Owhali and Mohammed Saddiq Odeh (M)
news.title: U.S. May Ask Death Penalty in Embassy Bombings

news.abstract: Meeting of international finance ministers and central bankers in Washington ends in gloom, with world financial crisis hanging over IMF meeting (M)
news.title: A Champagne Evening Awash in Gloom

news.abstract: Iran says that its troops clashed with Taliban forces along Afghan border and inflicted heavy casualties there in skirmish between neighbors who have been in a tense standoff; reported fighting, which follows more than two months of bellicose statements from both sides, would be first between Iran and Taliban, whose rival interpretations of Islam have contributed to open hostility; map (M)
news.title: Iran's Forces Said to Clash With Afghans Along Border

news.abstract: Kosovo refugees, many ailing, scramble to survive in hills, woods and fields; Doctors Without Borders, relief agency, says newest refugees of Kosovan crisis are the worst off; warns in report to diplomatic monitors that refugees have perilously little food and that carcasses of animals shot by troops threaten creek water that is used for drinking, cooking and washing; unlike longer-term refugees new contingent has had no time to put up reinforced tents with wood floors; they sleep sandwiched 8 to 10 in open-air trailers covered with flimsy swaths of plastic; photo (M)
news.title: New Kosovo Refugees, Many Ailing, Scramble to Survive

news.abstract: American envoy Richard C Holbrooke, who came to Belgrade, Serbia, to warn Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic to comply on Kosovo or face NATO attack, is in midst of full-dress talks; reportedly makes some progress; photo (M)p
news.title: A U.S. Message to Milosevic Turns Into Full-Dress Talks

news.abstract: German Chancellor-elect Gerhard Schroder, meeting with Pres Clinton, Washington, says he would back decision by caretaker German Government to authorize NATO use of force over Kosovo, if necessary; indicates any authorization for use of German troops and planes against Serbia should await seating of newly elected Parliament; Clinton stresses importance of forthcoming NATO vote to authorize use of force (M)
news.title: Schroder Tells Clinton He Backs Action by NATO in Kosovo

news.abstract: Chang Chong-Jen, Chinese painter and sculptor who was model for character in Tintin cartoons, dies at age 93; photo (M)
news.title: Chang Chong-Jen, 93, Model for Character in Tintin Comic

news.abstract: Prime Min Romano Prodi's center-left government loses confidence vote, 313-312, suggesting return to chronic political instability in Italy; Prodi resigns but will remain in charge as caretaker until new government is formed; photo (M)
news.title: Italy's Center-Left Government Is Toppled by One Vote

news.abstract: China lets director Chen Kaige hold world film premiere of his historical epic about ancient battles that led to China's unification in Great Hall of the People, Beijing; English title of film, set for United States distribution, has not been chosen; photo (M)
news.title: Beijing Journal; A New Epic With a History of Its Own

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II will pronounce Edith Stein, renowned Jewish intellectual who became Carmelite nun and died at Auschwitz, a saint and martyr for Roman Catholic faith at Mass in St Peter's Square; ever since she was beatified in 1987, many Jewish groups and members of her family have questioned Vatican's logic and sensitivity, arguing that Stein was sent to gas chambers because she was a Jew, and not because she was a nun; photo (M)
news.title: A Jew's Odyssey From Catholic Nun to Saint

news.abstract: Security officials and Japanese and American terrorism experts say Aum Shinrikyo, cult that planted nerve gas in Tokyo subway three years ago, killing 12 people and injuring thousands more, is back; they say cult is regrouping, recruiting new members at home and abroad and raising vast sums of money; State Department has designated it terrorist group, although it has not been linked to any illegal acts since 1995; resurgence of sect is due partly to Japan's unwillingness to ban it; photos (M)
news.title: Some in Japan Fear Authors of Subway Attack Are Regaining Ground

news.abstract: Western officials say NATO is ready to approve 'activation order' on Oct 12, opening way for its military commanders to order air strikes against Serbian targets in Kosovo and perhaps in Serbian heartland (M)
news.title: NATO Nears Final Order To Approve Kosovo Strike

news.abstract: World's governments, faced with prospect of pictures of emaciated, malnourished children as wellas thousands of deaths in southern Sudan, launches Operation Lifeline Sudan and appeals for funds to meet the 'emergency' in 1989; tons of food was delivered to suffering, where civil war was root cause of starvation; nearly a decade and more than $2 billion later, situation is virtually identical, despite what Operation Lifeline describes as one of largest relief operations ever; officials in Washington and at relief organizations wonder whether aid is helping perpetuate fighting between African Christians and Muslim Arabs, giving factions what they need to carry on war in which both sides are guilty of atrocities; photo (M)
news.title: Aid for Sudan's Hungry Keeps War Well Fed

news.abstract: Bloody struggle over future of Colombia, raging between shadowy groups of men and women with masks and false names, is closing in on Calamar, main transit point in coca trade; many residents have not left the town in a year; only road out is controlled by paramilitaries, who have established checkpoint a few miles from nearest military base and charge coca growers and food suppliers simply to get their products in and out of town; residents fear dying for simply coming from Calamar, which paramilitaries label a rebel support base; map; photo (M)
news.title: A Coca-Trade Jungle Town Trapped by Colombia's Strife

news.abstract: SEOUL—  On the third floor of the student center at Korea University, Lee Han Byul, deputy chief of a student union affiliated with a national student organization noted for sometimes radical activism, talks earnestly about his country's problems.
news.title: Putting Aside Activism, Students In Korea Focus on Hunt for Jobs : Campus Life:Work, No Fray

news.abstract: Deep-sea submersible, operated by Odyssey Marine Explorations Inc of Tampa, Fla, discovers hundreds of amphoras, clay storage jars of antiquity, deep in western Mediterranean; find has been tentatively identified as typical of Phoenician colony at Carthage (near modern-day Tunis) around fifth century BC near peak of Phoenician influence; discovery is stirring great scholarly interest because so little is known of Phoenicians, who were successful traders during first millenium BC who sailed mainly out of area that is now Lebanon, spreading colonies along Mediterranean coast; despite their early success, subsequent waves of civilization wiped out most traces of them; map; photo (M)
news.title: Deep-Sea Clues to an Ancient Culture Discovered

news.abstract: News analysis of effects of White House sex scandal on US domestic and foreign policy; with Pres Clinton distracted and his moral authority questioned, there is much room for US allies, Congress and even some major corporations to ignore, deflect or defy him; defiance by Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic over Serbia, refusal of Republican-controlled Congress to fulfill US obligations to International Monetary Fund and UN, and Clinton's failure to persuade major oil companies to build oil pipeline from Caspian Sea through Turkey, declared American strategic priority, discussed (M)
news.title: U.S. Policies: Testing Time

news.abstract: Pope John Paul II canonizes Edith Stein, Jewish intellectual who became Carmelite nun and died at Auschwitz; recalls her Jewish roots and suffering of Jews in Mass at St Peter's in Rome (M)
news.title: Pope Canonizes Jew Who Became Nun and Died at Auschwitz

news.abstract: Shortage of onions is producing long lines, high prices and anger in many Indian cities, threatening to topple Hindu nationalist state governments in Delhi and Rajasthan in November elections; maps; photo (M)
news.title: India's Hottest Political Issue: The Price of Onions

news.abstract: Russia mounts last-ditch campaign today to avert NATO air strikes against Yugoslavia, warning that such action could bring end to its cooperation with Western alliance; intensity of its diplomatic effort reflects ascension of new Prime Min Yevgeny M Primakov, former Foreign Min whose efforts have always been to circumscribe NATO's influence and contest American dominance; he has often cast Moscow as wounded great power in open-ended struggle with West (M)
news.title: Russia Sees NATO Raids as Imperiling Cooperation With West

news.abstract: US and its allies approve order clearing way for NATO to begin bombing campaign in Serbian province of Kosovo within four days, but White House says agreement to end crisis with Serbs appears imminent; senior American and NATO officials say significant progress was made in talks between special US envoy, Richard C Holbrooke and Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic over oppression of ethnic Albanians; say Milosevic has agreed to end all police and military operations in Kosovo, withdraw forces in verifiable way and make unilateral statement pledging partial autonomy in province; say he appears ready to allow force of 2,000 monitors, mostly civilian, into Kosovo; caution that differences remain over exact makeup of international mission; say Milosevic's reluctance to pledge cooperation with international war crimes investigations is also outstanding issue; Pres Clinton expresses guarded optimism over developments, noting Milosevic has failed to keep promises in past; says while US and allies prefer to settle issue peacefully, military force will be used if Milosevic fails to keep word; photos (M)
news.title: NATO OPENS WAY TO START BOMBING IN SERB PROVINCE

news.abstract: Pres Boris Yeltsin abruptly cuts short three-day visit to Central Asia after doctor announced he was suffering from bronchitis and slight fever; Kremlin's record of covering up his health problems leaves commentators questioning whether Yeltsin's illness was more serious; has compounded sense that nation lacks fully functioning leader during one of its gravest economic crises; photo (M)
news.title: A Rough Trip for Yeltsin Adds to Worries About Health

news.abstract: Newly declassified Government documents show US has relied on weak and unsubstantiated evidence that has never been fully investigated to detain six Iraqi dissidents who worked with Central Intelligence Agency against Pres Saddam Hussein; Iraqis, removed in 1996 by Clinton Administration along with 600 other CIA-supported dissidents and additional 5,000 Iraqis and Kurds as Hussein's forces attacked opposition groups in northern Iraq, have been in legal limbo in Immigration and Naturalization Service center in Los Angeles; have been denied asylum in secret hearing in which they were not allowed to see evidence, hear testimony or even know charges keeping them in custody; declassified documents show many of charges against them stem from unsubstantiated allegations made to FBI by rival Iraqis combined with other fragmentary evidence like family connections to other suspected foreign agents (M)
news.title: Evidence to Deny 6 Iraqis Asylum May Be Weak, Files Show

news.abstract: Young American men entering priesthood are far more conservative and tradition-bound than many of their elders and most American Roman Catholics, according to bishops, priests and church surveys; in sharp swing of pendulum, seminarians are rejecting liberalism and rebellion that swept Catholic Church after Vatican II and American society in 1960's and 1970's; while shift back to orthodoxy is welcomed by many church leaders after decades of confusion and conflict, others worry that trend could create rift between more rigid, conformist clergy and majority of American Catholics, who routinely ignore Rome's teachings on major issues; surge in enrollments at Pontifical North American College of Rome, seminary for Americans preparing for priesthood, to highest level in quarter-century, discussed; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Catholic Seminarians Turning to Orthodoxy

news.abstract: For nearly a century, the United States military has used the jungle terrain surrounding the Panama Canal as a testing ground for explosives and chemical weapons. Now, a little more than a year before those ranges must be handed back to Panama, Washington is balking at cleaning up some of the most hazardous of the ordnance its troops are leaving behind.    The deadly debris consists mostly of bombs and other unexploded munitions that for decades were tested at three ranges near the west bank of the canal. But the dangerous materials either tested or stored here also include lethal nerve gases, mustard and phosgene gases dating back to World War II, biological agents and, for a short time earlier this decade, depleted uranium projectiles.
news.title: U.S. Balks at Cleanup of Hazardous Canal Zone Sites

news.abstract: The grandly named Gaza Industrial Estate, an unprepossessing 120-acre collection of vacant factory sheds and water towers rising from the ragged flatlands east of Gaza City, is an unlikely focus for the highly charged, high-stakes Middle East peace negotiations.    Fenced off from potential markets by the barbed wire of the Israeli border, the park has been ready for business for nearly a year. But security-conscious Israeli officials had been unwilling to guarantee the unimpeded flow of goods that an industrial park needs to attract and sustain investment.
news.title: Prototype of Peace via Trade in Gaza

news.abstract: The Security Council called on Iraq today to resume cooperation with United Nations weapon inspectors, alluding to prospects for faster progress on easing economic sanctions against Baghdad if it heeds the call.    That and several somewhat conciliatory statements by various members of the 15-member Council followed a periodic review today of Iraq's compliance in eliminating its weapons of mass destruction.
news.title: U.N. Tries to Cajole Iraq Into Cooperating on Arms Inspections

news.abstract: The English, past masters at turning the raised eyebrow and the cold shoulder on others, are suddenly feeling looked down upon and left out in their own land.    In the last year the three other regions that make up Britain -- Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland -- are putting in place new legislatures to deal with parochial affairs no longer considered the preserve of the British Parliament in London. Some in England, traditionally the ruling power in the kingdom, are now thinking that maybe it should have one too.
news.title: London Journal; Has England Lost Its Identity? Or Just Its Cliches?

news.abstract: The Clinton Administration and Congressional Republican leaders met today to hammer out the final details of compromise legislation that would provide the International Monetary Fund with $18 billion in exchange for new restrictions on its loans to foreign governments.    Congressional officials said that the deal, part of an overall budget agreement between the Administration and Capitol Hill expected to be announced this week, would require the monetary fund to stop making many of its loans at below-market interest rates and compel borrowers to repay the loans within two and a half years.
news.title: Republicans Meet Aides To Clinton On I.M.F.

news.abstract: Over 2,000 mink set free when animal liberationists broke locks on cages of Onneley, Eng, mink farm recently wreaked havoc on surrounding countryside; Agricultural Ministry, while expressing ethical objections to mink industry, deplores attack, noting mink pose threat to other animals and are not prepared to fend for selves (M)
news.title: Set All of England's Mink Free! Oops. That's Killing Them.

news.abstract: Col Gaston de Bonneval, French Resistance fighter who spent two decades as Charles de Gaulle's confidant, dies at age 86; photo (M)
news.title: Col. Gaston de Bonneval, 86, De Gaulle's Closest Confidant

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  The United States intensified its criticism of Malaysia on Wednesday over the treatment of the dismissed deputy prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim.
news.title: In Protest, Clinton Downgrades Visit to Malaysia : U.S. 'Horrified' About Anwar

news.abstract: Much remains unresolved about exact role and powers of Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, which will send 2,000 unarmed civilians to Kosovo, Serbia, to verify that Yugoslav military and police forces end crackdown and let ethnic Albanians return to homes under accord worked out by United States envoy Richard C Holbrooke and Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic; organization chairman Bronislaw Geremek, Poland's Foreign Minister, is to meet with Serbian officials to clear way for monitors to arrive by end of week; American William Walker is leading candidate to head mission, which will be largely European (M)
news.title: 2,000 Monitors to Go to Kosovo, but Their Power Is Unclear

news.abstract: Shobha De, India's biggest-selling novelist writing in English, has built devoted following of middle-class readers; none of her racy, commercially successful novels has been published in United States; De, who has just come out with her memoirs, comments, interview; photo (M)
news.title: Bombay Journal; India Relishes the Novels She Sprinkles With Spice

news.abstract: Clinton Administration and Congressional leaders say deal for US to pay $200 million in back dues to UN as part of overall Federal budget package collapsed after issue became entangled again in abortion politics; Republicans made funds contingent on White House agreement to bar Federal grants to family-planning organizations that lobby for abortion rights overseas; Speaker Gingrich says UN money will be included in State Department authorization; urges Clinton to sign despite 'tiny' abortion provision (S)
news.title: Deal to Pay Back American U.N. Dues Collapses Over Abortion

news.abstract: Clinton Administration says budget agreement with Republican Congress that will inject $18 billion into IMF's depleted coffers will also give officials political leeway to try new strategies in global financial turmoil; accord paves way for other nations to increase their contributions, which will enable IMF to help Brazil with at least $30 billion; Pres Clinton's proposal for multibillion-dollar credit lines for countries is also boosted; Republicans have seen IMF as incompetent, but Repr Dick Armey, in talks with Sec Robert E Rubin, has been more conciliatory; highlights on review of IMF and its policies (M)
news.title: Clinton Officials Say I.M.F. Deal Expands Strategies to Halt Crisis

news.abstract: Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic has not complied with NATO demands to withdraw troops and police forces from Kosovo; heavily armed Serb police continue to saunter around camp in sight of ethnic Albanian villages as NATO reiterates threat of air strikes; map; Sec Gen Javier Solana, joined by NATO commander Gen Wesley K Clark, arrives in Belgrade and complains that Milosevic is not complying with agreement brokered by Richard Holbrooke; White House spokesman concurs; relief workers and diplomatic monitors are at same time returning to Kosovo, suggesting NATO will not carry out attacks; monitors confirm that Serb military presence remains intense (M)
news.title: YUGOSLAV LEADER IS NOT COMPLYING WITH KOSOVO PACT

news.abstract: Clint Hallam of Australia will leave French hospital with his transplanted hand; condition is reported good, although longtime outcome will not be known for year (S)
news.title: Australian Patient's Transplanted Hand Is Doing Well in France

news.abstract: PARIS—  Look down any chilly street this fall in Paris and what will you see: beautiful young girls with Mona Lisa smiles in crunchy knit tunics and A-line floor-sweeping skirts preferably in boiled wool. The fashion faithful these days is sliding into a new silhouette, one that makes top to bottom skinny chic and stilettos look like old hash.
news.title: A Soft, Voluminous Look Is Edging Out Skinny Silhouette : Loosening Up on Slim Chic

news.abstract: NATO grants Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic a reprieve, extending by 10 days its deadline for him to withdraw military and police forces cracking down on ethnic Albanians in province of Kosovo; in face of abundant evidence that Milosevic has not yet kept his pledges to withdraw forces, NATO's reprs in Brussels give him until Oct 27 to comply or face threat of NATO military attacks; they say reprieve brings time for international observers to arrive on ground in Kosovo; they also say it will allow NATO to start surveillance flights; photo (M)
news.title: REPRIEVE BY NATO ALLOWS MILOSEVIC ANOTHER 10 DAYS

news.abstract: Analysis of Pope John Paul II's latest encyclical, which amplifies historic church position that faith and reason cannot be separated; some scholars comment (M)
news.title: Catholic Scholars Call Message a Timely Critique

news.abstract: FBI, in rare public statement about August bombings of two American embassies in Africa, says that two vehicles had been used in attack on Embassy in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania; also indicates that it it has identified new suspects in blast in Dar es Salaam, and that they are at large (S)
news.title: New U.S. Disclosures on Tanzania Bombing

news.abstract: John Paul II celebrates his 20th anniversary as Pope; appears at window at St Peter's Basilica as tens of thousands of well-wishers gather beneath to hear and watch by live television hookup the ringing of bells of Crakow Cathedral, just as they had rung at same time on Oct 16, 1978; photo of Pope mingling with crowd of 25,000 Polish pilgrims gathered in St Peter's Square (M)
news.title: Nostalgic, John Paul II Celebrates 20-Year Reign

news.abstract: Massimo D'Alema, former Communist and leader of largest leftist party in Italy, is selected to try to form a new Govt; D'Alema, is chosen after Acting Prime Min Romano Prodi, who resigned after losing confidence vote last week, failed to gather enough support in Parliament to form a new Govt (M)
news.title: Leftist Leader to Try to Assemble a New Government in Italy

news.abstract: Long political squabble between Jean-Bertrand Aristide and other leaders of fracturing Lavalas coalition has left Haiti without working government, stalled foreign aid programs and disillusioned and exasperated foreign allies; repeated United States efforts to end impasse have failed; civil servants go unpaid in cities, while only private relief organizations attend to rural social problems; Pres Rene Preval, Aristide ally, lacks votes in Parliament to name Prime Minister to succeed Rosny Smarth, who resigned in June 1997; former allies charge Aristide tries to install dictatorship; photo (M)
news.title: Political Feuds Rack Haiti: So Much for Its High Hopes

news.abstract: Iraqi officials seem confident that they are closer than ever to easing of United Nations sanctions and that they can avert military strike even if they block arms inspections; most foreign diplomats agree Pres Saddam Hussein has come long way in shifting burden of making case for sanctions to United States and Unscom, UN body charged with dismantling Iraq's weapons of mass destruction (M)
news.title: Higher Hopes In Baghdad For Ending U.N. Embargo

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, trying to force pace of Mideast accord, meets separately with Palestinian and Israeli delegations, Wye Mills, Md (M)
news.title: Clinton Returns to Mideast Summit in Maryland

news.abstract: Recent barrage of unusually bizarre rumors about assassination attempts on Libyan leader Muammar el-Qaddafi, who is now hobbling on crutches, has people trying hard to piece together facts amid customary cloud of secrecy; clues include postponed trip, broken leg, reports of roadside ambush and untimely death of provincial governor; photo (M)
news.title: Rumors and Secrecy Cloud Issue: Is Qaddafi O.K.?

news.abstract: Analysis of peace talks in United States between Israelis and Palestinians; bitter 19-month freeze in peace process has left Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu wary of obligation to cede land to Palestinians and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat wary of cracking down on terror (M)
news.title: Arab-Israel Talks: Wary Dance on a Narrow Ledge

news.abstract: Legal scholars say arrest of former Chilean dictator Gen Augusto Pinochet by Scotland Yard on warrant by Spanish magistrate shows growing significance of international human rights law; say it suggests that officials accused of atrocities have fewer places to hide, even if they are carrying diplomatic passports (M)
news.title: Officials Accused of Atrocities Losing Places to Hide, Scholars Say
