news.abstract: Former Chilean strongman, Gen Augusto Pinochet, remains sequestered under police guard in London following arrest for war crimes on warrant by Spanish magistrate; is awaiting potentially devastating court hearing to weigh extradition to Spain to stand trial for human rights violations committed during 17-year dictatorship, from 1973 to 1990; detention leaves Labor Govt of Prime Min Tony Blair embarrassed by diplomatic implications of arrest that has enraged Government of Chile, which Britain regards as ally, and presents European officials with uncomfortable implications for handling of human rights violators closer to home (M)
news.title: Arrest Raises New Issues On Tracking Rights Crimes

news.abstract: Peace talks between Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat continue past original October 18 deadline at Wye Conference Center in Maryland, despite more than 20 hours of personal engagement by Pres Clinton; overall mood is called serious; US officials remain optimistic; Israeli official reports progress on different issues, including security, but no complete agreement on any major issues, specifically Israel's withdrawal from more of West bank and commitment from Palestinians to change their charter, which calls for destruction of Israel; photo (M)
news.title: MIDEAST  MEETING WILL BE CONTINUED INTO ANOTHER DAY

news.abstract: Yugoslavia begins withdrawing forces from Kosovo Province in Serbia in what Clinton Administration and NATO officials call significant step by Pres Slobodan Milosevic toward complying with demands to end military campaign against ethnic Albanians; officials express concern over slow pace with which Milosevic Govt is abiding by recently-brokered agreement, reached under threat of NATO air strikes against Yugoslav military and police forces (M)
news.title: Serb Forces Leaving Kosovo, But at a Slow Pace, U.S. Says

news.abstract: Indian and Pakistani diplomats end three days of talks in Islamabad, agreeing only to keep talking to each other about ways to reduce risk of nuclear conflict between them; present proposals to dispel mistrust and enmity that have characterized relationship since Pakistan gained independence 51 years ago (M)
news.title: India and Pakistan Agree Only to Future Talks

news.abstract: Gen Jehangir Karamat, Chief of Staff of Pakistan's Army, is uncharacteristically forced to resign after publicly criticizing Prime Min Nawaz Sharif and proposing stronger military role in making policy; Government has been able to exercise authority over military without dire consequences because of profound changes in political structure since landslide election of Sharif 18 months ago that have strengthened prime minister while weakening army; generals have ruled Pakistan for almost half of 51-year history, and prime ministers have been dismissed in earlier clashes; photo (M)
news.title: Pakistani Premier Prevails in Clash With General

news.abstract: Israeli Foreign Min Ariel Sharon, veteran politician and soldier of Arab-Israeli wars, is widely regarded as key player who could make or break Maryland peace summit between Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat, and feelings toward him have been distinctly ambivalent; hopes that his recent appointment as Foreign Minister could make him tough pragmatist in working through functioning deal with Palestinians have been tempered by awareness that he is also hard nationalist who was at forefront of creating West Bank settlements of 1970's and 1980's, voted against Government's decision to withdraw from most of Hebron, has opposed any withdrawal from more than 9 percent of West Bank territory and still regards Yasir Arafat as terrorist whose hand he will not shake; photo (M)
news.title: Sharon's Muscle Evokes Hopes and Some Fears

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  Germany's new government lost its most outspoken advocate of economic change when Jost Stollmann abruptly withdrew as the next economics minister on Monday.
news.title: In Boost for Left Wing, Stollmann Won't Take Economics Portfolio : Free-Marketeer Quits Schroeder's Team

news.abstract: ROME—  Massimo D'Alema became the first former Communist to lead a Western European government on Monday when he succeeded in obtaining the support he needed to form Italy's 56th postwar government.
news.title: Prodi Takes a Swipe At D'Alema for Way Majority Was Formed : Italy Gives Mandate To Former Communist

news.abstract: Roman Catholic Church may play important role in any political compromise that may result in accession of Massimo D'Alma, former Communist who heads largest leftist party in Italy, to post of Prime Minister; remains powerful political constituency; campaigned vehemently against Communist candidates during cold war and hardly relishes seeing former Communist in power (M)
news.title: Ex-Communist at Italy's Helm May, or May Not, Vex the Church

news.abstract: Some 40,000 cows, animal sacred to Hindus, roam streets of New Delhi, often blocking traffic and scavenging through garbage; are threatened by plastic garbage bags, which clog their digestive tracts; cow catchers, who take cows to refuge, often face resistance both from animals and onlookers; photo (M)
news.title: New Delhi Journal; Sacred Cows Are Wily Too; Just Try Catching One

news.abstract: Israeli Army says Salem Rajab al-Sarsour, Hamas militant arrested in grenade attack on Beersheba bus terminal, has confessed to September grenade attack on army post in Hebron and fatal August stabbing of elderly rabbi in Hebron; says he used grenades intended for Jerusalem attack when he became frustrated at failure to get work in Beersheba; Hamas's armed wing claims credit for attack; Palestinian security aide say he acted as individual and attack should not reflect negatively on Palestinians' commitment to cracking down on terrorists (M)
news.title: Beersheba Suspect Confesses to Other Terrorist Attacks, Israeli Army Aides Say

news.abstract: German Chancellor-elect Gerhard Schroder reaches accord with Green Party on shape of new left-of-center coalition Government; six leading economic institutes say his economic program will do little to solve nation's severe unemployment problems; new government will be younger, more female and in many ways more diverse than under Chancellor Helmut Kohl; Green Party will hold key posts for first time, with its leader, Joscka Fischer, named Foreign Minister and 'vice chancellor' (M)
news.title: Pact Reached on Shape of German Coalition

news.abstract: Concern is growing in Siberia that costly effort to keep Russia's Arctic region's eight million people fed and warm is cracking under economic strain; Russian Government is too broke to meet full cost of sending supplies; regional governments are picking up some of slack, even as ruble's crash has sent prices skyrocketing; many regions are also broke and some areas, especially along Russia's long border with Alaska, face winter with few or no supplies; there is talk of evacuating villages; maps; graphs of food output; photos (M)
news.title: Siberia as Winter Comes: Hungry, Cold and Broke

news.abstract: Swiss officials seize over $90 million from Raul Salinas de Gortari, brother of former Pres Carlos Salinas de Gortari of Mexico, after police probe finds he filled Swiss bank accounts with money he got for protecting drug shipments into US; ask Britain to seize added $23.4 million deposited there; find almost 80 witnesses who say they saw Salinas meet with traffickers, introduce them to politicians and get suitcases full of cash; Salinas, jailed in Mexico, denies charges; Swiss file no criminal charges and decline to charge his wife, Paulina Castanon (M)
news.title: Saying Salinas Aided Traffickers, Swiss Seize $90 Million

news.abstract: Amb Abdelhakim Mujahid, senior Taliban official, says Afghanistan will not extradite Osama bin Laden, accused by United States of planning bombings of American embassies in Kenya and Tanzania, interview at United Nations; says Muslim religious authorities will weigh response should US provide credible proof of his involvement; says bin Laden is barred from activities against other nations (M)
news.title: Taliban Aide Casts Doubt on Giving Up bin Laden

news.abstract: PARIS—  Ariane-5, the new European launch rocket, went into space Wednesday, putting into orbit a symbolic payload, a dummy telecommunications satellite, and, more important, Europe's hopes of keeping its leadership in the increasingly competitive global market for commercial space launchings.
news.title: Ariane-5 Success Follows Pair of Failures : Rocket Launch Keeps Europe Alive in Space

news.abstract: Tension, frustration and brinksmanship apparently have been building at Mideast peace talks at sylvan and secluded Wye Plantation, Maryland, erupting in Israeli threats to leave; feints, image and politics seem to be at least as important as substance as Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu comes under intensive pressure; he must either accept United States peace plan and face rebellion from his constituents, reject plan and be denounced by political opponents and much of world or play for more time, option both Pres Clinton and Palestinians seek to cut off; photos (M)
news.title: Fireworks At Wye As Dance Goes On

news.abstract: Congress and Pres Clinton, heeding warning from Central Intelligence Agency Dir George J Tenet that CIA needs big infusion of money and talent to remain relevant, approves $1.8 billion supplemental appropriation in addition to secret 'emergency assistance' approved in Apr; Rep Porter J Goss, former CIA operations officer, sees long-term rebuilding effort, interview; photo (M)
news.title: Big Cash Infusion Aims to Rebuild Anemic C.I.A.

news.abstract: Key points in talks on new Israeli-Palestinian accord focus on Israeli withdrawal from more West Bank land, security issues, custody of Palestinians accused of attacking Israelis, revision of Palestian charter and steps to curb anti-Israeli incitement (M)
news.title: Stalled Accord: Main Points in Dispute

news.abstract: EUROPE    ITALY: BUDGET INTACT -- Italy's new Prime Minister, Massimo D'Alema, left, presented to Parliament a stay-the-course program intended to reassure Italians concerned by the fact that he is the first former Communist to head a government. Mr. D'Alema, who had already promised to adhere to the same 1999 budget drafted by his center-left predecessor, Romano Prodi, also indicated that he would not give in to Communists' demands for a 35-hour work week.   Alessandra Stanley (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Palestinians and Israelis, be they religious or secular, are seen in complete accord on one item: Wye peace conference is not Oslo, in their eyes; they indicate that any legal agreement that would be signed at Wye Plantation in Maryland by two leaders who deeply mistrust each other would not be cause for either panic or celebration engendered by Oslo peace accord in 1993; hoto (M)cve
news.title: From Palestinian or Israeli, The Attitude Is Skepticism

news.abstract: Political controversy in Guatemala surrounding murder nearly six months ago of Juan Gerardi, Roman Catholic bishop and outspoken human rights advocate, continues to grow, while solution to his slaying appears further away than ever; despite mounting evidence to the contrary, Guatemalan Govt continues to maintain that killing was a crime without a political motive; however, Roman Catholic Church and human rights groups contend that elements of Guatemalan armed forces were involved in killing, and point to increasingly bizarre turns case has taken as proof of official cover-up; as result, Gerardi's death has become a major test of 1996 peace accord that brought an end to 36 years of civil war in Guatemala and was supposed to install principle of civilian supremacy; photos of Gerardi and of Rev Mario Orantes Najera, who has been charged with killing (L)
news.title: Guatemala Cover-Up Charged in Killing of Bishop

news.abstract: Arms Control and Disarmament Agency and United States Information Agency are abolished under catchall spending bill signed by Pres Clinton; their responsibilties will pass to State Dept (S)
news.title: Two Foreign Affairs Agencies Are Eliminated

news.abstract: BRUSSELS—  The European Union and other international organizations have brought wealth but not much style to the capital of Europe. The EU institutions, which occupy about 13 percent of the office space in Brussels, have grown haphazardly in response to the changing nature and the successive enlargements of the 15-nation community. It was only in 1992 that heads of government decided once and for all that Brussels would be the EU's permanent home and it is only since comparatively recently that serious thought has been given to the impact this decision will have on the city, at least from an architectural point of view.
news.title: Office-Block Brussels / Bureaucracy Is Their Business : Eurocapital in Search of a Human Dimension

news.abstract: Last minute demand by Israel that US free convicted Israeli spy Jonathan Pollard almost resulted in collapse of peace agreement reached between Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat and Israel's Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu; Netanyahu reportedly threatened to refuse to sign agreement withoutPollard's release, even as Israeli television and radio stations reported his freedom had already been won, infuriating Americans; Clinton Administration officials acknowledge fate of former Navy intelligence analyst had been discussed, but insist issue was never viewed as condition of peace agreement; Pollard is serving life sentence for spying for Isrealin 1980's (M)
news.title: As Deal Came Together, a Snag Over Release of an American Spy

news.abstract: Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat and Israel's Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu, after nine days of tortuous negotiations, sign modest agreement restoring life to Middle East peace effort and opening way for talks on final resolution of 50-year-old fight over possible Palestinian state; Pres Clinton presides over signing ceremony at White House, joined as host by visibly ailing King Hussein of Jordan; agreement in part serves to commit both sides to actions already promised in 1993 and 1995 agreements reached in Oslo; sets detailed timetable for withdrawal of Israeli forces from 13 percent of West Bank in three phases over 12 weeks, beginning soon after ratification, bringing to 40 percent total territory Palestinians control fully or partly; provides for specific steps by Palestinians to fight terrorism and formally amend charter to expunge clauses calling for Israel's destruction; Arafat pledges never to leave peace process or to return to violence and confrontation; Netanyahu says agreement will make Israel and entire region secure; Clinton urges both to carry out commitments and to have courage enough to withstand inevitable attacks from enemies of peace; photos (M)
news.title: ARAFAT AND NETANYAHU IN PACT ON NEXT STEPS TOWARD PEACE; MODEST DEAL TO 'REBUILD TRUST'

news.abstract: EUROPE    ITALY: VOTE OF CONFIDENCE -- Prime Minister Massimo D'Alema won a vote of confidence from the Chamber of Deputies, the lower house of Parliament, for his newly formed government, the first to include Communists in Italy since 1947.   Alessandra Stanley (NYT)    RUSSIA: AN OPTIMISTIC YELTSIN -- President Boris N. Yeltsin said that Russia's economic plight remained difficult but that the country was already starting down the long road out of crisis. Mr. Yeltsin's views are not shared by most officials. Russia is deep in recession, has no clear recovery plan and is threatening to print more money if it does not secure foreign loans. An aide also said that Mr. Yeltsin is fed up with speculation over his ailments and feels hurt that even former allies have fanned the gossip about his health.   (Reuters, Agence France-Presse)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Middle East peace agreement gives Central Intelligence Agency a new and potentially risky role in safeguarding security for Israel and Palestinian Authority; pact empowers intelligence operatives to referee disputes involving handling of suspected terrorists, to monitor who is arrested and jailed by Israeli and Palestinian authorities and to help establish sophisticated and reliable border checkpoints (M)
news.title: New Role As Umpire May Bring More Risk

news.abstract: News analysis of Wye Memorandum, new peace agreement reached between Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat and Israel's Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu; both leaders may have crossed painful and fateful political threshold, despite technical and tentative nature of actual arrangements and despite certainty that they will be violated (M)
news.title: After All the Talk, a Hesitant Peace

news.abstract: European Union leaders attending summit meeting in Alps welcome Yasir Arafat and praise agreement on Israeli withdrawal from additional Palestinian territory as triumph for Pres Clinton; Arafat briefs European leaders on accord and thanks them for years of political and economic aid to Palestinian cause; he and European leaders praise Clinton for his crucial role in reaching new accord (M)
news.title: European Leaders at Summit Greet Arafat and Hail Mideast Pact

news.abstract: United States, China and two Koreas agree on first step toward long-range goal of permanent peace on divided Korean peninsula; working parties will be set up to explore peace treaty to replace armistice that has existed since end of Korean War in 1953, and to take steps to reduce tensions on most heavily defended border in world; progress is made in separate, bilateral discussions between United States and North Korean officials, regarding American concerns that large North Korean underground installation could be used for nuclear purposes; official United States visit to site could be announced soon (M)
news.title: Koreas Take A First Step To Work Out Formal Peace

news.abstract: Argentines are treated to barrage of recent news coverage about suspicious deaths; deaths may simply be series of macabre concidences, but news reports have spawned vague suggestions lately that organized crime or Government of Pres Carlos Saul Menem itself is involved and blocking cause of justice; recent deaths of former presidential aide's brother and navy captain were officially attributed to suicide; list of other dead include general and another army officer who were killed in helicopter crash, two other Government and military employees who died in reported criminal assaults, and several more people who reportedly succumbed to heart attacks and brain seizures; even Pres Menem has called for reopening of probe into death of his son, thought to have been killed in helicopter accident three years ago; Menem's former wife has long expressed skepticism that crash was accident; photo (M)
news.title: Deaths in Argentina Feed a Taste for Conspiracy

news.abstract: United States will reportedly contribute several billion dollars in direct aid or loan guarantees as part of $30 billion global effort to insulate Brazil, and with it rest of Latin America, from worst effects of financial turmoil circling globe; details of American contribution have yet to be negotiated, but Congressional leaders have been alerted to likelihood that Clinton Administration will act while Congress is in recess; biggest role in rescue program for Brazil will be taken by International Monetary Fund, which will contribute at least $15 billion; another $9 billion will come from World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank (M)
news.title: U.S. PLANS TO SEND BILLIONS TO SHIELD BRAZIL'S ECONOMY

news.abstract: Participants at Wye River Middle East conference recall most dramatic moments of all-night stand during which agreement was finally clinched between Israel and Palestinians; say turning point was when Pres Clinton became so angry at Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu that he left room; Netanyahu relented, Clinton returned, and negotiations went into crucial home stretch; other incidents of high drama and some moments of levity recalled (M)
news.title: Mideast Marathon: How 9 Days of Talks Ended in 'the Long Night'

news.abstract: European Union leaders end summit conference, Klagenfurt, Austria, with broad accord on easing economic and monetary policies to guard against world recession; Germany, under new leadership of Chancellor-elect Gerhard Schroder, and other nations that have followed German lead in cutting Government deficits to get ready for common currency, now seem set to press independent European central bank to let them use euro to spur economic growth (M)
news.title: Europe's Leaders End Meeting With Call for Interest Rate Cuts to Fight Slump

news.abstract: Japanese drive to become more efficient to revive economy also poses threat to egalitarianism and other key values; Japan's commitment to equality is producing welfare state for inefficient, leading to growing misallocation of resources; spending to improve quality of life in remote areas helped boost budget deficit, spurring tax increase that plunged Japan into recession; heavy spending on remote school for one pupil is an example of glaring inefficiencies; graph of after-tax income distribution in major economies; maps; photos (M)
news.title: Japanese Are Torn Between Efficiency and Egalitarian Values

news.abstract: Turkey sets new cubs on use of Bosporus, increasing pressure on oil companies to route pipeline to carry Caspian Sea oil through Turkey to port of Ceyhan; Clinton Administration favors Turkish route, which oil companies say is too expensive for now; map (M)
news.title: Turkey Places New Limits on Oil Tanker Traffic in Bosporus

news.abstract: Rivals of Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso of Brazil win key gubernatorial races, complicating his effort to push through long-delayed government and economic reforms; Gov Mario Covas of Sao Paulo, endorsed by Cardoso, seems likely to win re-election over Paulo Maluf, whose victory could have further hurt Cardoso's reform effort (M)
news.title: Election of Rivals in Brazil Hurts Cardoso Reform Plans

news.abstract: Sen Richard C Shelby plans to have his Select Committee on Intelligence hold hearings on Central Intelligence Agency's role in new Israeli-Palestinian peace accord; expresses concern about CIA's open new role in verifying accord as departure from traditional role of intelligence gathering; State Sec Madeleine K Albright says CIA is already engaged in similar work, especially in Middle East; says CIA Dir George J Tenet will explain issues to Congress (M)
news.title: C.I.A.'s Role in Mideast Peace Prompts Outcry and a Call for Senate Hearings

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: CAN'T PAY DEBT -- Russia's Government will owe $17.5 billion in foreign debt next year but won't have sufficient hard currency to pay it, unless Russia first receives international aid, said Aleksandr Zhukov, head of Parliament's budget committee. Mr. Zhukov said tax receipts and other revenues for the first nine months of the year amounted to only 51 percent of targeted totals.    (AP)    RUSSIA: ELECTRICITY SHUT OFF -- At least 76 freight trains were stuck for hours on an eastern stretch of the Trans-Siberian railway after the local electricity company cut off the power for non-payment of bills. Power was restored late in the day, although there was no indication that the $3 million owed had been paid. (Agence France-Presse)    GEORGIA: ARMY BACKING -- President Eduard She-  vardnadze of Georgia, left, defended a decision to use the army to crush a military revolt last week without waiting for parliamentary approval. Mr. Shevardnadze said the revolt took place in a military unit, so the army had been responsible for re-establishing order. (Reuters)    CZECH REPUBLIC: HONOR WITHDRAWN -- President Vaclav Havel has withdrawn a high Czech honor, the Order of the White Lion, which was to be given to the former Mayor of Vienna, Helmut Zilk, because of charges that he was on the payroll of the Communist secret police in the 1960's. Mr. Zilk denied the allegations. (Reuters)    ASIA    AFGHANISTAN: LOOKING AT BIN LADEN -- The Taliban said it is looking into the activities of Osama bin Laden, the wealthy Saudi accused of involvement in the bombings of the American Embassies in Kenya and Tanzania, the BBC reported. It quoted a Taliban spokesman as saying that Mr. bin Laden, who is believed to live in Afghanistan, was not involved in the attacks, but the allegations needed to be cleared up.    INDIA: ONION EXPORTS BANNED -- The Indian Government banned the export of onions, the country's favorite vegetable, after a lingering shortage caused a more than 500 percent jump in its  price. The move comes ahead of local elections next month in New Delhi and three states, where the spiraling price of onions has become a major headache for the Hindu nationalist-led ruling coalition. (Agence France-Presse)    INDIA: 'STRATEGIC SIGNIFICANCE' -- Prime Minister Atal Behari Vajpayee said India's nuclear tests last May were a decisive step toward taking India's ''rightful place'' in a multi-polar world. A Government statement quoted Mr. Vajpayee as telling a conference of military commanders that the series of underground explosions had ''far-reaching strategic significance.'' (Reuters)    JAPAN: BLEAK PROSPECTS -- Japan's prospects for economic recovery remain bleak, and bad debts at its financial institutions threaten further harm to employment and income, the chief of the country's central bank said. Japan's banks are saddled with an estimated $1 trillion in bad debts left over from excessive lending during the 1980's. (AP)    SINGAPORE: ZERO GROWTH -- Singapore's economy will probably have zero growth in 1999, after shrinking in the last two quarters of this year, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said. Singapore's economy is shrinking dramatically, with growth at 1.6 percent in the second quarter of this year, down from 6.1 percent in the first quarter. (AP)    MYANMAR: FACING MORE SANCTIONS -- The European Union decided to step up sanctions against the ruling junta in Myanmar. The group's foreign ministers, meeting in Luxembourg, also said they backed the view of the country's opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi that ''in the present situation, it is inappropriate for tourists to visit Burma,'' as Myanmar was previously called. (Agence France-Presse)    AFRICA    CONGO: NO REBELS AT TALKS -- African defense and foreign ministers began talks in Lusaka aimed at securing a cease-fire in Congo, but rebels fighting to topple President Laurent Kabila were shut out. President Frederick Chiluba of Zambia told ministers from 19 African nations that the only item on the agenda was ending the war in the central African country before conflict spread beyond its borders. (Reuters)    NIGERIA: SUPPORTING CIVILIAN RULE -- The military ruler, Gen. Abdulsalami Abubakar, has warned soldiers not to intervene in Nigeria's planned transition to democracy. ''The Nigerian Army must remain a stabilizing factor ready to do our best to insure continuity,'' General Abubakar said in a leaflet handed out to troops. ''Military action is subordinate to political will.'' (AP)    THE AMERICAS    UNITED NATIONS: SANCTIONS ATTACKED -- The General Assembly adopted a Libyan-sponsored resolution, aimed at the United States, calling for the immediate repeal of laws that unilaterally impose sanctions on companies and nationals of other countries. The vote was 80 in favor, with only the United States and Israel voting against. But 67 delegations abstained, an unusually large number. (Reuters)    PANAMA: HEIR TO RULING PARTY -- Eager to retain power through the American handover of the Panama Canal on Dec. 31, 1999, Panama's ruling Democratic Revolutionary Party has nominated the 35-year-old son of Gen. Omar Torrijos, the country's former strongman, as its candidate in the presidential election next May 2. In primary balloting on Sunday, Martin Torrijos Espino handily defeated nine other aspirants. Larry Rohter (NYT)    ARGENTINA: BRITISH OLIVE BRANCH -- The British  Government offered an olive branch on the eve of a visit by Argentina's President, Carlos Menem, the first since the Falklands war, with Foreign Secretary Robin Cook hinting in London that an arms embargo may be relaxed soon. The embargo has been in place since 1982, when Argentine forces occupied the Falkland Islands, which Argentines call Las Malvinas, and were then expelled by British forces in a war that killed more than 900 men. (Agence France-Presse)    CUBA: KEEPING U.S. REPORTERS OUT -- President Fidel Castro said he was not ready to let American journalists operate permanently in Cuba. ''Once they are established it is hard to remove them,'' Mr. Castro told the leadership of the American Society of Newspaper Editors during a six-hour meeting in Havana. (AP)    BRAZIL: MIXED RESULT FOR CARDOSO -- President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's plan to pull Brazil out of economic turmoil received a strong boost with the re-election of a key ally, Gov. Mario Covas, as Governor of Sao Paulo, Brazil's largest state. But opposition candidates took 5 of the other 12 governorships in voting on Sunday, which many Brazilians saw as a referendum on Cardoso's austerity measures. (AP)    CANADA: EX-LEADER FALLS SHORT -- Former Prime Minister Joe Clark has been forced into a second round in his bid to regain the leadership of the Conservative party. Over the weekend, Mr. Clark, who was Prime Minister of Canada for nine months in 1979, far outdistanced four rivals with 48.7 percent of the party's vote but fell just short of the majority needed to win. A second ballot is expected on Nov. 14. Anthony DePalma (NYT)    CANADA: LOGGERS END BLOCKADE -- A group of Maine loggers angry about a Federal program that allows Canadian woodsmen to work in their state ended a weeklong blockade along the Quebec border today after being threatened with arrest. In agreeing to leave, the loggers said they would give the fEderal and state Governments two weeks to act on their complaints. (AP)    MEXICO: A VICTORY FOR PRI -- Tomas Yarrington Ruvalcaba, the candidate from President Ernesto Zedillo's party, known as the PRI, has won election by a wide margin as Governor of the northeastern state of Tamaulipas, which borders Texas, according to preliminary results of balloting on Sunday. Sam Dillon (NYT)       Compiled by Christopher S. Wren
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: 28-year-old Jewish security guard is shot to death by two Palestinian gunmen in Hebron; 69-year-old Palestinian in slain in apparent act of revenge in Nablus; killings, linked to signing of Israeli-Palestinian peace accord in Washington, are seen by many as manifestation of inevitable spasm of violence that will dog peace effort, and to others as evidence that there is no genuine good will; maps; photo (M)
news.title: A Jew, Then an Arab, Killed in the West Bank

news.abstract: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, in report wrapping up two years of hearings into human-rights abuses during apartheid era, is expected to lay overwhelming blame on Government, but will also implicate African National Congress; some 200 people--including former Pres F W de Klerk and P W Botha, several current ANC cabinet members and Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi, leader of Inkatha Freedom Party--have been notified that report will contain negative findings specifically about them; de Klerk says he will move to block report because of unfounded allegations; photo of commission chairman, Abp Desmond Tutu (M)
news.title: South Africa Braces Itself For Report by Truth Panel

news.abstract: Efforts begin in Geneva and Paris to have former Chilean dictator, Gen Augusto Pinochet, extradited to Spain to stand trial for genocide, even as his lawyers in London move to quash Spanish arrest warrant; his lawyers argue before High Court of Justice that Spanish arrest order is illegal since Pinochet, who has been under arrest at London clinic for past 10 days, is not Spanish citizen; lawyer for Spanish prosecutor defends warrant; says Pinochet was responsible for deaths of at least 4,000 people and had set out to destroy Chilean nationalists who did not share his ideological values (M)
news.title: New Actions On Pinochet Begin in Paris And Geneva

news.abstract: PARIS—  As long as it remains publicly unclear exactly what harm he did to the United States, it will be hard to understand exactly what made Jonathan Pollard, Israel's spy in the Pentagon, such a high-stakes issue that the U.S.-brokered accord last week between Israel and the Palestinians was nearly torpedoed.
news.title: A Spy Mystery:Why Did Clinton Deny Israeli Plea?

news.abstract: Mexico's Congress is adorned with wanted posters bearing image of central bank governor and former Finance Min Guillermo Ortiz Martinez, whom many opposition lawmakers consider to be unrepentant white-collar outlaw and want impeached; he has become opposition target because, as Finance Minister after catastrophic devaluation of peso, he stitched together emergency program in 1995 that subsidized overwhelmed debtors and bought bad loans from failing banks; opposition has accused Government of seeking to rescue high-living bankers at expense of overburdened taxpayers (M)
news.title: Mexico's Wanted Poster Exchanges Black Hat for White Collar

news.abstract: Gerhard Schroeder, Social Democrat, becomes Germany's seventh postwar Chancellor and first member of his party to lead country since unification in 1990; is officially elected in emotional session by Parliament in 351-287 vote; is congratulated by outgoing Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who governed for 16 years; official transition comes month after Schroeder swept to victory in election that showed strong desire for change in Europe's most powerful state; photo (M)
news.title: Era of Schroder and His Generation Begins

news.abstract: NATO suspends immediate threat of air strikes against Yugoslavia, concluding that Pres Slobodan Milosevic is in substantial compliance with demands to end attacks against ethnic Albanians in Serbian province of Kosovo; agrees to extend indefinitely so-called activation order that authorizes use of force and keeps more than 400 warplanes on alert; Pres Clinton welcomes development; says NATO's willingness to act, combined with determined diplomacy, created chance to end suffering and repression in Kosovo; confusion still persists over exact number of troops remaining in Kosovo despite pullout since NATO eased initial demands on number of special paramilitary police officers it is prepared to allow to remain (M)
news.title: SERBIAN PULLOUTS LEAD NATO TO LIFT THREAT OF ATTACK

news.abstract: Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel, under pressure from right-wingers, postpones ratification of new Israeli-Palestinian peace accord by Cabinet until Palestinians show plan to fight terrorism to US; postponement comes hours after Palestinian police report arrest of killers of Jewish settler, Danny Vargas, in Hebron--swift reponse seen as outcome of accord; postponement draws angry condemnations from Palestinian officials, who accuse Netanyahu of appeasing right-wing critics who have mounted fierce campaign against agreement and have vowed to unseat him; photo (M)
news.title: ISRAELIS POSTPONE VOTE ON RATIFYING NEW PEACE ACCORD

news.abstract: Article profiles Canada's Prime Min Jean Chretien, whose five years in office has been marked by directness uncommon among world leaders; at time of roundabout diplomacy and executive legalisms, he can be outspoken and blunt to degree that frightens and frustrates his handlers; photo (M)
news.title: Just Blunt, or a Bully? Canada Divided on Leader

news.abstract: Israel's Labor Party, which has promised to back Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu against his former allies on right to protect his peace accord with Palestinians, balks at endorsing him or his budget; Netanyahu backs down, delaying budget; episode makes clear to many Labor members awkwardness of their current role; they are concerned that he could retain power in any new elections by cutting into centrist constituency and that election could disrupt peace effort (M)
news.title: Peace Accord Leaves Israeli Labor Party in a Tough Spot Over Whether to Topple Netanyahu

news.abstract: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission is on verge of withholding its final report in face of court challenges from ex-Pres F W de Klerk and African National Congress, both apparently accused of gross human rights violations during apartheid era; Abp Desmond Tutu, panel chairman, is furious at last-minute tactics; says panel will reluctantly delete reference to de Klerk, but needs time to fight legal challenge; photo (M)
news.title: South Africa Truth Commission May Withhold Its Report

news.abstract: Serb forces and ethnic Albanians in Kosovo, Serbia, fueled by deepening hatred, seek ways to continue fighting around truce demanded and enforced by West; Kosovo Liberation Army takes lead in burial of youth killed by booby trap left behind by Serb police, Dragobilje; vows revenge; photo (M)
news.title: Despite a Truce, Kosovo Albanians Dig New Graves and Vow Revenge

news.abstract: Stanford University colleagues say Hua Di, top Chinese missile scientist who has lived in United States since 1989, was arrested in Jan on his first trip home and awaits trial for allegedly revealing state secrets; he had been assured by Chinese security officials that he would not be arrested; American Embassy says it has raised issue with China; Stanford officials have protested to Pres Jiang Zemin; colleagues express concerns about his health (M)
news.title: China Expert On Missiles Is Arrested On Return

news.abstract: Iran, as part of crackdown on Bahai faith, its largest religious minority, has shut down stealth university where volunteer faculty was educating nearly 1,000 students; school was started in 1987 in reaction to virtual ban of Bahais from Iranian universities; operated so quietly that many Bahai officials abroad and many intellectuals within Iran were unaware of it (M)2
news.title: Iran Closes 'University' Run Covertly By the Bahais

news.abstract: Opponents of Indonesia's control over disputed territory of East Timor say that documents leaked from Indonesian Ministry of Defense show that the army is not drawing down its forces in territory as Govt has reported (M)
news.title: Army Pullback in East Timor Disputed by Leaked Reports

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: BLAIR AIDE FORCED TO QUIT -- The Government of Prime Minister Tony Blair has suffered its first forced resignation since taking office 18 months ago. Ron Davies is out as Secretary for Wales after he was robbed Monday night by strangers he invited into his car in an area known as a meeting place for homosexuals and drug dealers. Mr. Blair has often attacked the previous Conservative Government for the number of its members who left office in disgrace.   Warren Hoge (NYT)    BRITAIN: NEW VOTE PROCEDURES PROPOSED -- A commission headed by the former Finance Minister, Lord Jenkins, proposed new proportional voting procedures in elections for the House of Commons that would give small parties greater representation and make Continental-style coalition governments more likely. Prime Minister Tony Blair has promised a referendum on the current ''first-past-the-post'' electoral system, in which the winner takes all, sometimes even without a majority of votes.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Gurkha guards of Nepal, who long served in British Army in Hong Kong, but who found themselves relieved of duty when Britain handed Hong Kong over to China last year, have reinvented themselves as protectors of choice for Hong Kong's rich; business people, fearing wave of kidnappings, are hiring Gurkhas by the dozens to protect themselves and their families; photos (M)
news.title: Hong Kong Journal; For Fearfully Rich, a New Fad: A Fierce Gurkha

news.abstract: Jeep carrying Israeli soldiers intercepts Palestinian suicide bomber as he is about to ram car packed with explosives into school bus carrying children from Jewish settlement at Kfar Darom, Gaza; jeep absorbs explosion, which kills one soldier and wounds three others; bomber also dies; Yasir Arafat issues quick and unusually fierce condemnation of attack and then places under house arrest Sheik Ahmed Yassin, spiritual leader of Islamic fundamentalist group Hamas; drawing; photo; illus (M)
news.title: Israeli Jeep Blocks a Bomber From School Bus Carrying 40

news.abstract: Excerpts from final report issued by South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission (M)
news.title: Pretoria's Words: 'Extrajudicial Killing'

news.abstract: PARIS—  As visitors streamed into the Maison de la Chimie to view the Picasso memorabilia that sold this week for 205 million francs, some must have wondered whether the Paris School master had not played a phenomenal prank on society.
news.title: Dora Maar's Picassos:A Trek Through Classicism and Caricature

news.abstract: Ali A Mohamed, former sergeant in US Army who is being held in connection with terrorist campaign of Osama bin Laden, was rejected in 1980's when he offered himself to CIA as spy; CIA officials decided that Mohamed, who was officer in Egyptian military at time, was too unreliable to be useful agent inside Egypt (M)
news.title: C.I.A. Said to Reject Bomb Suspect's Bid to be Spy

news.abstract: Leading industrial nations endorse Pres Clinton's proposal to help protect vulnerable but essentially healthy nations from currency and stock market upheavals that have battered nations from Asia and Latin America; proposal establishes new line of credit that would make billions of dollars available to some countries to ward off attacks on their currencies or markets that are set off by economic troubles elsewhere; plan, announced by Group of Seven industrial nations, offers new strategy for International Monetary Fund, which has usually offered money only after country is in deep economic trouble; plan was developed Treasury Sec Robert E Rubin and his aides (M)
news.title: Wealthy Nations Back Plan To Speed Help to the Weak

news.abstract: Security Council outlines how it might proceed with comprehensive review of Iraq's relations with United Nations, if and when Pres Saddam Hussein allows arms inspections to resume; issue of Iraq's ban on spot inspections, imposed on Aug 5, and prospects for review, are likely to be discussed by Security Council with US Rep Peter Burleigh in president's chair for Nov (M)
news.title: Security Council Outlines New Strategy on Iraq Arms

news.abstract: Three major United Nations agencies and World Bank are joining forces in coordinated campaign against malaria, leading killer of world's poorest people; project will be coordinated by World Health Organization in cooperation with UN Development Program, Unicef and World Bank; new drive is first project undertaken by WHO's new director general, Dr Gro Harlem Brundtland (M)
news.title: U.N. and World Bank Unite To Wage War on Malaria

news.abstract: Serb Pres Slobodan Milosevic is moving to still academic voices he considers troublesome to his regime; Vladimir Vodinelic, law professor at Belgrade University for 27 years, was dismissed four months ago, and blames revival of old Communist category of the politically correct person'; his photo; Milsevic is aided by coalition partners, Vojislav Seselj of far right party and his wife's far-left party; loyalty to triumvirate is now ticket to academic promotion; numerous professors have been ousted or banned from classrooms, with departments reorganized under loyalist deans; academics say Milosevic seems to believe that having given concessions to US on Kosovo he is free to do as he wishes elsewhere (M)
news.title: Yugoslav Wields Ax in 'Pacification' of Academia

news.abstract: *Libyan regime continues to project defiance, mocking six years of UN sanctions, but Col Muammar el-Qaddafi nevertheless is reported considering deal offered by US and Britain; he would be required to turn over two suspects in bombing of Pan Am flight 103 for trial in Netherlands by Scottish judges, and sanctions would be lifted as soon as two are surrendered; their photos; map (M)
news.title: Despite Bluster, Qaddafi Weighs Deal for 2 Bombing Suspects

news.abstract: Private aid groups, currently sending millions of dollars worth of food and medicine to relieve starvation and suffering in Sudan, are pressing the United Nations to make a vigorous new effort to end the nearly 30-year civil war there instead of merely feeding its victims.
news.title: Aid Groups Press U.N. for New Effort to End Sudan's Civil War

news.abstract: Pierre-Richard Prosper discusses his decision to give up comfortable lawyer's life in Los Angeles to work in Tanzania for UN war-crimes tribunal; Prosper has become first prosecutor to get genocide verdict involving killings in Rwanda in 1994, and he also persuaded judges to include rape among crmes constituting genocide; 35-year-old son of Haitian immigrants lived in New York and later worked for Los Angeles district attorney's office prosecuting gang members (S)
news.title: U.S. Lawyer A Champion Of Victims In Rwanda

news.abstract: King Hussein's cancer has inspired those around him in Jordan's ruling circles to plan for seamless transition that king himself envisioned when he named his younger brother, Crown Prince Hassan, as his successor more than three decades ago; 51-year-old Crown Prince, in rare interview, talks about close relationship with king, his aspirations for regional peace and irritation with those who criticize his manner as overly erudite and intellectual; photo; Hassan has been standing in since king went to Mayo Clinic for cancer treatment more than three months ago (M)
news.title: King Hussein Ails. His Brother Waits.

news.abstract: Hamas, militant Islamic group, lashes back at crackdown by Palestinian Authority by warning for first time that it might turn guns on Yasir Arafat's police force; Maj Gen Ghazi Jabali, Palestinian chief of police, says his officers will respond, and issues orders to shoot suspected assailants; threat by Hamas contradicts its longstanding position of avoiding civil war; signals deepening crisis with Palestinian Authority following signing of Isralei-Palestinian peace accord; since thwarted suicide bombing against Israeli school bus in Gaza Strip on October 29, Palestinian police have rounded up estimated 300 Hamas followers and placed leader, Sheik Ahmed Yassin, under house arrest (M)
news.title: After Crackdown, Militant Group Threatens Arafat's Forces

news.abstract: Peng Ming, leader of China Development Union, independent research group closed down by Government, is refused permission to leave China, and his passport is confiscated; is apprehended while trying to cross into Hong Kong; planned to travel to US, where he was invited to speak at Harvard and Columbia universities (M)
news.title: China Blocks Chief of Independent Research Group From Traveling

news.abstract: Israel holds first nationwide memorial for Prime Min Yitzhak Rabin, who was assassinated in 1995, signaling concerted effort to transform him from partisan hero into figure of consensus or national symbol of peace; politicians of all stripes gather at his grave in Jerusalem, broadening mourning that, until recently, has been domain of only centrists and leftists; as Israelis vent feelings in discussion groups nationwide, it remains clear that trauma of assassination remainly at least partly undigested and unresolved, as is fate of peace accord with Palestinians signed recently by Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu; photos (M)
news.title: Rabin's Lot Is Rancor, In Death As in Life

news.abstract: Unrest is building in Yugoslav republic of Montenegro, where Pres Milo Djukanovic and other leaders say they would like to remain part of Yugoslavia, but not if federation with Serbia means submitting to autocracy or Slobodan Milosevic, Yugoslav President; Montenegrins, who for most part have no ethnic or religious quarrels to pick with Serbia, say they hope to create open and democratic society as example of how all Yugoslavs should be able to live; are falling back on tradition of smuggling to achieve goals, arguing that this is only way to subsidize government cut off financially by Belgrade; smuggling has become problem for Western countries that praise Montenegrans for challenging Milosevic; map (M)
news.title: The Next Trouble Spot in the Balkans: Montenegro

news.abstract: Residents of Mexico City are abandoning once-sacrosanct tradition of long, leisurely lunches; many have grown too busy, are following international corporate schedule, or consider fast-food dining more efficient; many working-class Mexicans simply can no longer afford slightest culinary extravagance; photo (M)
news.title: Mexico City Journal; Let's All Do Lunch the Modern Way: Make It Fast

news.abstract: Libyan Govt of Col Muammar el-Qaddafi warns shopkeepers to lower prices to officially dictated levels or face violence by dreaded 'purification committees' (M)
news.title: Cut Prices Or Else, Libya Tells Its Shops

news.abstract: Prime Min Bertie Ahern of Irish Republic confers with Catholic and Protestant leaders of new Northern Ireland Assembly in an attempt to restart stalled Ulster peace effort, two days after killing of Brian Service, Roman Catholic man, in Belfast; is seeking to allay fears that murder, apparently by Protestant splinter guerrilla group, will lead to renewed violence (M)
news.title: Irish Leader Urges Restarting Ulster Peace Drive

news.abstract: Rescue workers throughout Central America struggle to reach scores of remote peasant settlements left battered and isolated by Hurricane Mitch as authorities in Nicaragua and Honduras predict combined death toll may exceed 7,000; focus of Nicaraguan rescue efforts is Posoltega region, located at foot of Casitas volcano, 50 miles northwest of capital of Managua, where 800 people are confirmed dead in mudslides and at least 2,000 are reported missing; Pres Carlos Flores Facusse, in grim television address, describes 'panorama of death, desolation and ruin' throughout entire country; numerous deaths and widespread damage to property and crops also reported in El Salvador and Guatemala; photos; map (M)
news.title: OFFICIALS PREDICT HURRICANE'S TOLL WILL EXCEED 7,000

news.abstract: Maj Pierre Bunel, French military officer at NATO headquarters in Brussels, is arrested on suspicion of telling Serbia about targets alliance was planning to bomb if Serbian forces failed to halt attacks against civilians in Kosovo Province; is accused of passing top secret documents to Serbian agents (S)
news.title: French Major Held in Spying At NATO Panel

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: TO PRINT $759 MILLION IN 2 MONTHS -- Russia plans to print a maximum of $759 million by the end of the year. Deputy Prime Minister Yuri D. Maslyukov said Russian and International Monetary Fund experts had worked out the limit. Another Deputy Prime Minister, Valentina Matvienko, said the Government would not be able to pay all the back wages promised to state workers before the end of the year.   (Agence France-Presse)
news.title: World Briefs

news.abstract: LONDON—  Ever since the introduction of the World Wide Web began triggering explosive growth of Internet use earlier this decade, technology gurus have been predicting a convergence between conventional voice telephony and the rapidly evolving market for transmitting data.
news.title: With Explosion in Data Networking, Companies Readjust Strategies to Meet New Demands : Equipment Makers Race to Get Right Products

news.abstract: Report by fact-finding team accuses members of Indonesian military of helping to instigate violence and looting in capital of Jakarta in May that killed nearly 1,200 people and led to resignation of President Suharto (S)
news.title: Indonesian Army Is Blamed For Role in Spring Violence

news.abstract: Israel and Palestinians appeal to US to salvage land-for-security peace accord, which has been severely tested by pattern of postponements by Israel's Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu, who has again delayed presenting it Cabinet for ratification because of persistent pressure from right-wingers; he is demanding that US wrest from Palestinians written timetable for arresting 30 fugitives wanted for terrorism; Palestinians accuse Netanyahu of political brinksmanship; accuse Israel of taking advantage of delays to establish footholds for new settlements on West Bank, which would be illegal once agreement takes effect; implore US to compel him to move beyond impasse; Statye Dept spokesman says Palestinians have submitted acceptable security plan, meeting their obligations for accord to take effect, and that US believes there is no reason to delay implementation; photo (M)
news.title: Middle East Accord in Peril As Both Sides Appeal to the U.S.

news.abstract: Spain's Prime Minister, Jose Maria Aznar, authorizes Govt to talk with people close to leading Basque guerrilla group to test trustworthiness of rebels, who recently announced indefinite cease-fire; has said that peace talks cannot be held directly with rebel group until it permanently renounces violence (M)
news.title: Spain Making Contact With Basque Rebels

news.abstract: Gen Olsegun Abasanjo, President of Nigeria from 1976 to 1979 who is country's only military ruler to relinquish power to civilian Govt, announces plans to run again and is immediately regarded by many Nigerians as front-runner in elections set for February 1999; emerged from three yers in prison in June, shortly after death of dictator, Gen Sani Abacha; pledge by military Govt to hand power over to civilian President in May 1999 noted (M)
news.title: Popular Ex-President Announces Plans to Run Again in Nigeria

news.abstract: Thousands of the 2.3 million high school students in France plan to resume protests against shortage of teachers and shortcomings in curriculum with demonstration in Paris; but at Lycee Gaston Bachelard in Paris suburb of Chelles, as in other schools across the country, students are torn about how hard to keep pushing; map (M)
news.title: French Youths Strike for the Right to Study Hard

news.abstract: Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu is set to present to Israeli cabinet West Bank withdrawal agreement reached last month with Yasir Arafat; Netanyahu has been delaying deal, which was reached at talks with Pres Clinton, because of dispute over when Palestinians would arrest 30 people wanted by Israel on charges of involvement in the deaths of Israelis; Arafat says 12 of the 30 have been arrested and rest are being pursued (M)
news.title: Netanyahu, After Delay, Will Offer Wye Pact to Cabinet

news.abstract: United States, in effort to prevent nuclear weapons and materials from being smuggled out of Russia, announces plans to train Russian customs agents in identifying and arresting smugglers; US Customers Service plan includes training Russian agents at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, Engergy Department's nuclear reservation in Paso, Wash (M)
news.title: U.S. Enlists Russians to Spot Nuclear Smuggling

news.abstract: Israeli Ambassador to Vatican, Aharon Lopez, urges it to wait 50 years before moving ahead with any plan to beatify Pope Pius XII, who has been criticized by Jewish groups and others for remaining silent during Holocaust (M)
news.title: Israeli Diplomat Urges Vatican to Delay Beatification of Pius XII

news.abstract: Federal grand jury in Manhattan returns 238-count indictment charging Saudi exile Osama bin Laden in bombings of two US Embassies in Kenya and Tanzania in Aug and with conspiring to commit other acts of terrorism against Americans abroad; Government officials offer two rewards of $5 million each for information leading to arrest or conviction of bin Laden and Muhammad Atef, his chief military commander; prosecutors also unseal earlier indictment, issued in June, that includes similar but less detailed charges against bin Laden; new indictment accuses him of leading vast terrorist conspiracy from 1989 to present, in which he is said to have been working in concert with Sudan, Iraq and Iran and terrorist groups to build weapons and attack US military installations; photos (M)
news.title: SAUDI IS INDICTED IN BOMB ATTACKS ON U.S. EMBASSIES

news.abstract: Berlin court rules that city's 35,000 Muslim children will be allowed to receive Islamic religious instruction in schools for first time; decision reflects Germany's gradual and painful reconciliation with fact that it is multi-ethnic state with large population of foreigners (M)
news.title: Long Dispute Ends as Berlin Court Backs Islamic School Lessons

news.abstract: Assistant Sec of State Susan E Rice ends weeklong trip to Africa by urging political solution to civil war in Congo, which has drawn in neighboring countries and threatens to widen into larger regional conflict (M)
news.title: U.S. Diplomat Pleads for Political Solution to Civil War in Congo

news.abstract: Brazilian Congress approves measures intended to reduce imbalances between its public and private pension systems, a major element of Government's austerity plan and critical step in restoring confidence of foreign investors and international monetary fund (M)
news.title: Brazil's Austerity Plan Clears Important Hurdle on Pension Cost

news.abstract: Upcoming Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Malaysia could hardly be held in a more provocative place; Malysia recently imposed sweeping controls on flow of capital in its stock and currency markets, particularly on investment from overseas; in doing so, Prime Min Mahathir Mohamad has in effect slammed the door on global economy that Pres Clinton and other leaders are coming to Malaysia to champion; photo (M)
news.title: Malaysia to Be Unlikely Host at Economic Meeting

news.abstract: Foundation for Human Rights in Cuba, an exile group in Miami, files suit in Spain against Pres Fidel Castro for human rights abuses (S)
news.title: Exiles Sue Castro in Spain

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: CRITICIZED ON ECONOMIC RETREAT -- Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott attacked Russia's retreat from free-market economics and warned that financial decline could lead to ''political drift, turmoil and even crack up'' there. Help from the International Monetary Fund, Mr. Talbott said in a speech at Stanford University, ''must wait until the Russian Government shows itself willing and able to make the difficult structural adjustments necessary for recovery and growth.'''   (Reuters)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Burning question for Kremlin these days is food; with winter fast approaching, nation is locked in primal struggle to feed its citizens and prevent them from freezing; it is race against time; food reserves are dwindling; remote cities are left without heat; and huge logistical task of moving grain, meat and fuel is well behind schedule; it is a mark of Russia's anxiety that Prime Min Yevgeny M Primakov's aides put aside its pride to buy $625 million worth of grain, meat, soybeans and other food from United States; photo (M)
news.title: Food Crisis Forces Russia To Swallow Its Pride

news.abstract: Chase Manhattan Corp says that it is investigating allegations that it froze accounts of Jewish customers in Paris during Nazi occupation of France before formal orders to freeze accounts were issued; Chase, one of largest American banks, says it is also examining whether its Paris office was 'overly cooperative' in providing banking services to Germany during occupation and whether assets seized by Nazis and Vichy Govt were ever returned (S)
news.title: Chase Reviews Nazi-Era Role

news.abstract: A day after France's Socialist Prime Minister called for the rehabilitation of French soldiers executed for refusing to fight in a World War I battle that cost 300,000 French lives, the country's Gaullist conservative President, Jacques Chirac, today called the Prime Minister's remarks ''inopportune.''    The 1917 battle, along a ridge road called the Chemin des Dames, remains a sensitive subject in France as it prepares to celebrate the 80th anniversary of the Nov. 11 armistice that ended the war.
news.title: World War I Sets Off A New Battle In France

news.abstract: People in Goma, Congo, rebels' home base, express skepticism, war-weariness and outright hostility at another rebellion, second one in two years, when last one produced so little to improve their lives; they say rebel troops are corrupt, and that in reality, rebellion is 'a foreigners' movement'; photo; map (M)
news.title: Goma Journal; One Rebellion Too Many for War-Weary Congolese

news.abstract: Most vexing of Russia's problems lie in its Rust Belt, interlocking series of industrial giants now living off barter and choking on bloated work force; many of industries are pillars of communities that have no other reason for being; solving their problems without causing social upheaval will be key test for Russia's new Government, headed by Prime Min Yevgeny M Primakov and staffed with old-style Soviet ministers who have pointedly set out to rescue Russian industry; many fault Pres Boris N Yeltsin's team of young free-market reformers for failing to anticipate economic disarray--and corruption--that followed their lifting of state controls; Magnitogorsk, once largest steel mill in former Soviet Union, is producing less than half raw steel it did decade ago, with same work force; bottom has fallen out of its domestic market as Russian factories that buy steel approach bankruptcy and struggle to sell what Russians either do not want or cannot afford; photos; map; charts (L)
news.title: Facing Oblivion, Rust-Belt Giants Top Russian List Of Vexing Crises

news.abstract: Russia and United States are engaged in trade war over hot-rolled steel; American steel makers brought anti-dumping case in Washington against Russia, Japan and Brazil, contending that their foreign competitors are selling steel below cost in United States, at grave damage to domestic industry; Russia is not biggest exporter of hot-rolled steel to US, but Russian producers have been squeezed by drop in domestic demand and collapse of their markets in Southeast Asia, and they have stepped up their shipments to US; imports of Russian steel rose to 2.2 million tons in first seven months of 1998; in Magnitogorsk, heart of Russian steel industry, exports to US are matter of survival (M)
news.title: Rising Russian Imports Fuel Dispute With U.S. Steel Makers

news.abstract: Chemin des Dames quarries in eastern France bear German, American and French World War I graffiti; nearby Fort Malmaison in Braye-en-Laonnnois was held by German invaders from 1914 to 1917 against countless French attacks; area is still marked by artillery shell craters and trench lines; World War I buffs digging near underground limestone quarries found evidecne left by soldiers of three nations who had fought one another in subterranean labybrinth for three years; photo; map (M)
news.title: Etched in Stone, Words From Great War's Dead

news.abstract: Revolution Day, formerly premier feast of Soviet Communism, is commemorated by 10,000 people who march through center of Moscow; turnout is better than in recent years, reflecting impact of latest economic crisis; in old Soviet days, Nov 7 was marked with military parade with huge banners proclaiming Soviet achievement and might (M)
news.title: For a Day, Russians Are United In Nostalgia

news.abstract: Huge amounts of oil and gas are believed to lie beneath Caspian Sea, and three new nations that share its shoreline--Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan--stand to reap billions of dollars; because Caspian region is landlocked, pipelines must be built to carry its oil to world markets; oil companies will soon announce which route they prefer for their main export pipeline from Baku in Azerbaijan; United States and many other nations believe decision will have profound economic and geopolitical consequences, and are lobbying intensely for their favored routes; Clinton Administration wants oil companies to build their pipeline across Georgia and Turkey; that route would promote American interests in region, but would be far more costly to construct than other routes being considered; Russia and Iran are pushing routes of their own, urging companies not to commit themselves to American-backed one; photos; map (L)
news.title: On Piping Out Caspian Oil, U.S. Insists the Cheaper, Shorter Way Isn't Better

news.abstract: Two Isrealis, Udi Hargov and Yigal Damary, are arrested on suspicion of spying on military installation in Cyprus, raising questions in Israel about whether it is latest in series of bungles by Israeli intelligence agency, Mossad; arrest spotlights increased regional tensions about growing security cooperation between Israel and Turkey (M)
news.title: Jailed Israelis: A Spy Fiasco Or a Warning By Cyprus?

news.abstract: Tibetans nurture fervent desire to see Dalai Lama, their exiled god and king, return to Potala Palace, and political atmosphere in China seems more open to negotiations on issue than at any time in a decade; Dalai Lama is proposing new initiative that he hopes will lead to talks with Chinese leaders, and he is expected seek support for it when he meets with Vice Pres Al Gore during his current visit to Washington; map; photo (M)
news.title: As Dalai Lama Woos Beijing, Tibetans Pray for His Return

news.abstract: HONG KONG—  A battle is intensifying between two of Asia's largest financial centers as a rapidly liberalizing Singapore and an increasingly interventionist Hong Kong seek to gain the upper hand in lucrative financial sector trading.
news.title: 2 Asian Tigers Gird for Battle to Get Lion's Share of Financial Trading

news.abstract: Over 100,000 people are expected to attend five-day Slow Food festival in Turin, Italy, celebrating languourous enjoyment of slowly prepared regional delicacies and demonstrating their disdain for fast food; Slow Food movement was begun 13 years ago by journalist Carlo Petrini and group of leftist intellectuals; has become fashionable in Italy and throughout Europe, with 40,000 members in 35 countries; it is catching on via Internet with American food and wine connoisseurs; photos (M)
news.title: Turin Journal; The Militant Epicures: Even the Barricades Groan

news.abstract: Gen Augusto Pinochet, former Chilean dictator, says he is 'hurt and bewildered' by his arrest in London, and he vows to fight attempts to extradite him to Spain to stand trial; photo (M)
news.title: Pinochet Vows to Fight 'With All My Spirit'

news.abstract: Interview with Dr Henry Morgentaler, Canada's most famous and vilified doctor performing abortions, who refuses to be silenced in wake of Buffalo, NY, slaying of Dr Barnett Slepian; murder has made clear that shootings of three Canadian doctors who performed abortions were linked and focused attention on Morgentaler; photo (M)
news.title: Toronto Journal; Canadian Fashion: Doctors in Bulletproof Vests

news.abstract: Local election campaigns have been particularly down and dastardly in Israel this season, with far more violence than in past; ethnicity, religious-secular divides, clan rivalries and municipal scandals inflame passions; dirty tricks are commonplace; map; photo (M)
news.title: Local Elections in Israel: A Virtual Free-for-All

news.abstract: Lord Hunt of Llanfairwaterdine, who led expedition in 1953 in which Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became first people to reach top of Mount Everest, dies at age 88; photo (M)
news.title: Lord Hunt, 88, Everest Trek Leader, Dies

news.abstract: Gen Augusto Pinochet's lawyer, tells Britain's highest court that his detention threatens 'delicate balance' between 'interests of justice and state stability' in Chile; holds Chile has made its peace with former dictator (M)
news.title: Pinochet Lawyer Asks Britain To Recognize Chile's Wishes

news.abstract: Mexican Pres Ernesto Zedillo's governing party wins gubernatorial races in Sinaloa and Puebla and may have regained municipal control over three state capitals that had fallen to opposition, closing out election year in which it has repeatedly humbled bickering opposition rivals; results fuel party's hopes of extending its 70-year domination of Mexican politics; leftist coalition wins governorship of Tlaxcala (M)
news.title: PRI Reverses Fortunes and Wins Crucial Mexican Governorships

news.abstract: Gen Jose Luis Chavez says rival marijuna-smuggling gang led by Lino Quintana was responsible for Sept massacre of 19 men, women and children at home of Fermin Castro, near Ensenada, Mex, news conference; says Quintana and his armed colleagues were drunk and high on cocaine when their talks with Castro turned violent; three people have been arrested; Quintana remains at large (M)
news.title: Mexican Official Links Massacre To Drug Rivalry

news.abstract: Rumors of blooming romance between British Prince Andrew and Argentine Pres Carlos Saul Menem's daughter, Zulema Maria Eva Menem, while most likely highly exaggerated, are being taken in Argentina as sign that two nations are finally putting 1982 Falkland Islands war behind them; Pres Menem apparently encourages gossip; photo (M)
news.title: Argentina Hears Rumors Of a Royal British Suitor

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  Unhappy German merchants already felt squeezed by a six-year slump before a fearsome new rival threatened to make things worse.
news.title: In Germany, Wal-Mart Touches Off a Price War

news.abstract: Dalai Lama, Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, meets with Pres Clinton, Washington, DC; presses for talks with China aimed at gaining some autonomy for Tibet; United States says Clinton agrees with him on need for direct talks; he also meets with Vice Pres Al Gore, Hillary Rodham Clinton and State Sec Madeleine K Albright (M)
news.title: Dalai Lama Tells Clinton of Chinese Balkiness

news.abstract: Brazil, which pledged to slash discretionary spending by $7 billion in effort to bolster its economic credibility, releases revised budget figures showing true cuts will be about half of promised amount; total spending will actually rise in 1999 (M)
news.title: Brazilians Scale Back Pledges to Cut Budget

news.abstract: In an important breakthrough, Argentina signaled that it would become the first developing country to adopt binding targets for controlling emissions of industrial waste gases that are believed to cause global warming. Until now, developing countries had presented a united front in resisting specific limits on their emissions of such gases, which are produced by the burning of coal, oil, wood and natural gas. Developed countries had agreed last December in Kyoto, Japan, to reduce emissions by an average of about 5 percent below 1990 levels in the period 2008 to 2012. However, poorer nations have refused to follow suit until industrial countries actually show results.    Article, page A7.
news.title: Argentina Joins War On Global Warming

news.abstract: Sec of State Madeleine K Albright says Israeli Cabinet's approval of Middle East accord is 'important step forward in the peace process' (M)
news.title: U.S. Calls Israeli Vote 'Step Forward' to Peace

news.abstract: New American Academy opens in Berlin mansion that was once wartime home of Hitler's chief economic adviser, Walther Funk; much of founding grant for academy was provided by descendants of Hans Arnhold, Jewish banker who fled mansion; former Sec of State Henry A Kissinger attends opening (M)
news.title: Germany and U.S. Nurture Bond At a Mansion With a Few Ghosts

news.abstract: Three legal experts appointed by Sec Gen Kofi Annan will go to Cambodia to study documents on Khmer Rouge atrocities and recommend how and where tribunal should judge those crimes; legal panel consists of Sir Ninian Stephen, Steven Ratner and Rajsoomer Lallah (M)
news.title: U.N. Panel to Visit Cambodia to Study Khmer Rouge Atrocities

news.abstract: Some two hundred people who have lost money in multimillion-dollar futures-market scam hold protest in Beijing, China (S)
news.title: March of the Sadly Bilked

news.abstract: KUALA LUMPUR—  Japan has mustered enough support from other Asian and Pacific countries hit hard by the region's economic crisis to derail a "fast-track" trade-liberalization plan that Washington says is critical if it is to combat protectionism in America, officials said Thursday.
news.title: Japan Moves to Thwart APEC's Free-Trade Plan

news.abstract: Morton H Halperin, former White House and Pentagon official, will become director of policy planning at State Department (S)
news.title: New Policy Planning Chief

news.abstract: Taxicab drivers strike in Rome, charging that mayor's proposal to allow them to set their own prices and hours would impoverish them; strike highlights attachment to statist status quo, even as country tries to liberalize economy by easing crippling bureaucracy and inflexibility in work force (S)
news.title: You Really Can't Get a Cab When Rome Proposes Reforms

news.abstract: Arrest of Gen Augusto Pinochet in London, on charges of human rights violations, revives deadly political grudges in Paine, town of grape and citrus growers in Chile; photo; map; mothers and sisters of men who disappeared after coup against Salvador Allende in 1973 speak bitterly of their loss and humiliation at hands of former soldiers and paramilitaries; Paine's turmoil began in late 1960's when landless farmers squatted on unused ranch land; invasions increased when Allende came to power in 1970 and socialist activists helped peasants organize cooperatives; movement came to violent end in 1973 (Paine Journal) (M)
news.title: Paine Journal; Pinochet's Arrest Revives Buried Fears in Chile

news.abstract: Israelis calmly pick up gas masks in case of Iraqi missile attack; people in Ramat Gan, which was hit hard by Iraqi missiles during Persian Gulf war, comment on latest crisis; Israeli officials are keeping low profile, avoiding threats of retaliation even as US prepares for possible military strike (S)
news.title: Israel Calmly Readies Itself, Just in Case

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: TROOP REDUCTION IN ULSTER  Because of the improving security situation, British troop levels in Northern Ireland are being reduced to 15,000, 2,000 fewer than this summer and the smallest number since 1970. Chief Constable Ronnie Flanagan of the Royal Ulster Constabulary said that 400 soldiers would be going back to mainland Britain and that checkpoints near the main airfield were being dismantled.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Violence erupts at student demonstration in Jakarta, killing at least eight people, as Indonesian Parliament votes to hold general elections next spring and to begin reforms; photos (M)
news.title: Student Protest in Indonesia Explodes in Violence, and 8 Are Killed

news.abstract: KUALA LUMPUR—  As the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum prepares to admit three new members on Saturday, before heading into its annual summit meeting next week, the group appears more divided and distracted than at any time since it was formed in 1989.
news.title: Divided and Distracted, APEC Prepares to Meet

news.abstract: NASA and Russian space agency agree to set aside last-minute Russian request to launch new international space station into an orbit closer to 12-year-old Mir station than previously planned; technical difficulties cited (M)
news.title: Request to Alter Space Station Orbit Is Dropped

news.abstract: Clinton Administration officials now acknowledge that one of the clear but unstated objectives of last August's raid in Afghanistan was to kill Osama bin Laden, the Saudi exile who has been charged by Federal prosecutors with leading a global war against American interests and who has been linked to the Aug. 7 bombing of two American embassies in East Africa.
news.title: Saudi Was Target In Raid, U.S. Says

news.abstract: Article describes massacre in Kosovo province of 21 members of ethnic Albanian family by Serbian forces; massacre of Delijaj clan occurred during fierce guerrilla resistance to onslaught by Serbian tanks, artillery and infantry near village of Gornje Obrinje; maps; photo (M)
news.title: Ethnic Albanians Recount Massacre of a Family in Kosovo

news.abstract: US reportedly called off huge campaign of air strikes against Iraq after last-minute flurry of diplomatic activity resulted in Iraq's decision to allow UN arms inspectors to resume work; was hours away from first wave of attacks, which would have involved hundreds of cruise missiles launched from ships and B-52 bombers, as well as bombing of Iraqi targets by jet fighters; US officials say attack was aborted because of Iraqi Govt's positive response to last-ditch plea from UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan (M)
news.title: U.S. Says It Was Just Hours Away From Starting Attack Against Iraq

news.abstract: Iraq's Pres Saddam Hussein appears to back down in face of imminent US military attack and says Iraq will resume cooperation with UN arms inspectors; letter to UN Security Council sets conditions on agreement, restating demands that have already been rejected by US, Britain and other Council members; is again rejected as inadequate by US, and American forces remain poised to strike; most Council members say they are prepared to take Hussein at his word; urge quick resumption of arms inspections; Great Britain remains strong in support of US, even though delegates suggest London might be willing to give Iraq chance to re-admit inspectors; Prime Min Tony Blair says until Iraq's compliance is unconditional, British forces will remain on alert; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. REJECTS PLAN

news.abstract: Special report, Dead Zones, on effects of Africa's AIDS epidemic on continents already shaky economies; epidemic is robbing Africa of much of its potential, striking first at educated its urban professionals, who are backbone of economic expansion; damage is immeasurable since it appears in ways that cannot be seen--namely, businesses that will never be founded, ideas that will never be advanced and university departments that will never be created; in eastern and southern Africa where epidemic is worst, infection rates vary between 10 and 25 percent and virtually all will die within 10 years; photos; charts; map; graph (L)
news.title: AIDS Stalking Africa's Struggling Economies

news.abstract: Negotiators from more than 150 countries meeting in Buenos Aires set deadline of two years for adopting operational rules for cutting emissions of waste and industrial gases believed to cause global warming (M)
news.title: Deadline Set To Form Rules For Reducing Gas Emissions

news.abstract: Iraqi representative at United Nations Nizar Hamdoon, is pressed to promise that no sites, including Presidential properties belonging to Saddam Hussein and his security services will be barred to inspectors as in past; says that certain 'modalities' govern searches of such places, according to agreement signed with Sec Gen Kofi Annan in Feb (M)
news.title: A Truckload of 'Howevers' Burdens the Iraqis' Promise

news.abstract: Pres Clinton all but calls for coup against Saddam Hussein, vowing to work with Iraqi opposition groups until 'a new government' takes power in Iraq (M)
news.title: Opponents Find That Ousting Hussein Is Easier Said Than Done
