news.abstract: Sec of State Madeleine K Albright meets in Kuala Lumpur with Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, wife of jailed Malaysian political leader Anwar Ibrahim, in gesture of solidarity that angers her hosts and suggests that politics could swamp economics at meeting of Asian and Pacific Rim countries; photo (M)
news.title: Albright Visits With Wife Of Dissident In Malaysia

news.abstract: Pres Clinton says that Pres Saddam Hussein of Iraq has unconditionally retreated and once again vowed complete cooperation with United Nations weapons inspectors; says US and British forces that nearly struck Iraq on Nov 14 will remain poised to act; says Iraq must live up to its obligations; calls for overthrow of Hussein; says he is threat to peace of his region and security of world; Pentagon says it is suspending its military buildup in Persian Gulf region; senior US officials say Iraqis have clarified their position in two letters that eliminated all unacceptable conditions; photo (M)
news.title: CLINTON ACCEPTS IRAQ'S PROMISE TO ALLOW WEAPONS INSPECTIONS

news.abstract: Forthcoming trial of Lin Hai, computer executive, heralds new electronic battleground for China's political dissidents and security forces determined to preserve Communist Party control; Lin is charged with 'inciting subversion of state power' by giving tens of thousands of Chinese E-mail addresses to hostile foreign publications (M)
news.title: A Trial Will Test China's Grip on the Internet

news.abstract: Reconstruction of weekend's events based on interviews with several participants indicates Pres Clinton called off missile attack on Iraq only minutes before it was set to begin on advice of national security adviser Samuel R Berger; Berger apparently responded to CNN report that Iraqis sent letter to United Nations agreeing to let arms inspectors resume work; Defense Sec William S Cohen apparently opposed delaying attack, holding Iraqi letter was too late and too confused; aides to State Sec Madeleine K Albright, who was en route to Asian economic summit conference, said she wanted attack to proceed; photo (M)
news.title: From the Brink to the Blink: Washington's Iraq Weekend

news.abstract: South Africa's Human Rights Commission says it will open probe into racism in press, using its powers of subpoena and arrest if needed; commission head, Barney Pityana, says probe is aimed at spurring debate about nature, meaning and incidence of racism he holds is endemic in nation; some editors see carefully timed effort to keep news organizations from criticizing Pres Nelson Mandela's Government on eve of national elections (M)
news.title: South Africa's Press to Face Bias Inquiry

news.abstract: Fugitive Kurdish Rebel Is a Headache for Italy**Italian Prime Min Massimo D'Alema, in first policy test, is under pressure from leftists in his coalition to offer political asylum to Kurdish rebel leader Abdullah Ocalan, arrested recently at Rome airport; Ocalan is sought in Turkey as terrorist and Germany on murder charges; D'Alema notes Italian law bars extradition of suspects to nations that have death penalty; refuses to pressure from Turkish prison inmates who took Italian prisoner hostage to press for extradition; Turkey says it will soon abolish capital punishment (M)
news.title: Fugitive Kurdish Rebel Is a Headache for Italy

news.abstract: French Min Hubert Vedrine reacts angrily to televised remarks by Sen John McCain he sees as charge France tipped off Iraq that American bombers were on their way; McCain denies directly accusing France; incident highlights longstanding differences between France and United States over Iraq (M)
news.title: Report on McCain's Remarks About Tip-Off Angers Paris

news.abstract: United Nations workers begin heading back to Iraq after latest confrontation; 150 relief workers who had been staying in Jordan return to posts; seek to untie logjams at border crossings caused by their departure that threaten to disrupt internationally monitored food shipments (M)
news.title: Taking Up Crucial Relief Efforts

news.abstract: Kuwaitis, who feel much affection for United States, regarding US as their liberator and protector after events of 1990, are puzzled by lack of US action now against Iraq; yet another peaceful end over weekend to showdown between Iraq and United States and Britain does little to dispel conspiracy theory held by many people in Kuwait and in other Arab countries that Pres Saddam Hussein of Iraq gives the West, and especially United States, an excuse to keep military presence in Persian Gulf to protect oil supplies (M)
news.title: Kuwaitis Are Puzzled By Lack of U.S. Action

news.abstract: Israeli Parliament approves American-brokered peace plan by significant majority, reflecting widespread, pragmatic acceptance of partioning the Land of Israel; Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu, whose Likud Party was created to defend Jewish homeland from territorial compromise, turns his back on his party's founding credo; in doing so, he wins far more substantial victory, with 75 yes votes, than Labor Party, with its slim margin of support, won for original Israeli-Palestinian peace accord signed in Oslo in 1993; but he does so with Labor opposition's support; only half of his coalition Govt votes for agreement; two of his Cabinet members vote against it; and five ministers, all Likud members, walk out of chambers, refusing to vote; photo of Arab legislator and member of National Religious Party arguing over West Bank map (M)
news.title: Without Joy, Netanyahu Wins Vote to Adopt Peace Agreement

news.abstract: PARIS—  Disease, pain and life-threatening conditions have been the usual reasons people turn to prescription drugs. But aging baby boomers, interested in continuing to feel and look good as long as possible, have recently fueled a vigorous new phenomenon in the pharmaceutical industry going by the name of "quality of life" or "lifestyle" drugs.
news.title: The 'Lifestyle' Phenomenon:Pills to Enhance Well-Being

news.abstract: LONDON—  To an industry afflicted with excess production capacity, a fragmented market and unforgiving regulatory regimes that put pressure on prices, corporate deal-making has been a useful tonic. The logic of combining operations has been compelling enough to generate more than $150 billion of mergers and acquisitions among pharmaceutical companies in the last six years.
news.title: Mergers Give Industry Boost in Developing New Products

news.abstract: British and Irish Govts, in gradual but distinct change in policy, are relaxing pressure on Irish Republican Army to disarm; operation of new Northern Ireland Assembly has been thwarted by disarmament issue since Assembly was set up by peace agreement approved in spring; comments on disarmament issue by Irish Prime Min Bertie Ahern and Mo Mowlam, Northern Ireland Sec, noted (M)
news.title: Disarmament of the I.R.A. Losing Some of Its Priority in Ulster

news.abstract: Senior French officials say France was not told by US or by Britain precisely when two countries planned to attack Iraq and could not have tipped of Baghdad; suspicions were raised that Iraqis learned of imminence of attack, whereupon they sent letter pledging to allow arms inspectors to begin work once again (M)
news.title: Tip Off Iraq? France Says It Couldn't, And Wouldn't

news.abstract: China expels Jurgen Kremb, reporter for German news magazine Der Spiegel, one day after eight officials burst into his office and accused him of possessing secret documents; Japanese reporter was charged with possessing state secrets and deported in Oct (M)
news.title: Beijing to Expel Foreign Reporter, 2d in a Month

news.abstract: Imported Western pharmaceuticals have taken China by storm, straining pocketbooks as they hold out promises of cure; Western drug companies have been aggressively courting China's doctors and hospitals not only with new pills, but also with gifts, money and even kickbacks, practices that are banned in US; their goal: to gain access to China's 1.2 billion potentially ailing citizens, most with seemingly unshakable belief in curative power of name-brand Western pills; doctors say that Western medicines and medical equipment have contributed to medical costs that are rising 35 percent a year in China; photo (M)
news.title: West's Medicine Is Raising Bills For China's Sick

news.abstract: Clinton Administration officials say North Korea has demanded that US pay hundreds of millions of dollars for right to inspect huge underground center that US intelligence analysts fear houses nuclear-weapons program; say US has rejected request (M)
news.title: North Korea Offers U.S. Access to Secret Plant, at a Steep Price

news.abstract: Leaders of 21 Pacific Rim countries wrap up contentious summit meeting in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, by pledging to revive region that has been set back decades by Asian economic crisis; US and Malaysia engaged in war of words during forum over speech by Vice Pres Al Gore; he accused Malaysia of suppressing freedom and threw his support behind protesters who are demanding ouster of Prime Min Mahathir Mohamad (M)
news.title: Rancorous Asia Pacific Talks End With a Pledge and a Sigh

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: MOVE TO CREATE WAR-CRIMES TRIBUNAL -- A Foreign Office official, Tony Lloyd, said that on Nov. 30 Britain will sign a treaty at the United Nations setting up an international war-crimes tribunal. The United States has opposed the treaty, saying it gives the new court too much prosecutorial power and leaves American troops and citizens vulnerable to potentially unfair prosecution.   (AP)    BRITAIN: CRACKDOWN IN TAX HAVENS -- Home Secretary  Jack Straw laid out a plan to crack down on tax-dodging and  money-laundering in the multibillion-dollar offshore tax havens of the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man. A retired Treasury official who helped draft the plan, Andrew Edwards, suggested that assets of the super-rich who were suspected of stacking up illegal gains and who could not account for their offshore wealth should be confiscated.   (Agence France-Presse)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Japanese politics takes turn to the usual as governing Liberal Democratic Party opts for political expedience and agrees to form coalition Govt with its archenemy, Ichiro Ozawa, and his Liberal Party; alliance will strengthen governing party's sway in Parliament, mollify its restive hard-liners and give it sure support in coming budget debates (M)
news.title: Japan's Ruling Party Agrees To Coalition With Archrival

news.abstract: Jewish Museum in Berlin begins talks with Steven Spielberg over possibility of housing his vast video history of Holocaust, as debate intensifies over how to recall Hitler's destruction of European Jewry in emerging new center of Berlin; museum is to open in 2000 (M)
news.title: Berlin Debates Spielberg Holocaust Video Offer

news.abstract: Signing of Wye peace memorandum by Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu drops like missile of doom on Israel's political right wing; shatters alliances, blurring political identity of movement built around defending Jewish homeland against territorial compromise; expands political center, and transforms those who clung to their right-wing ideology into a kind of fringe; what has emerged most powerfully is a new pragmatism, which puts settlers' guiding ideology on back burner, if not in waste bin; Netanyahu, who campaigned as hard-line ideologue, and Foreign Min Ariel Sharon, champion of new settlements, set the course, but leaders of settlers and even right-wing National Religious Party followed; photo (L)
news.title: Israel's Right Wing Turns From Fury to Resignation

news.abstract: Business analysts say that as cigarette sales threaten to decline precipitously in United States, American tobacco companies are are counting on China as land of extraordinary potential for growth; but American companies' plans are being thwarted by China's Govt monopoly (M)
news.title: U.S. Tobacco Industry Looks Longingly at Chinese Market, but in Vain

news.abstract: Sister Nirmala, who succeeded Mother Teresa as head of Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta, India, says she cannot replace Mother Teresa, only try to carry on her work; she is administering Missionaries' ascetic empire while also gathering evidence of miracles that will be needed to win sainthood for Mother Teresa from Vatican; photos (M)
news.title: Calcutta Journal; Living Up to Mother Teresa's Legacy

news.abstract: Soldiers in Jakarta, Indonesia, stop traffic to allow student demonstrators to mourn shooting deaths of several student demonstrators week ago; students are demanding that former Pres Suharto be put on trial; military promises investigation into whether live rounds had been fired after reports emerge that metal bullet fragments were found in several of victims' bodies (M)
news.title: Jakarta Troops Stand Aside as Students Mourn Protesters' Deaths

news.abstract: Prime Min Bertie Ahern of Irish Republic and David Trimble, first Minister of new Northern Ireland Assembly, say they made significant progress toward setting up council that would give Roman Catholic Ireland more influence in predominantly Protestant British province of Northern Ireland; under peace agreement approved in spring, cross-border council would havenorthern and southern officials cooperating on issues like tourism, agriculture and development; British Govt is to yield such powers next year; Ahern and Trimble say they made no progress on issue blocking work of new Assembly, disarming Irish Republican Army, and Trimble says accord will not work unless disarmament dispute is resolved (M)
news.title: Progress Seen in Setting Up Key Ulster Council

news.abstract: Top leaders of Mexico's Zapatista rebels, wearing trademark black ski masks, emerge from jungle hide-outs to appear in public for first time in two years; Indian rebels angrily complain that commission of federal lawmakers charged with organizing peace talks treated them 'like animals'; say many of 29 Zapatista delegates to three-day meeting had no beds; accuse lawmakers of being racist; Zapatistas demand apology but do not threaten to walk out of meetings (M)
news.title: Mexico Rebels Emerge, and Start Complaining

news.abstract: Iraq balks at handing over documents on chemical and biological weapons and missile systems, throwing up new roadblock to work of United Nations arms inspectors less than week after agreeing to cooperate; American and British officials warn that air strikes remain immediate option if Government of Pres Saddam Hussein does not honor its pledge to renew cooperation with inspectors; Iraq appears to believe it can balk on major issues pending comprehensive review of its relations with UN, but Security Council decided that review cannot take place until there is full cooperation with inspectors; confrontation has come sooner than expected; it raises questions about Hussein's understanding of seriousness of threat he faces and limited diplomatic help he can expect, if any, from former supporters like Russia, China and France (M)
news.title: BAGHDAD DISRUPTS ARMS INSPECTIONS

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, speaking at joint appearance with South Korean Pres Kim Dae Jung in Seoul, makes unusual direct appeal to North Korea to set aside any nuclear ambitions in favor of strengthening ties to South Korea and US; says construction site in North Korea that could be beginnings of nuclear weapons plant and test firing last Aug of missile over Japan are 'cause for deep concern'; Clinton also comments on Iraq's refusal to comply with request from weapons inspectors; he urges caution and says it is 'important that we not overreact'; photo (M)
news.title: Clinton Appeals To North Korea For Closer Ties

news.abstract: Bosnian political leaders are so good at resisting changes needed to revive economy that diplomats and foreign officials say their governments now face choice between providing large amounts of financial aid for years and watching country collapse; photo (M)
news.title: Bosnia Economy Still at Mercy of Political Leaders

news.abstract: Many scholars and jurists regard unexpected arrest in London of Chilean dictator, Gen Augusto Pinochet, and request for his extradition by Spain as unusual chance to test high-minded human rights conventions that oblige countries to prosecute great atrocities but are invariably ignored; say case will test whether Britain is willing to lets its international human rights commitments prevail over domestic law giving immunity to heads of state (M)
news.title: Pinochet Case Spurring Debate on International Laws

news.abstract: Britain's House of Lords has voted down and returned to House of Commons five times bill to change procedures in elections of British representatives in European Parliament; upper body has power only to delay, not defeat, legislation passed by Commons; real impulse behind rebellion is Prime Min Tony Blair's resolve to strip hereditary peers of their right to vote in Lords (M)
news.title: Lords Defy Commons And Labor Sees Red

news.abstract: Current talks between Zapatista rebels and mediators are not going well; there is no sign of peace between Mexican Government and rebels in Chiapas, and little reason to hope for settlment any time soon; map; photo (M)
news.title: Bad Faith Is Charged as Talks With Mexican Rebels Open

news.abstract: On a near-freezing pale-gray day on the tarmac of this U.S. Air Force base south of Seoul, President Bill Clinton did not have to offer any explanations for his conduct to GIs, most of them here on one-year tours without their families.
news.title: 'Leave the Guy Alone,' Troops Say as Clinton Visits Korea

news.abstract: Angry invective and rancor thwart progress between Mexican Govt mediators and top leaders of Zapatista rebels at two days of peace talks in Chiapas; maps (M)
news.title: Rancor Rules Out Progress At Peace Talks in Mexico

news.abstract: Israel's university students, who have well-earned reputation for indifference regarding political protests, are emerging as powerful voice for rearranging national priorities after month-long strike for lower tuition; are demanding shift from country's preoccupation with security to greater attention to social needs; have won support from labor unions and from unemployed and poor; photo (M)
news.title: Students Raise Voices In Israel

news.abstract: Gang fight between Muslims and Christian migrants erupt into fierce rioting in Jakarta, Indonesia; six are killed and nearly dozen churches are burned or damaged; rioting, unrelated to political demonstrations and military gunfire that have kept city on edge for more than week, is sharp reminder of potential for violence as nation suffers through political turmoil and deep economic pain; photo (M)
news.title: 13 Die in Muslim-Catholic Riots in Indonesia; Churches Looted

news.abstract: Iraq, week after averting military strikes by US, issues new series of defiant statements that it has little intention of cooperating with UN arms inspectors; remains on collision course with US; Foreign Min Mohammed Saeed al-Sahhaf rebuffs UN demand for more documents on country's arms program; reasserts that Baghdad has already produced more than two million pages of files and has no more documents to give; in second direct challenge in three days to US and Britain, Iraqis have in effect stated that they will step back only to October 31, when all cooperation with arms inspectors ceased, leaving all restrictions placed on monitors before final break in place; Clinton Administration warns US forces remain poised to act; national security adviser Samuel R Berger says Iraq's objection to request for documents is unreasonable and urges favorable response to UN request (M)
news.title: IRAQ RATCHETS UP RENEWED DEFIANCE OVER INSPECTIONS

news.abstract: Results of national surveys published in French daily, Le Figaro, finds 96 percent of French live in homes equipped with showers or baths in late 20th century, even more than those with bidets, but that only 47 percent bathe every day; found only 60 percent of Frenchman changed underwear daily--same percentage of all French people who regularly wash hands after going to toilet (S)
news.title: Hygiene Poll Bares Source Of the French Je Sais Quoi

news.abstract: Four senior Brazilian Govt officials resign, scalded by accusations that two may have tried to influence bidding on giant telephone system; include Communications Min Luis Carlos Mendonca de Barros, brother Foreign Trade Sec Jose Roberto and Andra Lara Resende, president of Govt's National Bank of Economic and Social Development (S)
news.title: 4 Brazilian Officials Resign As Bid-Rigging Scandal Erupts

news.abstract: FRANKFURT—  Deutsche Bank AG said Monday it was in the final stages of forming the world's biggest financial-services firm with the acquisition of Bankers Trust Corp.
news.title: Bankers Trust Deal Near, Deutsche Bank Confirms

news.abstract: Turkish Govt and Turkish citizens are enraged over decision by Italy not extradite Kurdish rebel leader, Abdullah Ocalan, who was recently arrested in Rome; most view Ocalan, who has led 14-year uprising that has cost estimated 30,000 lives as diabolical figure; Italian laws forbids extradition of prisoners to countries that apply death penalty (M)
news.title: Turks Are Furious Over Rebuff From Italy on Kurd Rebel Chief

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: EURO'S SUPPORTERS SPEAK OUT  Urging their  Government to end its ambivalence toward the euro, 114 British business leaders said failure to join the single European currency ''would pose a serious threat to our future prosperity and to our influence in the world.'' Britain is among four European Union nations that will not use the euro, left, when the new currency is introduced in six weeks.   Alan Cowell (NYT)    BRITAIN: QUANTIFYING LIFE'S QUALITY  The Government announced plans to measure the quality of life using such factors as housing, traffic and air pollution in an attempt to establish whether life in Britain is getting better or worse. Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott said he wanted the new statistics to be used alongside traditional measures. ''The quality of life is not simply economic,'' Mr. Prescott said.   (Reuters)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Vladimir P Demikhov, Russian surgeon whose pioneering work in performing organ transplants on dogs set stage for similar operations on humans in later years, dies at age 82 (M)
news.title: Vladimir P. Demikhov, 82, Pioneer in Transplants, Dies

news.abstract: Indonesia's human rights commission will probe charges that soldiers executed up to 50 people in East Timor earlier in November in military operation against armed rebels; International Committee of Red Cross says team it sent to area found no confirmation of large-scale atrocities; as many as 2,000 East Timorese students continue to occupy local parliament building, Dili, to protest alleged killings (M)
news.title: Indonesia Panel to Study Reports Of Army Slayings in East Timor

news.abstract: Richard Butler, chief United Nations arms inspector, tells Security Council that he is disappointed with Iraq's cooperation with resumed inspections, particulary refusal to provide requested documents; Council agrees to continue discussing issue; critics and supporter of Iraq apparently agree Pres Saddam Hussein should be given time to show how he intends to proceed; United States tries to portray firm resolve after earlier signaling new policy of patience (M)
news.title: Security Council Hears Report on Iraq and Takes No Action

news.abstract: Ethnic Albanian rebels in Kosovo, Serbia, release Serbian police officer Goran Zbiljic after American diplomats intercede; release is seen tiny advance in effort to prop up fragile cease-fire, as international monitors help in small ways to defuse tensions; photo (M)
news.title: Tiny Step to Help the Cease-Fire in Kosovo

news.abstract: Controversy is brewing in South Africa over first formal voter registration process since all-race elections began in 1994; fears are growing that administrative chaos could keep millions from voting; Independent Electoral Commission says it will delay registration drive in about half of nation, admitting it is not prepared to meet its optimistic goal of signing up 23 million to 25 million eligible voters in weekend; says it needs more time to train personnel to man registration booths (M)
news.title: South Africa Embroiled in Dispute Over Registration for '99 Vote

news.abstract: Turkish Prime Min Mesut Yilmaz's Government, plagued by competing pressure from Islamic groups and secular military, loses confidence vote, 214-314; vote comes after Yilmaz is implicated in corruption scandal involving purchase by gangsters of state-owned bank; military is expected to retain ultimate political power as rivalries among parties make it unlikely that elections will produce stable Government (M)
news.title: Centrist Ruler, Under Fire, Is Voted Out In Turkey

news.abstract: Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu is ready to bring former Foreign Min David Levy back into his Cabinet in bid to shore up his disintegrating coalition and fortify his chances at either re-election or assembling unity Government; Levy, moderate who resigned in Jan, says he will return; Netanyahu and Foreign Min Ariel Sharon cancel trips abroad to concentrate on stabilizing Government (M)
news.title: Former Ally Of Netanyahu May Return To Cabinet

news.abstract: Beijing says it wll bid for 2008 Summer Olympic Games; Mayor Jia Qinglin submits proposal to Chinese Olympic Committee, which will decide whether to apply to International Olympic Committee; importance of bid to Chinese leaders noted (M)i
news.title: Beijing Says It Will Bid For Olympics Set for 2008

news.abstract: British Law Lords, 3-2, reject former Chilean dictator Gen Augusto Pinochet's sovereign immunity claim and require him to remain in custody in London while Spain seeks his extradition on mass murder and genocide charges; Home Sec Jack Straw must now rule on matter; Amnesty International hails decision; photo (M)
news.title: British Court Rules Against Pinochet; Now Cabinet Must Weigh Extradition

news.abstract: Many European leaders hail British ruling that former Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet can be extradited to Spain; United States officials and legal experts seem uneasy with idea that former Government leaders can be held responsible by foreign courts; United Nations Human Rights High Comr Mary Robinson sees ruling heartening human rights defenders around world; photo (M)
news.title: Europeans, But Not U.S., Rejoice At Ruling

news.abstract: Valentin M Berezhkov, Russian who interpreted for Stalin and Molotov at conferences that they, Pres Franklin D Roosevelt and Winston Churchill attended during World War II, dies at age 82 (M)
news.title: Valentin M. Berezhkov, 82, Interpreter for Stalin at Talks

news.abstract: American rap star Coolio arrives at local courthouse in Boblingen, Germany, to face trial on charges that he stole $900 worth of clothes and assaulted store clerk at local boutique; Coolio claims it was misunderstanding, and his lawyers seek out-of-court settlement; police cordon off street in front of courthouse as streets are jammed with hundreds of Coolio's teen-age fans (M)
news.title: Coolio Thrills German Fans With Gangsta Or Theft Rap

news.abstract: Interior Min Sergei Stepashin says Russian authorities want new powers to check election candidates for criminal connections, after killing of Galina Starovoitova, liberal member of Parliament (S)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Quebec is divided from rest of Canada, and not just by its use of French language and desire of many to secede from Canada; Quebecers smoke more, get divorced more and are said to be more stressed out than people in rest of Canada; basic difference is way Quebecers see their country; Claude Meunier, host of wildly popular television program in Quebec, says Quebecers are eager for their French language and culture to survive; photo (M)
news.title: Montreal Journal; Canadians, Estranged, Even in Their Pop Culture

news.abstract: Spanish judge who wants former Chilean dictator, Augusto Pinochet, to stand trial, plans to go to Washington to try to see secret Government files; Judge Baltasar Garzon is particularly interested in United States Government files about events of 1970's, when Central Intelligence Agency and other American Embassy personnel were close to Pinochet Government and knew of activities of its powerful secret police; that police force is widely considered responsible for worst excesses of Pinochet Government, including kidnapping, torture and secret execution of leftist opponents (M)
news.title: Spanish Judge Is Hoping To See Secret Files in U.S.

news.abstract: EUROPE    YUGOSLAVIA: KIDNAPPED REPORTERS RELEASED -- Rebels in Kosovo freed two Serbian reporters who were kidnapped 40 days ago and also released two moderate ethnic Albanian politicians. The Kosovo Liberation Army called the releases a good-will gesture.   (Reuters)    RUSSIA: MOVE TO BLOCK COMMUNISTS -- Galvanized by last week's murder of the legislator Galina V. Starovoitova, prominent reformers announced plans to form a coalition to prevent the Communists from returning to power. The coalition includes former Prime Ministers Yegor Gaidar and Sergei V. Kiriyenko, and former Deputy Prime Ministers Boris Y. Nemtsov and Anatoly B. Chubais. In the past, Russian liberals have been torn apart by rivalry.   (AP)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Clinton Adm presents NATO with far-reaching program that seeks to define what alliance has become since cold war ended, and sets out its goals for next century; but proposals are running into European opposition that threatens to undermine 50th-anniversary NATO summit meeting in Washington in April; NATO diplomats say agenda for meeting is intended partly to convince Congress that NATO is still central to American security, but it has raised European concerns that United States is trying to turn orgn into freewheeling global vehicle for its own interests (M)
news.title: A POLICY STRUGGLE STIRS WITHIN NATO

news.abstract: Javier Garcia Paniagua, former senior Mexican official whose hard-line views aligned him with group within governing Institutional Revolutionary Party known as 'dinosaurs,' dies at age 61; photo (M)
news.title: Javier Garcia Paniagua, 61, Mexican Ruling Party Loyalist

news.abstract: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cut short a trip abroad to reconsider the Israeli Army's 20-year occupation of southern Lebanon after the killing of seven Israeli soldiers there in the last week and a half.
news.title: Israel Is Rethinking Its Stand on Lebanon

news.abstract: SINGAPORE—  Outlining a strategic blueprint for Asia that differs sharply from the approach of the United States, Defense Minister Chi Haotian of China said Friday that security in the region could not be achieved by military alliances.
news.title: Gently, China Flexes Strategic Muscles in Asia

news.abstract: French Pres Jacques Chirac says leaders of Congo and neighboring nations, in Paris for French-African summit meeting, met with United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan and agreed to cease-fire in revolt in Congo by mid-Dec; does not say whether rebels, who were not invited to summit, were consulted; Annan met with Congo Pres Laurent Kabila and leaders of Angola and Zimbabwe, who back him, and leaders of Uganda and Rwanda, who back rebels (M)
news.title: African Nations Agree on Cease-Fire for Congo by December

news.abstract: Scottish Nationalists, campaigning for election to new Scottish Parliament on platform of independence from United Kingdom, are attracting far more support than expected; are seriously challenging Labor Party's traditional domination of Scotland, forcing Prime Min Tony Blair to take bigger role in campaign; map; photo (M)
news.title: Blair Finds Autonomy Only Whets Scots' Appetite

news.abstract: Yugoslav Pres Slobodan Milosevic, in what may be sign of weakness, has purged his innermost circle, dismissing heads of army, air force and intelligence service and trusted political commissar; purge culminated with dismissal of Army Staff Chief Gen Momcilo Perisic; Milosevic is seen by former associates as increasingly insecure, even paranoid, as Kosovo drifts from his control, economy weakens and he bows to demands of his politically powerful wife, Mirjana Markovic, replacing his apparatchiks with hers; photo (M)
news.title: Purges Hint at Beginning of the End for Milosevic

news.abstract: Treatment of protesters during 1997 Asia-Pacific Economic Coooperation summit meeting, Vancouver, has turned into recurring political nightmare for Canadian Prime Min Jean Chretien's Government, which allegedly ordered police to be aggressive in protection former Indonesia Pres Suharto from embarrassment; inquiry into incident has been postponed; Solicitor Gen Andy Scott has resigned after being overheard talking about probe with fellow passenger on plane (M)
news.title: Police Action In '97 Haunts Government In Canada

news.abstract: Spanish Judge Baltazar Garzon, who seeks extradition of former Chilean dictator Gen Augusto Pinochet, is also probing role of Emilio E Massera, retired Argentine admiral, and other former Latin American military officers in Chilean military operation that sought capture of Chilean exiles abroad and their return to Chile for execution; inquiry has spurred Bolivian opposition to demand local probe of Pres Hugo Banzer, former military dictator; Argentine Pres Carlos Saul Menem, who pardoned Massera and other military officers involved in political kidnappings in Argentina, backs Chile's stand that former military leaders should be tried in own nations and opposes extradition of Argentine military officers; Massera is under house arrest in Argentina in case involving seizure of newborn infants from mothers who were then apparently executed (M)
news.title: Spanish Judge Investigating Rights Abuses In Argentina

news.abstract: Chile's Foreign Min Jose Miguel Insulza presses effort to persuade Britain to free Gen Augusto Pinochet, stating that Chile will pursueits own justice against former dictator; says popular view that 83-year-old Pinochet has unlimited immunity in Chile is wrong, adding that there 14 cases against him initiated by alleged victims of his dictatorship that are in hands of prosecutors in Santiago (M)
news.title: Chilean Official Says His Country Will Pursue Justice Against Pinochet

news.abstract: Reversal of symbols on campaign posters for election in Quebec is one of many reversals in election that has distracted voters, confounded experts and added layer of thick ambiguity to one of continent's most baffling political landscapes; signs that prominently feature blue and white fleur-de-lis flag, provocative symbol of Quebec separatist movement, currently belongs to anti-separatist Liberal Party and its leader Jean Charest; Charest, former leader of federal Conservative Party, who arrived in Quebec as great federalist hope to banish separatists, seems to have gone from hero to goat, with latest polls showing Liberals headed for stinging defeat; photos; map (M)
news.title: Shifts in Symbol and Substance Muddy Quebec Vote

news.abstract: Agriculture remains least reformed sector of Russian economy, despite vaunted talk of building free market; nation's chronically inefficient collective farms have been relabeled rather than reorganized as Govt has refused to approve sale of farmland and has done little to help fiercely conservative farmers cope with brave new world of capitalism; distress has been compounded by virtual collapse of banking system and ruinous drought; harvests are at lowest point in 45 years and production of staples continues to plummet--leaving country heavily dependent on imports; conditions at state-owned collective near Novogorod described; photos; map (M)
news.title: Soviet Mindset Blocks Capitalism on Farms

news.abstract: Ernest Wamba dia Wamba, leader of rebels on Congo, says he has not heard about cease-fire agreement announced in Paris and is therefore unable to commit to it; says fighting will continue until details become clear (S)
news.title: Congo Rebel Chief, Citing Lack Of Details, Holds Back on Truce

news.abstract: Leaders of Macedonia's most radical ethnic political parties, former enemies, are forming coalition to govern fragile former Yugoslav republic as war in neighboring Kosovo has underscored what could happen if they fail; Arben Xhaferi, leader of ethnic Albanians, is optimistic both sides can find common ground for ethnic integration through mutual understanding; is negotiating with nationalist leader Ljupco Georgievski, slated to be new Prime Minister; country's ethnic Albanians feel strongly that they are victims of systematic discrimination by Government, and foreign diplomats concur; are generally poorest, have worst social services and hold proportionally far fewer jobs in public sector (M)
news.title: Slavs and Albanians Form Unusual Coalition in Macedonia

news.abstract: Special report, Masking of a Militant, on shadowy past of Ali A Mohamed, former Egyptian Army officer who has been jailed in New York on charges of conspiring with Osama bin Laden, Saudi exile sought in US embassy bombings in Africa; Mohamed, who was turned down for job as CIA operative in 1984, entered US legally in 1985 despite being on State Department's terrorist 'watch list'; subsequently cultivated range of useful relationships with American Govt, such as enlisting in Army and being cooperating witness for FBI; his aggressive support for Islamic causes and open curiosity about intelligence matters raised eyebrows among colleagues in Army's elite Special Forces unit; before honorable discharge he regularly traveled to New York City area to train in basic military doctrine circle of Islamic militants, many of whom have since been convicted of plotting series of terrorist attacks, including 1993 bombing of World Trade Center; Mohamed reportedly forged ties with bin Laden as early as 1991; was said to be adept at obtaining false documents for bin Laden's organization and to have assisted with logistical tasks, such as bin Laden's move from Afghanistan to Sudan in 1991; US officials say he was fully enmeshed in dual life in early 1990's, simultaneously collaborating with bin Laden while talking regularly with Federal agents about Saudi exile and other issues; say case is modern espionage parable in which Mohamed was trying to manipulate American investigators even as they were using him to gain window into bin Laden's activities; photos (L)
news.title: THE MASKING OF A MILITANT: A special report.; A Soldier's Shadowy Trail In U.S. and in the Mideast

news.abstract: Threat by Zimbabwe's Government to seize 841 farms, owned mostly by whites, has thrown commercial farmers into confusion and added to country's sense of crisis; whites, fewer than 2 percent of population, own 70 percent of land, while millions of rural blacks are crowded onto 'communal areas' of stony depleted soil (M)
news.title: Air of Crisis in Zimbabwe Grows After Threat to Seize 841 Farms

news.abstract: Defense Sec William S Cohen and Colombia's new President, Andres Pastrana, announce steps to intensify military cooperation in war on drug trafficking, including pledge to increase Pentagon training of Colombia's armed forces and share more aerial and satellite intelligence data; both countries will sign agreement setting up formal working group to bring together officials from both countries for regular consultations; agreement follows sharp increase in aid and equipment, including six Black Hawk helicopters that Congress approved for fight against narcotics as part of recent increase in defense spending; Cohen's aides insist that new help to Colombia's police and military will only involve fight against drug treaffickers and not against leftist insurgents (M)
news.title: U.S. Pledges Military Cooperation to Colombia in Drug War

news.abstract: US pledges extra $400 million aid to Palestinians, which is expected to nearly double amount of their economic assistance from US over next five years; announcement is made by Pres Clinton at start of one-day international donor conference in Washington sponsored by State Dept, which brought estimated total of more than $3 billion in new pledges; Clinton says US decided to increase aid in hopes of convincing Palestinians to stick to peace accord with Israel; appeals for generous contributions from other wealthy nations, adding that peace efforts have so far brought little tangible improvements in lives of Palestinians; Yasir Arafat meets with Clinton at White House and warns donor nations that Palestinian economy has experienced continuous decline; accuses Israel of undermining economy through repeated closings of common border in response to alleged terrorist threats; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. and Other Nations Plan More Aid for Palestinians

news.abstract: Legions of revolver-waving bodyguards speeding in unmarked cars to protect limousines are newest danger for motorists on mean streets of Mexico City and are complicating country's efforts to subdue tidal wave of crime; private security guards, mostly armed but untrained, seem to rule streets in affluent neighborhoods, and authorities acknowledge they have little control over them; their abuses against unsuspecting passers-by grow more frequent each day--as are violent crimes by crooks posing as private policemen; chart photo (M)
news.title: Mexico City Journal; Above the Law: Bodyguards Swell a Wave of Crime

news.abstract: Anthony DePalma analysis contends that while result of Quebec's provincial election are muddy enough for both major parties to claim victory of sorts, and to bear some degree of defeat, real losers are those who had hoped election would provide clear sense of where Quebec, and Canada, are heading; notes that while separatists were returned to power, they could not even muster plurality of popular vote; holds that election results keep independence movement alive, but it is wounded; says that means Premier Lucien Bouchard will not call another referendum on breaking away from Canada anytime soon (M)
news.title: Quebec Questions

news.abstract: HONG KONG—  While some upbeat forecasters are saying the Asian economic crisis has bottomed out, an agency of the United Nations said Tuesday that the region's social crisis was far from over and was likely to get worse.
news.title: Risk of Social Crisis Rising In Asia, UN Agency Finds

news.abstract: Israeli Goverment, despite numerous appeals, may have to integrate its powerful all-Orthodox religious councils with Reform and Conservative Jews, in keeping with Supreme Court ruling that has outraged Ultra-Orthodox politicians; they have threatened to bring down Government if councils become 'mixed'; photo (M)
news.title: Battle Looms in Israel Over 'Mixed' Religious Councils

news.abstract: US has finally found customer for fighter planes that it sold to Pakistan but never delivered; New Zealand has agreed to acquire 28 F-16 fighters on 10-year lease-buy arrangement for about $105 million (M)
news.title: U.S. Will Sell New Zealand Planes It Denied to Pakistan

news.abstract: Sec of State Madeleine K Albright, speaking at Washington, DC, conference on Holocaust-era assets, talks emotionally about Jewish roots that she acknowledged almost two years ago and her own loss of family members whom she never knew; photo (M)
news.title: Albright Speaks With Emotion at Holocaust Conference

news.abstract: World Bank report concludes that decision last year by International Monetary Fund and US Treasury to push Asian nations to send their interest rates soaring was crucial blunder that worsened world financial crisis; graph (M)
news.title: Decisions by U.S. and I.M.F. Worsened Asia's Problems, the World Bank Finds

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: TALKS ON ECONOMIC CRISIS -- The head of the International Monetary Fund, Michel Camdessus, met again with Prime Minister Yevgeny M. Primakov and praised Russia's ''pragmatic'' course in dealing with its economic crisis. But Mr. Camdessus said a team from the Fund would have to return next month for further negotiations on releasing the frozen loans that Russia  badly needs.   (AP)    RUSSIA: STATUE TO RISE AGAIN -- The Communist- dominated lower house voted overwhelmingly to resurrect a statue of Felix Dzerzhinsky, left, the first chief of the Soviet Union's secret police, in the center of Moscow. The towering bronze statue of ''Iron Felix,'' a landmark during the Soviet era, was toppled by pro-democracy protesters in 1991 and has since languished in a city park.   (AP)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Government officials say unidentified senior aide of exiled Saudi terrorist Osama bin Laden has been talking to US investigators for two years; say informer pleaded guilty to terrorism in secret proceeding in Federal court, Manhattan; at least one operative of bin Laden's group in East Africa concluded over year ago that informer was Sidi Tayyib, businessman who was married to one of bin Laden's relatives (M)
news.title: Senior Aide Implicating Bin Laden In Terrorism

news.abstract: Environmental group Greenpeace accuses Petroleos Mexicanos, state-owned petroleum company known as Pemex, of dumping vast amounts of toxic waste into scores of illegal sites on the Gulf Coast; Greenpeace dir Alejandro Calvillo says Pemex is main environmental criminal in Mexico (M)
news.title: Mexico's Oil Monopoly Accused Of Polluting Scores of Gulf Sites

news.abstract: Wave of arms sales that many officials predicted after Clinton Administration lifted de facto ban on sales of most advanced American weapons to Latin American countries 16 months ago has not materialized, and there are few signs that any country will be able to afford weapons (M)
news.title: The Latin Arms Explosion That Fizzled

news.abstract: Protestant and Roman Catholic leader apparently fail to agree on several important issues in Northern Ireland peace effort (S)
news.title: Ulster Negotiations Stall Again, Unraveling This Time on Details

news.abstract: Israeli soldiers serving in Lebanon feel both pride and dread, a consequence of sporadically deadly conflict between Israelis and Shiite Muslim guerrillas who bomb and run; seven Israelis have been killed in two weeks; photo; map (M)
news.title: For Israeli Soldiers, Pride and Dread in Lebanon

news.abstract: Indonesian Govt sets June 7 as date for national elections for new House of Representatives, and say it will convene People's Consultative Assembly on Aug 29 to elect new Pres; students who have been pressing Pres B J Habibie for swifter democratic reforms continue their protests; block Jakarta's main thoroughfare, demnanding arrest of Suharto, former Pres, on corruption charges (S)
news.title: Election Set in Indonesia but Protests Persist

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: TORY REBELLION -- William Hague, left, the Conservative Party leader, found himself at odds with one group he thought he could count on, the Tory peers in the House of Lords. Mr. Hague dismissed his party's leader in the House of Lords, Viscount Cranborne, for striking a deal that could let 10 percent of the 759 hereditary peers retain their voting rights. Mr. Hague later endorsed the same legislative proposal himself, prompting the entire Tory leadership of the Lords to resign their front bench posts. Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: South Africa Pres Nelson Mandela, in move that outrages opposition parties and baffles police and foreign affairs officials, meets quietly with Rev Canaan Banana, former Pres of Zimbabwe, who is a fugitive after being convicted last week in Zimbabwe of sodomy and assault (S)
news.title: Fugitive Zimbabwe Ex-President Has Odd Meeting With Mandela

news.abstract: Issue of Palestinian statehood complicates Pres Clinton's trip to Israel and Palestinian Authority, and details of trip, such as the aircraft he uses and the sites he visits, will be scrutinized for their symbolic bearing on the issue (M)
news.title: Symbols Cast Shadows On Clinton Trip to Gaza

news.abstract: SEOUL—  Inside a basement tearoom secluded from the wreckage of nights of mayhem outside Korea's leading Buddhist temple, Mu Hyu boasted Friday of his ability to survive against the "gangsters" he said were trying to regain control of the order for personal profit and power.
news.title: Monk Factions Vie to Control Korea's Biggest Sect : Buddhist Temple Tug-of-War

news.abstract: Agreement on measures to refinance Mexican Government's troubled $61 billion bank bailout is reach by members of Congress from Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) and National Action Party, but the latter demands that Guillermo Ortiz resign as head of Bank of Mexico as part of agreement; PRI, following cues from Pres Ernesto Zedillo, opposes Ortiz's resignation on ground that central bank enjoys independence (M)
news.title: 2 Mexican Parties Near Accord on Bank Bailout

news.abstract: Tens of millions of Nigerians are expected to vote in local government elections on Saturday in the first of three elections that the military rulers have promised will lead to democracy.    The borders will be closed during the voting hours, officials said, to prevent candidates from paying foreigners to vote illegally. In Lagos, the largest city, the authorities announced that most cars would be banned from the streets and that  pedestrians would be limited to areas near voting centers.
news.title: In a Key Test, Nigerians Go to Polls

news.abstract: Suharto, former President of Indonesia, defends himself against charges of corruptly amassing huge personal fortune; says he is a good saver and landlord; estimates of his wealth range up to $40 billion; photo of demostrators calling for broader investigations of corruption under Suharto (M)
news.title: Suharto Says His Millions Were Earned, Not Stolen

news.abstract: Critics of Iran's conservative government and foreign diplomats are alarmed by the attack on 13 visiting American businessmen on Nov 21 and the fatal stabbing of Dariush Foruhar, a prominent dissident, and his wife, Parveneh, a day later; suspect the attacks may have been staged with at least tacit government approval; Pres Mohammed Khatami, a relative moderate, has condemned attacks in strong terms, but conservative figures who still wield most power in Iran have expressed fewer regrets (M)
news.title: Two Attacks Cause Worry To the Critics Of Iran Rulers

news.abstract: Spain marks 20th anniversary of its Constitution amid squabbling over whether it should be rewritten to shift more power to regions; drive for greater regional autonomy is led by Basques but is joined also by nationalists in Catalonia and Galicia (M)
news.title: Squabbling, Spaniards Mark 20th Birthday of Their Constitution

news.abstract: North Korea refuses to allow inspection of huge underground construction site that could be used to hide a nuclear reactor, a stand that could cause collapse of four-year-old agreement meant to freeze North Korea's nuclear weapons program; American officials are also alarmed by intelligence evidence suggesting that North Korea is making preparations to test-fire a medium-range ballistic missile over Japan (M)
news.title: North Korean Nuclear Arms Pact Reported Near Breakdown

news.abstract: The United States and 32 other countries concluded four days of arms control meetings here with a public commitment to exercise ''maximum restraint'' before selling weapons to regions of conflict.    Behind closed doors, the delegates to the so-called Wassenaar regime, an arms control organization that came into being after the cold war, made clear that the areas they were most concerned about were Central Africa, where a half dozen countries are fighting in Congo, and the Horn of Africa, where Ethiopia and Eritrea are on the brink of full-scale war.
news.title: New Weapons Sales to Africa Trouble Arms-Control Experts

news.abstract: Several hundred Khmer Rouge guerrillas surrender to Government in what is presented as final end to Cambodia's armed Communist movement; Ta Mok, Khieu Samphan and Nuon Chea, three top Khmer Rouge leaders who are targets of possible international tribunal for crimes against humanity, do not join in ceremony and remain at large (M)
news.title: Last Rebels In Cambodia Send Message Of Surrender

news.abstract: Hundreds of elderly in Beijing, China, are carrying on ancient traditon of appealing personally to higher authorities for redress of heartfelt grievances--some waiting for decades, camped outside city's Petitions and Appeals Office; many sleep in shoddy tents of canvas or plastic, cook food scrounged from garbage and use streets or nearby canal as toilet; some grievances date back to Cultural Revolution of 1966 to 1976; direct appeal to higher authorities was main means of redress when country lacked formal legal system; after Communists came to power in 1949, tradition was continued with formal appeals offices in provinces, and in Beijing for those still not satisfied; photos (M)
news.title: Beijing Journal; Please, Mr. Bureaucrat, Hear My 20-Year-Old Plea

news.abstract: David Levy, Israel's former Foreign Minister, says he will not rejoin Israeli Cabinet, potentially foiling Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu's latest effort to hold together his right-wing coalition since he signed land-for security accord with Palestinians in October; Levy heads five-member Gesher parliamentary group (M)
news.title: Angry Ex-Ally Rejects Netanyahu's Call to Rejoin the Cabinet

news.abstract: Gap between poor and well-to-do in Ireland is apparently widening even though country's economic boom of past several years has made it 19th richest country in world with fastest growth rate of any European Union nation; educated professionals and middle class administrative and technical workers are thriving in places such as Dublin, in contrast to those in poor areas of city, where unemployment averages 40 percent--with pockets where 90 percent have been out of work, some for several years; major problem keeping many from profiting from boom is that about 40 percent of men over 35 are functionally illiterate, descendants of dock workers whose jobs disappeared 25 years ago with arrival of huge containerships; photos (M)
news.title: As Most of Ireland Prospers, the Poor Lament a Deepening Social Chasm

news.abstract: MANDALAY, Burma—  When U Soe Thein Oo attended a concert a few months ago by Iron Cross, the most popular Burmese heavy metal band, he got more than just an earful of "Desert Moon," the band's hit love ballad.
news.title: Rise in Cigarette Smoking Doesn't Bother Burma Government

news.abstract: Officials who monitored Nigeria's local Government elections say, despite widespread logistical problems, voting was fair and is positive step toward presidential elections in February 1999; photo (M)
news.title: Monitors Call Nigerian Vote Fair, With Room to Improve

news.abstract: William K Stevens article surveys man's effects on the earth's water cycle and progress toward mitigating some of the harm he has done; photos; map; graph (M)
news.title: Pushing the Limits Of an Irreplaceable Resource

news.abstract: Article describes US efforts to expand cooperation between Russian and American biologists as part of effort to stem brain drain, discover more about Soviet germ warfare arsenal and learn from Russian strides in germ defenses; US will spend up to $6 million to upgrade security at Russia's germ bank that holds virus collection; has persuaded Europe and Japan to join it in financing International Science and Technology Center in Moscow, which tries to find peaceful work for former weapons scientists (M)
news.title: Dollars Are Weapon of Choice in the War on Bacteria Peril

news.abstract: Wang Youcai, founder of China's suppressed Democracy Party, will be tried on December 17 on charge of colluding with foreign enemies to incite subversion of state power (S)
news.title: China Appears Ready for Trial Of a Leader of Outlawed Party

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: FINANCIAL WOES PERSIST  The arrival of a World Bank team for more talks about loans did little to assuage fears that Russia will be left without foreign aid and may begin printing large sums of money to pay off a total foreign currency debt of $158.8 billion by January.    (AP)    BRITAIN: TORY BACKS DOWN ON KEY PLAN  William Hague, the leader of Britain's Conservatives, has abandoned plans to press for a new regional Parliament to represent England. The proposal, a centerpiece of his program at the annual party convention two months ago, was aimed at being a counterweight to the new Parliaments that the Labor Government of Prime Minister Tony Blair has created in Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.    Warren Hoge (NYT)    GERMANY: CALL FOR EAST GERMAN AMNESTY  Leaders of the Party of Democratic Socialism, successor to the Communists who governed the former East Germany, have called for an amnesty on crimes committed under Communist rule. The party's leader, Lothar Bisby, questioned whether people carrying out the law of East Germany, from border guards upward, should be liable to prosecution. Nearly 1,000 people were killed trying to flee to the West.    (Reuters)    MIDDLE EAST    IRAN: KHATAMI SPEAKS OUT ON REFORMS  President Mohammad Khatami, who was elected last year on promises of ushering in political reforms, accused conservative and traditionalist forces of blocking reforms in Iran. ''We are facing the three currents of counter-revolution, traditionalists hostile to progressive religion and revisionists,'' he told an assembly hall packed with 10,000 student supporters at Sharif University, Teheran.    (Agence France-Presse)    EGYPT: MOVE ON MINI-MOSQUES  The Ministry of Religious Endowments said it began putting into action a plan to control 6,000 ''zawya,'' or mini-mosques, in an attempt to put an end to Muslim fundamentalism. The ministry will appoint prayer leaders to the mosques, a spokesman said.    (Agence France-Presse)    ASIA    INDIA: STANDING FIRM ON KASHMIR  On his first visit to Kashmir since becoming Prime Minister of India in March, Atal Behari Vajpayee said India would never relinquish any of it to Pakistan.   Celia W. Dugger (NYT)    CHINA: ACID RAIN DAMAGE GROWS  China's rapid economic growth and reliance on coal have spread acid rain damage to 40 percent of the country, The China Daily reported. According to a new report by Chinese scientists, China emitted 23.5 million tons of sulfur dioxide last year, up 30 percent from 1993, and coal use doubled to comprise 75 percent of total energy consumption.    (AP)    NORTH KOREA: TALKS WITH U.S. CONTINUE  The United States and North Korea resumed talks in Washington on an American demand for access to an underground building site that could be connected with a revived nuclear program in North Korea. The negotiators met in New York on Friday and Saturday, with their agenda restricted to Washington's insistence that North Korea allow inspections of the site at the village of Kumchang-ri.    (Reuters)    JAPAN: ECONOMY IN 'SEVERE STATE'  The head of the Bank of Japan said Japan's economy remains in ''an extremely severe state.'' The central bank governor, Masaru Hayami, told Parliament that corporate earnings had slipped and industrial production had fallen.    (AP)    AFRICA    SOUTH AFRICA: ELECTION PLAN CHALLENGED  The opposition National Party said it would ask the High Court to rule on the constitutionality of requiring citizens to have new ''bar-coded'' identity documents before they can register to vote in national elections next year. The ruling African National Congress is insisting on the documents, but that could result in fewer white voters getting to the polls because many have not applied for the new documents.    Suzanne Daley (NYT)    UGANDA: PRESIDENT'S BROTHER QUITS  The brother of Uganda's President resigned as the nation's security adviser after admitting his involvement in a secret deal to buy a 49 percent interest in the Uganda Commercial Bank. Maj. Gen. Salim Saleh, a military adviser to his brother, President Yoweri Museveni, has been criticized for corruption and the military's support of the rebellion in Congo.    Ian Fisher (NYT)    ANGOLA: REBELS TELL OF ATTACKS  The rebel movement Unita said Government forces bombed its strongholds in the towns of Andulo and Bailundo in breach of a four-year peace treaty. Paulo Lukamba Gato, Unita's secretary general, told a Portuguese radio station that the attacks could signal a return to all-out fighting in Angola.    (Reuters)    THE AMERICAS    ST. VINCENT AND THE GRENADINES: MARIJUANA WAR  Caribbean troops backed by six United States Marine Corps helicopters are beginning a two-week campaign to eradicate an estimated 12,000 acres of marijuana on St. Vincent, BBC News reported. It said the island's marijuana growers' association, warning that the destruction of the crop would drive up the island's 40 percent unemployment rate, has written to President Clinton demanding compensation.    UNITED STATES: GORE'S GLOBAL CONFERENCE  Vice President Gore is inviting law enforcement and other officials from more than 60 countries to what his office calls the world's first conference on fighting corruption and safeguarding integrity among justice and security officials. The conference is scheduled from Feb. 24 to 26 at the State Department.   (NYT)     Compiled by Christopher S. Wren
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: German Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder, seeking consensus on ways of combating cripplingly high unemployment of 10.6 percent, summons labor unions, employers and several members of Cabinet to first meeting of much-vaunted 'alliance for jobs' but initial achievement is little more than list of good intentions; as global competition has increased while wage costs have remained high country's economy, based on free market and high level of social protection, has frayed; Schroeder's chosen method of building consensus is seen as attempt to demonstrate that German model that has had great difficulty responding to challenges of 1990's can be revived (M)
news.title: Schroder Tries For Consensus In Fight to Cut Jobless Rate

news.abstract: Tabriz, Iran, celebrates 1,129th birthday of prophet Mahdi, whom Shiite Muslims believe will return someday; photo (M)
news.title: In Iran City, Prophet's Day Is Safe Excuse For a Party

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: START II DEBATE POSTPONED -- The Parliament again postponed discussion of Start II, the strategic-arms reduction treaty that the United States and Russia signed in 1993. The Duma Council of the Parliament delayed debate because only the liberal Yabloko Party had submitted proposals, the Interfax news agency reported. Yabloko leaders accused Communist legislators of stalling on the treaty, which the United States Senate ratified in 1996.   (AP)    BRITAIN: PINOCHET LAWYERS SEE BIAS -- Lawyers for Gen.  Augusto Pinochet, the former Chilean dictator, questioned the impartiality of a decision on Nov. 25 by the Law Lords, England's highest court, denying the general immunity from arrest on charges of human rights violations. The lawyers complained that a judge, Lord Hoffmann, left, was a director of a fund-raising charity associated with Amnesty International, which joined the case against the general. A spokeswoman for Amnesty International said Lord Hoffmann was an unpaid director of the charity, but was not directly involved with Amnesty International.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: US proposals for broad new strategic concept for NATO, to counter global threat from chemical, nuclear and biological weapons, receive quizzical responses from European allies at NATO conference in Brussels; many allies resist Sec of State Madeleine K Albright's suggestion that alliance could intervene in regional crises even if it did not have explicit authorization from United Nations (M)
news.title: Europe Looks Quizzically at U.S. Proposal for NATO Strategy

news.abstract: Unicef study finds that nearly one-sixth of 5.9 billion people in world cannot read or write and predicts that illiteracy rates will steadily grow into next century (M)
news.title: Unicef Study Predicts 16% World Illiteracy Rate Will Increase

news.abstract: Secret Pentagon report concludes that Hughes Space and Communications, without proper authorization, gave China technological insights that are crucial to successful launchings of satellites and ballistic missiles; says Hughes scientists helped Chinese engineers in 1995 to improve sophisticated mathematical models necessary to predict effects of wind and other natural forces on rocket launching; says Chinese had been using 'oversimplified' mathematical analysis, resulting in failed satellite launchings; concludes that Hughes provided 'defense service' to China that violated US standards against helping Beijing make better satellites and missiles and required State Dept review; Hughes says that its actions were approved at time by Commerce Dept (M)
news.title: Satellite Company Faulted Over Rocket Aid to China

news.abstract: Yao Zhenxian, Chinese dissident fleeing new round of arrests of democracy activists in Shanghai, arrives in New York City and announces that he and other opponents of Chinese Government plan demonstration at United Nations on Dec 10 to protest crackdown (M)
news.title: Dissident From Shanghai Arrives in New York

news.abstract: Pres Clinton will commemorate Human Rights Day by announcing creation of early-warning center to focus US intelligence resources on uncovering potential genocide and large increase in funding for programs to stop child labor around world (M)
news.title: Clinton to Focus on Genocide and Child Labor Issues on Rights Day

news.abstract: Spanish Judge Baltasar Garzon, who issued arrest warrant for Gen Augusto Pinochet, will complete criminal indictment against him and send it to London (S)
news.title: Spanish Judge Draws Up His Indictment

news.abstract: Pres Saddam Hussein's Government bars inspectors from Baghdad city headquarters of his ruling Baath Party, barely two days into crucial round of surprise arms inspections in Iraq (M)
news.title: Ruling Party In Iraq Bars Inspectors From Offices

news.abstract: Article on Omagh, Northern Ireland, notes that it is still suffering after-effects of car bombing by Irish Republican Army splinter group that killed 29 people and wounded about 400 in Aug; map; photo (M)
news.title: Omagh Journal; After the Terror, the Epilogue Is Horror and Loss

news.abstract: Richard Butler, chief UN arms inspector for Iraq, tells Security Council that Iraqis have been interfering with inspections at number of sites; Baghdad toughens its stand against allowing entry to ruling party's offices, in contravention of Council resolutions; Butler says Iraqis have refused to explain why and where equipment and microorganisms thought to be associated with biological weapons program had been moved during break in inspections last month; photo (M)
news.title: Iraq Again Hindering Inspections, U.N. Told

news.abstract: EUROPE    SERBIA: EXAMINATION OF GRAVES IS BLOCKED -- A team of 19 Finnish forensic specialists investigating atrocities in Kosovo said the Serbian police barred them from opening a mass grave thought to contain the bodies of ethnic Albanians. Troops with armored vehicles blocked the Finns as they headed to the first of six sites they plan to search for bodies of civilians slaughtered in the conflict between Serbs and ethnic Albanian separatists in the province, in southern Serbia.    (AP)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Russian Govt finally unveils its 1999 spending plan to halt Russia's economic tumble; Yevgeny M Primakov calls economic blueprint, his first as Prime Min, a bold effort to boost Russia's hard-pressed factories and farms while clamping down on wasteful spending; 1999 budget is criticized as political exercise to attract Western financial aid while placating powerful constituencies at home; from tax revenues to inflation, budget is based on highly optimistic assumptions, which are unlikely to survive their bruising contact with Russia's dour economic realities; photo (M)
news.title: Russia Offers 1999 Budget: 'Honest' or 'Unrealistic'?

news.abstract: Iranian scientist, Mehdi Rezayat, denies that he had tried to recruit biologists who formerly worked on Moscow's germ-warfare program to develop similar weapons for Iran, as American officials and Russian scientists have reported; Rezayat was identified by New York Times on Dec 8 as a key figure in an Iranian purchasing network meant to speed development of nuclear, chemical and biological weapons (S)
news.title: Iranian Denies Seeking Biological Arms in Russia

news.abstract: Spanish judge indicts Gen Augusto Pinochet 'for the crimes of genocide, terrorism and torture' during his 17-year dictatorship in Chile, key step toward his trial in Madrid if he is eventually extradited from Britain (S)
news.title: Judge Lays Out Pinochet Case In Full Detail

news.abstract: Leaders of supposedly united Europe, at summit meeting in Vienna, squabble about how much expansion will cost; argument is about money and efficiency of procedures assuring vetoes of original three small members of 1957 European Economic community--Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands--over decisions by original three large ones--Germany, France and Italy; another large issue is fat agricultural subsidies designed when France was weak agricultural economy and Germany was powerful industrial one, formula that would lead to political paralysis and financial chaos unless it is changed; photo (M)
news.title: Soon, a Common Currency, But No European Consensus

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  21 Republicans:Yes 16 Democrats: No
news.title: House Panel Votes to Impeach Clinton for Perjury : In Late Appeal, President Says, 'I Am Profoundly Sorry'

news.abstract: Sir Otto Frankel, plant geneticist who was among first to warn of threat to whole species, dies at 98; photo (S)
news.title: Sir Otto Frankel, Geneticist, 98; Warned of Extinction of Species

news.abstract: Brazil is under immense pressure to convince investors it can streamline its Government to reduce its dependence on outside financing; Asian collapse last year prompted total cooperation by local legislators, but now Government of Pres Fernando Henrique Cardoso faces tough fight to push through unpopular economic measures; there is $41.5 billion bailout from International Monetary Fund in the offing; photo (M)
news.title: Pressure Builds on Brazil to Reassure Investors

news.abstract: Delegates from more than 120 countries attend first global convention of government represenatives to deal with so-called Millennium bug, held at United Nations; some of countries represented have not yet set up national projects to deal with problem; some last-minute attendees, notably France, express skepticism about extent of threat; common assumption is that most of world is far behind United States in preparing for 2000; Garter Group, consulting firm, projects that 30 countries, including Russia and China, are in highest-risk category, and that two-thirds or more of all businesses and government agencies in those countries will run into at least one major problem (M)
news.title: At the U.N., Nations Are Urged to Prepare for 'Millennium Bug'

news.abstract: France's National Front is in upheaval after Jean-Marie Le Pen, founder, expels Bruno Megret, the man who was behind party's drive for right-wing respectability; rift follows months of subterranean dissension (M)
news.title: Le Pen Feud With Key Deputy Has French Right in Upheaval

news.abstract: Joseph E Estrada, who successfully campaigned for President of Philippines as a champion of the poor, is accused of running an administration that does more for the nation's rich; critics say his relaxed style of leadership is allowing country to slip back into the corruption and cronyism that were hallmarks of Marcos regime (M)
news.title: Manila Leader, Ally of Poor, Now Courts the Rich

news.abstract: US moves to undermine Pres Slobodan Milosevic's tight control over Yugoslavia; his grip has weakened because of his mishandling of rebellion in Serbian province of Kosovo; US now openly supports democratic Government in Montenegro, a part of Yugoslavia that Milosevic has hinted he might move against (M);
news.title: U.S. Hardens Stance on Yugoslav Leader

news.abstract: Dennis McNamara, a senior United Nations official in charge of protecting refugees, says tougher qualifications for asylum in both rich and poor countries are threatening the lives and safety of displaced people almost everywhere; singles out US as a major problem, citing severe new restrictions on asylum seekers and refugees trying to enter US (M)
news.title: Stiffer Rules Are a Threat To Refugees, Agency Says

news.abstract: Palestinian Legislative Council, Palestinian Supreme Court and other fledgling institutions of democracy are increasingly frustrated with Yasir Arafat's viselike grip on reins of power in Palestinian Authority; still, experts say Pelestinians have moved more quickly and closer toward developing authentic democracy than any of their Arab neighbors, thanks largely to their relatively sizable intellectual elite, international help and the model of Israel; photo; map (M)
news.title: There's No Bossing a Democracy, Arafat Learns

news.abstract: News analysis of Pres Pres Clinton visit to Israel and West Bank; even though Clinton suffered lukewarm greeting from Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu and his effort to save Wye peace agreement faces uncertain success, there is little question that he is engaged in critical mission and has made himself indispensable authority figure in blood feud between Israelis and Palestinians; photo (M)
news.title: Indispensable Man

news.abstract: Pres Clinton, forced to confront issue of impeachment, reluctantly interrupts efforts to rescue Middle East peace plan during visit to Jerusalem by addressing vote in Congress he says he cannot control; tells news conference his deposition in Paula Corbin Jones's sexual misconduct case was 'difficult and ambiguous and unhelpful,' but expresses none of recent remorse about affair with former intern, Monica S Lewinsky; says coming Congressional vote on impeachment is out of his hands; reportedly makes calls to two Democratic members of House Judiciary Committee to assess situation; makes most forthright appeal to members of House to consider censure as alternative; says approximately three-quarters of American people believe it is right thing to do; dismisses calls by Republican moderates who might support censure for admission that he lied under oath; both he and Israeli Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu seem far apart and peace initiative is in doubt as each try to grapple with complex interplay of domestic and foreign concerns; Clinton receives pugnacious reception from Netanyahu, who repeatedly reminds him at state dinner of Israel's fears and determination; lectures Clinton on Jews' lonely and turbulent history in presence of Israeli leaders whose support his Govt needs; reminds Clinton of ancient Jewish ties to Gaza and Bethlehem, Palestinian-controlled areas that Clinton will visit in next two days; Clinton repeatedly affirms American commitment to Israeli security, but also promotes Wye agreement, which calls for Israel to withdraw in phases from additional 13 percent of West Bank in exchange for Palestinian steps against terrorism; joins Pres Ezer Weizman in lighting first candle of Hanukkah; places oval stone, reportedly taken from Wye River, on tombstone of late Prime Min Yitzhak Rabin; photo (M)
news.title: In Jerusalem, Clinton Visits A Fellow Embattled Leader

news.abstract: Bank of Japan reports business confidence is at lowest level in four and a half years (S)
news.title: Outlook Is Bleak in Japan

news.abstract: Refurbishment of golf course at Soweto Country Club has become symbol of renewal in South Africa's most famous black township; club, which many say was built to create buffer zone between black and mixed-race areas during era of apartheid, is trying to attract new members; its efforts described; photos (M)
news.title: Soweto Journal; That Little White Ball Is Suddenly Colorblind

news.abstract: SEOUL—  The mysterious death of a South Korean Army officer has touched off a debate here between U.S. and South Korean forces over who should command a joint battalion at the critical crossing between South and North Korea.
news.title: Seoul and U.S. At Odds Over Joint Battalion

news.abstract: EUROPE  BRITAIN: CHALLENGE BY PINOCHET  Lawyers for Gen. Augusto Pinochet said they would turn to England's High Court to challenge the approval last week by the Home Secretary, Jack Straw, of the Spanish petition to extradite their client to Madrid to face charges of crimes against humanity. In another legal move, the lawyers will also go to the House of Lords to seek a review of its decision denying the former Chilean dictator immunity from arrest.    Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: British and Irish Governments move to deal with rising tension between Protestant majority and Roman Catholic minority in Northern Ireland; hostility stems from lagghing peace effort and from old dispute about Protestant parade through Catholic area; police fear new violence (S)
news.title: London and Dublin Tackle Dual Threats to North's Pact

news.abstract: Subversion trial of Qin Yongmin and Wang Youcai, prominent dissidents trying to promote new political party in China, will be held on December 17; relatives say both have been denied access to legal counsel (M)
news.title: China to Try 2 Dissidents on Thursday but Denies Them Lawyers

news.abstract: North Korea reportedly drops demand that US pay hundreds of millions of dollars for right to inspect huge underground center American intelligence agencies fear could be used to make nuclear weapons; reportedly suggest they would be willing to allow US to inspect center in exchange for food to ease famine that has plagued country for years (M)
news.title: North Korea Said to Drop Demand on Atom Inspection

news.abstract: Book by American anthropologist David Stoll, Rigoberta Menchu and the Story of All Poor Guatemalans, casts doubt on accuracy of her 1992 autobiography--I, Rigoberta Menchu--for which she received Nobel Peace Prize and became overnight celebrity and much-sought-after crusader for human rights, special report, Tarnished Laureate; autobiography, first published in Spanish in 1983 at height of Guatemala's brutal civil war, tells wrenching tale of violence, destruction, misery and exploitation; Stoll, after decade of interviews with more than 120 people and archival research, concludes that key details of her story are untrue; says book is not eyewitness account since Menchu repeatedly describes experiences she never had herself; his assertions are corroborated by New York Times in interviews with members of Menchu's family, as well as with friends, neighbors and former classmates that indicate many of book's main episodes are either totally fabricated or seriously exaggerated; Menchu defends book as part of historical memory and patrimony of Guatemala, dismissing criticisms as part of racist political agenda to gain attention and publicity; photos; map (L)
news.title: TARNISHED LAUREATE: A special report.; Nobel Winner Finds Her Story Challenged
