news.abstract: American group opposed to sanctions against Iraq runs into trouble with Federal Government for taking medicines and toys to Baghdad to give to Iraqis who are suffering from effects of embargo; group, Voices in the Wilderness, plans to announce at news conf in Chicago that it and four members had received warning from Office of Foreign Assets Control in Justice Dept that orgn might be fined more than $160,000 for taking goods to Iraq without authorization in 1996 and last year (M)
news.title: Justice Dept. Warns Group Aiding Iraq That It Needs a Permit

news.abstract: United States and other countries providing support to carrying out Bosnian peace accord meet in Madrid and agree that they should press for deeper economic and governmental reforms to prepare nation to survive on its own (S)
news.title: Aid Nations Asking Reforms By Bosnians

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: START TREATY BACKED -- The commander of the strategic missile force, Gen. Vladimir Yakovlev, backed ratification of the Start II arms-reduction treaty with the United States, saying Russia's nuclear weapons will soon reach the end of their service life. The United States Senate ratified the treaty in 1996. But the Communist-led opposition in the Russian Parliament has blocked ratification, contending that dismantling the weapons would harm security and be too expensive.   (AP)    RUSSIA: STATE OF EMERGENCY IN CHECHNYA -- The Chechnya Parliament declared a one-month state of emergency to combat a wave of crime in the breakaway republic. Four Western hostages were beheaded there last week. On Monday the Parliament refused to let President Aslan Maskhadov call up army reservists to pursue criminal gangs.   (AP)
news.title: WORLD BRIEFING

news.abstract: Irish Government is moving cautiously but unmistakably toward a relaxation of Ireland's bedrock national policy: military neutrality it has proudly maintained since gaining independence from Britain 76 years ago; change is being pressed by Foreign Min David Andrews, whose governing political party, Fianna Fail, has always denounced any move away from strict neutrality as disloyal to Ireland, if not treasonous; now Andrews is arguing that Ireland's neutrality should be considered to permit country to join so-called Partnership for Peace, American-sponsored group of nations that do not belong to NATO but have agreed to coordinate military policies with it (M)
news.title: Tie to NATO Forces Ireland To Reconsider Neutral Role
Bin Laden Plot Alleged

news.abstract: Critic's Notebook column on television coverage of start of US air strikes against Iraq on December 16 (M)
news.title: 2 Rival Dramas, Inevitably Entwined

news.abstract: News analysis of Pres Clinton's decision to launch air strikes against Iraq; reaction among politicians has pushed him closer to reality that long months of evasions and legalisms and his enemies' unceasing denunciations of him as liar have been costly to both him and nation; his credibility is crumbling, especially but not exclusively among Republicans on Capitol Hill; some sober and experienced leaders no longer accept his word (M)
news.title: No Reservoir Of Credibility

news.abstract: New scandal emerges in Ireland over assertions of corruption and nepotism at highest level of Government, plunging country into national debate; debate comes after disclosure of official ruling that former Prime Min Charles J Haughey owes no taxes on $2 million gift from businessman, Ben Dunne, and that decision was made by Ronan Kelly, tax official who is brother-in-law of present Prime Min Bertie Ahern, whose political career was fostered by Haughey (M)
news.title: A New Scandal Rocks Ireland, Provoking Turmoil in Parliament

news.abstract: Federal prosecutors, in first detailed account of August 7 bombing of US Embassy in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, say it was carried out by group of men who detonated bomb packed with car batteries and oxygen tanks, apparently to enhance lethal force of explosion; say explosion, which killed 11 people including one bomber, and wounded 80 others, was photographed by one suspect who later fled; identifies five men as followers of Saudi exile Osama bin Laden, who is suspected of organizing simultaneous attacks on embassies in Tanzania and Kenya as well as other acts of terrorism against Americans abroad; listed as Fahad Mohammed Ali Msalam, Ahmed Khalfan Ghailani, Khalfan Khamis Mohammed, Sheik Ahmed Salim Swedan, Mustafa Mohammed Fadhil; their photos (M)
news.title: Details Given, and 5 More Charged, in Tanzania Bombing

news.abstract: Zimbabwe's former President, Rev Canaan Banana, who fled Zimbabwe before conviction on sodomy and sexual assault charges, surrenders to authorities in capital of Harare (S)
news.title: A Fugitive Zimbabwean Leader Surrenders

news.abstract: Student demonstrators clash with soldiers in Jakarta as Indonesian Pres B J Habibie warns that continued protests could lead to 'disintegration of the nation'; scores of students are treated at hospitals after about 4,000 demonstrators, some of them throwing gasoline bombs, challenge security forces guarding Parliament building; photo (M)
news.title: Indonesia's Leader Warns of 'Disintegration' From Strife

news.abstract: Pentagon officials say US and British forces are taking care to avoid hitting Iraqi factories suspected of producing chemical and biological weapons; say that damage at military, intelligence and communications targets has been extensive; say strikes avoided plants out of fear of unleashing plumes of poisons and killing civilians; say attack, which represents Pres Clinton's biggest military operation, appeared to surprise Iraqis, who had done little to disperse troops or weapons; Defense Sec William S Cohen and Joint Chiefs of Staff Chmn Henry H Shelton outline mission intended to weaken Saddam Hussein's Government and military, including missile sites and bases central to launching chemical or biological weapons; map; photo (M)
news.title: JETS SAID TO AVOID POISON GAS SITES

news.abstract: Limerick, Ireland, 1,000-year-old city of 52,000 people, is seen losing its inferiority complex; few years ago, third-largest Irish city was known in rest of country as a bad place to visit, but you wouldn't want to live there, either; city has changed for the better, as Ireland's economy has boomed (M)
news.title: Limerick (Stab City, No Less) Rebounds

news.abstract: Mexican forensic examiners say that American reporter Philip True, who disappeared while hiking through rugged mountains in western Mexico, was killed by being hit over the head and choked; earlier reports say he had died in accidental fall; Pres Ernesto Zedillo orders Federal and state authorities to spare no resources in investigating slaying; True, 50, was Mexico-based correspondent for San Antonio Express-News; had been a solo hiker since he was teen-ager (M)
news.title: U.S. Journalist Slain in Mexico, Autopsy Shows

news.abstract: US closes 38 embassies in Africa for at least two days to protect employees against possible terrorist reprisals for US air strikes on Iraq; State Dept officials say embassies in South Africa and Nigeria will remain open (M)
news.title: U.S. Closes 38 Embassies In Africa as a Precaution

news.abstract: EUROPE    POLAND: OPENING SECRET FILES Polish legislators, overriding the veto of President Alexander Kwasniewski, pushed through a bill opening access to the files of the Communist-era secret police. The bill will allow Poles who felt they were the victims of Communist repression to see personal files compiled by the authorities before 1989 and determine if they were discriminated against and possibly who informed against them.   (Reuters)    GERMANY: A BREAK FOR DESERTERS Germany gave World War II deserters and their families another year to apply for a onetime payment of $4,500. Parliament offered compensation in May 1997 to men convicted by the Nazis of fleeing Hitler's army, after years of debate about whether they were heroes or traitors. Since then, 2,124 people have applied.   (AP)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Pentagon has limited its attack on Iraq to sharp, swift assault lasting no more than few days, with no intention of even seriously crippling Pres Saddam Hussein; finite list of targets was drawn up with eye toward avoiding American casualties, and creating such vague and limited benchmark of success that it would be fairly easy to declare mission achieved; some Republicans in Congress have called on Clinton Administration to do more to punish Iraq and oust Hussein, but few support what that would take: prolonged commitment of American forces, including ground troops; map; charts (M)
news.title: Pentagon Is Sticking To Timetable And Targets

news.abstract: For first time since Ireland was partitioned in 1922, leaders of Northern Ireland's Protestant majority and Catholic minority agree to specific reforms that will give Catholics more power in British province; breakthrough after eight months of stalemate allows both sides to set up 10-member ruling Executive Cabinet that would include two representatives of Sinn Fein; negotiators sidestep issue of disarming Irish Republican Army and other guerrillas, problem that has blocked peace effort since general agreement was reached in April; photo (M)
news.title: Both Sides in Ulster Carve Out Crucial Accord on Cabinet

news.abstract: Russian Parliament is trying to impeach Pres Boris N Yeltsin over accusations of genocide, treason and abetting murder, and almost no one gives it second thought; most people expect proceedings to continue past time when Yeltsin ends his second term and leaves office in 2000; Communist Party and its allies on far right inspired and have managed impeachment from its start in May; photo (M)
news.title: Memo From Moscow; Impeachment Over Sex? Try Genocide or Treason

news.abstract: Defense Department says it is able to confirm that only 18 of 89 targets were destroyed or severely damaged on third day of air assault on Iraq, despite waves of bombers and more laser-guided cruise missiles than were used during 1991 Persian Gulf war; Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen Henry H Shelton acknowledges that results of US and British air campaign have been mixed so far; Pres Saddam Hussein remains defiant; calls attackers 'agents of Satan' in first televised address since start of bombing campaign; US military planes drop thousands of leaflets warning Iraqi ground troops they face bombing raids if they try to mobilize (M)
news.title: U.S. Reports Mixed Results on 89 Targets in Iraq

news.abstract: Israeli parliament tries to counter wide influence of American popular culture with bill to require that half of songs on national radio stations be in Hebrew; Israeli music itself is melange of East and West, with heavy Middle Eastern and Mediterranean influences that mix with rock; photo; critics see hopeless attempt to legislate tastes (S)
news.title: Israel Battles New Foreign Foe: Music

news.abstract: UN weapons inspectors and other arms experts say Iraqis are masters at hiding weaponry, and have extremely well-developed plans for moving them out of way of bombs; Iraqis reportedly have also fine-tuned ability to reconstitute programs quickly; Scott Ritter sys UN inspectors have seen emergency dispersal plan; photo of Iraqi airfield, showing planes that were removed from hangars before allied bombing (S)
news.title: Iraqis Are Called Masters of Concealment

news.abstract: French parliamentary committee on French military role in Rwanda concludes that succesive Governments made 'errors of judgment,' but absolves France of any responsibility for mass killings in 1994; French press charged that military advisers helped train Rwandan forces that carried out slaughters; committee criticizes UN for delaying military action, and pins blame for that on international community, led by US (S)
news.title: Panel Finds French Errors In Judgment On Rwanda

news.abstract: Switzerland is concerned that rich free-spending Russians who have appeared since fall of Communism are using country as haven where they can stow ill-gotten cash from former Soviet Union; authorities recently detained former Ukrainian prime minister, Pavlo Lazarenko, who entered on Panamanian passport, and indicted him for money-laundering; Geneva prosecutors also brought organized-crime charges against Sergei Mikhailov, reputed Moscow mob kingpin who had been living quietly in Switzerland; Mikhailov was acquitted for insufficient evidence, thwarting effort to send message to Russian gangsters; Russia and Ukraine have both tried to seek out illegal funds deposited in Switzerland (M)
news.title: Ex-Soviets Are Focus Of Inquiry By the Swiss

news.abstract: Gerald Regan, former premier of Nova Scotia, is aquitted of rape and attempted rape charges related to incidents that allegedly took place forty years ago; three women testified that Regan, now 70, attacked them when they were teen-agers; court does not permit 19 other women to testify to alleged assaults or harassment (S)
news.title: Nova Scotia Ex-Premier Is Cleared of Charges of Rape in 1950's

news.abstract: Iraq's capital of Baghdad appears to have avoided heavy damage in American and British air raids that lasted for 70 hours; preliminary Western assessments of damage suggest nationwide attacks were effective, even though life in city seems to have been hardly disrupted; even if raids were successful in destroying Iraqi military bases and centers where chemical and biological weapons may have been developed, there is no sign that they came near to achieving West's larger political objective of removing Pres Saddam Hussein; Hussein has emerged at least as powerful as he was before military campaign; photo (M)
news.title: This Time, Little Damage Is to Be Seen in Baghdad

news.abstract: Once-prestigious Allhabad University, alma mater of three former Indian Prime Ministers and formerly called Oxford of India, has lost its way and is mired in stagnation and decay; buildings are decrepit and campus built for 5,000 students now has 60,000; academic calender has so many postponed sessions that years can go by without required courses being offered, and long delays in grading exams are commonplace; university's decline, while extreme case, is symptomatic of system overstuffed with students and undernourished with resources; India has approximately 10,000 universities and colleges, double number of 20 years ago; while some remain first-rate, large portion of rest, especially in poorest 27 states, are overwhelmed creations of haphazard growth; map; photos (M)
news.title: Allahabad Journal; Caste and Campus: India's Ivy Is Overwhelmed

news.abstract: Deal to sell state-owned copper mines in Zambia is reached after two years of on-and-off negotiations; Anglo American Corporation of South Africa will take over important Nchanga, Nkana and Konkola mines (M)
news.title: Zambia Announces Deal to Sell Copper Mines

news.abstract: Xu Wenli, top Chinese disident, receives 13-year sentence after three-hour trial in Beijing on charges of trying to overthrow state; previously spent 12 years in prison for peacefully advocating democratic change; reportedly condemns sentence as political persecution (M)
news.title: Top Dissident Gets 13 Years After Trial In Beijing

news.abstract: News analysis finds four days of American and British air strikes have only increased doubts over US and UN policy toward Iraq; Pres Saddam Hussein has emerged with position strengthened in Arab public opinion for having withstood high-tech US military might, and with capacity and scientists to produce biological and chemical weapons (M)
news.title: What Now? Doubts About U.S. and U.N. Policy on Iraq Increase

news.abstract: PARIS—  With United Nations arms inspectors no longer able to function in Iraq, the Clinton administration intends to apply open-ended, direct military pressure on the Baghdad regime until the Iraqi leader, Saddam Hussein, finds a way to clear his country's record on clandestine weapons, a senior American official said Monday.
news.title: U.S. Plans to Keep Up Pressure on Saddam : 'Cat and Mouse' Over

news.abstract: US tells Libya on 10th anniversary of bombing of Pan American jetliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, that it will face more sanctions if two Libyan suspects are not turned over for trial by Scottish judge in Netherlands by February 1999; Libyan leader Col Muammar el-Qaddafi apparently rejects compromise plan for trial in Netherlands, saying he wants international tribunal to hear case; photo (M)
news.title: 10 Years After Lockerbie, Still No Trial

news.abstract: China belatedly grants balloonist Richard Branson, Steve Fossett and Per Lindstrand overflight permission, allowing them to continue round-the-world journey; permission comes after intense diplomatic efforts--including appeal by Prime Min Tony Blair; map (M)
news.title: 3 Balloonists Press Flight, Then China Lifts Its Ban

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: MIXED RESULTS IN RUNOFF -- Runoff elections for the St. Petersburg legislative assembly, widely seen as a bellwether for democratic reformers, drew less than one-third of the eligible voters and ended with mixed results. Centrist and reform candidates took 23 of the 50 seats at stake. The Communist Party won 5, and independents and smaller factions the remaining 22. The leading reformist bloc, Yabloko, captured 8 of the 23 seats that it contested.   Michael Wines (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Andre de Wavrin, the 'Col Passy' who forged French Resistance intelligence network during World War II; photo (M)
news.title: Andre de Wavrin, 87, 'Col. Passy' of Resistance Fame, Dies

news.abstract: Some 2,000 people gather at graves of 45 people, mostly women and children, massacred year ago in Acteal, Mexico, church; military helicopters interrupt re-enactment showing men in police uniforms taking part in massacre, deadliest single attack in Chiapas since Zapatista rebellion began; residents who fled small pro-Zapatista village in Chiapas return after six days in forest, but continue to fear attack from larger nearby pro-Government community; map; photos (M)
news.title: Acteal Journal; Where Killings Defiled a Church, No Forgiveness

news.abstract: Pres Clinton and Congressional Republicans are deeply divided over how aggressively United States should pursue overthrow of Iraqi Pres Saddam Hussein; Senate Intelligence Committee reportedly blocks Central Intelligence Agency plan to subvert Iraqi Government because key Republicans are not convinced Clinton is serious about ousting Hussein; Administration officials hold there is no quick way to oust him and admit they are not yet willing to undertake aggressive military and intelligence actions they say are needed to support any coup (M)
news.title: Defining Goal in Iraq

news.abstract: Jordan offers citizenship to Prabowo Subianto, former Indonesia general and ex-Pres Suharto's son-in-law, who has been living in Amman for four months; he refuses offer; eleven soldiers he once commanded go on trial on charges of abducting and torturing political dissidents (M)
news.title: Jordan Accepts Suharto Relative, Ex-General

news.abstract: Iraq's one-time cultural elite suffer from crushing economic sanctions; several sophisticated professionals blame United States for destroying their way of life and shredding prospects of entire generation, interviews (M)
news.title: Iraqi Cultural Elite Pine for Old Days

news.abstract: Ontario's draft plan for development of vast tract of publicly owned northern woodlands stirs anger in Canada, where many urban residents cherish ideal of sparsely populated region as wilderness frontier and vacation area; plan balances increase in park lands with more diverse opportunies for industry, satisfying neither conservationists nor logging and mining industries (M)
news.title: Anger Rises Over Plans For Ontario

news.abstract: Three-man crew of ICO Global Challenge become first balloonists to cross Asian continent from one end to the other and the first to fly over towering Himalayan range; are relaxing over Yellow Sea after contronting series of crises; map (M)
news.title: Balloonists Cross China And Leave The Mainland

news.abstract: Muslim guerrillas in Lebanon fire rockets into Israel in retaliation for killing of a Lebanese woman and six of her children in an Israeli bombing raid on suspected guerrilla targets on Dec 22; 13 people are wounded; Party of God, or Hezbollah, claims responsibility; Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu says Israel will respond; photo; map (M)
news.title: Guerrillas Fire Rockets Into Israel

news.abstract: Defense Sec William S Cohen and United Services Organization roadshow visit Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, aircraft carrier Enterprise in Persian Gulf and Army and Marine troops at Camp Doha in Kuwait; rock-and-roll show at Saudi site is killed out of fear of offending Saudi sensibilities during holy Islamic month of Ramadan; Ramadan, however, is not seen as obstacle to bombing of Iraq (M)
news.title: U.S.O. Lightens Life at Two Gulf Sites

news.abstract: Frustrations of modern Iraq are especially poignant in and around Babylon, whose ancient glory is invoked by Pres Saddam Hussein but whose people struggle under deprivations caused by eight years of economic sanctions; photo; map (L)
news.title: The Misery Of Babylon In the Age Of Hussein

news.abstract: Prabowo Subianto, son-in-law of Indonesia's former president, Suharto, denies reports that he has been granted Jordanian citizenship; Government is investigating whether he was involved in abduction and torture of dissidents or instigation of riots that claimed 1,200 lives in May (S)
news.title: Suharto Aide Denies He's a Jordan Citizen

news.abstract: Jean-Marie Le Pen, founder of France's far-right National Front party, expels his former deputy, Bruno Megret, and six other party leader from party's executive body in clash over strategy for European Parliament elections; one of expelled members says it now seems likely two separate National Front slates of candidates would run in elections, with Megret and Le Pen running at top of two separate slates, both calling themselves 'National Front' (M)
news.title: French Far-Right Party Likely to Split as Le Pen Expels 7 Aides

news.abstract: Emilio Fermin Mignone, lawyer who became Argentina's best-known campaigner for human rights, dies at age 76; photo; Mignone's daughter Monica, who worked in slums with Catholic volunteers, was arrested by armed men at family home in 1976 and was never seen again, one of thousands of Argentinians who disappeared during military's 'dirty war' (S)
news.title: Emilio F. Mignone, 76, Dies; Argentine Rights Campaigner

news.abstract: Osama bin Laden reportedly tells Taliban rulers of Afghanistan that he had no role in deadly bombings of two American embassies in Africa, but he does not regret what happened; bin Laden says he knows and respects some of men suspected in Aug 7 bombings in Kenya and Tanzania; Federal authorities have indicted at least 14 people, including bin Laden, in their investigation of embassy bombings and what investigators have called global terrorist organization; United States intelligence authorities consider bin Laden one of world's most dangerous terrorists (M)
news.title: Bin Laden Denies Role in Embassy Bombings

news.abstract: Serbian forces attack separatist guerrillas in northern Kosovo Province, ripping apart tenuous two-month cease-fire; leaders of international monitoring mission question whether it is pointless--and too dangerous--to stay; say two sides do not intend to solve their differences peacefully; diplomats say this latest attack is worst violation since cease-fire went into effect, and follows 11 days of combat and assassinations; photo; map (M)
news.title: Attack by Serbs Shatters a Cease-Fire in Kosovo

news.abstract: Rebellion in Congo has been hard on diamond businesses in Kisangani; dealers say prices used to be fairly uniform when telephones worked and they could call brokers in other cities or countries; now there is no way to get in touch with outside world; with lack of foreign buyers, dealers are stockpiling what they buy, waiting for latest war to be over; meanwhile, rebels are thought to be buying up diamonds, presumably to help finance war; photo; map (M)
news.title: Kisangani Journal; Where War Is Forever, the Diamonds Are Cheap

news.abstract: Initial tests of tons of waste dumped outside Sihanoukville, Cambodia, by Formosa Plastics Corp of Taiwan indicate that mercury level is thousands of times higher than safety standards permit (S)
news.title: Tests Show High Mercury At Cambodia Dump Site

news.abstract: Pres Boris Yeltsin of Russia and Pres Aleksandr G Lukashenko of Belarus say they intend to begin unifying their currencies and much of their economies in 1999, an action that would stop just short of a political merger that would again extend Russian territory to the border of Poland; announcement is victory for Lukashenko, who says he hopes that two countries will enter millennium as one; Russian officials are cooler to idea; American officials have quietly opposed attempts at greater unity for fear that i will destabilize young democracies in eastern Europe (M)
news.title: Yeltsin Agrees To Closer Ties With Belarus

news.abstract: North Korea warns US that it is prepared to launch another medium-range missile; Clinton Administration has warned the North that such a step would jeopardize international aid it was promised in exchange for freezing its nuclear weapons program (M)
news.title: North Korea Warns U.S. That It Can Launch Another Missile

news.abstract: Police in Canada and US are unable to identify a young found naked and dazed in Montreal parking lot on Oct 12; he has no idea who he is or how he got there; is given hypnosis and injection of 'truth serum,' after which he says he might be James Edward Brighton from Morristown, NJ; photo (M)
news.title: A Search For Identity At Impasse In Canada

news.abstract: Lightning and tornadoes harass South Africa, whose weather is generally benign; one tornado nearly gets Pres Nelson Mandela (M)
news.title: South Africa Is a Magnet For Weather With Drama

news.abstract: Pres Aleksandr G Lukashenko pursues his dream of making Belarus a model socialist state and merging it into Russia, thus beginning the rebuilding of former Soviet empire, which he might have a good chance of leading; such a union would be hard enough to achieve, given that Russia is moving in capitalist direction while Belarus is entrenched in old-style socialism, and harder still if Belarus's stumbling economy should ground to a complete halt, saddling Russia with the cost of maintaining another 10 million impoverished people; Minsk in 1998 resembles Moscow in late 1980's; photo; map (M)
news.title: Belarus's Chief Pursues Dream To Revive the Old Soviet Union

news.abstract: Iraqi people are remarkably friendly to American visitors despite American air strikes and deterioration of their lives under economic sanctions; the animosity they bear toward US Government is increasingly focused on Pres Clinton, who is for them the personification of forces that are bombing and blockading them (M)
news.title: An Ugly America, Iraqis Say; No Reflection on Americans

news.abstract: Informal Government proposal for severing Canada's ties to Queen Elizabeth II is widely assailed, and its backers are now backpeddling (M)
news.title: Canadians Riled at Plan To Cut Ties To Queen

news.abstract: Another article in Dead Zones series describes how efforts to contain AIDS epidemic in Africa, especially South Africa, have been undermined by prevalence of substandard condoms; most condoms are made in India, Malaysia, Thailand and China, and while some operate very scientifically, others turn out a high percentage of defective condoms that makers try to unload wherever they can; South Africa became a dumping ground because it is rich enough to buy its own condoms and used ineffective test regimen; has now adopted testing standards used by British, American and other big aid agencies; photo; map (M)
news.title: Faulty Condoms Thwart AIDS Fight in Africa

news.abstract: Much has changed for better in Amazon rain forest of Brazil in 10 years since murder of Francisco (Chico) Mendes, outspoken defender of rubber tappers and the forest; his Workers' Party has just won mayoralty of Xapuri and governorship of Acre, and party members fill state's two seats in Brazil's Senate; millions of acres of rain forest have been reserved for the rubber tappers and nut gatherers whom Mendes defended; however, tappers' lives are as wretched as ever because of decline of rubber prices; and Mendes's widow, Ilzamar Gadelha Mendes, is in bitter feud with his party; photo; map (M)
news.title: A Crusader's Legacy Blurs in Brazil's Bitter Politics

news.abstract: Belated discovery of research on new and deadlier generation of germ warfare weapons by Russian military officers in Kazakhstan just as Soviet Union was ending its confrontation with West in 1980's fuels fierce debate in Washington over whether military is heeding Pres Boris Yeltsin's 1992 order to abandon germ warfare; discovery of animal testing of highly contagious Marburg virus at remote laboratory complex near Stepnogorsk in final days of cold war has led Clinton Administration officials and Republicans in Congress to assert that Russia is still secretly researching germ weapons; US officials say while there is scant hard evidence to support suspicions, Moscow's reluctance to open up military bases is ominous sign; skeptics of Western aid programs that pay salaries to former Russian germ scientists to thwart their recruitment by rogue or terrorist states say Moscow's lies about germ warfare program in past make trust and cooperation impossible; note Yeltsin has banned Russian experts from discussing any aspect of country's germ history and has retained several generals instrumentsl in Soviet program; worry particularly that research may be quietly proceeding on some of least known Soviet advances, such as 'bio-regulators' or germ compounds capable of controlling human moods, heart rhythms and sleep patterns; supporters of Western programs say while Russia may not be trusted unconditionally, partnership is best chance for verifying Moscow's claim to have renounced germ weapons; photos; map (L)
news.title: Germ Weapons: In Soviet Past Or in the New Russia's Future?

news.abstract: China sentences 42-year-old Zhang Shanguang to 10-year prison sentence for providing intelligence to hostile foreign organizations; charges related to interview about farmer protests with US-financed Radio Free Asia; Zhang, who is fourth dissenter to receive lengthy prison sentence in week, previously served seven years for organizing independent labor union in 1989 (M)
news.title: In Drive on Dissidents, China Gives 4th Severe Sentence in Week

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: 10 NUCLEAR MISSILES DEBUT -- Russia deployed 10 new Topol-M nuclear missiles in the Saratov region, 450 miles southeast of Moscow. The deployment was a major step for Russia's cash-shy military, because the Government does not have enough money to maintain all its armed forces and decided to concentrate on developing the single-warhead Topol-M, which has a range of 6,200 miles.    (AP)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Iraq's medical system is all but paralyzed as result of economic sanctions imposed by UN in 1990; hardest hit are childrens' hospitals where patients are succumbing to easily curable ailments because of lack of drugs and equipment; Governmment spending on medicine and equipment has fallen by more than 90 percent since sanctions were imposed; no new hospitals have been built during period, even though population has grown from 15 million to 22 million; photo (M)
news.title: Iraq a Pediatrician's Hell: No Way to Stop the Dying

news.abstract: BERN—  Ruth Dreifuss says it almost before her visitors are settled into their chairs: She will not be an alibi, a public relations prop depicting Switzerland as reconciled with its past, or a marker to paint its history with the harsh, dark lines of caricature.
news.title: Challenge for Jewish President/ Weighty Matters of Conscience : A Swiss 'Facilitator' Searches for the Middle

news.abstract: Article profiles Germany's Interior Min Otto Schily, who typifies new class that has come to power and is changing country's political culture; new breed of politicians has more checkered past and more nuanced allegiances; represent departure from scene of more predictable German--solid, solemn and unsurprising--which US and allies find disorienting; Schily comments; photo (M)
news.title: Schroder Aide Typifies New German Subtlety

news.abstract: Annual festival commemmorating Jalaluddin Rumi, Islamic mystic poet who conceived dervish dance as part of lifelong quest for religious rapture, is held in Konya, Turkey, which is world capital of Rumi cult; annual festival is city's main tourist attraction; map; photo (M)
news.title: Konya Journal; Festival of Rumi, Poet of Life's Dance

news.abstract: US warplanes patrolling northern Iraq attack Iraqi antiaircraft missile battery near Mosul after coming under fire themselves; Iraq says it repulsed attack and probably shot down enemy aircraft; says four soldiers died in attack; US Defense Dept dismisses claim; says all 27 American and British aircraft returned safely to bases in Incirlik, Turkey; latest incident comes two days after Iraq's warning that it would fire on any aircraft flying in 'no flight' zones US and allies created over northern and southern Iraq after Persian Gulf War ended in 1991; appears to mark Iraqi attempt to provoke new confrontation with US; photo; map (M)
news.title: U.S. JETS ATTACK IRAQ MISSILE POST

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: WARNING ON PINOCHET CASE  Britain's Lord Chancellor -- the Government's chief law officer -- said the legal system risked being brought into disrepute by the Augusto Pinochet case. Lord Derry Irvine referred to the decision by the House of Lords, the highest court, to set aside its own ruling in November that the former Chilean dictator did not have immunity from prosecution because he was a former head of state.    (Reuters)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Iraq's Pres Saddam Hussein complicates situation with UN Security Council with stream of bellicose statements against not only his enemies in London and Washington but also friends like Russia, France and his Arab neighbors; Iraq's future ties with UN remain in doubt as Govt vows it will never allow arms inspectors to return and is balking at further cooperation with agency, which administers huge relief program in country; had generally cooperated with aid workers, despite objections to presence of arms inspectors (M)
news.title: Iraqi Chief Finds New Enemies, Even Among Former Friends

news.abstract: WASHINGTON—  President Bill Clinton's supporters in the Senate acknowledged Tuesday that they were making little headway with proposals for censure of the president — rather than conviction and banishment from office on articles of impeachment — and they worked with Republicans to settle details of a Senate trial next week that has become all but certain.
news.title: Democrats' Hopes Fade for Pretrial Censure of Clinton in the Senate

news.abstract: Profile of scene in Hamilton, Scotland; Hamilton is first community in Britain to impose curfew on its young people, with special child safety officers questioning anyone they know to be under age of 16 on streets after eight PM and taking them home if they cannot supply sound reason why they are out; curfew measure has met with almost unanimous approval of parents; studies show it has cut theft and vandalism, but curfew is mainly aimed at curbing more of cheeky kid variety of misconduct, youths on street corners marking out territory, smoking and drinking cheap wine; photo; map (M)
news.title: Hamilton Journal; Of Stern Scots, Cheeky Kids and an Early Bedtime

news.abstract: Residents of Kinshasa, Congo, once euphoric, are increasingly weary of nation's war against rebels, war that has drawn in seven of Congo's neighbors; Congo Pres Laurent Kabila refusees to meet with rebels; many in Kinshasa think officials should meet with rebels; photo; map (M)
news.title: Long War Saps Spirit And Money In Congo

news.abstract: Gen Wiranto, head of Indonesia's armed forces, pledges that military will be neutral and not try to influence national elections next year (S)
news.title: Vow of Neutrality In Indonesia Election

news.abstract: EUROPE    BRITAIN: CHILD PROSTITUTE AS VICTIM -- The Government issued guidelines aimed at treating child prostitutes as victims of abuse rather than as criminals and at marking their employers and clients for prosecution. The latest annual figures, for 1995-1996, show that 177 youths under 17 were convicted of prostitution and another 207 were formally cautioned.   Warren Hoge (NYT)    BRITAIN: BATONS VS. TRUNCHEONS -- The British police are being warned that the growing substitution of longer and heavier American-style batons for the 11-inch wooden truncheons traditionally carried by officers has resulted in an increased number of brutality complaints. The report from the independent Police Complaints Authority says British police forces should instruct their members in restrained use of the new weapons to reduce the possibility of serious injury.   Warren Hoge (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: Israel's Environment Minister, Rafael Eitan, becomes fourth right-wing candidate to throw his hat into ring to replace Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu; many important issues face country, but so far, only lightning rod for debate has been Netanyahu's character; Netanyahu sees race as between him and 'the left,' term he uses as slur; but now he faces opposition from his own side; even Ariel Sharon, hawkish Foreign Minister and Netanyahu's most powerful ally, would not categorically rule out run for Prime Minister; photo (M)
news.title: Netanyahu Challenged From Left And Right

news.abstract: Chief judge of Jerusalem District Court orders Israeli Government to recognize conversions to Judaism performed by non-Orthodox rabbis; decision is expected to reawaken divisive issue of who is a Jew; Orthodox Jewish politicians denounce ruling and promise to circumvent it by bringing bill to Parliament that confers sole right to perform conversions on Orthodox rabbinate; leaders of minority Reform and Conservative movements celebrate what they consider landmark victory in battle to win equal status for their movements in Jewish homeland, where Orthodox control religious life (M)
news.title: Non-Orthodox Rabbis Win A Court Skirmish in Israel

news.abstract: China says it achieved economic growth of 7.8 percent for 1998, essentially meeting 8 percent goal set by political leaders at beginning of year; many economists around world are skeptical of growth report, citing indicators such as slow growth in electricity use and declining retail prices (M)
news.title: China Reports 7.8% Growth, Close to Goal It Set for '98

news.abstract: Mexican lawmakers reach compromise on country's most austere budget in modern times, just hours before constitutional deadline; full Congress is expected to adopt package, which includes deep spending cuts and increases in tariffs and fuel prices (M)
news.title: Just Hours Before Deadline, Mexicans Draft an Austerity Budget

news.abstract: EUROPE    RUSSIA: YELTSIN ATTACKS EXTREMISM -- President Boris N. Yeltsin ordered the Government to fight political and religious extremism in the wake of several recent anti-Semitic outbursts by Russian politicians. Mr. Yeltsin told Prime Minister Yevgeny M. Primakov and other senior officials to draw up a program to oppose extremism, the President's spokesman said.   (AP)    SPAIN: CONCERN OVER BASQUES -- The conservative Government and opposition Socialist Party expressed concern that the new regional government formed by Basque nationalists could undercut the fledging peace effort in the Basque region. The crucial votes came from the leftist coalition Euskal Heritarrok, which is considered close to the Basque separatists who have observed a cease-fire since September.   (NYT)
news.title: World Briefing
